Workers are deployed with natural-language (no-code) descriptions and automate workflows across revenue, IT, customer service, operations, finance, security, and HR. The platform serves 36,000+ active users, runs production digital workers, and is backed by Sapphire Ventures following a $9M raise. Jeeva AI does not currently publish a public API reference or OpenAPI definition; enrichment here is identity, trust, and security posture.

companies.name: o1 Labs
companies.description: o1 Labs (o1Labs) is a zero-knowledge cryptography company and the incubator of Mina Protocol, a lightweight blockchain that stays a constant ~22KB using recursive zk-SNARKs. o1 Labs builds the developer tooling for privacy-preserving applications: o1js, a TypeScript framework for writing zk-SNARKs and zkApps (formerly SnarkyJS); Kimchi, the underlying proof system; mina-signer for transaction signing; and Mina Node SDKs for JavaScript, Go, Python, and Rust that talk to the Mina GraphQL API. Developer documentation, zkApp guides, and the node/GraphQL API reference are published at docs.minaprotocol.com, and all tooling is open source on GitHub under the o1-labs organization.

companies.name: Flow Engineering
companies.description: Flow Engineering builds a requirements-management and AI-agent platform for hardware engineering teams. Its Systems Graph connects requirements, CAD, simulation, code, and test into a single system of record, and its AI agents continuously run impact analysis, check test coverage, verify compliance, and track mass, cost, and power budgets as designs change. Flow integrates with CAD, PLM, simulation, and developer tools (Onshape, GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Confluence, and more) and is used by hardware teams at companies such as Rivian, Joby, Skydio, and Isar Aerospace. The platform is backed by a GraphQL API at api.flowengineering.com secured with AWS Cognito OAuth2/OIDC, with API access included on paid plans. Flow Engineering is a portfolio company of EQT Ventures.

companies.name: Groundcover
companies.description: Groundcover is a cloud-native observability platform using eBPF for zero-instrumentation monitoring of Kubernetes workloads.

companies.name: Monte Carlo
companies.description: Monte Carlo is a data observability platform that uses ML to detect, resolve, and prevent data quality issues.

companies.name: Moogsoft
companies.description: Moogsoft is an AIOps platform that uses AI to reduce alert noise, correlate incidents, and automate root cause analysis.

companies.name: Pabbly Connect
companies.description: Pabbly Connect is a workflow automation platform for connecting cloud applications and automating business processes.

companies.name: pnpm
companies.description: pnpm is a fast, disk space efficient package manager for JavaScript and Node.js projects. It uses a content-addressable store and a strict, symlinked node_modules layout so every version of every package is stored exactly once on disk and projects can only access dependencies they explicitly declare. pnpm provides first-class monorepo support via pnpm-workspace.yaml, the workspace protocol, Catalogs, package filtering, and a shared lockfile, and ships supply-chain safety features such as minimumReleaseAge, opt-in lifecycle scripts, dependency overrides, and a built-in patch workflow. Developed in the open under the MIT license on GitHub with an Open Collective sponsorship model, pnpm is used by major JavaScript projects including Next.js, Vue, Vite, Nuxt, Material UI, Prisma, Astro, and SvelteKit.

companies.name: ScienceLogic
companies.description: ScienceLogic is an AIOps platform providing IT infrastructure monitoring, service management, and automated remediation.

companies.name: Faraway
companies.description: Faraway is a web3 gaming company building an interoperable gaming ecosystem for players, creators, and studios. Its platform lets game studios integrate player-driven, blockchain-based economies into their titles across EVM-compatible chains and Solana, with a unified player identity and wallet (id.faraway.com), a creator platform for user-generated content and monetization (create.faraway.com), and an in-game marketplace and secondary-trading shop (shop.faraway.com). Faraway publishes a developer platform with an API reference and an llms.txt index at docs.faraway.com. The company is backed by a16z, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Pantera Capital.

companies.name: IFTTT
companies.description: IFTTT (If This Then That) is a consumer and prosumer automation platform that connects more than 750 apps, devices, and services through conditional Applets that chain triggers to actions. The IFTTT Maker Webhooks service exposes a public HTTP API that lets developers fire triggers and execute Applets from any internet-connected device using a personal Webhooks key for authentication, with both form-encoded and JSON payload variants supported.

companies.name: iGent
companies.description: iGent AI is a UK-based artificial intelligence company (Altrincham, Cheshire) building Maestro, an autonomous AI software-engineering agent. Maestro pairs adaptive autonomy with an ensemble of frontier AI models to plan, generate, test, and refine code across large multi-file codebases inside secure cloud sandboxes, letting developers start from scratch, upload existing code, or clone a repository. Founded by Sean Ward (CEO) and Martin Szummer (CTO), iGent AI is backed by HV Capital, XTX Markets Ventures, Twinpath VC, 10x Founders, and Dhyan VC. The product publishes developer documentation, a quick-start guide, integrations, skills, and a credits-based billing model. iGent was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network; it does not currently publish a first-party public REST API.

companies.name: Logseq
companies.description: Logseq is a privacy-first, open-source platform for knowledge management and collaboration, built around a local-first outliner that stores notes as plain Markdown and Org-mode files linked into a personal knowledge graph. Its developer surface is a JavaScript/TypeScript plugin SDK (@logseq/libs) plus an in-app HTTP APIs server that exposes the same Editor and App proxy methods to local automation; there is no hosted public REST API. The project is developed in Clojure/ClojureScript, licensed AGPL-3.0, and backed by a16z.

companies.name: Standard Operating Procedures
companies.description: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are documented step-by-step instructions for routine operations and processes to ensure consistency, quality, and compliance across an organization. They are essential for regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceuticals, finance, food service, aviation, and manufacturing. SOPs establish clear responsibilities, document institutional knowledge, support regulatory compliance, enable process auditing, and facilitate employee onboarding. Software platforms for SOP management include SweetProcess, Trainual, Guru, Document360, and Notion; many offer developer APIs for embedding SOP workflows into other business systems.

companies.name: API League
companies.description: API League is a comprehensive API marketplace aggregating 60+ best-in-class APIs across categories including books, news, humor, food, knowledge, art, web, text processing, and media. It offers code examples in 21 languages, SDKs, Postman collections, and free API key access for developers to launch projects quickly.

companies.name: APIsec
companies.description: APIsec (listed as "Fxlabs" in Canaan Partners' portfolio directory, which resolves to apisec.ai) is an AI-powered API and application security platform that delivers continuous, automated security testing across the full API lifecycle. Rather than only flagging potential issues, APIsec combines threat modeling, attack-surface mapping, and AI-driven exploit validation to prove which vulnerabilities are actually exploitable at runtime — producing replayable evidence and remediation guidance. Its products span the APIsec Platform (continuous scanning and OWASP API Top 10 coverage), apisec Surface (open-source mapping of APIs, endpoints, and AI connections), and a large practitioner community through APIsec University (150,000+ practitioners) and Discord (15,000+ members). The company also publishes open-source security tooling and Agent Skills that embed OWASP API Security Top 10 intelligence directly into AI coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Copilot.

companies.name: AVAP BRUNIX
companies.description: AVAP BRUNIX is an AI-powered API development platform that serves as a copilot for developers, integrating artificial intelligence directly into the core of the AVAP framework to enhance efficiency and productivity in API development, testing, and management.

companies.name: Citrine Informatics
companies.description: Citrine Informatics is an enterprise AI software company for materials and chemicals product development, positioning itself as the world leader in generative AI for the space. The Citrine Platform pairs Citrine DataManager (capturing and organizing organizational materials knowledge on the open-source GEMD data model) with Citrine VirtualLab (running thousands of virtual experiments via Sequential Learning to identify promising formulations), supported by Citrine Catalyst and professional services. Developers integrate through the first-party Python SDK (the "citrine" and "gemd" PyPI libraries) to upload and manage data, build tables, and configure predictors and design spaces. Citrine serves 15+ industries including specialty chemicals, coatings/adhesives/sealants, plastics, personal care, food & beverage, batteries, and metals & alloys, with customers such as LyondellBasell, Eastman, Grace, Stepan, and Collano, plus a DARPA INTACT ceramics program.

companies.name: Furhat Robotics
companies.description: Furhat Robotics builds the Furhat social robot, a customizable robotic platform with a back-projected, animated digital face and multi-language voice synthesis designed for natural, multi-party human-robot conversation. Developers build interactions using the Kotlin Skill API and the Furhat SDK (with a Virtual Furhat for desktop development), stream live data through the Realtime API over WebSocket, and rapidly prototype LLM-driven characters with the FurhatAI Creator. A deprecated REST Remote API with an official Python client is also available. Furhat is widely used across academic research, clinical training, mental health, hospitality, and automotive human-machine interaction.

companies.name: Joggr
companies.description: Joggr is a documentation platform purpose-built for software teams. It bridges the gap between traditional dev docs and modern development workflows, helping engineering teams create and maintain technical documentation. Joggr ships native MCP integration with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) and APIs for building custom Slackbots, agents, and workflows on top of the platform. The primary domain has moved from joggr.io to joggr.ai.

companies.name: Open Service Mesh
companies.description: Open Service Mesh (OSM) is a lightweight, extensible, cloud native service mesh built on Envoy and the Service Mesh Interface (SMI) specification. OSM provides traffic shifting, mutual TLS, access control, observability, and automatic sidecar injection for Kubernetes-based microservices. The project is now archived by the CNCF.

companies.name: Optic
companies.description: Optic is an open source tool for OpenAPI linting, diffing, and testing that helps prevent breaking changes, publish accurate documentation, and improve API design through behavior-aware specification comparison and forwards-only governance.

companies.name: Quirrel
companies.description: Quirrel is an open source job queueing and workflow scheduling service designed for serverless and containerized JavaScript and TypeScript applications. It enables developers to enqueue, schedule, retry, and orchestrate background jobs in environments such as Next.js, Blitz.js, Redwood, Remix, SvelteKit, Nuxt.js, Express, Vercel, and Netlify Functions. Quirrel was acquired by Netlify in 2022 and remains available as an open source project.

companies.name: Runscope
companies.description: Runscope is an API monitoring and testing platform that lets teams create, schedule, and run automated tests against their APIs to catch performance problems, uptime issues, and functional regressions before customers do. Originally an independent, a16z-backed startup, Runscope was acquired by CA Technologies in 2017 and is now delivered as the API Monitoring capability of BlazeMeter (a Perforce company). The product exposes a REST API for managing buckets, tests, environments, and test results, along with scheduled runs, integrations, and real-user Radar monitoring.

companies.name: Alkira
companies.description: Alkira delivers Network Infrastructure as a Service (NaaS) through its Cloud Services Exchange, letting enterprises build, deploy, and manage a global multi-cloud network from a unified portal without provisioning physical hardware. The platform connects clouds, sites, remote users, and SaaS through Cloud Exchange Points (CXPs) with built-in segmentation, routing, integrated firewall/security services (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point, Cisco, Zscaler, Infoblox, F5), and full-stack visibility. Everything provisioned in the portal is driven by the Alkira Portal REST API and exposed as infrastructure-as-code via an official Terraform provider, a Go client library, and a published Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.

companies.name: General Intelligence
companies.description: The General Intelligence Company of New York builds Cofounder, an AI agent orchestration platform that lets a founder run an entire business through a coordinating network of specialized agents. Cofounder breaks a company into repeatable Flows and deploys agents across engineering, design, marketing, sales, finance, and support - handling product code, brand assets, outbound campaigns, incorporation, and customer service with human-approval checkpoints before significant actions execute. It provisions managed GitHub, Vercel, and Supabase, connects Stripe, Linear, Postmark, and Composio-powered MCP toolkits, and coordinates departments over shared company context. The company raised an $8.7M seed led by Union Square Ventures. Cofounder is a product workspace, not a public developer API - it consumes external APIs and MCP servers rather than publishing its own REST surface.

companies.name: GraphQL Code Generator
companies.description: GraphQL Code Generator is an open source tool from The Guild that generates typed code from GraphQL schemas and operations. It supports TypeScript, React Query, Apollo Client, Urql, and many other plugins for producing type-safe GraphQL clients and server resolvers.

companies.name: KCL
companies.description: KCL (Kusion Configuration Language) is a constraint-based record and functional programming language designed for configuration and policy scenarios. It provides features like type safety, automation, and validation for cloud-native configurations.

companies.name: Kiota
companies.description: Kiota is an open source API client generator from Microsoft that produces strongly-typed, lightweight clients from OpenAPI descriptions. It supports C#, Go, Java, PHP, Python, Ruby, Swift, and TypeScript, with a focus on minimal dependencies and idiomatic code patterns.

companies.name: Kreya
companies.description: Kreya is a GUI client for gRPC, REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, and Server-Sent Events APIs. All data is stored in git-diffable files for easy reviews and versioning. Kreya provides automated snapshot and scripted tests, flexible environments, and support for all gRPC streaming modes.

companies.name: LF Edge
companies.description: LF Edge is an umbrella organization under the Linux Foundation establishing an open, interoperable framework for edge computing independent of hardware, silicon, cloud, or operating system. It hosts projects like Akraino, EdgeX Foundry, and Open Horizon.

companies.name: Privado
companies.description: Privado (Privado.ai) is a privacy engineering and data-privacy compliance company that helps engineering and privacy teams build privacy-first products. Its flagship is an open-source static code-analysis scanner that detects personal-data flows in source code, finds data-security violations, and generates compliance artifacts such as RoPA and Google Play Store Data Safety reports. The scanner runs locally or in CI/CD (Docker-based) via the Privado CLI, and results can optionally sync to the Privado Cloud dashboard where products like Wren (an AI privacy analyst), Agentic Assessments, Dynamic Data Maps, Web Auditor, and App Auditor automate data mapping and privacy impact assessments. Privado is a DevSecOps / privacy-governance tool rather than a public REST API provider; its developer surface is the open-source scanner, the CLI, and the docs at docs.privado.ai. Backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Protocol Buffers
companies.description: Protocol Buffers (protobuf) is Google's language-neutral, platform-neutral extensible mechanism for serializing structured data, providing a code generation engine that produces efficient data access classes in multiple programming languages.

companies.name: Zefchain
companies.description: Zefchain Labs is the company behind Linera, a decentralized Web3 protocol designed for highly scalable, low-latency applications using a "microchain" architecture in which each user or application runs its own lightweight chain. Developers build applications in Rust with the open-source Linera SDK, deploy them to a public Testnet, and expose chain state to web frontends through a GraphQL node service. Zefchain also operates Linera Markets, a 24/7 on-chain trading platform. The project (formerly branded Zefchain) is developed in the open at github.com/linera-io under Apache-2.0 and is backed by a16z. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public sources.

companies.name: LogicMonitor
companies.description: LogicMonitor is an AI-powered infrastructure monitoring and observability platform for hybrid IT environments.

companies.name: University of Reading
companies.description: The University of Reading is a public research university in Reading, England, ranked #172 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on open research and scholarly metadata rather than a formal developer portal. The university operates two EPrints-based repositories — CentAUR (the Central Archive University of Reading) and the University of Reading Research Data Archive — both of which expose live OAI-PMH metadata harvesting endpoints. No general-purpose, self-service developer portal, public REST API catalog, or official GitHub organization could be confirmed; administrative, identity, and student-information interfaces are gated behind institutional affiliation and federated authentication.

companies.name: Unweave
companies.description: Unweave is a London-based developer platform that describes itself as "Supabase for Machine Learning" — open source machine learning development environments with serverless GPU sessions, persistent volumes, SSH/VS Code access, project linking, and bring-your-own-cloud provider support (e.g. LambdaLabs), driven by a first-party CLI. Backed by Speedinvest. The platform is open source (Go) on GitHub, but development has been dormant since mid-2023: the docs and API hosts are offline while the marketing site, blog, changelog, and pricing pages remain up.

companies.name: App.net
companies.description: App.net (ADN) was a paid, ad-free real-time social networking and microblogging platform launched in 2012 by Dalton Caldwell's Mixed Media Labs after a public crowdfunding campaign. It was explicitly developer-first: the App.net Stream API exposed posts, users, follows, files, channels, private messaging, filters and a real-time streaming/subscription surface, all governed by OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens and a consistent data/meta response envelope. Third-party clients (Alpha, and many community apps) were built entirely on the public API. App.net announced in 2016 that it would not renew and the service was shut down on 2017-03-14; the live API hosts (api.app.net, developers.app.net) no longer resolve and the app.net domain is now operated by an unrelated apps directory. The API documentation (appdotnet/api-spec), terms of service, and official SDKs remain publicly preserved on the appdotnet GitHub organization, which is the basis for this profile.

companies.name: Kipu Quantum
companies.description: Kipu Quantum GmbH is a Berlin-based deep-tech company building application-specific, hardware-efficient quantum algorithms and delivering them as a managed cloud platform. Its flagship product, the Kipu Quantum Hub (hub.kipu-quantum.com), is an end-to-end platform for industrial quantum computing: it provides unified access to 20+ quantum backends (IBM Quantum, IonQ, IQM, QuEra, Rigetti, Pasqal, Azure Quantum), a visual workflow designer for quantum-classical pipelines, an AI "matchmaker" (Tinkuq) that translates a business problem into a solver configuration, and a Quantum Service Store of pre-built solvers (Miray, Rimay, Iskay, HUK) targeting optimization, portfolio mix, network routing, and classification. Developers automate runs and integrate via a Python SDK, REST API, and CLI, authenticating with API keys and OAuth2/OIDC (Keycloak, PlanQK realm). Founded and led by Prof. Dr. Enrique Solano and Dr. Tobias Grab. Backed by HV Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network via VC-portfolio enrichment.

companies.name: Locofy
companies.description: Locofy.ai is an AI-assisted design-to-code platform that converts Figma and Adobe XD designs into production-ready front-end code. The flagship product Locofy Lightning is a Figma/Adobe XD plugin that tags designs and exports responsive code; Locofy Builder is a web-based workspace for refining the generated app, wiring data, and shipping to repositories. Output targets include React, Next.js, React Native, HTML/CSS, and Gatsby. The platform is primarily delivered as plugins and a web app rather than a public REST API.

companies.name: Payform
companies.description: PayForm is a no-code payment form builder that lets creators and small businesses accept one-time and recurring credit-card payments without writing code. Users design customizable checkout forms with flexible fields, run recurring billing with trial periods and setup fees, and deliver digital content such as e-books, videos, and music through a members-only area. It supports 50+ currencies and 30+ languages, connects to the Stripe and PayPal payment gateways, and provides a subscriber self-service portal, Zapier automation to 2,000+ apps, and webhooks for custom integrations. Payform is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

companies.name: AtomicJar
companies.description: AtomicJar is a developer-testing company, founded in 2021 by the original creators and maintainers of the open-source Testcontainers project and acquired by Docker in December 2023. AtomicJar builds tooling that lets developers run reliable integration tests against real service dependencies (databases, message brokers, and other systems) defined in code and wrapped in Docker containers, replacing brittle mocks and in-memory fakes. Its product line spans Testcontainers OSS (the open-source libraries for Java, .NET, Go, Node.js, Python, Rust, and more), Testcontainers Desktop (a companion app for local development), and Testcontainers Cloud (a hosted service that offloads container execution to the cloud so tests run consistently from a laptop through CI without a local Docker daemon). AtomicJar and its Testcontainers products are used by engineering teams at companies including Spotify, Uber, Capital One, Elastic, Netflix, and Zalando.

companies.name: Control Seat
companies.description: Control Seat is an AI-native industrial systems integrator building a modern replacement for legacy SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) platforms such as Ignition, WinCC, and FactoryTalk. It designs, builds, deploys, and runs the full industrial control stack, from PLC programming (Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff) and HMI/SCADA operator screens to OT/IT networking, historians, and analytics, on a single unified platform. The product connects to field devices over OPC UA and MQTT (Sparkplug B), integrates with AVEVA PI, Ignition, and standard SQL/time-series databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, InfluxDB, Prometheus) plus REST APIs, and streams 10k+ tags per second at sub-100ms latency. AI-native features let operators generate control screens in seconds, run anomaly detection and forecasting, and query the historian in plain English. Enterprise capabilities include SSO, SCIM, role-based access control, and audit logs, with deployment on managed cloud or self-hosted on-premises. Founded in 2025 by Jack Grodnick and Warren Shepard, Control Seat is based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026).

companies.name: Dredd
companies.description: Dredd is a language-agnostic, open source HTTP API testing framework that validates API implementations against API Blueprint or OpenAPI (2.0/3.0) description documents.

companies.name: Fusebit
companies.description: Fusebit is a developer-first embedded integration platform for adding third-party integrations to SaaS products. The company was acquired and the Fusebit platform and developer documentation are no longer actively maintained, but the historical API surface and SDK assets remain available via the Fusebit GitHub organization for reference.

companies.name: Genie
companies.description: Genie is an open source, full-stack web framework for the Julia programming language, developed by the Barcelona-based company Genie (backed by Speedinvest) to let data scientists and R&D engineers turn Julia models, simulations, and analyses into production-ready, data-centric web apps, APIs, and interactive dashboards. The framework has three core components: Genie.jl for backend routing and REST APIs, Stipple.jl for low-code reactive UIs, and SearchLight.jl as the database ORM, plus first-party authentication and authorization plugins and Genie Builder, a VS Code extension with a drag-and-drop UI builder and AI assistant. It is used to build data exploration dashboards, financial data products, ML/AI and simulation apps, bioinformatics tools, and internal tooling. Distributed as MIT-licensed Julia packages via the Julia General registry.

companies.name: Ingresse
companies.description: Ingresse is a Brazilian ticketing-as-a-service (TaaS) platform that powers event ticket sales, access control, and the attendee experience for organizers and partners. Its public developer platform lets integrators build tools and services on top of Ingresse — creating events, selling and validating tickets, managing users, and handling payments — through a versioned REST API (v1 and v2) authenticated with an individually issued API key. Ingresse publishes first-party SDKs for JavaScript/Node, Android, iOS, and PHP, plus message-queue libraries, and hosts its reference documentation on a ReadMe developer portal. Ingresse is backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Kpt
companies.description: kpt is a package-centric toolchain that enables a configuration authoring, automation, and delivery experience, which simplifies managing Kubernetes platforms and KRM-driven infrastructure at scale by utilizing resource configuration as the artifact of record.

companies.name: Monograph
companies.description: Monograph is firm-management software purpose-built for architecture and engineering (A&E) practices, unifying project management, resourcing and staffing, time tracking, budgeting, invoicing and client payments in one connected system. Used by thousands of US-based A&E firms, it integrates with QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, but publishes no public developer API, webhooks, or SDKs. Backed by Homebrew and Index Ventures.

companies.name: NSwag
companies.description: NSwag is an open source .NET toolchain for generating C# and TypeScript API clients and Swagger/OpenAPI specifications from ASP.NET controllers and vice versa.

companies.name: OpenAPI TypeScript Codegen
companies.description: OpenAPI TypeScript Codegen is an open source tool that generates TypeScript API clients from OpenAPI specifications, producing lightweight, fully typed client code with support for multiple HTTP libraries and runtime environments.

companies.name: Openprose
companies.description: OpenProse, Inc. builds an open-source (MIT) programming language for AI sessions: standing AI jobs are declared as durable Markdown contracts (`*.prose.md` files) that state what should stay true, and the system works out how much model work it takes to keep it true. The language ships as an agent skill (`open-prose`) that runs on any compliant agent host such as Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, and is paired with Reactor — a deterministic harness (`@openprose/reactor` SDK plus the `@openprose/reactor-cli` `reactor` binary) whose model spend scales with surprise, not the clock: a render runs only when a node's subscribed input fingerprints move, and each commit is a content-addressed receipt with no LLM in the wake/commit decision. Contract kinds are responsibility, function, gateway, pattern, and test; Forme is the semantic dependency-injection layer that wires `### Requires` facets to `### Maintains` facets. A Y Combinator company founded in 2026 (San Francisco) with open-source traction; distributed as npm packages rather than a hosted REST API.

companies.name: Orval
companies.description: Orval is an open source tool that generates TypeScript API clients, React Query hooks, Angular services, and mock service workers from OpenAPI specifications. It produces type-safe, framework-integrated code with support for custom transformers and output formats.

companies.name: Portman
companies.description: Portman is an open source CLI tool that auto-generates Postman collections with contract and variation tests from OpenAPI specifications, supporting OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1, fuzzing, request customization, pre-request scripts, and direct upload to Postman or execution via Newman in CI/CD pipelines.

companies.name: Rafay Product Documentation
companies.description: Rafay product documentation, API references, Kubernetes platform guides, and resources covering the Rafay Kubernetes Operations Platform (KOP), GPU PaaS, AI workloads, and ecosystem integrations.

companies.name: Ready (formerly Argent)
companies.description: Ready (formerly Argent) is a self-custodial crypto wallet and smart-account platform for Starknet and Ethereum. It builds account-abstraction wallets (Ready Wallet, Ready Multisig, Web Wallet), the Ready Card for cashing out, and developer tooling for dApps — session keys, paymasters / gas abstraction, outside execution, multicalls, and signature/cosigner verification — shipped as first-party client SDKs (StarknetKit, @argent/x-sessions, web3.swift, starknet.swift). The company rebranded from Argent to Ready; developer resources live at docs.ready.co and the argentlabs GitHub organization. Its developer surface is client SDKs rather than a public REST API.

companies.name: Sunscreen
companies.description: Sunscreen is a cryptography company building the Secure Processing Framework (SPF) — an end-to-end platform for Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) on blockchain. SPF lets web2 and web3 developers write programs, compile them to the Parasol FHE processor, and run them over encrypted data on-chain without ever exposing plaintext. The stack includes the open-source Sunscreen FHE/ZKP compiler (a family of Rust crates on crates.io), the Parasol processor runtime, a TypeScript SDK (@sunscreen/spf-client) and a Rust CLI for encrypting values, uploading FHE programs and ciphertexts, requesting threshold decryption, and managing on-chain access control (ACL). Founded by cryptographers and engineers from Nucypher, Microsoft, Meta, Tableau, Two Sigma and Caldera, and backed by Northzone.

companies.name: Audiomob
companies.description: Audiomob is an in-game and in-app audio advertising platform that lets mobile game and app publishers monetize their titles with non-interruptive, skippable and rewarded audio ads while advertisers reach engaged gaming audiences at scale. Publishers integrate through the Audiomob Unity plugin or native iOS and Android SDKs (plus a community React Native adapter), add their games to the Audiomob developer dashboard, and configure ad units, an Ad Availability API, and server-to-server webhooks for reward and event tracking. The platform is Open Measurement (IAB Tech Lab) compliant, supports consent management via OneTrust and Sourcepoint, exposes Impression Level Revenue Data (ILRD), and integrates with mediation partners such as AdMob and LevelPlay (MAX) and mobile measurement partners including Adjust, Singular and Tenjin. The current SDK line is SDK 10. Audiomob is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

companies.name: B12
companies.description: B12 is an AI-powered website builder that generates professional websites, online stores, and web apps from a short prompt. Founded on a human-in-the-loop model and now driven by its B12 3.0 AI Agent (launched February 2026), the platform lets solopreneurs, consultants, freelancers, and growing teams describe a business idea and launch a site in minutes, then run that business online with built-in tools for SEO, online payments and invoicing, scheduling, email marketing, client intake, contact management, and contracts with eSignatures. B12 offers self-serve DIY plans as well as Expert plans where its design and content team handles setup and ongoing updates. Over 4 million websites have been built on B12. B12 exposes its website-generation capability to AI agents through a published Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, a Claude plugin, and a Website Generator GPT, but does not publish a general-purpose public REST API.

companies.name: Pingdom
companies.description: Pingdom is a website uptime and performance monitoring service from SolarWinds that tracks availability, response time, transactions, real user monitoring, and page speed from a global network of probe servers. It alerts teams via email, SMS, webhooks, and integrations when websites, APIs, or critical user journeys experience downtime or degraded performance. The Pingdom Public REST API (v3.1) provides programmatic access to checks, results, alerts, contacts, maintenance windows, and reports using Bearer token authentication.

companies.name: Geordie AI
companies.description: Geordie AI is an enterprise AI governance platform that gives organizations visibility into and control over the autonomous AI agents deployed across their environments. It discovers agents across code, cloud, endpoints, and SaaS; maps each agent's posture (permissions, tools, MCP connections, and system prompts); provides behavioral observability with continuous audit trails and anomaly detection; delivers risk intelligence mapped to standards such as OWASP, NIST, ISO 42001, and the EU AI Act; and offers Beam, a real-time remediation layer that applies deterministic controls at the agent level. Geordie raised a $30M Series A and is used by enterprises including Xapo Bank, Fitch Group, Synthesia, AlphaSense, Owkin, OakNorth, and A+E Global Media. The company is SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and General Catalyst and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Geordie publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Stoik
companies.description: Stoïk is a European cyber-insurtech, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, that pairs cyber insurance with active security prevention for small and mid-market businesses (up to roughly €1B revenue). Insurance coverage of up to €10M is backed by Tokio Marine HCC, Swiss Re and Axeria IARD and sold 100% online through a broker platform used by 1,500+ partner brokers across France, Germany, Spain, Austria, Belgium and the Netherlands. Beyond insurance, Stoïk ships a free risk-monitoring suite — Stoïk Protect (external scan, phishing simulation, Active Directory and cloud scanning, leaked-credential monitoring), Managed Detection & Response (MDR), and managed email security — plus 24/7 incident response. Stoïk is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Anthemis. No public developer API is published today; the developer-adjacent surface is a GitBook help center (docs.stoik.io, with an llms.txt index and a dated changelog), the insured/broker platform at app.stoik.io, and the GitHub org github.com/stoikio.

companies.name: Analytics
companies.description: A curated index of analytics platforms, SDKs, and open source solutions spanning the full analytics spectrum — from web and product analytics (Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog, Plausible, Matomo, Heap) to customer data platforms (Segment, mParticle, RudderStack), mobile analytics (Firebase Analytics, Adjust, AppsFlyer, Braze), business intelligence (Looker, Tableau, Metabase, Redash), event streaming (Kafka, Kinesis), and real-time analytics infrastructure (ClickHouse, Druid, Pinot). Covers both SaaS and self-hosted, open source and commercial offerings.

companies.name: API Insights
companies.description: API Insights is a free online tool powered by Treblle that provides advanced API analysis and monitoring by evaluating OpenAPI specifications across multiple dimensions including AI readiness, design quality, performance, and security. It scores APIs against industry benchmarks and provides actionable recommendations for improvement.

companies.name: Cline
companies.description: Cline (formerly Claude Dev) is an open-source autonomous coding agent. The Cline VS Code extension has 5M+ installs; JetBrains is in early access; the Cline CLI is also available. Edits files, runs commands, uses the browser, and federates to multiple LLM providers. An MCP Marketplace extends Cline with custom tools. There is also a hosted/managed offering (Cline.bot) with free and paid tiers plus enterprise sales.

companies.name: Coefficient Works
companies.description: Coefficient Works, Inc. (operating as Coefficient) is a San Mateo, California no-code data platform that connects live business data to Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel. Founded in 2019 by Navneet Loiwal and Tommy Tsai, the company provides point-and-click connectors to 60+ business systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, MySQL, Stripe, Looker, Tableau and Google Ads, with scheduled two-way sync, spreadsheet-native alerting through Slack and email, live web dashboards, and an AI assistant that builds pivot tables, formulas, charts and data-cleaning steps from natural language. Coefficient is a consumer of other providers' APIs rather than a producer: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI or AsyncAPI description, no client SDKs, and no developer portal. Distribution is through the Google Workspace Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource. The company is backed by Battery Ventures, Foundation Capital and S28 Capital.

companies.name: Coinbase OnchainKit
companies.description: Coinbase OnchainKit is a TypeScript React framework from Coinbase for building onchain applications on Base and other EVM networks. It bundles ready-made React components (wallets, identity, transactions, swap, checkout, fund, NFT), TypeScript utilities, and integrations with Smart Wallet, Base Account, Frames, and Mini Apps. OnchainKit is distributed as the @coinbase/onchainkit npm package along with companion CLIs (create-onchain) and a MiniApp manifest generator. It is built on top of Wagmi, Viem, and TailwindCSS and is the recommended client SDK for the Base ecosystem.

companies.name: Garden
companies.description: Garden is an open-source Kubernetes-native development and CI/CD platform. Garden Core, a declarative CLI and engine, models a project as a graph of Build, Deploy, Test, and Run actions powered by pluggable providers (kubernetes, local-kubernetes, container, exec, jib, helm, terraform, pulumi). Garden Cloud / Garden Enterprise add a hosted control plane for remote container builds, ephemeral preview environments, team dashboards, team-wide caching, secrets, RBAC, audit, and SSO. The CLI integrates with any CI system and IDE; teams use Garden to standardize how dev, preview, staging, and prod environments are built and deployed.

companies.name: Magic Leap
companies.description: Magic Leap is an augmented reality company headquartered in Plantation, Florida, building see-through AR optics (waveguides and display systems) and the Magic Leap 2 enterprise AR headset, along with a developer platform for spatial computing. Developers build on-device applications using the Magic Leap Unity SDK, an OpenXR runtime, and a native C API, distributed through the Magic Leap Hub package registry and the company's GitHub organization. Magic Leap does not publish a public hosted REST API or OpenAPI specification; its integration surface is the device SDK. The company holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II attestations. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (a16z, Kleiner Perkins, Obvious Ventures).

companies.name: Rezonant
companies.description: Rezonant is a London-based product development workspace, founded by former Stripe UK engineering leader Emma Burrows, that captures product intent and carries it all the way through tasks, coding agents, and shipped code. It helps product managers and engineering teams turn product vision into engineering-ready work by connecting to their existing stack (Jira, Linear, GitHub, and docs), shaping intent into buildable tasks, and delivering code while keeping teams in control. Rezonant exited stealth in 2026 with $6M in seed funding from General Catalyst and firstminute Capital. It is offered as a credit-metered SaaS with Free, Business, and Enterprise (SSO/SCIM) plans plus a Chrome extension. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio; the company publishes a product help center but no public developer API at this time.

companies.name: Sintra
companies.description: Sintra is a no-code AI-employees platform that gives small businesses a team of role-based digital workers. It ships 12 specialized AI helpers — such as Soshie (social media), Cassie (customer support), Seomi (SEO), Buddy, and Vizzy (meeting notetaker) — that handle social media, inbox, content, customer support, SEO, and sales and business operations. Users chat with helpers, schedule recurring background tasks, build custom helpers with the Helper Builder, and connect tools like Facebook, Instagram, Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Google Drive, Notion, and Strava through consumer OAuth integrations. Sintra is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. As of this profile Sintra publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or API reference — it is an end-user low-code product rather than a developer platform.

companies.name: Tdaycom
companies.description: tday (tday.com) is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) AI platform that turns a software product into on-brand marketing content. It connects to a company's GitHub repository or live website, and on every release automatically produces a launch package — an end-to-end demo video generated from real product flows, feature showcases, and on-brand social graphics and ads — then publishes that creative to social and ad channels and measures how it performs, closing the loop from what a team ships to what it posts. tday operates through the browser like a user, with no SDK embedded in the customer's product, using isolated per-run workspaces, scoped repository access, secure credential storage, and secret redaction. tday exposes a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://tday.com/api/mcp secured with OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, dynamic client registration, RFC 8414 / RFC 9728 discovery), making it the agent-facing surface of the platform.

companies.name: Agile Delivery
companies.description: A collection of resources, tools, and APIs related to agile delivery practices — the iterative approach to project management and software delivery that helps teams ship value faster through sprints, continuous feedback, and adaptive planning. Agile delivery frameworks emphasize cross-functional collaboration, working software over documentation, and responding to change over following a plan. This topic covers project management APIs, sprint planning tools, backlog management platforms, and delivery metrics services used to implement agile delivery at scale.

companies.name: Agile SDLC
companies.description: A collection of resources, tools, and APIs covering the Agile Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) — an iterative and incremental approach to software development that integrates agile principles across every phase from requirements through deployment. Agile SDLC replaces the rigid waterfall model with continuous planning, development, testing, and delivery through short sprint cycles. This topic covers the APIs and platforms that support each phase of the agile SDLC including requirements management, code review, CI/CD, testing, and deployment.

companies.name: Augmentus
companies.description: Augmentus is a no-code adaptive robotics company (founded 2019, offices in Singapore and Pflugerville, Texas) that turns industrial robots into AI-driven automation systems programmable without code or a teach pendant. Its platform pairs 3D scanning and computer vision with AI motion planning to auto-generate robot toolpaths for welding, surface finishing, spraying, sandblasting, sanding, and material removal across ABB, FANUC, KUKA, Yaskawa, Kawasaki, Universal Robots, and Techman arms — cutting process automation from weeks to minutes. Sold as Standard (CAD-based toolpaths) and Pro (vision-guided) tiers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures; profiled here from public sources. Augmentus ships a desktop/on-prem product rather than a public web API, so this profile is identity-and-presence oriented.

companies.name: Kaizo
companies.description: Kaizo is an AI-powered quality assurance, coaching, and performance management platform for customer support teams working in Zendesk and Salesforce. Its AutoQA engine automatically scores 100% of support conversations in real time, analyzing sentiment and empathy, generating conversation summaries, surfacing escalation risks, and turning support data into performance insights. AI coaching builds data-driven improvement roadmaps for agents, while dashboards and reporting help support leaders compare team and individual outcomes. Kaizo delivers its product primarily as native apps for the Zendesk Marketplace and Salesforce AppExchange rather than as a public developer API. The company is SOC 2 certified, ISO 27001 certified, GDPR compliant, and continuously monitored by Secureframe. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: NanoVMs
companies.description: NanoVMs builds unikernel infrastructure that lets developers run a single application as its own lightweight, secure virtual machine with no operating system and no devops. Its open-source toolchain centers on OPS (the ops CLI, ops.city) for building and deploying unikernels to any cloud in seconds, and Nanos (nanos.org), a kernel designed to run one and only one application in a virtualized environment. The project ships editor extensions, a Terraform provider, a Homebrew tap, a package repository (repo.ops.city), and an official MCP server (ops-mcp) for driving the toolchain from AI agents. NanoVMs is a Bloomberg Beta and Initialized Capital portfolio company.

companies.name: Bearer
companies.description: Bearer is a developer-first static application security testing (SAST) platform whose open-source CLI (written in Go, Elastic License 2.0) scans source code and analyzes data flows to discover, filter, and prioritize security and privacy risks. It detects OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 vulnerabilities, tracks sensitive data (PII/PHI) across a codebase, and produces GDPR / DPIA / PIA privacy reports. Bearer supports Go, Python, PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, and Java, and integrates into CI/CD via SARIF, GitLab SAST, and reviewdog output formats. The company's commercial platform was acquired by Cycode in 2024; the Bearer CLI remains open source. Bearer surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech and Point Nine and has been enriched from its public docs, GitHub org, and live domain probes.

companies.name: Distroless
companies.description: Distroless images by Google contain only the application and its runtime dependencies, stripping out package managers, shells, and other OS-level utilities to minimize attack surface and image size. The smallest variant (gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12) is roughly 2 MB. Distroless ships base images for static binaries, glibc-based binaries, C/C++, Java (17, 21, 25), Node.js (22, 24), and Python 3, with multi-architecture support including amd64, arm64, arm, s390x, ppc64le, and riscv64. Adopters include Kubernetes, Knative, Tekton, and Teleport.

companies.name: Echo
companies.description: Echo is a software supply-chain security company that delivers vulnerability-free (CVE-free), secure-by-design base container images, language libraries, hardened virtual machines, serverless runtimes, and OS packages. Its artifacts are built as drop-in replacements so engineering teams eliminate known CVEs across their software supply chain without changing application code, cutting remediation toil and easing compliance with frameworks like FedRAMP, FIPS, PCI DSS, DORA, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Echo operates as a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) and publishes a Trust Center with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and FIPS 140-3 assurance. The company is backed by GGV Capital.

companies.name: Flyby Robotics
companies.description: Flyby Robotics is an American manufacturer of open-architecture, NDAA-compliant medium-lift drones built as a platform for physical and edge AI. Its F-11 series (F-11T, F-11S, F-11H) pairs onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX GPU compute (up to 314 TOPS) and an open ArduPilot/CubePilot flight controller with a developer-facing C++ SDK, so engineers can register custom payloads, stream video over GStreamer, and programmatically control the aircraft. The company ships the Flyby SDK (flyby-sdk-release) through GitHub and documents it at docs.flybydev.com, targeting ISR, photogrammetry, public-safety, research, and drone-delivery use cases. Flyby Robotics raised a $4M pre-seed backed by investors including MaC Venture Capital, Gaingels, and Anthemis Group. This profile captures Flyby's developer surface as it exists today: an on-board SDK and docs rather than a hosted REST API.

companies.name: Qt
companies.description: Qt Group is a global software company that builds cross-platform development, design, and quality-assurance tools used across more than 70 industries and billions of devices. Its portfolio spans the Qt Framework (cross-platform C++ software libraries and APIs), the Qt Creator IDE, Qt for MCUs, Qt Design Studio, and the quality-assurance suite (Squish GUI test automation, Coco code coverage, Test Center, and Axivion static analysis). Qt does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; its "APIs" are C++/QML/Python library APIs shipped with the framework, with the official Python bindings (PySide6/PySide2) distributed on PyPI. Documentation, learning, and support are provided through doc.qt.io, the Qt Academy, and forum.qt.io.

companies.name: RACE Protocol
companies.description: RACE Protocol is a multi-chain, on-chain infrastructure for developing and deploying secure and fair web3 games. It is delivered primarily through a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK (sdk-core, sdk-solana, sdk-sui, sdk-facade) and a command-line tool (race-cli) for game bundle publishing, account management, and payment claims, rather than as a traditional REST API. Smart contracts run on Solana and Sui.

companies.name: Seezo
companies.description: Seezo is an automated, AI-powered security design review platform. It analyzes design documents and product requirement docs (PRDs) to generate explainable, consistent, and contextual security requirements — threat models, data-flow diagrams, and component maps — before developers begin coding, then routes those requirements into the tools engineering teams already use (Jira, GitHub, Slack, Confluence, Linear, ServiceNow, and more). Seezo is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition; its OAuth surface authenticates users of the Seezo web app.

companies.name: Noble
companies.description: Noble (operated by Benga Inc.) is a no-code risk and credit decisioning platform that provides risk infrastructure for the full customer lifecycle. Fintech companies, lenders, and banks use Noble to verify customer identity, aggregate and assess credit and financial-health data from multiple sources, build and launch automated underwriting and decisioning workflows with a no-code Workflow Builder, and monitor customer behavior and creditworthiness over time. Noble exposes this capability as a SaaS platform, an API, and an embeddable widget, plus pre-built data-partner integrations, so teams can build, launch, and scale digital financial products faster. Founded in 2021 and based in San Mateo, California, Noble is a Y Combinator company backed by Insight Partners, Paradigm, and Polychain.

companies.name: Testlio
companies.description: Testlio is a managed software testing and quality assurance company that pairs a global, vetted community of expert testers with a testing-management platform (powered by its Leo AI Engine) to deliver on-demand manual, automated, functional, regression, payments, localization, accessibility, usability, and AI testing across web, mobile, streaming, and voice experiences. Founded in Estonia and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Testlio is a Techstars-backed company serving enterprise engineering and QA teams. It exposes no public REST API; the platform integrates with engineering toolchains (Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, GitLab, TestRail, Xray, Slack, BrowserStack, SauceLabs, Playwright) and ships first-party CI/CD integrations, including a CircleCI orb and a Jenkins plugin, alongside a documented Trust Center.

companies.name: Agile
companies.description: A collection of resources, standards, and APIs representing the broader agile landscape — the set of software development principles first codified in the 2001 Agile Manifesto. Agile values individuals and interactions over processes and tools, working software over comprehensive documentation, customer collaboration over contract negotiation, and responding to change over following a plan. This topic index covers the full ecosystem of agile frameworks, methodologies, tools, and APIs including Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, XP, and Lean.

companies.name: Agile Methodology
companies.description: A collection of resources, standards, and APIs related to agile methodology — the set of principles and frameworks that guide modern software development. Agile methodologies including Scrum, Kanban, SAFe, and XP emphasize iterative delivery, customer collaboration, and adaptability. This topic covers the ecosystem of project management APIs, ceremony-facilitation tools, and metrics platforms that teams use to implement agile methodology in practice.

companies.name: Bun
companies.description: Bun is a fast, all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit built by Oven (oven-sh). A single self-contained binary bundles a Node.js-compatible runtime, a package manager (a drop-in, dramatically faster replacement for npm/yarn/pnpm), a native bundler and single-file executable compiler, and a Jest-compatible test runner. Bun is designed as an incrementally adoptable drop-in replacement for Node.js, emphasizing startup speed, install speed, and elegant built-in APIs. It is open source, distributed as a binary via an install script, Homebrew, Docker, and npm, and is surfaced here as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company. Bun exposes no hosted REST API; the CLI and the runtime/bundler APIs are the developer surface.

companies.name: Double Robotics
companies.description: Double Robotics builds telepresence robots for hybrid work and education, best known for the self-driving Double 3 videoconferencing robot and the earlier iPad-based Double 2. Its developer program spans three surfaces: the Double 3 SDK (a local command-and-event API exposed over a Unix domain socket on the robot, covering base movement, navigation, PTZ cameras, depth sensors, WebRTC calling, and standby/sidebar apps), iOS SDKs for the Double 2 (Basic Control and Camera Kit), and a Fleet REST API for programmatic access to fleet-management data such as robots, users, call logs, and visitor passes. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched against the company's public developer surface.

companies.name: Jules
companies.description: Jules is Google's autonomous, asynchronous AI coding agent, developed inside Google Labs and powered by the Gemini family of models (currently Gemini 2.5 Pro on the free tier and Gemini 3 Pro on paid tiers). Jules connects to a user's GitHub repositories, clones the target repo into a sandboxed Google Cloud VM, generates a multi-step plan, and then executes coding tasks such as bug fixes, refactors, dependency bumps, test authoring, and small feature builds, ultimately opening a pull request for human review. Jules ships three surfaces beyond the web app at jules.google.com: a documented REST API in alpha at jules.googleapis.com/v1alpha (Sources, Sessions, Activities) authenticated via X-Goog-Api-Key, a lightweight CLI called Jules Tools installable via npm, and a Gemini CLI extension that exposes Jules as a /jules slash command. Access is gated to Google account holders and the API is experimental. Jules is sold as part of the Google AI subscription bundles, with a free introductory plan (15 tasks/day, 3 concurrent), Google AI Pro at $19.99/month (100 tasks/day, 15 concurrent, Gemini 3 Pro), and Google AI Ultra at $124.99/month (300 tasks/day, 60 concurrent, priority Gemini 3 Pro access).

companies.name: KeyRunner
companies.description: KeyRunner is a local-first API platform combining a desktop API client, request monitor, mock server, and secret manager. It is delivered as desktop applications (Windows, macOS Intel, macOS Apple Silicon), a VS Code extension, and a CLI, with all requests and secrets kept inside the developer environment.

companies.name: MOSN
companies.description: MOSN (Modular Open Smart Network) is a cloud-native network proxy written in Go, open-sourced by Ant Group. It serves as a Service Mesh data plane and can function as L4/L7 load balancer, API gateway, and cloud-native ingress, with multi-protocol support including HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC.

companies.name: Motadata
companies.description: Motadata is an AIOps platform for IT infrastructure monitoring, log management, network analytics, and service desk automation.

companies.name: OneAPM
companies.description: OneAPM (Beijing Blueware Technology / 北京蓝海讯通科技) is a Chinese application performance management and intelligent IT operations vendor founded in 2008. Its product suite instruments applications and infrastructure end to end: Application Insight (server-side, code-level tracing for Java, .NET, PHP, Python, Node.js, Ruby and Go), Browser Insight and Mobile Insight (real user monitoring), Infrastructure Insight and Network Insight, LogInsight for log analytics, Cloud Alert (OneAlert) for intelligent alerting, Cloud Test for performance testing, OneITSM for IT service management, and the Intelligence Insight (I²) AIOps platform. It serves over 60,000 enterprise users across telecommunications, finance, government, transportation, energy and e-commerce, delivered as SaaS or on-premise, and instruments applications via language-specific agents (SDKs) published to npm, RubyGems and a private index.

companies.name: Operant
companies.description: Operant AI is a San Francisco-based runtime security company (founded 2021, backed by Felicis) that protects cloud and AI applications with real-time, Kubernetes-native "3D Runtime Defense" — discovery, detection, and defense across APIs, services, LLMs, and agents. Its platform delivers automatic API discovery and catalogs, API-to-API microsegmentation, protocol-specific authentication/authorization, traffic rate limiting, inline auto-redaction of sensitive/PII data, and OWASP/MITRE guardrails that block a majority of the OWASP Top 10 threats. Product lines include Agent Protector, Endpoint Protector, AI Gatekeeper, an MCP Gateway, and Cloud Application Detection and Response (CADR). Operant is SOC 2 Type II compliant and publishes open-source tooling such as Woodpecker (red teaming for AI and cloud).

companies.name: Prism
companies.description: Prism is an open source HTTP mock and validation server from Stoplight that generates dynamic mock responses and validates requests against OpenAPI specifications.

companies.name: Radiant Security
companies.description: Radiant Security is an AI-powered Security Operations Center (SOC) platform that automates alert triage, investigation, and response so security teams can scale coverage without adding headcount. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in the SF Bay Area with offices in Tel Aviv and Sao Paulo, Radiant ingests alerts from 120+ security tools across email, endpoint, identity, network, cloud, insider-threat, SIEM, WAF, DLP, and OT/IoT sources, triages 100% of them with transparent AI reasoning, and escalates only genuine risks to analysts. It pairs automated investigation with integrated, SIEM-cost-free log management (unlimited retention with customer S3 buckets) and one-click response actions. The product is delivered as a hosted SaaS console; its public surface is product documentation and inbound connectors rather than a developer-facing REST API.

companies.name: Serverless Workflow
companies.description: Serverless Workflow is a vendor-neutral specification for defining cloud-native serverless orchestration workflows.

companies.name: Zenoss
companies.description: Zenoss is an AIOps and full-stack monitoring platform for hybrid IT infrastructure observability and event management.

companies.name: BladeLogic
companies.description: BladeLogic is a data center automation platform for provisioning, configuring, patching, and enforcing compliance across large fleets of physical, virtual, and cloud servers. Founded in 2001 and acquired by BMC Software in 2008, it shipped as BMC BladeLogic Server Automation and later TrueSight Server Automation. It exposes a Java-based command line interface (BLCLI) and an on-premises RESTful web services API (Swagger-specified) served from the customer's own Application Server, enabling CRUD automation of servers, jobs, patches, and the software Depot. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with BMC's publicly documented developer, security, and compliance surfaces.

companies.name: Riverbed Technology
companies.description: Riverbed Technology is an enterprise unified observability and digital-experience-management (DEM) company. Its platform spans network, application, infrastructure, cloud, and end-user experience monitoring. Core products include the Aternity DEM suite (employee, mobile, and customer experience), AppResponse / NetProfiler / NetIM network observability, SteelHead WAN optimization and the Data Express high-speed data movement service, and the Riverbed IQ AIOps intelligence layer for autonomous IT operations. Riverbed exposes secure APIs and a 50+ partner integrations library (ServiceNow, Splunk, PagerDuty, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and more) so teams can build and customize their own observability, ITSM, and automation workflows. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead, this profile has been enriched from Riverbed's public trust, security, and developer surfaces.

companies.name: AMMP
companies.description: AMMP (AMMP OS) is a distributed energy monitoring and operations platform for operators of commercial and industrial (C&I) solar and battery-storage portfolios. It unifies visibility across multi-vendor fleets, pulling data directly from more than 30 manufacturer cloud platforms and its own AMMP Edge data logger, and layers on monitoring, alerting, stakeholder reporting, commercial (SLA/cost) tracking, and customizable dashboards. AMMP OS monitors over 10,000 sites across 35+ countries and emphasizes vendor independence and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified security. Surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and enriched by the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Codeium
companies.description: Codeium has been rebranded as Windsurf. The codeium.com URL now redirects to windsurf.com. The legacy Codeium product offered AI-powered code completion, search, and chat across IDEs (VS Code, JetBrains, Vim, Emacs, etc.). Codeium for Enterprise lives on as the enterprise / self-host SKU within Windsurf, alongside the Windsurf Editor and Plugins.

companies.name: Modeinspect
companies.description: Modeinspect (operated by Acreom Inc.) is an AI-native design tool that runs inside your codebase. Branded "Mode", it turns a product's real code into editable canvas frames so design engineers can shape production-grade UI on a visual canvas using the actual shipping components, design tokens, live data, breakpoints, and interaction states, then explore variants with AI and hand off pixel-perfect changes as a merge-ready pull request rather than throwaway mockups. The product is in early access / private beta. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and profiled in the API Evangelist network; enriched 2026-07-20. No public developer API, OpenAPI, docs portal, or SDK surface was found at this stage.

companies.name: Ontic
companies.description: Ontic is a corporate and physical security management software company based in Austin, Texas, that unifies protective intelligence, executive protection, incident management, threat intelligence, corporate investigations, and Global Security Operations Center (GSOC) workflows into a single "Connected Intelligence" platform. Its software helps enterprise and government security teams detect threats earlier, coordinate response, run behavioral threat assessments and case management, and demonstrate measurable impact. Ontic serves Fortune 500 companies and federal agencies across government, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, financial services, pharma/biotech, tech/telecom, and media, and holds FedRAMP Moderate Authorization along with SOC 2, ISO 27001, and CSA STAR certifications. The product is delivered as a closed SaaS application (app.ontic.ai); no public developer API is currently published. Backed by Felicis.

companies.name: Splunk On-Call (VictorOps)
companies.description: Splunk On-Call, formerly known as VictorOps, is an incident management and on-call alerting platform that helps DevOps and SRE teams reduce mean time to resolution by routing alerts, managing on-call schedules, and orchestrating incident response. The platform integrates with monitoring and observability tools to deliver context-rich alerts and supports collaborative chat-based remediation workflows. The VictorOps REST API enables programmatic management of users, teams, schedules, escalation policies, incidents, and integrations using API ID and API Key authentication headers.

companies.name: Swimm
companies.description: Swimm is a codebase-understanding and modernization platform that combines deterministic static analysis, AI agents, and senior engineers to help teams understand, document, and safely transform large or legacy codebases. Its core product is an AI coding assistant that helps developers understand complex code and capture that knowledge as code-coupled documentation that stays in sync with the source, with IDE integrations, CI verification, and an agentic context layer that feeds validated knowledge to tools like Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code. Swimm also runs large-scale modernization engagements (.NET, Java, monolith-to-microservices, and mainframe/COBOL). Swimm publishes product documentation, a getting-started guide, IDE and CI integrations, and a GitHub organization, but does not expose a public REST/developer API, SDK packages, or OpenAPI specification at this time.

companies.name: Thinglink
companies.description: Thinglink is an educational technology company offering a no-code, AI-powered platform for creating and deploying immersive, interactive learning experiences. Users enrich images, videos, and 360deg / virtual-tour media with clickable "tags" that surface text, audio, links, and embedded content, producing multimodal content for XR, AR, and 360deg training that runs on any device. Thinglink serves K-12 and higher education as well as corporate learning and safety-training teams, and integrates with learning-management systems. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Thinglink publishes a public trust center (ISO 27001, GDPR) but exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: Apphive
companies.description: Apphive is a no-code, AI-assisted platform for building native iOS and Android mobile applications without writing code. A visual drag-and-drop editor with live phone previews lets makers assemble screens and app logic, add native device capabilities (GPS and maps, push notifications, camera, authentication, databases, in-app purchases), connect third-party APIs and payment gateways such as Stripe and Openpay, and then compile and publish finished apps to the Apple App Store and Google Play. Vertical marketplace templates cover delivery, taxi, e-commerce, real estate, gym management, and more. Apphive is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Branding Brand
companies.description: Branding Brand is a Pittsburgh-based digital and mobile commerce technology company that has built native apps, progressive web apps, and websites for enterprise retailers for more than fifteen years. Its public developer surface is the open-source Flagship and Flagship Code React Native toolkits — a configuration-as-code framework with reusable commerce components, commerce data adapters, analytics/CMS modules, and a CLI — published under the @brandingbrand npm scope. The company also offers Shipcode, an AI-assisted no-code platform for building digital commerce experiences. Branding Brand is backed by Insight Partners. It publishes no public REST API or OpenAPI; this profile catalogs its open-source packages, CLI, and developer resources.

companies.name: Clad Labs
companies.description: Clad Labs is a San Francisco developer-tools startup (Y Combinator, Fall 2025) building Chad IDE, a desktop development environment that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor CLI, and OpenAI Codex — from a single interface. Developers spin up teams of parallel agents, keep each task isolated in its own workspace, then merge clean changes back together, while a built-in analytics dashboard tracks coding habits and productivity metrics. The IDE also fills AI-inference downtime with an in-app "Chad Browser" for entertainment that automatically hands focus back to the code when generation completes. Clad Labs ships a downloadable macOS and Windows application rather than a public web API; it exposes no REST/OpenAPI developer surface at this time.

companies.name: DVC
companies.description: DVC (Data Version Control) is an Apache 2.0 open-source CLI and Python library for versioning datasets, models, pipelines, and ML experiments on top of Git. It is not a network service — there is no DVC REST API.

companies.name: Highway9
companies.description: Highway 9 Networks is a Silicon Valley company delivering AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service through its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform. The platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), a distributed 5G core and edge AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device/workload groupings (Mobile Zones) to give enterprises deterministic, ultra-reliable private mobile networks and in-building cellular coverage. It targets manufacturing and warehousing (autonomous robots, drones, logistics), higher education (AI labs and research), and energy (predictive maintenance, remote operations). The Mobile Center Streaming APIs let partners integrate configuration, device management, monitoring, analytics, and operational workflows with the platform. Founded by an ex-VMware team behind NSX/SDN, hybrid cloud, and the Telco 5G/Edge cloud platform.

companies.name: Keybase
companies.description: Keybase is an end-to-end encrypted messaging, file-sharing, and key-directory platform built on public-key cryptography, founded by Chris Coyne and Max Krohn and acquired by Zoom in 2020. It maps human-readable usernames to public keys and cryptographically verifiable social-identity proofs (Twitter, GitHub, Reddit, Hacker News, personal domains, and cryptocurrency addresses), and provides encrypted chat, teams, KBFS encrypted filesystem, git, and a wallet. Keybase exposes a public read-oriented HTTP JSON API (version 1.0) at keybase.io/_/api/1.0 for user lookup, PGP key fetch, Merkle-tree verification, and session/signature auth, plus officially supported chat-bot SDKs for Node.js, Python, and Go that script the local keybase client and CLI.

companies.name: Kitura
companies.description: Kitura was an open source web framework for server-side Swift, originally developed by IBM, that allowed developers to use Swift for building web applications and REST APIs with support for databases, WebSockets, and OpenAPI. The project is now archived and no longer actively maintained, but remains a useful historical reference for server-side Swift API development.

companies.name: Linzumi
companies.description: Linzumi is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company in San Francisco building a Slack-shaped team chat that runs a fleet of AI coding agents inside every channel. Engineering teams kick off work, watch agent activity in real time, review output, and ship code without leaving the thread. Unlike sandboxed cloud agent products, Linzumi runs agents on the developer's own machine through a local "Commander" runner installed from the @linzumi/cli npm package, so agents work against real environment variables, dotfiles, and branches inside explicitly trusted folders. The product adds a decision inbox that surfaces only the choices needing a human, continuously compiled team context, git safety snapshots taken before each agent turn, and a bundled local MCP server that lets coding agents read scoped Linzumi message, thread, and channel context. It supports OpenAI Codex today with Claude Code announced as coming soon. The service is in beta via a macOS desktop app and a web workspace; there is no public developer API program, documentation portal, or published OpenAPI at this time.

companies.name: Mandiant
companies.description: Mandiant, now part of Google Cloud, is a threat intelligence and cyber defense company whose Mandiant Advantage platform exposes several authenticated REST APIs documented at docs.mandiant.com. The Threat Intelligence (MATI) API v3 serves indicators, finished intelligence reports, threat actors, malware families, vulnerabilities and campaigns; the Digital Threat Monitoring API surfaces exposed credentials and brand/deep-and-dark-web threats; the Attack Surface Management API inventories an organization's external assets; and the Security Validation (MSV) API drives automated testing of security controls. These APIs authenticate with an API key and secret that is exchanged for a short-lived bearer access token. Mandiant's frontline threat data now also powers Google Threat Intelligence alongside VirusTotal.

companies.name: Red Planet Labs
companies.description: Red Planet Labs builds Rama, a unified platform for constructing end-to-end scalable backends in as little as 1/100th the code of traditional stacks. Rama integrates durable indexed data storage (PStates), computation, and background processing into a single JVM programming model (Java and Clojure) with ACID semantics, automatic scaling, replication, and fine-grained reactivity — replacing the usual sprawl of databases, queues, caches, and workers. Rama ships a built-in REST API for non-JVM clients and is self-hosted, free for clusters up to two nodes. Backed by Initialized Capital.

companies.name: tldraw
companies.description: tldraw is an infinite-canvas SDK for building whiteboard and canvas applications. The primary distribution is the `tldraw` React component package; tldraw also offers a multiplayer sync server. License is the tldraw SDK License (free with watermark for small businesses; paid commercial license to remove watermark).

companies.name: Yaskawa / Motoman
companies.description: Yaskawa Electric Corporation is a Kitakyushu, Japan industrial automation company and the world's largest manufacturer of AC servo motors and motion controllers, with major business segments in motion control (AC servo motors, SERVOPACK amplifiers, machine controllers), AC drives / inverters, industrial robotics (under the Motoman brand), and systems engineering. Yaskawa's Motoman robotics division supplies articulated, SCARA, delta, collaborative, and mini robots used across automotive, EV, semiconductor, electronics, food, biomedical, and logistics manufacturing, alongside its Sigma-X servo family and GA / U1000 industrial AC drives. The company exposes a developer surface through the Yaskawa Motoman Developer Portal at developer.motoman.com and the Yaskawa-Global GitHub organization, including YMConnect (a modern PC-side communication library for C++ 17 and C#), MotoPlus SDK (on-controller C code for deterministic motion, I/O, jobs, and alarms), MotoROS2 (a native ROS 2 / micro-ROS node running on DX200, YRC1000, and YRC1000micro controllers), MotoCom SDK (legacy Windows communication SDK), the Smart Pendant SDK (Java extensions for the Smart Pendant teach interface), and YIP (Yaskawa Innovation Plus) packages and Smart Packager tooling. The catalog is SDK- and protocol-driven rather than HTTP/REST — there are no public OpenAPI specifications, so this profile captures the SDK, ROS, GitHub, and developer-portal surface without generated OpenAPI artifacts.

companies.name: Zed
companies.description: Zed is an open-source, high-performance multiplayer code editor written from scratch in Rust and built around GPU-accelerated rendering through its own GPUI framework.
