Created by Zed Industries — founded by Nathan Sobo, Antonio Scandurra, and Max Brunsfeld, the team behind Atom, Electron, and Tree-sitter — Zed combines a native desktop editor with real-time collaboration, native Git integration, Language Server Protocol and Debug Adapter Protocol support, and a first-class AI agent surface that includes edit prediction powered by the open-weight Zeta2 model, an inline assistant, parallel agents, and integrations with external coding agents (Claude, Codex, OpenCode) via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and Model Context Protocol (MCP). The editor itself is free and triple-licensed (AGPL / Apache-2.0 / GPL-3.0) with paid Pro and Business tiers that bundle hosted AI capabilities, edit prediction quotas, organization controls, and data governance. Zed runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows and exposes a WASM-based extension API (themes, languages, debuggers, snippets, MCP servers, agent servers) with extensions published through the zed-industries/extensions repository.

companies.name: Anoma
companies.description: Anoma is a distributed operating system that abstracts blockchain complexity into a single intent-centric interface, letting developers build applications once and run them across any chain. It introduces generalized intents for improved UX, programmable and compliance-ready privacy, and the Anoma Resource Machine (ARM) for native intents, interoperability, and scaling. Anoma ships the TypeScript Anoma App SDK (@anomaorg/anoma-app-sdk) with typed HTTP API clients for transfers, on-chain resource indexing, and public-nullifier queries that power Anoma Pay and related privacy applications. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub, this profile has been enriched from Anoma's public developer surface.

companies.name: Blameless
companies.description: Blameless is an SRE and incident management platform for reliability, incident resolution, and blameless retrospectives.

companies.name: Karate
companies.description: Karate is an open source API test automation framework combining API testing, mocks, and performance testing in a single tool using BDD syntax.

companies.name: Lura Project
companies.description: Lura Project (formerly KrakenD framework) is an open source ultra-performant API gateway framework for building custom API gateways with middleware and plugin support.

companies.name: Massdriver
companies.description: Massdriver is an internal developer platform providing self-service infrastructure, ephemeral environments, and cloud operations for engineering teams.

companies.name: MorphCast
companies.description: We expertly craft safe browser-processing, energy-efficient, accurate Emotion AI solutions to analyze facial emotions, empowering AI Agents and delivering empathetic, data-driven, and dynamic digital experiences.

companies.name: Netflix Zuul
companies.description: Netflix Zuul is a JVM-based API gateway providing dynamic routing, monitoring, resiliency, and security for microservice architectures.

companies.name: Newman
companies.description: Newman is the open source command-line companion for Postman that runs Postman collections from the CLI for automated API testing in CI/CD pipelines.

companies.name: Oculus
companies.description: Oculus is the virtual-reality company founded in 2012 that Kickstarter-launched the Rift headset and was backed by Spark Capital, Matrix Partners and others before Facebook acquired it in 2014 for roughly two billion dollars. The Oculus consumer brand has since been folded into Meta Quest, and the Oculus developer platform now lives as the Meta Horizon developer program at developers.meta.com/horizon. It offers the Oculus/Meta Platform SDK, the Meta Spatial SDK, OpenXR-native, Unity and Unreal engine integrations, and Immersive Web tooling for building mixed- and virtual-reality apps for Horizon OS and the Horizon Store. The oculus.com domain now redirects to Meta Quest, and developer.oculus.com redirects to the Meta Horizon developer portal.

companies.name: Ogen
companies.description: Ogen is a high-performance Go code generator that produces type-safe HTTP clients and servers from OpenAPI v3 specifications with validation, middleware, and observability built in.

companies.name: Paw
companies.description: Paw (now RapidAPI for Mac) is a full-featured HTTP client that lets you test and describe the APIs you build or consume. It provides a native macOS API testing experience with collaboration features.

companies.name: Second Front Systems
companies.description: Second Front Systems is a public-benefit, venture-backed software company that accelerates government access to emerging technologies for the world's democracies. Its 2F Suite delivers DevSecOps and continuous-accreditation tooling for defense and public-sector software teams: 2F Workshop (integrated security and compliance tooling for accredited development), 2F Game Warden (a fully accredited FedRAMP High and DoD ATO DevSecOps platform that fast-tracks commercial software to classified and unclassified government networks in roughly 90 days), and 2F Frontier (edge deployment to disconnected and denied environments). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It exposes no public developer API; its primary technical surface is the Game Warden platform documentation, a compliance Trust Center, and a broad certification posture (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FIPS 140).

companies.name: Functionize
companies.description: Functionize is an AI-native intelligent test automation platform that uses generative AI and computer vision to author, run, and self-heal web and mobile UI tests. The Functionize Architect agent generates tests from natural-language prompts, while Smart Test Agents reduce maintenance by adapting to UI changes at runtime. Tests execute against the Functionize Test Cloud and integrate with CI/CD pipelines via the Functionize CLI and a partner-gated REST API. Programmatic surfaces are not publicly documented; access is gated behind a Functionize tenant and a customer support portal at support.functionize.com.

companies.name: Live Aware Labs
companies.description: Live Aware Labs (LIVE AWARE) is a virtual playtesting and player-insights lab for game studios and researchers. The platform consolidates gameplay footage, player feedback, and community discussion from sources such as Discord, Twitch, YouTube, and internal playtests into a single dashboard, then applies AI to surface trends, player sentiment, and critical feedback in real time. A PC-based SDK captures video, telemetry, and in-game events, with plugins for Unreal Engine and Unity and no-code integrations into Slack, Jira, Monday.com, and OBS. Live Aware Labs is backed by a16z and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this profile is enriched from the company's public web surface.

companies.name: LiveAction
companies.description: LiveAction is a network observability and intelligence platform that provides visibility and monitoring across physical, virtual, cloud, and SD-WAN infrastructure. Its product family includes LiveNX (network performance monitoring using flow, API, SNMP, and cloud telemetry), LiveWire (network forensics and packet capture), LiveSP (monitoring for service providers), and Omnipeek (protocol analyzer), alongside AI-driven operations offerings. LiveAction's products expose product-embedded REST APIs authenticated with API tokens for automation and integration; there is no public hosted developer API or OpenAPI specification, as the APIs run on customer-operated deployments and the reference is served in-product. LiveAction is part of BlueCat Networks and a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

companies.name: LottieFiles
companies.description: LottieFiles is the platform and open-source runtime ecosystem for Lottie and dotLottie — a lightweight, JSON-based vector animation format that ships motion on any platform as easily as a static asset. Rather than a hosted HTTP API, LottieFiles' developer surface is a family of first-party, Rust+WASM-powered "dotLottie" players and framework/native components (Web, React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, React Native, iOS, Android, Flutter), plus embeddable web components and design-tool plugins for Adobe After Effects, Figma, Canva, VSCode, Framer and Webflow, letting developers render and control animations client-side.

companies.name: Pachyderm
companies.description: Pachyderm is an open-source (Apache-2.0) platform for data-centric pipelines and data versioning, widely used for MLOps. It provides immutable, git-like data lineage through the Pachyderm File System (PFS) and data-driven, containerized pipelines that reprocess only changed data through the Pachyderm Pipeline System (PPS), all running on Kubernetes. The platform is driven by a gRPC/protobuf API with first-party Python, Go, Ruby and Rust clients and the pachctl command-line tool. Pachyderm was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in January 2023; the standalone marketing, documentation and hosted (Pachyderm Hub) sites have since been retired, but the source, releases, SDKs and CLI remain actively published on GitHub and the language package registries (latest release v2.12.2, January 2025).

companies.name: Pelico
companies.description: Pelico is a manufacturing orchestration platform that bridges the execution gap between planning and real-world production. It unifies data from suppliers, production, inventory, quality, maintenance, and customers into a single operational view across multi-level BOMs and multi-plant networks. Domain-specific AI agents continuously monitor disruptions, determine upstream and downstream impact, simulate recovery options (alternates, stock transfers, resequencing), and keep cross-functional teams synchronized in real time. Pelico integrates with major ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Infor) and cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), exposing APIs to ingest new data sources and push actions into existing enterprise systems. The company is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified and GDPR compliant. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Pelico is a portfolio company of General Catalyst and does not publish a public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI at this time — its API surface is enterprise integration only.

companies.name: Wonder Workshop
companies.description: Wonder Workshop (GitHub org "playi", originally Play-i) is an educational technology company that makes the Dash, Dot, and Cue programmable robots and the Make Wonder K-8 coding and robotics learning platform, used by more than 40,000 schools across 65 countries. Its developer surface is a set of official SDKs that give granular realtime control of the physical robots' sensors and actuators over Bluetooth Low Energy: WonderPy (Python, on PyPI), @wonderworkshop/wwjs (JavaScript, on npm), and an iOS/Android robot framework shipped in the playground sample-app repository. There is no HTTP/cloud REST API, OAuth, or webhook surface; integration happens locally over BLE. Backed by GV.

companies.name: Librato
companies.description: Librato was a hosted metrics, monitoring and analytics service for operational data — time-series measurements, tagged metrics, dashboards ("spaces"), charts, annotations, alerts and notification services — delivered as a developer-first SaaS with a JSON REST API at metrics-api.librato.com/v1. Backed by Cowboy Ventures among others, the San Francisco company was acquired by SolarWinds in 2015 for a reported $40 million, and its metrics platform was folded into SolarWinds AppOptics — released in November 2017 — which has itself since reached end of life. The librato.com domain and every product subdomain (metrics., status., www.) now 301-redirect to the SolarWinds AppOptics end-of-life notice, the metrics-api.librato.com API host no longer resolves in DNS, and the github.com/librato organization was archived on 2024-01-02. This profile is retained as a historical record of a well-regarded developer API: the API reference source, the first-party Ruby, Python, Java and Node client libraries and the collection agents remain publicly archived and are catalogued here. The successor product is SolarWinds Observability SaaS.

companies.name: Queen Mary University of London
companies.description: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) is a public research university in London, United Kingdom, and a member of the Russell Group, ranked #120 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible footprint is research- and library-oriented rather than a formal developer program: Queen Mary Research Online (QMRO) is an open-access DSpace institutional repository that exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interface, and the university maintains a public GitHub organization (QMUL) for code released by its staff. QMUL does not publish a central, branded developer portal with signup-gated REST APIs; core student, timetable, and library platforms (QMplus/Moodle, MyQMUL, library discovery) sit behind institutional authentication.

companies.name: Tulip Interfaces
companies.description: Tulip is a manufacturing operations platform that enables frontline operations teams to build apps, connect machines and devices, and analyze production data without code. The Tulip REST API provides programmatic access to apps, tables, connectors, stations, automations, and analytics, supporting integration with ERP, MES, and industrial equipment on the shop floor.

companies.name: Cloud Native Buildpacks
companies.description: Cloud Native Buildpacks (CNB) is a CNCF-graduated specification and set of tooling for transforming application source code into OCI images that can run on any cloud. The project unifies the Heroku and Cloud Foundry buildpack ecosystems around an open standard for detection, build, and image export. The reference implementation lifecycle, the pack CLI for local builds, the kpack server-side builder, and a registry of distribution buildpacks together form the CNB ecosystem. CNB is built around a documented Buildpack API, Platform API, and Distribution API, all versioned and published in the github.com/buildpacks specifications.

companies.name: marginfi
companies.description: marginfi is a decentralized borrowing and lending protocol built on the Solana blockchain by mrgn labs. Users lend supported Solana tokens to earn yield and borrow against supplied collateral, with account-health, e-mode, liquid staking token (LST), and leveraged looping (mrgnloop) products layered on top of the core mrgnlend market. marginfi exposes no hosted REST API — developers integrate on-chain through the marginfi-v2 Solana program using the official TypeScript SDK (marginfi-client-v2, mrgn-common) and the Rust (CLI) SDK, with an early-alpha Python SDK (marginpy) and a Rust CPI interface crate also published. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and Pantera Capital.

companies.name: Fiberplane
companies.description: Fiberplane is an Amsterdam-founded developer-tools company, backed by Northzone, building agent-native tooling for the "software factory" era of AI coding agents. Its current lineup centers on fp (fp.dev), a local-first CLI for tracking work when coding with AI agents such as Claude Code; EV, an AI-powered code-review tool that turns diffs into narratives; and DRIFT, an open-source tool that binds specifications to code and lints for drift before stale docs reach production. Fiberplane also maintains a Model Context Protocol (MCP) toolchain — mcp-lite (a small, fetch-first SDK for building MCP servers), an MCP Gateway for intercepting and debugging MCP servers, and a Console for reviewing and evaluating MCP servers. Earlier work includes the Hono-native API Playground/Studio, the HONC.dev stack (create-honc-app), @fiberplane/agents for introspecting Cloudflare Agents SDK apps, and collaborative observability notebooks for incident response. The company ships its libraries on npm under the @fiberplane scope and distributes its CLI binaries via a Homebrew tap and an install script.

companies.name: ObjectBox
companies.description: ObjectBox is a high-performance, low-footprint, offline-first on-device database with built-in data synchronization and on-device vector search, designed for mobile, IoT, embedded, and edge computing applications. It is delivered as native language bindings (Java, Kotlin, C/C++, Go, Swift, Flutter/Dart, and Python) rather than a hosted REST API, giving apps ACID-compliant local persistence that works reliably offline and is described as up to 10x faster than SQLite. ObjectBox was the first on-device vector database on the market, targeting Edge AI use cases such as semantic search, recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation, and offers optional bi-directional Data Sync between devices and the cloud, including a direct connector to MongoDB. Founded in Germany and backed by Techstars.

companies.name: Observe.AI
companies.description: Observe.AI is an agentic AI platform for the contact center, providing purpose-built AI agents that handle customer support end-to-end across voice and chat, real-time AI Copilot guidance that assists frontline agents during live interactions, and Conversation Intelligence that evaluates every interaction for quality assurance, compliance, and business insight. Its AI agents connect to CRM, CCaaS, knowledge base, and backend systems to read and write data and trigger workflows, backed by 250+ prebuilt integrations and API/integration toolkits. Observe.AI serves regulated industries including banking and financial services, healthcare, insurance, and travel and hospitality, and maintains SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliance. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Scale Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund.

companies.name: Offchain
companies.description: Offchain (formerly Offchain Labs) is a blockchain infrastructure company that builds and maintains core technology for the Ethereum ecosystem. It is the creator of Arbitrum, the leading Ethereum layer-2 scaling solution offering high throughput with Ethereum-grade security; Prysm, a Go implementation of the Ethereum proof-of-stake consensus client that powers roughly a quarter of the network's consensus nodes; and Stylus, which lets developers write smart contracts in Rust, C, and C++ compiled to WebAssembly. Offchain also operates ZeroDev (smart-account / ERC-4337 account-abstraction infrastructure) and the Arbitrum (Orbit) chain SDK for launching custom layer-2 and layer-3 chains. The developer surface is Ethereum-compatible JSON-RPC plus first-party TypeScript and Solidity libraries published under the @arbitrum npm scope; the company does not expose a single hosted REST API. Backed by Redpoint Ventures.

companies.name: Otterize
companies.description: Otterize is an open-source, Kubernetes-native platform for intent-based access control (IBAC). Application teams declare which services need to talk to which other services using ClientIntents, and Otterize automatically calculates, provisions, and enforces the underlying access controls: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, AWS/GCP/Azure IAM, Istio Authorization Policies, Kafka ACLs, and MySQL/PostgreSQL grants. It ships three open-source operators (intents operator, credentials operator, network mapper) deployed via Helm, a Go CLI, and a managed Otterize Cloud. Its developer surface is the CLI, Kubernetes Custom Resources, and Helm/Terraform tooling rather than a public REST API. Otterize was surfaced as an Index Ventures portfolio company; otterize.com now redirects to Cyera following acquisition, while the open-source components, documentation, and CLI remain live.

companies.name: Refact.ai
companies.description: Refact.ai is an open-source, local-first AI coding assistant and autonomous software-engineering agent built by Small Magellanic Cloud Ai Ltd. ("SmallCloud"). The product combines an IDE-integrated chat experience (Ask / Explore / Debug / Review / Plan modes), accurate code completion powered by Qwen2.5-Coder with RAG over the workspace, and the Refact Agent — an autonomous mode that plans, executes, and iterates on engineering tasks end-to-end, integrating with Git hosts, databases, shells, browsers, and MCP servers. The full agent stack — a Rust HTTP/LSP engine (`refact-lsp`), a React/Vite chat GUI, and VS Code + JetBrains plugins — is open source under BSD-3-Clause at github.com/smallcloudai/refact and ranked #1 open-source agent on SWE-bench Lite (60.0%) and 93.3% on Aider's Polyglot benchmark with thinking mode. Refact supports a cloud SaaS tier (Free / Pro / Enterprise) — though Refact Cloud is being wound down in favor of BYOK + self-hosting — plus enterprise on-premise deployment with LLM fine-tuning, AWS Marketplace listings, and bring-your-own-key access to Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, GitHub Copilot, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Refact is positioned as a privacy-preserving, self-hostable alternative to closed cloud coding agents — workspace context, checkpoints, knowledge graphs, and trajectories are stored locally; no code is sent to the vendor's servers in self-hosted mode.

companies.name: Tempo Labs
companies.description: Tempo (Tempo Labs) is an AI app builder at tempo.new positioned around the "Prompt. Develop. Design. Collaborate." loop - users describe an app in natural language, Tempo generates code, and developers iterate either in the visual canvas or directly in code. The product targets design-to-code and prompt-to-code workflows for React / Next.js apps and is primarily consumed as a hosted web product rather than as an API. Public developer surface is limited; integrations and connected services (auth, database, hosting) are surfaced inside the product rather than via a documented public API.

companies.name: Wuilt
companies.description: Wuilt is an Egypt-based, Arabic-first no-code website and online-store builder that lets individuals and small businesses create a website, e-commerce storefront, or landing page in a few steps without prior design or development experience. The platform bundles hosting, domains, templates, a store/checkout with shipping, forms, multilingual sites, and a chat widget. Wuilt operates a public GraphQL backend at api.wuilt.com/graphql (introspection enabled) that powers its builder app, exposing read operations across sites, sections, pages, menus, forms, plans, payments, and domains. Wuilt is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

companies.name: CloudHealth Technologies
companies.description: CloudHealth Technologies is a cloud financial management (FinOps) and multi-cloud governance platform, founded in Boston and backed by Kleiner Perkins before being acquired by VMware in 2018 and now sold as CloudHealth by Broadcom. The platform helps organizations analyze and optimize cloud cost, usage, security, and governance across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. It exposes a public developer surface: a REST API (organized around resource-oriented URLs, JSON responses, and standard HTTP status codes) and a GraphQL API for programmatically retrieving and managing accounts, assets, perspectives, billing rules, metrics, reporting (OLAP reports), policies, tagging, SSO, and partner/organization administration. Authentication is via a per-user API Key presented as a bearer token or api_key query parameter, enforcing the same role and organization scoping as the platform UI.

companies.name: Hyperprobe
companies.description: Hyperprobe is a runtime data platform for AI-native software development, built by a San Francisco team in Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch. It lets developers and coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Windsurf) set live, non-breaking breakpoints in running production services directly from the IDE — capturing exact variable snapshots, injecting logs, and tracing call stacks without pausing threads, redeploying, or changing source code. Probes are read-only and non-blocking with under 1% overhead, and PII is redacted in-process before any data leaves the container's memory boundary (password, secret, token, authorization, cookie, key, signature, ssn and creditCard patterns are masked by default). Hyperprobe ships in-process SDKs for Node.js (@hyperprobe/node-sdk), Java (a bytecode-instrumentation agent), and Python (hyperprobe-agent), a VS Code extension, and an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (@hyperprobe/mcp-server) that lets AI assistants autonomously register conditional probes and read real runtime evidence instead of flat logs. The platform can run fully self-hosted via Docker Compose. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead, this profile has been enriched from Hyperprobe's public developer surface.

companies.name: Ithaca
companies.description: Ithaca is a crypto-infrastructure company (backed by Paradigm) building open-source developer tooling to accelerate the crypto frontier. Its flagship product, Porto, is a TypeScript SDK for passwordless authentication and payments on the web — letting applications and wallets create, manage, and interact with next-generation Ethereum accounts (keychains with passkeys, permissions, subscriptions, and native cross-chain interoperability) without passwords, extensions, seed phrases, or API keys. The stack also includes the Account smart contracts (Solidity), the Relay cross-chain transaction router and RPC server (Rust) for EIP-7702 accounts, and Odyssey, an experimental open-source Layer 2 testnet. The Ithaca team has since joined Tempo (tempo.xyz), and the Porto product is sunsetting on 2026-07-24 with users moving to porto.sh.

companies.name: Jellyfish
companies.description: Jellyfish is a software engineering intelligence (SEI) platform that turns data from developer tools — issue trackers (Jira, Linear, Azure Boards), source control and CI/CD (GitHub, Azure DevOps), and AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q, Gemini Code Assist) — into productivity and business-impact insights for R&D leaders. The platform measures AI adoption, engineering allocation, and delivery across the software development lifecycle through a Data Hub, extensible dashboards, and AI-assisted custom queries. Jellyfish is an enterprise, demo-gated product with no public self-service API; data access is delivered through the product and its integrations rather than a documented developer API. Backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Wing Venture Capital.

companies.name: Mask API
companies.description: Mask API is a powerful and flexible tool designed to help programmers and companies customize the response format of endpoint APIs, enabling selective field filtering and data transformation in API responses.

companies.name: Mirage JS
companies.description: Mirage JS is an open source API mocking library for JavaScript that lets you build, test, and share complete frontend features without depending on a backend. It runs alongside your frontend code as in-browser middleware, providing a built-in database, factories for seeding data, route handlers, and serializers. It is framework-agnostic and works with React, Vue, Angular, Ember, and any modern test runner. Mirage JS is itself a library (not a hosted REST API), so this entry indexes its documentation and project resources.

companies.name: MLOps
companies.description: MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) is an engineering discipline that unifies machine learning development with operations to deploy, monitor, govern, and maintain machine learning models in production. MLOps.org publishes an end-to-end reference for designing, building, and managing reproducible, testable, and evolvable ML-powered software, including the CRISP-ML(Q) process model, the MLOps Stack Canvas, MLOps principles, and ML model governance practices. This index curates the canonical references, frameworks, and ecosystem resources for practicing MLOps across data engineering, ML pipelines, and model serving.

companies.name: Oxia
companies.description: Oxia is a scalable metadata store and coordination service designed for distributed systems, providing strong consistency guarantees and high availability. It is developed by StreamNative as an alternative to ZooKeeper.

companies.name: Razer
companies.description: Razer is a global lifestyle brand for gamers that designs gaming hardware (Blade laptops, mice, keyboards, headsets and other peripherals), software (Synapse, Cortex) and services. For developers Razer operates the WYVRN immersive gaming platform, exposing the Razer Chroma RGB SDK and REST API for controlling 16.8-million-color lighting across devices, the Razer Sensa HD Haptics and THX Spatial Audio SDKs, Razer ID for user sign-in, and the Razer Gold / Razer Silver virtual-currency payment and rewards APIs for in-app monetization across 34,000+ integrated games and apps.

companies.name: RESTful Microservices
companies.description: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services that communicate via REST APIs using HTTP methods and standard web protocols. This collection covers RESTful microservices patterns, tools, service mesh technologies, API gateways, observability, and the ecosystem of frameworks and platforms for building, deploying, and scaling microservice architectures.

companies.name: Tech Soft 3D
companies.description: Tech Soft 3D builds developer SDKs and enterprise applications that power 3D data exchange, visualization, and analysis across engineering, manufacturing, and design. Its HOOPS toolkits (Exchange for CAD data translation and access, Visualize for high-performance 3D graphics, Access, Mesh, Solve, and Envision) are licensed to OEMs and independent developers building CAD, CAM, CAE, and PLM software, and it also distributes Siemens Parasolid and Polygonica. Alongside the native toolkits it publishes the HOOPS Visualize Web Components (open, first-party npm packages), SpinFire enterprise viewing/conversion apps, and OEM technologies such as AutoCAD OEM, Inventor OEM, and RealDWG. Tech Soft 3D is backed by Battery Ventures.

companies.name: Zend
companies.description: Zend is the enterprise PHP platform business of Perforce Software, providing production-grade PHP runtimes, tooling, and long-term support for mission-critical applications. Its portfolio spans ZendPHP (a hardened, enterprise-supported PHP runtime with LTS builds for end-of-life PHP versions), ZendHQ (PHP application observability and monitoring), Zend Server, Zend Studio, and Zend Guard, along with migration, modernization, performance auditing, and Black Belt support services for Laravel, Symfony, CodeIgniter, and CakePHP teams. Zend ships product tooling and a documentation surface rather than a public REST API.

companies.name: BrainCo
companies.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

companies.name: Omni Network
companies.description: Omni Network is a crypto interoperability protocol that makes the entire multi-chain ecosystem feel like a single chain for users and developers. Its core product, SolverNet, is a network of solvers that fulfill cross-chain intents on a user's behalf, letting a dApp deployed on one chain be used by people whose funds live on another. Developers integrate SolverNet through the Omni SDK (the @omni-network/core and @omni-network/react TypeScript packages) to bridge, swap, deposit, and bundle arbitrary contract calls across any supported chain from a single frontend. The project is built on a Go/Cosmos-SDK monorepo with Solidity contracts and ships the OMNI ERC-20 token on Ethereum L1. In 2026 the company rebranded from Omni to Nomina, consolidated on Ethereum, and now also operates Nomina, a unified trading terminal for power users trading perpetual futures across decentralized exchanges. It is backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, Two Sigma, Spartan Group, and Vessel.

companies.name: Gimlet Labs
companies.description: Gimlet Labs is an applied research lab building high-performance AI infrastructure — inference systems, schedulers, and compilers optimized for agentic and multimodal AI workloads across heterogeneous hardware. Its products include Gimlet Cloud, an agent-native serverless managed inference cloud for deploying single- and multi-agent systems that combine LLMs, multimodal and diffusion models, code sandboxes, web search, and custom data sources with automatic scaling; and kforge, a tool that autonomously generates optimized low-level PyTorch kernels across CUDA, ROCm, and Metal backends (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple) without manual kernel writing. The lab's research spans autonomous kernel generation, SLA-aware scheduling of multi-stage agent workloads across datacenters, edge/cloud workload partitioning, an MLIR-based universal AI compiler, headless DPU/accelerator hardware architectures, and cost-aware optimization for multitenant environments. Gimlet Labs is backed by Menlo Ventures. As of mid-2026 the developer surface is largely pre-launch, with a waitlist and access-gated documentation; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP server were found during enrichment.

companies.name: Shoreline
companies.description: Shoreline is an incident automation platform that enables operators to build automated remediation for recurring incidents.

companies.name: Vorlon
companies.description: Vorlon is an agentic ecosystem security platform that helps enterprises deploy AI agents and SaaS applications safely by protecting sensitive data in real time. The platform maps and monitors data flows between AI agents, enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, and cloud data stores, detecting threats, masking sensitive data in transit, and restricting agent access. Its patent-pending DataMatrix engine models the SaaS ecosystem — linking alerts, identities, APIs, data flows, and secrets — and a remote MCP server lets LLMs query security data and orchestrate investigations. Vorlon is backed by Accel and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

companies.name: Bridgecrew
companies.description: Bridgecrew was a developer-first cloud security company that pioneered infrastructure-as-code (IaC) security by creating Checkov, the open-source static analysis scanner for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, ARM, Serverless, and Dockerfile configurations. Founded in 2019 and backed by Battery Ventures, Bridgecrew shipped a SaaS platform that scanned IaC and connected cloud accounts for misconfigurations, enforced policy guardrails in CI/CD, and remediated findings through automated pull requests. Palo Alto Networks acquired Bridgecrew in March 2021 for roughly $156 million and folded the platform into Prisma Cloud (now the PANW Application Security offering). The standalone Bridgecrew developer API and docs.bridgecrew.io documentation have since been retired, while Checkov remains actively maintained open source under the bridgecrewio GitHub organization and the www.checkov.io docs site.

companies.name: Coral
companies.description: Coral is the Solana developer platform company (originally Coral / coral-xyz) behind Anchor, the most widely used framework for writing Solana Sealevel smart-contract programs. Anchor provides a Rust eDSL, an IDL/codegen toolchain, TypeScript and Rust clients, the anchor CLI (via the Anchor Version Manager, avm), and testing tooling that abstract away Solana program boilerplate. Coral also built Backpack, an application-first crypto wallet for executable NFTs (xNFTs). The company raised a $20M strategic round led by FTX Ventures and Jump Crypto with participation from Multicoin Capital. This is a developer-framework / smart-contract-tooling provider rather than a REST/HTTP API provider, so REST-oriented artifacts (OpenAPI, OAuth scopes, webhooks) are not applicable; its developer surface is packages, a CLI, and framework documentation.

companies.name: Dylibso
companies.description: Dylibso, Inc. is the company behind Extism, the open-source, cross-language framework for building with WebAssembly (Wasm). Its focus is AI-driven application extensibility: giving developers an off-the-shelf, secure-by-default, fully sandboxed plug-in system that is "just a library import away" and runs almost anywhere, with idiomatic Host SDKs for JavaScript, Python, Rust, Ruby, Go, .NET, PHP, Java, C/C++, OCaml, Haskell, Perl, and Zig. Beyond Extism, Dylibso builds Chicory (a native pure-JVM WebAssembly runtime) and Turbo MCP (formerly mcp.run / XTP), a standards-compliant, self-hosted Model Context Protocol gateway and management platform with OIDC identity integration and audit controls. Dylibso is backed by Felicis.

companies.name: FintechOS
companies.description: FintechOS is an AI-powered financial product operations platform that enables banks, lenders, and insurers to configure, price, launch, and manage financial products with reduced dependency on legacy core systems. The platform combines unified product operations, agentic workflow orchestration, and governed AI to streamline origination, servicing, underwriting, and compliance across banking and insurance. It exposes a low-code development environment with Server SDK and Client SDK layers and REST APIs, documented at docs.fintechos.com, with a gated developer community and an academy for onboarding. Founded in Romania with headquarters in the United Kingdom, FintechOS is a portfolio company of Earlybird and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Quadric
companies.description: Quadric is a semiconductor IP company based in Burlingame, California that licenses the Chimera GPNPU (general-purpose neural processing unit) processor IP and its accompanying software stack for on-device and edge AI inference. The Chimera architecture unifies scalar, vector, and matrix compute in a single fully C++ programmable core so both AI graph operators and classic DSP/C++ code run on one pipeline, giving SoC designers a future-proof target for evolving model roadmaps. Quadric ships a developer toolchain rather than a hosted web API: the cloud-based DevStudio portal, the Chimera SDK (ONNX import from PyTorch and TensorFlow), the ChiPy Python programming interface, an LLVM-based C++ extensibility path, and an instruction-set simulator for pre-silicon performance modeling. This profile catalogs Quadric's developer surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: RapidFort
companies.description: RapidFort is a software supply chain security platform focused on container hardening and automated CVE remediation. Its platform analyzes container vulnerabilities across build and runtime, profiles what software actually executes, and removes unused components to shrink the attack surface - remediating up to 95% of CVEs without code changes. RapidFort publishes a registry of 9,000+ near-zero-CVE curated container images and malware-scanned open-source libraries, and its CART capability automates compliance validation and remediation reporting for programs such as FedRAMP, cATO, CMMC, NIS2, and SOC 2. The company operates its platform through a hosted web application and a command-line workflow (analyze, profile, harden), with an open-source community-images catalog and the Kimia Kubernetes-native OCI image builder published on GitHub.

companies.name: 7AI
companies.description: 7AI (Seven AI, Inc.) is a Boston-based cybersecurity company building an agentic security platform that offloads repetitive, non-human security-operations work to swarming AI agents. Founded in 2024 by Cybereason co-founders Lior Div and Yonatan Striem-Amit, 7AI delivers "Service as Software" for the SOC: autonomous agents ingest and triage alerts, enrich data, and run end-to-end investigations, response, threat hunting, and case management so human analysts focus on high-value work. The platform spans Cases, Investigations, Detection, Response, Hunting, and Enterprise Insights. 7AI is a Greylock-backed portfolio company and raised the largest cybersecurity Series A on record. This API Evangelist profile is a company/identity record; 7AI does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Clearvector
companies.description: ClearVector is an identity-driven detection and response platform for cloud production environments. It attributes every action in real time to human, non-human, and third-party identities across AWS, GCP, and Azure, threading together activity across GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, cloud control planes, and runtime (EC2, Lambda, containers). Per-customer predictive behavioral models surface risky behavior, and one-click isolation contains compromised identities and resources without disrupting production. Offered as SaaS, an Enterprise plan, and a ClearVector Private SaaS deployment for teams that need complete infrastructure control. Backed by Menlo Ventures. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearVector publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — the product is delivered through a login-gated application at app.clearvector.com.

companies.name: Devv
companies.description: Devv (devv.ai) is an AI coding agent and instant-backend platform that lets indie builders, small teams, and non-technical creators ship full-stack, AI-powered web applications from natural-language prompts. It began as a developer-focused AI search engine and was rebuilt as Devv 2.0 into a no-code app builder with a three-step workflow. The platform pairs code generation with built-in backend integrations — authentication, database, email, LLM chat, image and audio generation — plus third-party connectors such as OpenRouter, Replicate, and ElevenLabs, alongside web search and web reader tooling. Devv is a product company rather than a public API provider: it publishes docs, a dated changelog, and an llms.txt, but exposes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted MCP server at this time. Backed by DCM Ventures.

companies.name: Ellipsus
companies.description: Ellipsus is a collaborative writing platform built for creative and fiction writers, combining a modern text editor with granular, Git-style version control so authors can draft, branch, share, and merge work together across devices. Founded in 2022 and operated by a small distributed team across Berlin (Germany), Madrid (Spain), and Szczecin (Poland), the product threads collaboration through every stage of writing — organizing drafts, discussing feedback, tracking changes, and preserving public version history — with a writers-first, artist-ownership, anti-AI-generated-content stance. Ellipsus offers a free tier and a paid Plus license, and is backed by Speedinvest. It is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Evvy
companies.description: Evvy is a women's health company offering at-home vaginal microbiome testing and personalized care. Its CLIA-certified metagenomic (mNGS) Vaginal Health Test identifies over 700 bacteria and fungi from a self-collected sample, with results reviewed by licensed clinicians who deliver personalized insights and clinician-designed treatment programs for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis, aerobic vaginitis, yeast infections, recurrent UTIs, and fertility-related concerns. Evvy also sells a line of vaginal health products including probiotics and boric-acid, hyaluronic-acid, and probiotic suppositories, plus a provider program for clinicians and a large library of science-backed educational content. Backed by General Catalyst, Evvy was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Evvy is a direct-to-consumer health and e-commerce business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface.

companies.name: Hyground
companies.description: Hyground GmbH (Hamburg, Germany) builds a sovereign, self-hosted AI SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) agent for European enterprises. The multi-agent platform deploys as a Kubernetes-native Helm chart inside the customer's own perimeter and correlates Kubernetes, observability (Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch), cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), CI/CD, and ticketing data to produce evidence-backed root cause analysis, autonomous incident response, and scheduled operations work such as CVE blast-radius mapping, RBAC drift audits, cluster right-sizing, and cost triage. It runs read-only by default, is bring-your-own-model (Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama), and keeps all data in-cluster with no external egress, targeting GDPR, BaFin, DORA, and NIS2 compliance requirements. Backed by partech; raised a EUR 3M pre-seed round.

companies.name: Divshot
companies.description: Divshot was a front-end and static web application hosting platform based in Santa Monica, California, and a 500 Global portfolio company. It offered command-line deploys of single-page and static applications across development, staging and production environments, with instant environment URLs, custom domains and SSL certificate upload, environment variables and app configuration, HTTP basic-auth protection of environments, cache purging, release promotion and rollback, and per-app webhooks. Divshot published a first-party CLI (divshot-cli) and a JavaScript API client (divshot-api) on npm, and open-sourced Superstatic, the static web server behind the platform. Divshot was acquired by Google in 2015 and folded into Firebase Hosting. The service is defunct - divshot.com no longer resolves and no live API, documentation or developer portal remains. This profile is a historical record built from the surviving first-party npm packages and GitHub repositories.

companies.name: PlayPlay
companies.description: PlayPlay is an online video and visual creation platform that lets business teams produce on-brand videos and images without prior editing experience. Through a drag-and-drop editor, AI-assisted tools (text-to-video, script and voice-over generation, automatic subtitles) and enterprise collaboration, brand-kit and review workflows, it serves marketing, communications and HR teams at large organizations. Founded in France and backed by Balderton Capital, Insight Partners and Point Nine, PlayPlay is a SaaS product without a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its published identity, legal and security surface (ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR).

companies.name: Prompt Driven
companies.description: Prompt Driven (PDD) is the company behind Prompt-Driven Development, a prompt-native programming system in which .prompt files are the human-authored source language and traditional code (Python, TypeScript, Go, and others) is generated as an artifact. PDD ships as a single open-source Python CLI, pdd-cli, plus a local web interface, and offers agentic commands that implement GitHub issues automatically through a Define -> Generate -> Verify -> Test -> Update cycle. Positioned as "The Last Programming Language," the project is MIT-licensed, maintained by Greg Tanaka, and backed by 500 Global. It is a developer tool rather than a hosted API — there is no public REST/GraphQL API, OpenAPI spec, or MCP server; the developer surface is the CLI and its GitHub repository.

companies.name: Operation Support Equipment
companies.description: API for managing and accessing operation support equipment data, inventory, maintenance records, and deployment information for operational logistics and equipment lifecycle management.

companies.name: Codewisp
companies.description: Codewisp is an AI-powered game creation platform that lets anyone build and publish real web games from natural-language prompts, with no coding or game-development tools required. Users describe the game they want and the platform generates the code, structure, and assets automatically, supporting 2D, 3D, and multiplayer browser games with instant, prompt-driven refinement. Founded by game developer Elvin Fu and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch, Codewisp reports 2,000+ weekly active creators and 17,000+ games created, offering a browser-based block editor, a community explore and marketplace surface, and shareable instant-play links. Codewisp is a consumer creation product and does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Simantic
companies.description: Simantic builds simulated hardware for embedded QA, modernizing embedded firmware development through hardware simulation designed for AI adoption in hardware engineering. Its platform emulates microcontroller (MCU) systems so engineers can inject sensor readings and observe how their firmware reacts over CAN, Ethernet, and BLE, running full firmware test suites in CI (for example GitHub Actions) on every push and pull request without physical boards. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI agents step through firmware, inspect peripheral state, and replay scenarios against a simulated MCU, and a CLI drives simulations locally. Simantic offers private, self-hosted deployment so firmware and test data never leave a team's own servers. Founded in 2025, Simantic is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) company.

companies.name: Thunkable
companies.description: Thunkable is a no-code, AI-powered platform for building native iOS and Android mobile applications through a visual drag-and-drop designer, a block-based logic editor, and conversational AI prompts. Creators assemble screens and app logic without writing code, and connect their apps to external services using the built-in Web API blocks (HTTP GET/POST/PUT/DELETE against any REST endpoint), realtime databases, cloud storage, maps, media, push notifications, and payment providers such as Stripe. More than 5 million users across 185 countries have created over 11 million apps on the platform. Note that Thunkable itself does not publish a first-party developer REST API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK for programmatically managing Thunkable projects; its "API" surface is the in-app Web API component used to consume third-party APIs from within apps built on Thunkable.

companies.name: Vertical Bar Inc.
companies.description: Vertical Bar Inc. builds CrossCheck, a DevOps and operations-visibility platform for NetSuite environments. CrossCheck gives NetSuite teams configuration tracking, change management and deployment safety: environment snapshots, comparisons and restore, automated record-and-replay regression testing that catches issues before production, AI-assisted error analysis with fix suggestions, and process mining to surface workflow delays and inefficiencies. Vertical Bar also offers managed services and industry-specific solutions for medical device, food and beverage, chemical, and aerospace and defense manufacturers, plus the FieldTrail browser extension for NetSuite field customization. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its public web surface.

companies.name: Vidjet
companies.description: Vidjet is a shoppable video platform for e-commerce that lets merchants embed on-site video without impacting page speed. Merchants build video feeds, tag products inside videos, and display formats such as Stories, Carousel, Bubble, Embed, Popup, and a Sticky Play Button across thousands of product pages. It is a no-code product installed via a JavaScript embed, Google Tag Manager, or platform plugins for Shopify, WooCommerce/WordPress, Magento, Wix, Webflow, PrestaShop, and Salesforce Commerce Cloud, with analytics, multilingual support, and email collection integrations to Klaviyo and Google Sheets. Vidjet is a Seedcamp portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public developer REST API, SDK, OAuth surface, or webhooks — integration is via the client-side embed script.

companies.name: Bloomfilter
companies.description: Bloomfilter is a process intelligence platform that gives enterprises end-to-end visibility, traceability, and control over how AI agents and humans execute software delivery work. It unifies data across development and design tools such as Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, and Figma into a structured, AI-enabled data stream and builds a connected process graph across the software development lifecycle. Teams use Bloomfilter to govern hybrid human-agent workflows through process mining, compliance monitoring, cycle-time analysis, and performance measurement, so leaders can see how work actually flows and where value is created or lost. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

companies.name: Databand
companies.description: DBND (Databand) is an open-source Python framework — a library, a set of APIs, and a CLI — for building, tracking, and observing data pipelines across data ingestion, preparation, ETL/ELT, and machine-learning workflows. It collects pipeline metadata (runs, metrics, dataframes, schemas) to give data-engineering teams a system of record for runs and to detect pipeline failures and data quality issues before they hit downstream consumers. The DBND SDK integrates with Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, Databricks, dbt, and IBM DataStage. Databand was acquired by IBM in 2022 and is now IBM Databand, part of IBM's data observability offering; the open-source DBND SDK remains published on PyPI and GitHub under the databand-ai organization.

companies.name: Directus
companies.description: Open-source data platform that wraps any SQL database with a REST and GraphQL API, auto-generated from the schema, plus a no-code admin app for data management. Directus turns any new or existing SQL database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MS SQL, OracleDB, CockroachDB) into an instant REST and GraphQL API with a visual Data Studio for non-technical users. The platform includes policy-based access control, an automation engine (Flows), a built-in AI assistant, digital asset management, real-time WebSockets, and an MCP server for AI agent integration. Deployable as a self-hosted open-source project or as Directus Cloud.

companies.name: Openspec
companies.description: OpenSpec (by Fission-AI) is an open-source, lightweight spec-driven development (SDD) framework for AI coding assistants. It adds a durable spec layer so you and your coding agent agree on what to build before any code is written: each change gets its own folder with a proposal, specs, design, and tasks, following a propose - apply - archive workflow. OpenSpec is a CLI and agent contract (installed via npm, no API keys or MCP required) that works with 30+ AI tools including Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and Copilot via slash commands. A Y Combinator company, OpenSpec has 60k+ GitHub stars and is building Workspaces for teams needing multi-repo planning and collaboration.

companies.name: Pynt
companies.description: Pynt is an API security testing platform that helps developers identify and remediate security vulnerabilities in REST APIs including CSRF, Injection attacks, and insecure direct object references.

companies.name: Wing Cloud
companies.description: Wing Cloud is the company behind Wing (Winglang), an open-source, cloud-oriented programming language created by Elad Ben-Israel, the creator of AWS CDK. Wing unifies infrastructure and application code into a single model: a "preflight" phase compiles to Terraform/CloudFormation while an "inflight" phase compiles to JavaScript for runtime. Developers build and test distributed cloud systems locally with the Wing Simulator and Wing Console, then deploy to any major cloud provider. The project is MIT-licensed, ships the `wing` CLI (npm: winglang) and the standalone Wing SDK (@winglang/sdk, Apache-2.0), and the company is backed by Battery Ventures. Wing is a language and developer-tooling company; it does not publish a public REST/HTTP API.

companies.name: Exaforce
companies.description: Exaforce is a security operations platform that pairs AI agents with a unified data layer to help teams detect, triage, investigate, and respond to threats faster. Its four autonomous "Exabot" agents (Detect, Triage, Investigate, and Respond) automate SOC workflows across 100+ data sources spanning cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and code repositories, and can run as a self-operated platform or as a managed detection and response (MDR) service staffed by expert analysts working alongside the AI 24/7. Exaforce positions itself as an agentic-SOC alternative to traditional SIEM tooling while retaining integration compatibility. The company is backed by Mayfield and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or reference documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, security, and trust surface.

companies.name: MelodyArc
companies.description: MelodyArc is an enterprise AI operations platform that orchestrates data, business rules, AI agents, and human workers in one governed system, so the right judgment is applied at the right moment, every time. It turns messy, cross-system, high-consequence operational work into modular building blocks: Points (atomic units of work capturing context, action, state, and ownership), Point Sets (reusable workflow configurations), a Point Engine (a dynamic decision graph routing tasks through rules, automation, AI, and human intervention in real time), AI Operators (configured workers with instructions and tools), a Portal for oversight and intervention, and Record for built-in traceability. It targets enterprise operations teams handling high-consequence work at scale and runs on managed or self-hosted infrastructure. Backed by Bloomberg Beta.

companies.name: Sakana AI
companies.description: Sakana AI is a Tokyo-based AI R&D company founded by ex-Google researchers focused on collective intelligence, evolutionary optimization, and nature-inspired AI methods. The company's first commercial product is Sakana Fugu - a multi-agent orchestration system with an OpenAI-compatible API (currently in beta). Sakana also publishes Sakana Chat (consumer) and Sakana Marlin (beta).

companies.name: Sazabi
companies.description: Sazabi is an AI-native observability platform that helps engineering teams find and fix production issues faster. Autonomous agents watch application logs (stdout/stderr) to detect anomalies, unfamiliar errors, traffic spikes, and failed deployments without traditional dashboards, then deliver contextual, root-cause alerts into Slack and Microsoft Teams. Engineers investigate in natural language by mentioning the Sazabi agent, and the platform can hand off context to coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, and Codex or open pull requests to remediate. Sazabi instruments 35+ hosting providers with no code changes and exposes a hosted Sazabi MCP server so agents can query logs, inspect issues and projects, and discover Sazabi tools. Founded by Sherwood Callaway; part of the Y Combinator P26 (Spring 2026) batch; backed by an $8M seed round led by J2 Ventures, Village Global, and Y Combinator, with an open beta.

companies.name: Pulse Labs
companies.description: Pulse Labs is an AI-powered user experience research platform, founded in 2017, that helps product, design, and UX research teams gather and analyze real-world user feedback. The platform combines surveys, moderated and unmoderated interviews, task-based evaluations across web, mobile, smart devices, and automotive, and naturalistic observations, alongside its FlightRecorder SDK for embedded in-app feedback and session replay on iOS, Android, Web, React, and Flutter. Participant recruiting is powered by the proprietary Pulse Voices panel. Backed by Google, Amazon, Bezos Expeditions, Techstars, and Madrona Ventures, Pulse Labs emphasizes privacy, ethical AI, and enterprise-grade security including ISO 27001 certification and GDPR compliance. Pulse Labs does not currently publish a public REST API or OpenAPI; its developer-facing surface is the FlightRecorder embedded SDK and GitBook product documentation.

companies.name: Tonk
companies.description: Tonk, built by Tonk Labs, is an open-source containerized format, host environment, and protocol for multiplayer, local-first software you keep and share like files. A .tonk bundle packages an application together with its data into a single self-contained file that runs anywhere, works offline, and stays under user control. It is built on a document-based virtual file system using Automerge CRDTs, a browser/WebAssembly runtime compiled from Rust, and peer-to-peer synchronization through WebSocket relays. Tonk ships first-party npm client libraries, a CLI, a sync relay, an authentication library, and an MCP worker rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Electric Capital.

companies.name: Sym
companies.description: Sym was a developer-first authorization and access-management platform for platform, security, and infrastructure engineering teams. Rather than a REST API, Sym exposes its control plane as infrastructure-as-code: teams declare access flows, environments, targets, and user-facing fields with the Sym Terraform provider, customize runtime behavior with the Python SDK (hooks and reducers in impl.py), and operate the platform with the symflow CLI. It automated context-based, time-bound access requests and approvals across AWS (IAM, SSO), Okta, GCP, Jira, Slack, and other targets with centralized governance embedded in an organization's existing SDLC. The Sym product is now largely wound down — the docs root is sunset and most source repositories under github.com/symopsio are archived — but its published packages, Terraform provider, and changelog remain available.

companies.name: Upmem
companies.description: UPMEM is a French fabless semiconductor company pioneering Processing-In-Memory (PIM). Its Data Processing Units (DPUs) are embedded directly in DRAM on standard DIMM modules, putting thousands of programmable cores inside memory to accelerate data-intensive workloads such as analytics, genomics, and AI inference. Developers program DPUs in C using the UPMEM DPU SDK (LLVM-based compiler, DPU runtime, C/C++/Java/Python host libraries, dpu-lldb debugger, and a functional simulator), distributed from sdk.upmem.com and an APT PPA. UPMEM publishes no hosted web API; its developer surface is the SDK and an open-source GitHub organization. The corporate website (www.upmem.com) is offline as of 2026-07-21, while the SDK documentation and release archive remain live.

companies.name: Kamal
companies.description: Kamal is an open-source deployment tool from 37signals (DHH / Basecamp) for deploying containerized web applications to any infrastructure — bare metal, cloud VMs, or a mix — with zero-downtime rolling restarts. Originally built for Rails apps, Kamal works with any web application that can be packaged as a Docker container. It uses SSHKit to drive remote commands over SSH and pairs with kamal-proxy, a lightweight HTTP proxy written in Go that seamlessly switches request traffic between old and new containers during a deploy. Kamal is imperative and Capistrano-like in feel, with a single `config/deploy.yml` describing servers, image, registry, accessories, env, secrets, and proxy/SSL settings. Capabilities include auto-provisioning Docker on new servers, remote builds, asset bridging, accessory services (databases, Redis, cron sidecars), automatic TLS via Let's Encrypt, host- and path-based routing, and hooks for custom pre/post-deploy logic. Kamal is the operational backbone of 37signals' on-premises exit from major cloud providers and powers their ONCE product line. Kamal itself is a CLI tool, not a hosted service — there is no public REST API, no SDK, and no paid tier. The project is released under the MIT License and developed openly on GitHub under the `basecamp` organization.

companies.name: Native Security
companies.description: Native Security is a cloud security control plane that unifies security posture and enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and OCI. The platform translates security intent expressed in natural language into enforceable architectural controls, shifting teams from reactive detection toward proactive, secure-by-design defense using built-in cloud security primitives. Capabilities include multi-cloud policy enforcement from a single definition, automated organization topology discovery and mapping, architectural segmentation and perimeter enforcement, AI-agent guardrails through architectural boundaries, and compliance automation with audit readiness. Native Security is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; product documentation and the application console sit behind authentication.

companies.name: Spheron
companies.description: Spheron Network is a decentralized GPU and cloud compute marketplace that aggregates enterprise-grade NVIDIA GPU capacity from certified Tier 3/4 data centers worldwide and exposes it through a single on-demand, per-minute billed interface. The marketplace covers H100, H200, B200, B300, A100, GH200, L40S, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, RTX 4090, and pre-order GB200/GB300/ R100 inventory, priced 40-60% below hyperscaler rates with spot, reserved, and custom-cluster (8-512+ GPU) options. Teams access the platform through a web dashboard, a documented REST API at app.spheron.ai/api, a TypeScript Protocol SDK, an MCP plugin for Claude, SkyPilot integration, and Helm charts for self-hosted provider nodes. The Spheron Foundation also maintains an open compute protocol with Fizz nodes, provider nodes, ICL YAML configuration, and an on-chain payment system supporting both traditional payment rails and USDC/USDT stablecoin settlement. The company is transitioning from a pure decentralized protocol model toward an enterprise GPU procurement and aggregation marketplace while keeping the underlying provider network open and community-operated.

companies.name: Symbl.ai
companies.description: Symbl.ai is a conversation-intelligence platform for understanding and generating insights from human conversations across voice, video, and text. Its developer platform exposed Async, Streaming, and Telephony APIs plus the Nebula LLM for real-time speech-to-text and conversational insights — action items, topics, questions, follow-ups, sentiment, and custom trackers — with first-party SDKs for JavaScript, Web (browser), Python, and Go. Symbl.ai was acquired by Invoca; the standalone developer platform (api./docs./platform. symbl.ai) has since been decommissioned, but the official client SDKs remain published on npm, PyPI, pkg.go.dev, and the github.com/symblai organization, and the marketing, blog, pricing, and support surfaces stay live.

companies.name: Zibra AI
companies.description: Zibra AI is a Ukrainian deep-tech company building AI-powered real-time volumetric rendering and compression technology for VFX, gaming, virtual production, film, and TV. Its flagship product, ZibraVDB, compresses OpenVDB volumetric datasets to roughly five percent of their original size while preserving visual quality, enabling real-time playback of smoke, fire, fog, and other volumetric effects. Zibra ships a native C++ ZibraVDB SDK (DirectX 12, Vulkan, and Metal on Windows, Linux, and macOS) alongside plugins for Unreal Engine, Houdini, and Unity, with Blender support in progress. It exposes no public REST/HTTP API; integration is through the SDK and digital-content-creation plugins. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Eye Security
companies.description: Eye Security is a European cybersecurity company providing managed detection and response (MDR) and managed XDR for mid-market organizations across logistics, manufacturing, healthcare, and professional services. It combines AI-driven threat detection with a 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC), incident response and threat hunting, security awareness training, EU-native log retention, and integrated cyber insurance. Headquartered in Europe with an EU-focused stance on compliance and data residency, Eye positions itself as enterprise-grade security made for the mid-market. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and product surface.

companies.name: Growatt
companies.description: Growatt New Energy is a global manufacturer of solar PV inverters, energy storage systems, and smart energy management products for residential, commercial, and utility-scale installations. Growatt operates the ShineServer / ShinePhone cloud monitoring platform and publishes a token-authenticated Open API (V1) that lets third-party systems read plant and device telemetry, retrieve historical energy data, and read or write inverter parameters for MIN (TLX) string inverters and SPH (MIX) hybrid inverters across regional endpoints. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; enriched from Growatt's public developer surface.

companies.name: TipLink
companies.description: TipLink is a Solana wallet-link platform that lets anyone create a shareable link or QR code holding crypto or an NFT, so a recipient can claim digital assets without first setting up a wallet. It ships as first-party TypeScript/JavaScript SDKs (notably @tiplink/api) and Solana Wallet Adapter UI components rather than a hosted REST API, and is used for airdrops, tipping, payments, and onboarding new users to Solana. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

companies.name: Hubble Protocol
companies.description: Hubble Protocol is a Solana-based decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that lets users borrow the USDH stablecoin against multiple crypto collateral assets (SOL, mSOL, stSOL, ETH, BTC and more) with interest-free, fixed-fee loans held open for unlimited time. The protocol pairs a Stability Vault, a Peg Stability Module, a hybrid liquidation model, and native yield on deposited collateral. Developers integrate with Hubble on-chain through its Anchor programs (IDLs published on GitHub) and the open-source "@hubbleprotocol/hubble-sdk" TypeScript client, which exposes borrowing market states, HBB staking and USDH stability-pool data, user loans, treasury and circulating-supply metrics, and peg-stability swaps. Hubble published security audits (Arcadia, Kudelski, Smart State, Sec3) and runs a funded bug-bounty program; its core contributors later built Kamino Finance.

companies.name: Astral
companies.description: Astral (Astral Software Inc.) builds high-performance developer tools for the Python ecosystem, written in Rust. Its products are uv, an extremely fast Python package and project manager that replaces pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, twine, and virtualenv; Ruff, an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter; and ty, a fast Python type checker and language server. Founded by Charlie Marsh (creator of Ruff) and backed by Accel, Caffeinated Capital, and angel investor Guillermo Rauch, Astral ships open-source command-line tooling distributed via PyPI, crates.io, npm, and Homebrew. In March 2026 Astral agreed to join OpenAI as part of the Codex team.

companies.name: Coasts
companies.description: Coasts (Containerized Hosts) is an open-source, MIT-licensed CLI tool that provides localhost service isolation and orchestration for git worktrees. It spawns multiple fully isolated development runtimes for the same project on a single machine, giving each worktree its own ports, databases, and services so parallel AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Conductor, and others) can build and test side by side without clashing. Built on Docker Compose, with a thin CLI client talking to a local coastd daemon over a unix socket plus a bundled React/Vite web observability UI, Coasts is local-first and offline-capable, with optional extension to remote machines over SSH. Backed by Y Combinator (Fall 2025) and founded by Jamie Sunderland and Dan Hyman.

companies.name: Crash Override
companies.description: Crash Override is a software supply chain security company building a control plane for software development in the agentic era. It monitors code from developers and AI coding agents, inspects builds across CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins), cryptographically tags software artifacts, and tracks them from development through production. The company delivers its capabilities primarily through open-source tools — Chalk (code provenance tagging) and Ocular (Kubernetes-native software asset scanning orchestration) — plus a hosted control plane with enterprise SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM support. Founded by Mark Curphey (founder of OWASP) and John Viega, and backed by GV, Syn Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Blackstone. Philosophy: "Tag. Track. Trust." No public REST API or OpenAPI specification is published at this time; this profile was enriched from the company's public web, GitHub org, and security surface.

companies.name: Effectful
companies.description: Effectful Technologies is the company behind Effect, an open-source ecosystem of production-grade TypeScript libraries. The flagship `effect` library is a composable standard library and execution engine that unifies error handling, resource management, concurrency, dependency injection, observability, schema, and testability, letting developers focus on what a program should accomplish rather than how. Effect is positioned as "Layer 0" of a broader vision extending into distributed systems — RPC, SQL, clustering, AI integrations, and durable execution. The ecosystem ships as first-party npm packages under the `effect` and `@effect/*` scopes (MIT licensed) from the Effect-TS GitHub organization. Effectful is developer-tooling / library company, not an HTTP API provider, and is backed by Amplify Partners.

companies.name: Mech-Mind Robotics
companies.description: Mech-Mind Robotics provides industrial 3D cameras (the Mech-Eye industrial 3D camera and laser profiler line) together with software suites — Mech-Vision machine-vision software, Mech-Viz robot-programming software, and the Mech-DLK deep-learning toolkit — that give industrial robots embodied AI and 3D vision. Typical applications include bin picking, depalletizing, machine tending, piece picking, and item picking; the company reports 3000+ deployed applications for 1000+ clients worldwide. The developer surface is the Mech-Eye SDK (a C++ core with Python and C# bindings), ROS and ROS2 interfaces, and the Mech-DLK SDK, all published under the MechMindRobotics GitHub organization; there is no public REST/HTTP API.

companies.name: Nori
companies.description: Nori (Nori Robotics) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) hard-tech company in San Francisco building affordable bimanual humanoid home robots — the NORI L2, a sub-$1,300 wheeled robot with dual Z-axis lift arms that autonomously handles household chores like loading dishes, making beds, food prep, and cleaning, with multiple units able to collaborate on coordinated tasks. Beyond the hardware, Nori publishes a developer surface: the @nori/sdk robot-local teleoperation SDK connects to a robot over WebRTC to stream video and telemetry and drive it from the browser in ~20 lines, with all safety mechanisms (clamping, watchdog, E-STOP, motor torque lifecycle) enforced on the robot's control daemon. The SDK targets the nori-protocol v1 wire format (NDJSON over a WebRTC data channel to the daemon on port 7777), is Apache-2.0 licensed, and is distributed to a small set of collaborating developers as a tarball rather than on public npm.

companies.name: Rebellions
companies.description: Rebellions is an AI infrastructure company that designs energy-efficient AI inference hardware (NPUs) and the software stack to deploy large language and multimodal models on it at scale. Its products include the Rebel100 inference chip (FP8, HBM3e), the ATOM-Max Server and POD, and RebelServer. The RBLN SDK compiles and serves HuggingFace Transformers/Diffusers, PyTorch, and TensorFlow models on RBLN accelerators, with integrations for vLLM, NVIDIA Triton, TorchServe, and Kubernetes. Rebellions does not expose a public REST/HTTP API; developers integrate through first-party Python SDKs (optimum-rbln, vllm-rbln), the RBLN compiler and driver, and the model zoo. Backed by Kindred Ventures and partnered with Samsung, Arm, IBM, and AWS.

companies.name: Silicon Labs
companies.description: Silicon Labs (Silabs) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas that designs silicon, software, and solutions for a more connected, IoT world. Its portfolio includes wireless connectivity SoCs and modules for Bluetooth, Bluetooth Mesh, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, and proprietary sub-GHz protocols, along with 32-bit microcontrollers, sensors, and timing devices. Developers build on Silicon Labs hardware using the Simplicity Studio IDE, the Simplicity SDK (formerly Gecko SDK), the docs.silabs.com developer documentation, and the Silicon Labs Community. Silicon Labs is a hardware and embedded-software provider rather than a web-API vendor: its public developer surface is embedded C/C++ SDKs, tools, and reference examples on GitHub (github.com/SiliconLabs), not a hosted REST API — so this profile carries identity, developer-portal, and security signals rather than API specifications.

companies.name: Streamfold
companies.description: Streamfold is the company behind Rotel, a high-performance, resource-efficient OpenTelemetry collector written in Rust. Rotel focuses on minimal overhead and fast cold-starts for resource-constrained environments such as AWS Lambda, serverless functions, and embedded systems, supporting OTLP/gRPC, OTLP/HTTP, and Kafka receivers with exporters for ClickHouse, Datadog, AWS X-Ray, Kafka, and OTLP. It ships Python (pyrotel) and Node.js (@streamfold/rotel) embeddings, an AWS Lambda extension layer, a CloudWatch Lambda forwarder, and a Rust processor SDK. Rotel is open source under Apache-2.0. In March 2026 Streamfold announced it is joining Cursor to bring observability to agentic, AI-driven software systems. Streamfold was a portfolio company of Uncork Capital.

companies.name: Tobii
companies.description: Tobii is the global leader in eye tracking and attention computing, headquartered in Danderyd, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm.
