Its developer offering centers on the Tobii Pro SDK — Python (tobii-research), .NET, C and Matlab bindings for streaming gaze and eye-tracking data from Tobii's screen-based and wearable eye trackers — together with the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 API (with official g3pylib Python and .NET client SDKs) and XR / consumer game-integration developer kits. Tobii's technology serves scientific and behavioral research, UX, healthcare, XR/VR, automotive driver monitoring and PC gaming markets.

companies.name: Ambiq Micro
companies.description: Ambiq Micro is a semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for battery-powered and endpoint-AI devices. Its proprietary Subthreshold Power Optimized Technology (SPOT) platform lets its Apollo family of Arm Cortex-M microcontrollers and Artasie real-time clocks run at extremely low energy, powering wearables, hearables, healthcare, smart-home, industrial and gaming devices. Ambiq's developer surface is an embedded C/C++ toolchain - the AmbiqSuite SDK and the open-source neuralSPOT AI SDK/Toolkit - plus a set of first-party Python AI toolkits (heartKIT, sleepKIT, physioKIT, neuralspotx) published on PyPI and GitHub (AmbiqAI, AmbiqMicro). This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

companies.name: depthfirst
companies.description: depthfirst is an applied AI lab building an autonomous application security platform that protects software from design through production. Its General Security Intelligence platform builds context across a company's code, infrastructure, and business logic to detect complex vulnerabilities, cut false positives, and generate merge-ready fixes. Product surfaces include a code scanner, dependency firewall, secrets detection, supply-chain mapping, and agentic pentesting, alongside in-house security models such as dfs-mini1. Backed by Accel, Meritech Capital, Forerunner Ventures, and The House Fund, depthfirst works with companies including ClickUp, Lovable, Supabase, incident.io, and Moveworks.

companies.name: Graphcore
companies.description: Graphcore is a semiconductor and AI-computing company that designs the Intelligence Processing Unit (IPU), a processor purpose-built for machine intelligence workloads, along with the IPU-Machine, IPU-POD and Bow systems that scale it. Its developer surface is the Poplar SDK software stack -- Poplar, PopART (Poplar Advanced Runtime), PopTorch (a PyTorch interface for the IPU) and PopLibs -- distributed as open-source components on GitHub and as prebuilt wheels in the Poplar SDK download. Graphcore targets training and inference for deep-learning models and integrates with standard frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and ONNX. Founded in Bristol, UK, Graphcore became part of SoftBank Group in 2024. It exposes no public REST API; this profile catalogs its software developer surface. Surfaced originally as a portfolio company of Atomico, Balderton Capital and DCVC and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Stratasys
companies.description: Stratasys Ltd. (Nasdaq: SSYS) is a global leader in polymer additive manufacturing (industrial 3D printing), headquartered in Rehovot, Israel and Eden Prairie, Minnesota. Stratasys builds FDM, PolyJet, stereolithography (SLA), selective absorption fusion (SAF) and powder-bed (P3) printing systems, the materials that feed them, and the GrabCAD software platform that drives them. Its developer surface is the GrabCAD ecosystem: GrabCAD Print / GrabCAD Print Pro for job preparation, GrabCAD Control and GrabCAD Shop for fleet and shop management, and the GrabCAD Software Development Kit — a partner program of connectivity SDKs (Printer Connectivity SDK, MT Connect SDK, PLM SDK) that use standard protocols and APIs to integrate Stratasys printers with ERP, PLM, MES and smart-factory systems for automation, data collection and analytics.

companies.name: NAVER Z
companies.description: NAVER Z Corporation is the South Korean metaverse subsidiary of NAVER, headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, with additional offices in Los Angeles and Tokyo. The company builds immersive digital experiences spanning ZEPETO, its avatar-based metaverse and social app launched in 2018; ZEP, a spatial collaboration and virtual-space platform launched in 2022; and Sticker.ly, a sticker creation and sharing app launched in 2019. NAVER Z's public developer surface is ZEP Script: a first-party JavaScript SDK, CLI, and build toolchain (published on npm under the official @zep.us scope) that creators use to build in-space apps and mini-games, documented in the ZEP Guidebook at docs.zep.us with a dedicated ZEP Script API reference. NAVER Z publishes no REST/OpenAPI web API or OAuth program; ZEPETO Studio remains a Unity-based content-creation tool rather than an API surface.

companies.name: Turintech
companies.description: TurinTech AI builds Artemis, a code and AI optimization platform that searches configuration spaces across models, runtime, hardware, and source code to make production AI systems and software faster, cheaper, and more reliable without changing the existing stack. Artemis spans AI inference, agentic software, latency-critical infrastructure, and planning & scheduling, and is driven through the Artemis CLI, which imports Git repositories, generates and validates AI-optimized code versions (via LLM, agent, or genetic-algorithm methods), runs compile/test/benchmark validation, and opens optimization pull requests. TurinTech also offers evoML for automated machine-learning model building. Access is via the Artemis CLI and platform using an API key (ARTEMIS_API_KEY). The company is backed by Speedinvest.

companies.name: Xtype
companies.description: xtype is an automated governance platform for ServiceNow, giving enterprises visibility, control, orchestration, and compliance across every instance in their ServiceNow estate — tracking changes, access decisions, and configurations and enforcing policy in real time. Products include xtype Enterprise and the free xtype View. The company is backed by ServiceNow Ventures, Columbia Capital, Norwest Venture Partners, Inner Loop Capital, and SaaS Venture Capital, with offices in Covina (CA), Tel Aviv, and Vienna. xtype publishes no public developer API: api.xtype.io is a live Kong gateway with no publicly documented routes.

companies.name: Zama
companies.description: Zama is an open-source cryptography company building state-of-the-art Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) solutions for blockchain and AI. Its developer surface is a suite of libraries and protocols rather than a hosted REST API: TFHE-rs (a Rust implementation of TFHE), Concrete (a Python-to-FHE compiler), Concrete ML (privacy-preserving machine learning), fhEVM and the Zama Protocol for building confidential smart contracts and dApps on EVM-compatible chains, plus TypeScript SDKs (the fhEVM Relayer SDK and React SDK). Zama publishes the ERC-7984 confidential token standard, a developer hub, GitBook documentation, and an active open-source GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched from Zama's public developer surface.

companies.name: Argent
companies.description: Argent (rebranded to Ready, ready.co, in 2025) is a self-custodial smart-contract wallet company focused on Starknet and Ethereum. It builds account-abstraction wallets - the Ready / Argent X browser extension and mobile app, a seedless email and password Web Wallet, and a multisig - plus the open-source developer tooling dapps use to integrate them: the starknetkit connection SDK, session keys (@argent/x-sessions), multicall batching, get-starknet, and the Swift starknet.swift and web3.swift libraries. Argent ships no first-party REST API; integration is via these client SDKs and on-chain smart contracts, with developer documentation hosted at docs.ready.co. Surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched here.

companies.name: DoubleZero
companies.description: DoubleZero is a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that builds and operates a global, permissionless, dedicated-fiber backbone for distributed systems like blockchains — delivering low-latency, high-throughput connectivity where milliseconds matter. Its two-ring architecture pairs edge-node filtering with private high-bandwidth transport, connecting Solana validators, RPCs, and market-data consumers directly to one another. The network is coordinated by onchain smart contracts on Solana and powered by the 2Z SPL token, which meters bandwidth access, rewards fiber and device contributors for measured performance, and drives stake delegation. Operators connect through the first-party `doublezero` CLI and `doublezerod` daemon. Founded by Austin Federa with Malbec Labs; backed by Multicoin Capital and Dragonfly Capital.

companies.name: Harpoon
companies.description: Harpoon is a no-code Kubernetes deployment platform that lets teams deploy commercial or open-source software to Kubernetes clusters in seconds using a drag-and-drop interface, without writing code or configuration scripts. It automates cloud account security, cluster provisioning and autoscaling across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and VMware, and integrates with CI/CD tooling such as GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Argo, Docker Hub and Harbor. The product is delivered as a hosted web application (app.harpooncorp.com) aimed at both startups and enterprises; it is surfaced here as an a16z portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass Harpoon publishes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI or webhook surface.

companies.name: Humio
companies.description: Humio is a log management and observability platform built for ingesting, storing, and searching machine data in real time at scale. Backed by Accel and acquired by CrowdStrike in 2021, Humio is now delivered as CrowdStrike Falcon LogScale. It provides high-throughput streaming ingest (including Splunk HEC and Elastic bulk compatible endpoints), a live query language for dashboards and alerts, and index-free retention. Developers integrate through a REST API for ingest and search plus a GraphQL API for administration (repositories, parsers, users, ingest tokens), with official client libraries for Python, Node.js, Go, and JavaScript and the humioctl command-line client.

companies.name: Singtel
companies.description: Singtel (Singapore Telecommunications Limited) is Singapore's largest mobile network operator and the anchor communications group of Southeast Asia, with a regional footprint that includes Optus in Australia and associate stakes in Airtel, AIS, Globe and Telkomsel. In the network-API value chain Singtel sits on the supply side: it owns the mobile network signals — SIM, line, device, location, call state — that the CAMARA specifications turn into callable APIs, and it packages them for Singapore as SingVerify, a five-API anti-fraud and identity suite built on the GSMA Open Gateway framework. It also operates Paragon, its own 5G/edge/network orchestration platform, which powers the Bridge Alliance API Exchange (BAEx) federating network APIs across Bridge Alliance member operators, and it is one of the twelve carrier equity partners in Aduna, the Ericsson-led joint venture that aggregates operator network APIs into a single global commercial channel. Its API posture, however, is partner-gated and sales-led: as of July 2026 there is no first-party developer portal (developer., developers., docs. and opengateway. subdomains do not resolve), no published OpenAPI, no sandbox, no SDKs and no self-serve signup. Every SingVerify and CPaaS API page on singtel.com terminates in an enterprise enquiry form, and the BAEx portal is an explicit login wall for approved partners. Developers reach Singtel's network capabilities through aggregators — Aduna and its platform partners (Vonage, Sinch, Infobip, Google Cloud), the Bridge Alliance exchange, or identity vendors such as IPification — rather than directly from Singtel. Two surfaces do exist and are captured here: www.singtel.com publishes a first-party llms.txt family (root plus consumer, support and corporate companion files, last updated 2026-06-30) that indexes its marketing and support estate for AI systems while naming none of its APIs, and Singtel runs a footer-linked vulnerability disclosure programme at vdp.singtel.com and on HackerOne. api.singtel.com is a live Apigee gateway behind Imperva that answers every unrouted path with an Apigee fault envelope — a real gateway with nothing publicly bound to it.

companies.name: Talus Network
companies.description: Talus Network is a decentralized Layer 1 platform for building and running autonomous, verifiable AI agents fully on-chain. Its core product, Nexus, is an agentic workflow engine that lets developers compose agents as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of reusable Tools — LLM calls, HTTP requests, storage, exchanges — executed and settled on-chain. Talus is built on Sui Move smart contracts with a Cosmos SDK / CometBFT Protochain node, and ships a developer surface as Rust crates (nexus-sdk, nexus-cli, nexus-toolkit), a Homebrew/AUR CLI, GitBook developer docs, and on-chain Move module API references. Backed by Polychain, Talus positions itself as infrastructure for the autonomous digital economy. There is no traditional REST / OpenAPI HTTP API; the platform is consumed through the SDK, CLI, and Move contracts.

companies.name: Chui
companies.description: Chui, now operating as Trueface (part of BigBear.ai after the Pangiam acquisition), is a facial recognition and computer vision company. Originally launched as "Chui," the world's first faceprint API for access and identity, the technology is delivered today as a licensed developer SDK with C++, Python, Android, and iOS bindings, plus a Dockerized on-premises REST API (Trueface On-Prem / PTOP) for 1:1 and 1:N face matching, spoof and liveness detection, object detection, and identity verification. Deployment options span on-device, self-hosted Docker, and AWS. The technology has been evaluated in NIST FRVT and DHS/CBP testing and is applied across fintech, education, security, healthcare, retail, hospitality, and government. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled by the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Columnar
companies.description: Columnar is a data-infrastructure company advancing open standards for database connectivity. It builds and maintains tooling around ADBC (Apache Arrow Database Connectivity), including dbc — a cross-platform command-line package manager that installs and manages ADBC drivers across macOS, Linux, and Windows and eight programming languages — and databow, a command-line SQL query tool over ADBC. Columnar also ships the DuckDB ADBC community extension and publishes Agent Skills so AI agents can connect to and query databases through ADBC. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and is built on the Apache Arrow open-source ecosystem.

companies.name: Datacore
companies.description: DataCore Software is a software-defined storage and data management vendor serving approximately 15,000 customers worldwide, from Fortune 500 enterprises to small and medium businesses. Its portfolio includes SANsymphony (SAN and HCI storage virtualization), Swarm (scalable S3-compatible object storage for archives and backups), Nexus (a high-performance parallel file system for HPC and AI workloads), Puls8 (container-native persistent storage for Kubernetes), and StarWind hyperconverged infrastructure for edge, ROBO, and SMB deployments. DataCore does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI-described REST API; programmatic access is delivered through product-embedded interfaces and open-source integration plugins (CSI, Docker Volume Plugin, OpenStack Cinder) maintained on its GitHub organization.

companies.name: GoSky AI
companies.description: GoSky AI Inc. is a Taipei-based no-code conversational marketing and social CRM platform that helps creators, brands, and enterprises automate customer engagement across Instagram, Threads, and Facebook Messenger. Founded in 2018, its product suite spans the GoSky AI Chatbot Platform (build no-code chat flows, capture leads, and auto-reply to comments and DMs in minutes), GoSky Loyal (a digital loyalty and membership points program), GoSky Ads (precision ad placement across Google, Meta, and Shopee), and GoSky AI Customer Service (generative-AI-powered 24/7 support). The company operates a hosted SaaS console at platform.goskyai.com and reports serving 400+ enterprises including Mercedes-Benz, VOGUE, and Lazada. GoSky AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass GoSky AI publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

companies.name: O1labs
companies.description: o1Labs is a blockchain and cryptography company catalyzing a new generation of applications powered by zero-knowledge cryptography. It builds Mina Protocol — the world's lightest blockchain (~22KB constant chain size), secured by recursive zk-SNARKs — and o1js, an open-source TypeScript framework for writing zero-knowledge smart contracts (zkApps) without deep cryptography expertise. o1Labs also maintains the Kimchi proof system, the Pickles recursive SNARK, the zkApp CLI, and a family of Mina node, archive, and Rosetta SDKs across TypeScript, Go, Python, and Rust.

companies.name: Royco
companies.description: Royco is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol offering transparent, structured yield markets for capital allocators. Through Royco Dawn, users allocate capital into tranched yield markets - senior tranches prioritize base yield with first-loss protection, junior tranches accept first loss for amplified yield - or delegate allocation to independent curators via vaults, with Loop leverage and a coming secondary market and fixed-rate structures. All deposits flow through the RoycoEntryPoint gateway, deployed on Ethereum and Avalanche, with critical upgrades gated by 3-of-5 council approval and timelocks. The protocol has undergone 5 independent audits and formal verifications (Hexens, Cantina, Certora, Nethermind, Immunefi) and ships an official TypeScript SDK plus subgraphs for building frontends on top of it.

companies.name: SolveBio
companies.description: SolveBio is a platform for biomedical and genomic datasets that lets developers query, harmonize, and automate bioinformatics workflows over curated reference data through a REST API and first-party client libraries (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and R). SolveBio has been rebranded to QuartzBio, a Precision for Medicine company: the solvebio.com website now redirects to quartz.bio, the legacy API is served as the QuartzBio EDP REST API on per-customer instance hosts, and the SolveBio SDKs are being deprecated in favor of the quartzbio packages (Python client end of maintenance 2026-03-31). Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched from its public GitHub organization and package registries.

companies.name: Web Methods
companies.description: Web Methods (webMethods) is an enterprise integration platform pioneer, founded in 1996 by Phillip and Caren Merrick in Fairfax, Virginia to connect software applications in real time using web standards such as HTTP and XML. Its 2000 IPO was one of the largest first-day pops of the dot-com era. webMethods was acquired by Software AG in 2007 for $546 million, and its integration portfolio - now including webMethods.io Integration (iPaaS), API Gateway and API Management, the Developer Portal, B2B/EDI, messaging, managed file transfer, and event-driven integration - was acquired by IBM in July 2024 as IBM webMethods Hybrid Integration. Mayfield was an early venture backer of the company.

companies.name: Aceiss
companies.description: Aceiss is a security monitoring and access-visibility platform that gives CISOs and risk managers continuous insight into who has access to their GitHub organizations and repositories. It monitors user access across repositories, detects unauthorized or anomalous activity in real time, and produces governance and compliance reporting mapped to frameworks such as NIST, CIS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, CSA STAR, HITRUST, and SOC 2. Aceiss installs from the GitHub Marketplace as a read-only app requiring admin privileges and exposes an API for integrating its real-time access data into existing systems, with spreadsheet and PDF export. The company is backed by Canaan Partners.

companies.name: Universe
companies.description: Universe is a no-code website builder that lets anyone design and publish a custom website from a phone, tablet, or computer, using a drag-and-drop GRID block system with built-in commerce, mail tools, analytics, and SEO. A 2023 Apple Design Award winner with more than one million sites built, Universe is a Y Combinator W18 company backed by GV and General Catalyst. Universe is a consumer creation platform and publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Zinier
companies.description: Zinier is a no-code field service management platform that helps enterprises schedule and manage their workforce, assets, and customers, powered by generative AI. Its office and field experiences pair ready-to-use productivity tools with a no-code Task Builder for building custom workflows, and an Integration Marketplace advertising 1,000+ out-of-the-box connections to ERP, CRM, and EAM systems such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow, IBM, and Infor. Zinier targets asset-intensive field-service operations, from scheduling and dispatch through mobile task execution and customer communication. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and ICONIQ Capital. No public developer API, API reference, or OpenAPI surface is published today — integration is delivered through the marketplace and end-user product documentation.

companies.name: App Onboard
companies.description: AppOnBoard, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based technology company founded in 2016 that builds AI-driven creative and advertising tools for app and game marketers. Its best-known product is Buildbox, a no-code platform for making games and apps without programming, and its current flagship is Quvy, an AI ad-creation and testing platform that generates static, video, and concept ad variations and predicts their performance against synthetic audiences before any real ad spend. Quvy targets marketers, indie and studio game developers, SaaS companies, and brands that want to replace slow, expensive A/B testing and agencies with fast simulation-based creative optimization. AppOnBoard is backed by 500 Global; its original apponboard.com domain now redirects to the Quvy product at quvy.com. This profile carries the company identity and website properties; AppOnBoard publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

companies.name: Track Titan
companies.description: Track Titan is a sim racing analytics and coaching platform that records in-game telemetry from simulators including iRacing, Assetto Corsa and ACC, the F1 series, Automobilista 2, Forza Motorsport, and Le Mans Ultimate, turning laps into time-loss analysis, AI coaching feedback, auto-installed esports car setups, and structured Academy learning content for a community of over 295,000 sim racers on PC and console. Founded by former professional sim racer and Porsche coach Max Teichert and backed by investors including Partech, Track Titan is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of July 2026 (api.tracktitan.io serves only an internal backend service).

companies.name: TruEra (Snowflake)
companies.description: TruEra was an AI quality, observability, and governance platform that was acquired by Snowflake in May 2024. The standalone TruEra product is being absorbed into Snowflake's Cortex/AI platform. The open-source TruLens evaluation library (originally from TruEra) remains active as a standalone Python project for LLM and RAG evaluation.

companies.name: Cloudflare.com
companies.description: cloudflare-com is an alias profile for Cloudflare. The canonical company profile lives at the cloudflare repository in the API Evangelist Network; this entry exists so that the ".com" form of the brand resolves into the same canonical record. Cloudflare's developer surface includes a single unified REST API at api.cloudflare.com covering DNS, zones, SSL/TLS, Workers, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, R2, Pages, Stream, Email Routing, Zero Trust, WAF, Magic Transit, Spectrum, Load Balancing, Analytics, and Account Management. Authentication is via API tokens with scoped permissions or legacy global API keys.

companies.name: Perennial Labs
companies.description: Perennial is an on-chain (EVM) perpetual-derivatives protocol — a composable, fully on-chain primitive for permissionless perpetual markets, liquidity provisioning (LPs up to 50x), vaults, collateral accounts, and intent-based order flow with off-chain solvers. Built by Equilibria and backed by Polychain, its developer surface is Solidity smart contracts (MultiInvoker batching) plus first-party TypeScript and Python SDKs and a subgraph, rather than a hosted REST API. The v2 protocol has been audited by Zellic and Sherlock and runs an Immunefi bug-bounty program (up to $500k). The hosted application (perennial.finance) has since been sunset, but the protocol contracts, documentation, and SDKs remain published.

companies.name: ShapeCI
companies.description: ShapeCI is software for industrials — a next-generation PDM (product data management) platform enabled by modern version control that helps hardware enterprises go from design to start of production in weeks rather than years. It brings a Git-style workflow to hardware and CAD: teams and projects hold design files under version control with merge requests, documents, and the ability to review 3D models in-browser and auto-sync engineering knowledge with the model-base. A desktop Connector application lets engineers clone a project, create workstreams, and publish or sync changes. ShapeCI is currently an invite-only beta and does not publish a public developer API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Signal Sciences
companies.description: Signal Sciences is a web application and API protection (WAAP) company whose Next-Gen Web Application Firewall (WAF) and Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP) defend web apps, APIs, and microservices against the OWASP Top 10, account takeover, and malicious bots without the tuning burden of legacy WAFs. Founded in 2014 by Andrew Peterson, Nick Galbreath, and Zane Lackey and backed by CRV, Index Ventures, and others, Signal Sciences was acquired by Fastly in October 2020 for approximately $775M and is now sold as the Fastly Next-Gen WAF. The product retains its own control plane and REST API at dashboard.signalsciences.net/api/v0, which remains live for existing customers and lets developers programmatically manage corps, sites, requests, events, custom signals, rules, redactions, lists, rate-limited sources, thresholds, virtual patches, and workspace alerts. Product documentation now lives on the Fastly developer documentation site.

companies.name: Upstream
companies.description: Upstream is a no-code, full-stack platform for launching and operating DAOs (decentralized autonomous organizations), letting communities create a DAO with a Gnosis multi-signature wallet, DAO contract, and vote delegation contract without technical experience. The platform blends on-chain smart contracts (built on OpenZeppelin, audited by Upshield) with off-chain forums, proposals, polls, and events, and maintains the open-source Fortuna service that indexes ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155 transfer events on Ethereum. Upstream is backed by Bloomberg Beta. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; its backend at api.upstreamapp.com is undocumented and product documentation lives at guide.upstreamapp.com.

companies.name: Vega
companies.description: Vega (vega.io) is the operating system for agentic SecOps, a post-SIEM security operations platform whose Security Analytics Mesh (SAM) powers AI-native federated detection, agentic triage, and analytics on every security data source in place, with no ingestion or migration. Founded in 2024 and backed by Cyberstarts, Accel, Redpoint, and CRV, Vega raised $120M (announced September 2025) and continuously assesses detection coverage against MITRE ATT&CK. The platform is sales-led; its application and developer documentation sit behind a customer login.

companies.name: XtGem
companies.description: XtGem is a visual mobile website builder operated by UAB XtGem of Vilnius, Lithuania, letting anyone build and host mobile sites on *.xtgem.com subdomains (10 million+ sites hosted) with a drag-and-drop builder, file hosting, community blocks (forums, blogs, guestbooks), and the XtScript templating language. XtGem publishes no public developer API, webhooks, or SDKs; its GitHub organization ships the open-source XtFramework PHP framework.

companies.name: SentinelOne
companies.description: SentinelOne is an AI-driven extended detection and response (XDR) cloud security platform delivering autonomous endpoint protection, EDR, identity security, cloud workload protection, and threat hunting through its Singularity Platform. The Management API exposes the same operations as the web console for agents, threats, alerts, sites, accounts, exclusions, and policy management. Authentication uses tenant-issued API tokens passed in the Authorization header as `ApiToken <token>`.

companies.name: Amperecloud
companies.description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

companies.name: Blocks
companies.description: Blocks is a cloud cost-optimization service that guarantees up to 20% savings on AWS spend by aggregating the purchasing power of hundreds of companies into group-buying negotiations, then layering automated cloud management on top. Its AI-powered DevOps agent, Major Tom, continuously monitors connected AWS accounts through read-only billing access, surfaces cost-saving and security findings in Slack, and can propose Terraform fixes without requiring root or code access. Onboarding is a one-click read-only AWS cost-data integration with no long-term contracts and no infrastructure changes. Blocks is backed by Speedinvest and is profiled in the API Evangelist network; it currently exposes a marketing and product surface rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: Ellipsis Labs
companies.description: Ellipsis Labs builds decentralized finance applications and infrastructure on Solana. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a fully on-chain, atomically-settled limit order book exchange for spot assets, now expanded with Phoenix Perps for on-chain perpetual futures. The team also develops Atlas (a high-performance DeFi Layer 2), Gavel (token distribution and liquidity bootstrapping), and Plasma (a sandwich-resistant AMM reference implementation). Ellipsis exposes its protocol to developers through open-source SDKs (TypeScript, Rust, Python), command-line tools, and on-chain Solana programs rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Electric Capital and Paradigm.

companies.name: Zenbu 2
companies.description: Zenbu is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) developer-tools startup building a fully hackable desktop interface for managing AI coding agents. The macOS app is a customizable client for the "Pi" coding agent, letting developers run multiple agents in parallel across Git worktrees, review changes, and extend the app at runtime through plugins. Zenbu is built on Zenbu.js, the company's open-source TypeScript framework for building extensible ("hackable") applications, which handles plugin loading, cross-process state sync, RPC, and hot reloading. The framework and its scaffolding tooling are published to npm under the zenbu-labs organization. Zenbu does not currently expose a hosted HTTP/REST developer API; its developer surface is the client-side Zenbu.js framework, its plugin model, and its command-line scaffolders. Founded by Rob Pruzan (ex-Vercel Next.js core, co-author of React Scan).

companies.name: AppNeta
companies.description: AppNeta is a network performance monitoring (NPM) platform for the distributed, cloud-connected enterprise, now delivered as a Broadcom product under its IT Operations Management / Network Management portfolio. AppNeta Performance Manager continuously measures network paths, delivery quality, usage, and end-user application experience across SaaS, cloud, and internet paths using a combination of active (synthetic) and passive monitoring from distributed monitoring points. It exposes a RESTful API (v3 for AppNeta Classic and v4 for AppNeta with Intelligent Alarms) for programmatic access to monitoring policies, web paths, web applications, alarm connectors, and event/observer integrations, authenticated with API access tokens. As of February 2026 the API interface and documentation were upgraded from Swagger to OpenAPI 3.0. AppNeta was originally an independent, Battery Ventures-backed company before joining Broadcom.

companies.name: GoTenna
companies.description: goTenna is a mobile mesh networking company that builds off-grid, long-range communication hardware and software. Its consumer goTenna Mesh and professional goTenna Pro devices pair with smartphones over Bluetooth to relay text messages, GPS locations, and data across a decentralized VHF/UHF radio mesh with no cell towers, wifi, or satellite dependency. The Aspen Grove mesh protocol stack and the Radio SDK (RSDK) let third-party developers embed goTenna radio connectivity into Android, iOS, and Linux JVM applications for public safety, defense, and outdoor use. goTenna exposes no public REST/web API; developer integration is via the native RSDK, which requires an SDK app token obtained from goTenna.

companies.name: Nordson Corporation
companies.description: Nordson Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Nordson Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Over
companies.description: Overworld is an open-science AI research lab building interactive world models - AI-generated video environments that respond in real time to text prompts and controller input at game-level framerates. Its open-source World Engine is a Python inference library that loads Waypoint world models and LoRA adapters from HuggingFace to generate playable, promptable worlds locally or in the browser. Founded by Louis Castricato (CEO) and Shahbuland Matiana (Head of Mathematical Research), both formerly of CarperAI and Stability AI, the team operates openly and publishes its infrastructure as public open-source repositories. Overworld does not currently expose a hosted REST API; its primary developer artifact is the first-party world_engine Python SDK.

companies.name: Primodium Inc.
companies.description: Primodium Inc. (primodiumxyz) is a developer-focused studio building fully on-chain applications and games on Ethereum and Solana. It ships two on-chain games — Primodium, a space-based factory-building game, and Primodium: Empires, a turn-based prediction-market game — both built with MUD and Phaser, alongside a suite of open-source developer libraries and infrastructure: Reactive Tables (a strictly-typed reactive table library for MUD apps), a Solana DEX Indexer Stack exposing a GraphQL API over Hasura/Timescale, a tRPC transaction-sponsoring DEX server, an off-chain MUD indexer, and gasless-transaction relayers. All tooling is published open-source under the MIT license via the primodiumxyz GitHub organization and the @primodiumxyz npm scope.

companies.name: Verbal
companies.description: Verbal (tryverbal.com) is an AI-powered clinical compliance and quality-assurance platform for healthcare organizations. It automatically audits patient interactions — phone and video calls, telehealth visits, AI-agent conversations, and clinical chart notes — against customizable regulatory and quality checklists, scoring compliance in real time and surfacing gaps for supervisors and QA teams. Verbal integrates with communications and EHR platforms including Zoom, Five9, Epic, and Athena. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and customer app but no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Arrcus
companies.description: Arrcus is an AI-native networking software company that builds policy-driven routing, switching, and AI fabric spanning the edge, datacenter, and cloud. Its flagship ArcOS network operating system runs on merchant-silicon hardware and is complemented by ArcRR (scale-out route reflector), ArcIQ (analytics and visibility), ACE / ACE-AI (the Arrcus Connected Edge control and AI-networking platform), AINF (Arrcus Inference Network Fabric), and the TGAX AI switch. Arrcus targets GPU cluster connectivity for AI training and low-latency inferencing networks that reduce token cost. The company is venture backed by General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It exposes a login-gated customer portal and academy rather than a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

companies.name: Albertinvent
companies.description: Albert Invent builds Albert OS, an AI operating system for chemists and R&D teams that unifies electronic lab notebooks, structured molecular-level experimental data, chemical drawing, and safety/compliance data (safety data sheets for roughly 400,000 substances) with chemistry-trained AI models built on a foundation of 15 million molecular structures. The platform helps materials, formulation, and specialty-chemical teams capture proprietary experimental data and accelerate discovery, training custom predictive models on each customer's own chemistry. Albert Invent is a scientific R&D / developer-tools SaaS company backed by Homebrew; its APIs and developer surface are not publicly documented (product documentation at docs.albertinvent.com is access-gated).

companies.name: PulseMCP
companies.description: PulseMCP is a community platform and directory dedicated to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — the open protocol for connecting AI assistants and agents to external tools, data, and systems. Founded by Tadas Antanavicius (MCP Steering Committee) and Mike Coughlin in early 2025, PulseMCP curates searchable directories of MCP servers and clients, publishes use cases, runs the "Agentic Loop" newsletter, and operates a Discord community for builders. It also exposes a public PulseMCP Registry API (api.pulsemcp.com, v0.1) implementing the Generic MCP Registry API specification with PulseMCP-specific enriched metadata such as popularity, security analyses, and compatibility data. The PulseMCP GitHub organization additionally maintains MCP servers, the AIR collaboration framework, and shared agentic-engineering templates and artifacts. Access to the API requires contacting PulseMCP for a key and tenant ID; the directory and content are free to browse.

companies.name: Regression Games
companies.description: Regression Games builds AI agents and bots for video games. Its platform lets studios create bots for QA testing, multiplayer simulation, game balancing, and NPC behavior with minimal code. The Unity SDK (gg.regression.unity.bots / RGUnityBots) adds AI-driven automated playtesting, UI and screenshot regression testing, replay and validation, and CI/CD integration for Unity projects, while the earlier rg-bot JavaScript/TypeScript/Python libraries let developers program bots for Minecraft and Capture-the-Flag tournaments. Distribution is via open-source SDKs and templates on GitHub rather than a hosted public REST API. Backed by a16z and NEA ($4.2M seed, 2022).

companies.name: Spirl
companies.description: Spirl is a non-human identity and access management (IAM) startup that in 2025 rebranded to Defakto (defakto.security); spirl.com now redirects to the Defakto site. The company secures automated systems — workloads, services, CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes, and AI agents — by replacing static secrets and hardcoded credentials with short-lived, cryptographically verifiable identities built on open workload-identity standards (SPIFFE/SPIRE style). Co-founded by Eli Nesterov (ex-ByteDance infrastructure) and Danny Oliveri, it targets the enterprise gap where organizations run millions of non-human identities protected only by static secrets. Defakto was named a 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor in Identity-First Security. It is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site, blog, and security page but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, or developer portal — access is via demo request, so there is no API surface to enrich at this time.

companies.name: Meshery
companies.description: Meshery is the cloud native manager for Kubernetes and cloud native infrastructure. It is an extensible, self-service engineering platform that enables collaborative design, lifecycle and performance management of cloud native applications and infrastructure. Meshery exposes REST and GraphQL APIs for automating multi-cluster operations, design management, performance profiling, and integration with hundreds of CNCF and ecosystem projects.

companies.name: Telepresence
companies.description: Telepresence is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox open source tool that enables fast local development for Kubernetes and OpenShift microservices. It creates a bidirectional network bridge between a developer's local machine and a remote Kubernetes cluster, allowing services to run locally while connecting to remote dependencies. Originally created by Ambassador Labs, Telepresence lets developers intercept traffic destined for specific cluster workloads and route it to their local environment for testing and debugging.

companies.name: Brevis
companies.description: Brevis is a highly efficient ZK coprocessor and zkVM that empowers smart contracts to read from the full historical on-chain data across all supported blockchains and run customizable computations in a completely trust-free way. Developers build application circuits with the Brevis SDK (available in Go and TypeScript), implementing a Data Access Module to specify the historical blockchain data needed, an App Circuit for the computation logic, and an App Contract to receive ZK-verified or coChain-verified results on-chain. Brevis also operates ProverNet, an open marketplace for zero-knowledge proofs, and Pico, an open-source high-performance zkVM. Backed by Polychain.

companies.name: Clover Security
companies.description: Clover Security is a Tel Aviv-based product security company (founded 2023) that builds design-led AI security agents for the software development lifecycle. Its agents plug into the tools engineering teams already use — GitHub, Cursor, Confluence, Jira, and Slack — to automate security design reviews, run continuous threat modeling, detect design-to-implementation drift, and keep agentic and spec-driven development secure by default. Clover has raised $36M from Notable Capital, Team8, and Silicon Valley CISO Investments, serving enterprise, fintech, and banking customers including Lemonade, Plaid, Notion, Udemy, and ServiceTitan. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and enriched from the company's public web surface; Clover exposes no public developer API at this time.

companies.name: Coin98
companies.description: Coin98 is a crypto super-app built around a non-custodial, multi-chain wallet spanning 80+ blockchains across iOS, Android, a Chrome browser extension, Telegram, and web. Its product surface includes the Coin98 Super Wallet, an AI wallet with autonomous agents (Cypheus), the SwapX DEX aggregator routing across 50+ DEXs, on-chain perpetual futures (Coin98 Perps), the Fusion Visa debit card, PowerPool C98 staking, the Zen hardware card, Coin98 Markets data, and a token distribution Vault. For developers, Coin98 publishes a Developer Guide and the Coin98 Adapter — a React/Next.js wallet-connection SDK with useWallet and useWalletModal hooks and prebuilt connect UI — plus a Connect SDK and Telegram Mini App SDK, integrating dApps with the wallet across 40+ chains. Surfaced originally as a multicoin-capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: DoubleDutch
companies.description: DoubleDutch was a San Francisco mobile event technology company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Its Developer Platform (DDDP) let event organizers and third-party developers build React Native extensions that install into any DoubleDutch event app, with a Firebase-backed data layer, a UI component library, an admin/CMS client, and a command-line interface — all published as official @doubledutch npm packages. DoubleDutch was acquired by Cvent in 2019 and its technology now lives under Cvent's mobile event apps product; www.doubledutch.me redirects to Cvent. The developer surface (GitHub org, the doubledutch.github.io documentation site, and the npm packages) remains published but is unmaintained. There is no public REST OpenAPI — the platform is a client-side extension SDK rather than a hosted web API.

companies.name: HELP
companies.description: This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The website pointer on this record resolves to Venturz (operated by GoVenturz, LLC), an all-in-one business operating system for founders that bundles 15+ tools — website builder, CRM, email marketing, payments, and analytics — behind a single dashboard alongside an "AI co-founder" assistant, a founder community, a startup academy, and Venturz Capital funding. As of this enrichment pass Venturz publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. See x-identity-note regarding the stub name versus the linked brand.

companies.name: Prized
companies.description: Prized is an AI-powered platform that lets non-technical operations, support, and finance teams build, deploy, and share secure internal tools without engineering. Users describe a workflow in natural language (or bring their own coding agent such as Claude Code) and Prized builds real software on company data that is pre-connected and scoped, with least-privilege database access per tool, credential isolation, outbound-traffic proxying, and an audit trail on every access. Tools deploy behind corporate authentication and connect to 20+ services including Salesforce, Postgres, Slack, Stripe, and Notion. Prized is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded by Hudson Griffith and Marinos Eliades, both formerly of Gander (YC F24, acquired by Archer Aviation). Added to the API Evangelist network via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from the company's public web surface.

companies.name: Sanlo
companies.description: Sanlo is a multi-platform payments and monetization platform built specifically for game developers and studios. Its products let studios run live ops and accept payments outside the walled gardens of the major app stores to reduce platform commission fees: Webshop Builder (a full-stack direct-to-consumer web shop), Web Checkout (accept payments on any website, web shop, or web game), and Unity Checkout (native iOS/Android in-game checkout for Unity titles via a first-party SDK and API, with one-click checkout, fully customizable UI, and creator-code support). Card and payment collection is powered by Adyen underneath. Sanlo also offers game funding to help studios finance user acquisition and growth. The company is backed by Index Ventures and other gaming-focused investors.

companies.name: Brokk
companies.description: Brokk (Brokk, Inc.) builds AI tooling for large codebases. Rather than a hosted REST API, Brokk ships open-source developer tools centered on "bifrost" — a Tree-sitter-backed multi-language static-analysis engine that gives coding agents structured code intelligence (symbols, definitions, references, call graphs, usage analysis) across 12 languages. Bifrost runs as a CLI, a workspace-aware language server (LSP), and a stdio MCP server, and is published to crates.io (brokk-bifrost) and PyPI (brokk-bifrost-searchtools). The company, founded by Jonathan Ellis (Apache Cassandra / DataStax) and backed by Mayfield, also ships the core Brokk application, the brokk-cli launcher, and Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tooling (anvil, mjolnir).

companies.name: Colibri
companies.description: ColibrITD (Colibri) is a French quantum-computing deep-tech company founded in 2019 in Paris by Dr. Laurent Guiraud and Hacene Goudjil, with a mission to make quantum computing accessible to any enterprise. It develops quantum software for scientific and industrial applications, including QUICK (a quantum multiphysics simulation platform), QUICK-PDE (a Qiskit function for solving partial differential equations), the H-DES hybrid differential-equation solver, and MPQP (Multi-Platform Quantum Programming) - an open-source Python library for building quantum circuits and executing them across IBM Qiskit, Eviden myQLM, Google Cirq, AWS Braket, and Microsoft Azure Quantum backends. ColibrITD serves the semiconductors, finance, defense, aerospace, automotive, and energy industries. Its primary developer surface is the MPQP Python SDK (PyPI + GitHub) and its documentation, rather than a hosted REST API.

companies.name: MQTT
companies.description: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is an OASIS-standard, lightweight publish/subscribe messaging transport protocol designed for constrained devices and low-bandwidth, high-latency, or unreliable networks, making it the de-facto messaging protocol for IoT and machine-to-machine (M2M) communication. MQTT is a protocol specification rather than a hosted API: clients connect over TCP/TLS (typically port 1883 or 8883) or WebSocket (8080/8081) to an MQTT broker (such as Mosquitto, HiveMQ, EMQX, or AWS IoT Core) and exchange CONNECT, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE, and other control packets defined by the standard. The current standard is MQTT Version 5.0 (OASIS Standard, 7 March 2019); MQTT 3.1.1 remains widely deployed.

companies.name: Proximie
companies.description: Proximie is a health-tech company building a cloud platform it describes as the operating system for intelligent operating rooms, connecting surgical teams, medical devices, and data for remote telementoring, telesurgery, session recording, and AI-powered surgical insights across 500+ facilities in 50 countries. For developers, Proximie ships a pre-release C++ SDK (media streaming and session management, with an internal REST layer) and runs a Development Partners program that lets OEMs and medtech companies embed real-time connectivity, secure data routing, and white-label collaboration into their own devices. Proximie also open-sources WebRTC/Janus tooling (jarust, janus-mobile-sdk). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

companies.name: Locale
companies.description: Locale is a no-code workflow automation platform that lets operations, data, and engineering teams build, run, and monitor automated workflows without writing glue code. Its visual builder chains together apps and actions — HTTP requests, AI Actions, run-your-own code, email, Slack, PostgreSQL, Sendgrid, and Fireflies.ai — with flow controls such as conditional branching, delays, and list iterators, then passes data between steps to orchestrate real business processes. Workflows can be built, connected, debugged, and published from the Locale app, and the platform positions itself as an operational automation layer for teams that want internal alerting and process automation without a heavy engineering lift. Locale is backed by a16z. This profile was enriched from Locale's public documentation surface (docs.locale.ai); Locale publishes no first-party public REST API or OpenAPI at this time.

companies.name: Nile
companies.description: Nile is a San Jose, California enterprise networking company delivering an AI-native Secure Network as a Service (NaaS). Founded in 2018 by former Cisco executives Pankaj Patel and John Chambers (chairman), Nile replaces traditional campus and branch LAN/Wi-Fi hardware-and-license procurement with a subscription-based, outcome-guaranteed wired and wireless network stack delivered as a service. The Nile Access Service combines its purpose-built Zero Trust Fabric (switches, access points, gateways, and sensors) with cloud-based autonomous operations, the Nile Services Cloud, Nile AI, Nile Nav, and Nile Digital Twin to plan, deploy, monitor, and self-heal enterprise networks. The platform emphasizes built-in Zero Trust segmentation, continuous performance guarantees (coverage, capacity, availability), and consumption-based pricing — marketed against 60%+ breach reduction, 99%+ ticket reduction, ~3x faster change management, and ~40% TCO savings versus traditional enterprise networking. Nile does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or Terraform provider; its programmable surface is limited to a closed admin/portal API and outbound webhooks used for documented integrations with ServiceNow (ticket and alert webhooks), Splunk HEC, CrowdStrike, Zscaler ZIA, Microsoft Entra (SCIM), Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Global Secure Access, Palo Alto Networks, Forescout (device inventory API), SecureW2, Aruba ClearPass, VeloCloud, Graphiant, Hamina, and Ekahau. Nile is available through the AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription.

companies.name: Quantum Metric
companies.description: Quantum Metric is a continuous product design and digital experience intelligence platform that captures and quantifies every user session across web and mobile, replaying interactions and surfacing friction, errors, and conversion opportunities in real time so that product, engineering, and customer-experience teams can prioritize work by quantified business impact. The platform exposes data-export and integration APIs to customers within their authenticated instance; during enrichment no public, unauthenticated developer portal or OpenAPI definition was discoverable (developer.quantummetric.com and docs.quantummetric.com redirect to the marketing site and the help center returns a maintenance page).

companies.name: Glen
companies.description: Glen is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building a shared organizational learning and memory system for fleets of AI agents. The platform acts as a centralized store that every AI agent in a company can read from and write to, so that when one agent learns something the whole organization gains access to it. Glen preserves decisions, customer insights and operational procedures with full audit trails, applies role-based access control per observation at recall time, and connects to coding agents, PR assistants, bug bots and sales agents over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It integrates with the tools where work already lives (code repositories, pull requests, issues, documentation and meetings) to give both agents and humans unified organizational context, aiming to eliminate knowledge silos, reduce new-hire ramp time and retain institutional knowledge through employee turnover. The company is pre-launch and operating a waitlist; its primary integration surface is an MCP server rather than a traditional REST API.

companies.name: Resolve Systems
companies.description: Resolve Systems (resolve.io) is an enterprise IT automation and AIOps platform that helps IT and operations teams automate incident resolution, service-desk workflows, and cross-domain remediation at scale. Its "Agentic Resolution Fabric" combines a Knowledge Agent (contextual answers across chat, portals, and collaboration tools), an Automation Agent (autonomous cross-domain workflows that remediate, configure, and orchestrate IT processes in real time), and Agent Assist (enriched diagnostics, related incidents, and next-best actions). Product lines include Resolve Actions, Actions Pro, Actions Express, and Barista, spanning IT process automation (ITPA), robotic process automation, and agentic service management. The company positions itself around cutting manual tickets by up to 90% and reports large aggregate customer savings. Resolve is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. This profile was enriched from public web sources; Resolve does not appear to publish a public, self-service developer API, OpenAPI definition, or open developer portal — integration and automation are delivered through the platform's connectors and customer-gated documentation.

companies.name: Stellate
companies.description: Stellate is a GraphQL edge caching and API management platform that caches GraphQL query results at 60 data centers worldwide, reducing origin traffic by up to 95% and delivering responses in milliseconds. The platform provides edge caching, real-time metrics and insights, rate limiting, and security features to help teams scale, protect, and optimize their GraphQL APIs.

companies.name: NeonRain, Inc.
companies.description: NeonRain, Inc. is a 500 Global portfolio company whose public product surface resolves to Playabl (playabl.ai), an AI-powered, no-code platform that lets anyone create web games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Users describe a game idea in plain English and Playabl's generative AI produces a playable prototype instantly, which can be refined conversationally and published to the web. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in the United States, the product targets educators, indie developers, marketers, and hobbyists. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web application with no developer-facing API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal surface.

companies.name: Praxis AI (Vortexify)
companies.description: Praxis AI is a Y Combinator (Fall 2024) company that now operates as Vortexify (vortexify.ai). Vortexify is an AI-native platform that generates operational software directly from a company's data: teams connect data sources through 20+ prebuilt connectors (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, NetSuite, Oracle, S3, Azure Blob, Google Sheets/Drive, SharePoint and more), describe requirements in plain English, and AI agents plan, code, test and deploy backend logic plus custom frontends with no infrastructure to manage. The platform emphasizes building complete apps on operational data rather than just dashboards, with built-in scheduling, serverless compute execution, role-based access control, audit logs, sandboxed environments, token-based authentication, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Praxis AI was founded by Aditya Tewari (ex-Palantir) and Ransika Liyanage (ex-Tesla, GM, Deloitte), originally focused on manufacturing-specific AI agents for predicting and preventing machine failures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator. Vortexify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification.

companies.name: Saffron
companies.description: Saffron (trysaffron.ai) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-native technical assessment platform for engineering hiring. Candidates build real features on a company's actual codebase using AI coding tools such as Claude Code inside a sandboxed environment, while Saffron captures every keystroke and AI interaction to score submissions against custom rubrics. It provides line-by-line attribution distinguishing human-written, AI-generated, and AI-modified code, and replaces traditional phone screens, take-homes, and on-site interview loops with a single AI-integrated assessment.

companies.name: Stride
companies.description: Stride is a multichain liquid staking protocol built as a Cosmos SDK appchain (chain-id stride-1) and secured by Cosmos Hub interchain security. Users stake proof-of-stake assets such as ATOM, TIA, DYDX, OSMO, DYM, SAGA, and LUNA and receive liquid staking receipt tokens (stATOM, stTIA, and others) that keep accruing staking rewards while remaining usable across DeFi for trading, lending, collateral, and liquidity provision. Stride is IBC-connected and uses a Hyperlane bridge for cross-chain reach. Its machine-readable surface is the Cosmos SDK gRPC and REST (LCD) query interface plus IBC, wrapped by the official stridejs TypeScript SDK; Stride does not publish a REST OpenAPI. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

companies.name: Brandcast
companies.description: Brandcast is a no-code digital customer experience and website platform, founded in 2013 and backed by Shasta Ventures, that fuses web design, content creation, and brand asset management into a single system. Business and marketing teams use its Design Studio to build and maintain branded websites, sales proposals, brochures, and content programs, with Salesforce integration for personalized, trackable sites. The Brandcast API opens the Design Studio to developers to create websites from templates and update site content, authenticated with an API key sent in the x-api-key header over HTTPS. Brandcast's website product has since been rebranded as "Sites" and joined Vev; the developer API portal remains at developer.brandcast.io.

companies.name: CERPRO
companies.description: CERPRO is a Berlin-based industrial software company building AI-powered quality-assurance and process automation for small and medium-sized manufacturers. Its flagship product, QualiSpec, uses computer-vision and large-model AI to automatically extract features, dimensions, tolerances and drill-hole specifications from technical drawings (PDF, JPG, DXF) and generate inspection reports and quality documents in customized templates such as VDA, EMPB and inspection plans. This removes manual copy-paste and data-entry work from quality control, cutting documentation time by up to 70-90% and reducing errors while creating a unified data foundation that connects OEMs and suppliers. Since launching in December 2024 the software has been adopted by more than 100 SMEs across aerospace, medical devices and mechanical engineering. CERPRO is a Techstars portfolio company and raised a ~EUR 2M pre-seed round in 2025. The product is delivered as a cloud SaaS platform (platform.cerpro.io) hosted on AWS in Germany, with an ISO 27001 certified, GDPR/BDSG-compliant data-security posture.

companies.name: roli
companies.description: ROLI (Luminary ROLI Ltd.) is a British music-technology company known for expressive electronic instruments — the Seaboard, LUMI Keys keyboards, and the modular BLOCKS system — together with companion software such as ROLI Dashboard, ROLI Connect, Equator, and ROLI Learn. Its instruments pioneer MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) for per-note pitch, timbre, and dynamics control. For developers, ROLI publishes first-party SDKs under the github.com/weareroli organization — the C++ BLOCKS-SDK and roli_blocks_basics for building applications that talk to BLOCKS hardware, and the archived mpejs library for MPE MIDI in the browser. ROLI is backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with real developer, SDK, and domain-security artifacts.

companies.name: Sphero
companies.description: Sphero designs programmable robots and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) learning tools for K-12 education. Its product line spans indi, Mini, Snap, BOLT+, littleBits, RVR+ and Blueprint robots, paired with standards-aligned curriculum (NGSS, CSTA, ISTE) delivered through Sphero Central. For developers and educators, Sphero publishes a public robot-control SDK (sdk.sphero.com) that programs Sphero RVR+ / RVR robots from development boards — Raspberry Pi, micro:bit and Arduino — using Python, Node.js/TypeScript and C++. Sphero exposes robot-control SDKs and a locally-run Node.js RESTful interface rather than a hosted public web API. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist as part of the APIs.io network.

companies.name: Werf
companies.description: Werf is an open-source CNCF sandbox project providing a complete GitOps-based CI/CD solution for Kubernetes. It implements the full application delivery lifecycle — building images, managing dependencies, deploying Helm charts, and cleaning up container registries — using Git as the single source of truth (Giterminism). Werf integrates natively with all major CI systems, Buildah, Helm, and Kubernetes.

companies.name: ReadyAPI
companies.description: ReadyAPI is SmartBear's enterprise-grade automated API testing platform. It unifies functional, security, performance, and virtualization testing for REST, SOAP, GraphQL, Kafka, JDBC, and JMS APIs. ReadyAPI is delivered as a desktop and CI/CD tool rather than as a public REST API, integrating with Jenkins, Azure DevOps, Git, and other automation platforms via TestEngine.

companies.name: Eye Security
companies.description: Eye Security is a European (Netherlands-founded) cybersecurity company delivering enterprise-grade Managed Detection and Response (Managed XDR), 24/7 incident response, security awareness training, EU-native log retention (Eye Log), and bundled cyber insurance to the mid-market. Rather than building its own detection stack, Eye Security combines the human expertise of European security analysts with vetted EDR/ITDR technologies, integrating with a customer's existing tech stack. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a VC-portfolio stub under the mis-expanded legacy name "eEye Digital Security"; the wired domain (eye.security), HackerOne program, and Bessemer backing identify the live company as Eye Security. Eye Security operates internal control-plane APIs (api.control.eye.security, portal, agent) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal, so this profile carries identity and security posture artifacts rather than API specifications.

companies.name: Nixpacks
companies.description: Nixpacks is an open-source build tool that converts application source code into OCI-compliant Docker images by combining language-specific providers, Nix packages, and Buildkit. Originally created by Railway as the build system powering the Railway platform, Nixpacks inspects a project's source, selects one or more providers (Node, Python, Ruby, Go, Java, Rust, PHP, Elixir, Deno, Crystal, .NET, Swift, Scala, Dart, Haskell, Gleam, Zig, Clojure, Lunatic, Cobol, Scheme, F#, Staticfile, and more), and produces a reproducible build plan composed of setup, install, build, and start phases. The plan declares Nix packages, apt packages, environment variables, commands, and cache directories, and can be customized via a `nixpacks.toml` file, CLI flags, or environment variables. Compared with Cloud Native Buildpacks, Nixpacks uses Nix as its package layer, ships as a single Rust CLI, and outputs a plain Dockerfile/OCI image without requiring a buildpack lifecycle. The project is MIT licensed and currently in maintenance mode; Railway recommends Railpack as the actively developed successor.

companies.name: Qevlar AI
companies.description: Qevlar AI is an autonomous Security Operations Center (SOC) platform that investigates every security alert the way a top analyst would — without playbooks, without hallucinations, and without adding headcount. Founded in 2023 by Ahmed Achchak and Hamza Sayah and headquartered in Paris, France, the company runs a proprietary graph-based AI orchestrator (not an LLM agent) that delivers deterministic, evidence-based investigations across the full security stack. As soon as an alert fires from SIEM/EDR tools, Qevlar autonomously pulls, enriches, and analyzes internal and external data, then returns a conclusive malicious/benign verdict, a full investigation report, and recommended remediation — typically in under three minutes, closing up to 80% of tickets automatically. The SaaS platform is SOC 2 Type 2 certified, hosted in the EU (Belgium) on GCP, and connects via API to 50+ security tools (Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, CrowdStrike, Cortex, Google SecOps, and more). It is trusted by Fortune Global 500 enterprises and leading MSSPs/MDRs across Europe and the US. Backed by EQT Ventures and Partech.

companies.name: EZKL
companies.description: EZKL (by Zkonduit Inc.) is a developer-friendly engine for verifiable AI and analytics that generates zero-knowledge proofs (ZK-SNARKs, Halo2) for machine learning model inference. Given a model in ONNX format and sample input, EZKL automatically compiles a proving circuit and produces a cryptographic proof that a computation ran correctly without revealing the underlying private data or model weights. Proofs are verifiable on-chain (EVM-compatible), in the browser, or on edge devices. EZKL ships as a command-line tool, Python and JavaScript (WebAssembly) bindings, and a Rust library, and supports tree-based models, transformers, CNNs, and RNNs. Lilith is its high-performance compute cluster for cloud-scale proof generation. The codebase was audited by Trail of Bits and is developed in the open at github.com/zkonduit/ezkl.

companies.name: Raven
companies.description: Raven is a runtime security platform that protects applications from the inside, detecting and preventing malicious code execution as it happens rather than relying only on perimeter defenses. Its capabilities span Runtime Prevention (blocking exploit execution regardless of CVE availability), Runtime ADR (application-level attack detection and response with forensics), Runtime AI-Agents (discovering and monitoring AI agents in an environment), Runtime SCA (prioritizing vulnerable dependencies by actual execution), and Runtime Gatekeeper (keeping risky applications out of production). The platform is self-hosted on Kubernetes, deployed via Helm/OCI charts and a sensor operator across AWS, Azure, and GCP, and is positioned as an application-level alternative to WAF, EDR, RASP, SCA, and ASPM tools. Raven is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners.

companies.name: Threat Stack
companies.description: Threat Stack was a Boston-based cloud security company providing full-stack cloud security observability, intrusion detection, and compliance monitoring for infrastructure and applications across cloud-native workloads including virtual machines, containers, and Kubernetes. Its platform combined rules and supervised machine learning to detect threats, vulnerabilities, and attacks in real time. Threat Stack exposed a RESTful V2 API (HAWK/HMAC authenticated) and trigger-based webhook alerts, along with first-party SDKs, a Go CLI, and configuration-management modules (Chef, Ansible, Puppet, Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm). The company was acquired by F5 in 2021 and the product is now F5 Distributed Cloud App Infrastructure Protection (AIP); the original threatstack.com and api.threatstack.com domains have been decommissioned.

companies.name: Waterfall
companies.description: Waterfall is a sequential software development methodology where progress flows steadily downward through defined phases including requirements, system design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. It emphasizes thorough documentation, fixed-scope planning, and phase-gate reviews before proceeding to subsequent stages. Waterfall remains widely used in regulated industries, government contracting, and projects with well-understood, stable requirements.

companies.name: WestRock
companies.description: WestRock (now Smurfit Westrock following its 2024 merger with Smurfit Kappa) is one of the world's largest paper and packaging companies. The company provides differentiated paper and packaging solutions including corrugated containers, consumer packaging, displays, and specialty packaging. WestRock serves consumer and industrial markets with an integrated supply chain connecting mills, converting operations, and customers globally.

companies.name: Enclave
companies.description: Enclave (enclave.ai) is an AI-powered application and cloud security platform that operates as an "agentic security engineer." It continuously builds a living model of an organization's attack surface across services and cloud providers, then autonomously triages and investigates vulnerability findings against known CVEs to determine real-world exploitability and reachability. Rather than flooding teams with signature-based noise, Enclave traces data flows to confirm whether a CVE is actually reachable, surfaces cross-service exploits that traditional scanners miss, and routes prioritized remediation plans with proof to the owning teams. Founded by veterans from Stripe, Box, VMware, Salesforce, and Yelp, the company is backed by 8VC and Marc Benioff. Added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer API is currently published.

companies.name: ProductNow
companies.description: ProductNow turns data agents can't reach into living docs — context that travels everywhere. The platform connects to a company's scattered data sources — code repositories, sales systems, financial records, legal documents, and support tickets — and indexes them into searchable documentation that stays current automatically, then surfaces that knowledge to AI agents and teams through Slack, Claude, ChatGPT, and other enterprise tools via Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, with version history, access controls, and knowledge graphs. ProductNow is SOC 2 Type II certified and is backed by Sierra Ventures.

companies.name: Uplevel
companies.description: Uplevel is an engineering intelligence platform for enterprises — an operating system for engineering transformation that helps leaders see team performance clearly, solve root causes, and sustain improvement in the AI era. The platform pulls data from existing tools and uses machine learning to produce engineering metrics and actionable insights: DORA metrics, time allocation and ML issue classification, deep-work and interruption measurement, developer-experience metrics, and AI-impact analysis, framed by the company's WAVE framework of engineering KPIs. Founded in 2018 and led by CEO Joe Levy, Uplevel is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Madrona Ventures, and Voyager Capital. Uplevel serves enterprise customers such as Xactly, Accolade, Braze, Avalara, and Qualtrics; it operates an internal API behind the product (api.uplevelteam.com, AWS API Gateway) but publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: wacai
companies.description: Wacai (挖财, Hangzhou Wacai Network Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fintech and personal-finance company founded in 2009, best known for its "挖财记账" personal accounting and bookkeeping app and its internet wealth-management platform. Beyond its consumer apps, Wacai operates a partner-facing open API gateway (挖财开放平台) at open.wacai.com that exposes services through a single JSON-over-HTTPS entry point using appKey/appSecret signed requests, with official client SDKs published for Java (Maven Central), Node.js, PHP, Go, and C#. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

companies.name: Actualyze AI
companies.description: Actualyze AI is an enterprise AI governance and management company building tools that give organizations the visibility and control they need to adopt AI at scale without slowing their teams down. Founded by Rafi Khardalian (CEO) and Sean Lynch (CTO) — veterans of building and operating distributed systems at global scale — the company designs for regulated industries from day one, embedding compliance, defense-in-depth data protection, comprehensive audit logging, and continuous monitoring into the platform rather than bolting it on. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: AdaCore
companies.description: AdaCore is a software company with more than 30 years of experience building compilation, static and dynamic analysis, and formal-verification toolchains for reliable, safe, and secure software in safety- and mission-critical systems. Its product line includes GNAT Pro (Ada, C/C++, and Rust compilation), SPARK Pro (formal proof), GNAT Static Analysis, CodeSonar for C/C++, the GNAT Dynamic Analysis Suite, and the GNAT Studio IDE together with the open-source Ada Language Server and VS Code extension. AdaCore tooling is used across aerospace, defense, rail, automotive, energy, telecommunications, finance, and medical-device industries. AdaCore is a compiler and toolchain vendor and does not publish a hosted REST API or API client SDKs; this API Evangelist profile catalogs its developer tooling, packages, and public developer resources. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

companies.name: ChipAgents
companies.description: ChipAgents is the Agentic AI Chip Design Environment, helping semiconductor engineers iterate on chip design and verification up to 10x faster by collaborating with AI agents inside their favorite code editor. The platform spans design and verification workflows, coverage analysis, and Root Cause Analysis (RCA), surfaced through a project dashboard and the ChipAgents CLI, and is powered by the company's first model, Renoir. ChipAgents is delivered as a managed, authenticated web application (agent.chipagents.ai) rather than a public API; the company holds a SOC 2 Type II attestation and is backed by Micron, Samsung, MediaTek, and Bessemer Venture Partners, with a team drawn from Cadence, Synopsys, and Mentor Graphics.

companies.name: Nobl9
companies.description: Nobl9 is a service-level objective (SLO) management platform that helps engineering and SRE teams define, measure, and act on reliability targets across cloud and observability tools. The platform aggregates data from Datadog, Prometheus, New Relic, Splunk, AWS CloudWatch, and other sources to compute error budgets and surface reliability insights. Nobl9 exposes a suite of REST APIs for managing SLOs, annotations, budget adjustments, audit logs, and reports using access token authentication.

companies.name: SmartSuite
companies.description: SmartSuite is a collaborative work management platform that helps teams plan, track, and manage workflows, projects, and everyday tasks using customizable solutions, tables, records, and automations.
