The platform combines spreadsheet, database, project management, and workflow automation capabilities into a unified workspace. SmartSuite's REST API provides programmatic access to Solutions, Tables, Records, and Fields using token-based authentication.

companies.name: TOPdesk
companies.description: TOPdesk is a Netherlands-based service management vendor offering an ITSM and Enterprise Service Management platform used by IT, facilities, HR, and customer service teams for incident management, change management, asset management, self-service portals, and shared service workflows. The TOPdesk REST API uses application password authentication (basic auth) and exposes resources for incidents, changes, assets, persons, operators, and locations for building integrations against on-premises and SaaS TOPdesk environments.

companies.name: Wiz
companies.description: Wiz is a cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) that provides agentless security across AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and containers, covering CSPM, CWPP, CIEM, vulnerability management, DSPM, and threat detection in a unified security graph. The Wiz GraphQL API exposes inventory, issues, vulnerabilities, configurations, and reporting using OAuth 2.0 client credentials authentication.

companies.name: Scalyr
companies.description: Scalyr was a cloud log management, server monitoring, and observability platform for engineering, DevOps, and security teams, known for an index-free, columnar architecture delivering sub-second queries across hundreds of terabytes of structured and unstructured log data. Founded in 2011, Scalyr was acquired by SentinelOne in 2021 and rebranded as DataSet; the scalyr.com domain now redirects to dataset.com. Its REST API (hosted at app.scalyr.com) covered log ingestion (addEvents), querying, and account/file management via API-key authentication. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta, gv, and susa-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Wallet Studio
companies.description: Wallet Studio, built by Miss Moneypenny Technologies GmbH, is a no-code SaaS platform for creating, deploying, and managing Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes. Aimed primarily at insurance carriers, it turns policy administration, claims, and CRM systems into wallet-based customer engagement channels reaching the four billion people who already carry a digital wallet, without replacing existing backend infrastructure. The platform offers visual pass editors with one-click publishing, prebuilt insurance templates, integrated automation, a REST API and webhooks for connecting to third-party systems, and authenticated links to portals and value-added services. Hosting is GDPR-compliant and the company describes the platform as certified for enterprise security standards. Backed by Earlybird, the company raised roughly EUR 7 million in 2025. There is no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; the REST API is provisioned per customer.

companies.name: Zogo Finance
companies.description: Zogo Finance is a gamified financial education platform (founded 2018, a Techstars portfolio company) that helps banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions engage and educate their customers. Its library of 1,200+ bite-sized financial literacy modules is delivered to end users through an embeddable, white-label SDK that partners drop into their existing digital banking apps and websites, plus a standalone mobile app and desktop web experience. Users earn redeemable points for completing lessons. Zogo is a B2B/enterprise offering distributed via SDK embed and mobile-banking integrations (Q2, NCR, Jack Henry Banno) rather than a public developer API; as of this pass no public API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

companies.name: DevAI
companies.description: DevAI (DevAI Solutions, Inc.) is a Silicon Valley enterprise IT company, founded in 2024 by Susie Wee (CEO) and Edwin Zhang, that builds agentic AI for IT operations teams. Its DevAI Network Intelligence Engine reconciles data across fragmented IT tools of record (CMDB, vCenter, NetBox and other infrastructure, network, compute, and security systems) into a single trustworthy operational view, and its Network Intelligence Agent "Neo" streamlines IT planning, incident response, patch management, and security and compliance workflows through a chat interface. DevAI reports deployment at Fortune 50 enterprises and won Best-in-Show (Automation) at the AI Networking Summit 2025. The company raised a $6M seed round led by Emergence Capital with Pear VC, Base10 Partners, and Benchstrength. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal has been published to date; this profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web surface.

companies.name: Gigster
companies.description: Gigster is an enterprise software-development services company that connects businesses with top-tier global talent for custom software development, AI solutions, and digital transformation. Through a network of 50,000+ vetted developers, designers, and product experts, Gigster delivers work under three engagement models: Fully Managed (Gigster owns scoping through delivery), Dedicated Teams (skilled teams that scale with a client's goals), and Talent On Demand (specialists who blend into an existing team). Specialized practices cover AI development, innovation/design/UX, applications and platforms, and system modernization. Gigster reports 1,000+ enterprise engagements, a 95% on-time/on-budget delivery rate, and average staffing under 10 days, and is backed by a16z, Bloomberg Beta, and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio company profile.

companies.name: HeavyConnect
companies.description: HeavyConnect is a digital documentation and compliance platform purpose-built for agricultural operations, serving growers, harvesters, shippers, and processors. Its mobile-first, offline-capable modules cover food safety compliance, worker training and certification, time and productivity tracking, quality assurance inspections, end-to-end traceability, and supplier management. The platform replaces paper-based recordkeeping with audit-ready digital documentation and real-time analytics dashboards, helping food and agriculture operations stay inspection-ready. HeavyConnect reports 2,600+ active users across operations including Sysco, Naturipe, Talley, and Empire. It is offered as a month-to-month subscription with a request-a-demo onboarding path. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio-company lead (500 Global, Techstars) and enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Highway 9 Networks
companies.description: Highway 9 Networks delivers AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service, providing secure private mobile networks and deterministic 5G connectivity for enterprise AI workloads. Its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), distributed edge running a 5G core and AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device and robot fleets (Mobile Zones) to give autonomous robots, cameras, and edge devices ultra-reliable, ultra-low-latency connectivity across manufacturing, warehousing, higher education, and energy environments. Highway 9 exposes Mobile Center streaming APIs for orchestration, telemetry, device management, alerting, and analytics, though the full specification is available only through its partner portal for signed partners. The company is backed by Mayfield and was added to the API Evangelist network as an enriched provider profile.

companies.name: Horizon Quantum Computing
companies.description: Horizon Quantum Computing is a Singapore-based quantum software company founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons. It builds software infrastructure for quantum applications, centered on Triple Alpha, an integrated development environment that lets developers write hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction and deploy them to quantum processors. Triple Alpha's final workflow step packages a program and deploys it as an API so developers can invoke quantum backends from Python scripts, web pages, and other technologies. Horizon operates its own quantum computing testbed at its Singapore headquarters and supports a range of external quantum processors, aiming to bridge the gap between today's quantum hardware and real-world applications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or client SDK; API-based program deployment is offered to early-access users of the Triple Alpha platform.

companies.name: LabLabee
companies.description: LabLabee is an AI-powered enablement, testing and troubleshooting platform for telecom teams, positioning itself as "the Copilot for Telco Engineers." The platform delivers on-demand, hands-on labs, sandboxes, learning paths and skill tests covering 4G/5G and Open RAN, IMS, network OAM, SDN and IP networking, telco cloud (OpenStack, OpenShift, Kubernetes, Docker), DevOps and GitOps automation (Terraform, Ansible, CI/CD), Linux, IAM and cybersecurity, and Industry 4.0 and IoT. Three AI capabilities sit on top of the lab catalog: AI Ask (search across telecom standards, vendor documentation and enterprise knowledge), AI Test (automated test execution and configuration validation) and AI Troubleshoot (automated trace analysis and root-cause identification). LabLabee serves telcos, universities, system integrators, network vendors and industrial private-network operators. Founded by Samir Tahraoui (CEO) and Mahfoud S. A. Mebarek (CPO), the company is backed by Accel, Kima Ventures, Reach Capital, Brighteye Ventures and 500 Global, and has been recognized as Best Telecom Startup by the World Communication Awards and with the TM Forum Growth Challenge Award. As of this enrichment pass LabLabee publishes no public developer program - no API documentation, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, CLI or public package artifacts were found on any of its surfaces.

companies.name: MemVerge
companies.description: MemVerge is a memory and AI-infrastructure software company whose Memory Machine and Memory Machine Cloud (MMCloud) platforms virtualize and orchestrate memory and compute for AI, high-performance computing, and life-sciences workloads. MMCloud is operated through the OpCenter control plane and the first-party "float" command-line interface, which submits, migrates, checkpoints, and monitors containerized jobs across cloud and on-prem infrastructure, with spot-instance resiliency (SpotSurfer / WaveRider). MemVerge integrates with Nextflow, Snakemake, and Flyte through open-source plugins and SDKs published on its GitHub organization. Originally surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company, this profile is enriched from MemVerge's public documentation, CLI reference, and GitHub org.

companies.name: Earthly
companies.description: Earthly is an open source build automation tool that combines the best of Dockerfiles and Makefiles into a single, consistent build system, providing reproducible builds that run the same way on a developer laptop as they do in CI. Earthly Cloud and Earthly Lunar extend the open source CLI with hosted runners and code governance guardrails. No public REST or GraphQL API has been published; integration is via the Earthly CLI and Earthfile build definitions.

companies.name: Insta360
companies.description: Insta360 (Arashi Vision Co., Ltd) is a consumer and professional imaging company best known for its 360-degree and action cameras (the X, GO, ACE, Link, and Pro/Titan lines). For developers, Insta360 runs a first-party developer program through its Insta360Develop GitHub organization and a VitePress developer-documentation site. Cameras expose on-device HTTP control APIs: consumer models implement Google's Open Spherical Camera (OSC) API over the camera Wi-Fi AP, and the Pro/Titan line adds a JSON-over-HTTP command API (ProCameraApi) for capture, live streaming, and file access. Native SDKs wrap this surface for C++ (camera control and media stitching/editing), Android, and iOS so third-party apps can connect to, configure, capture from, and post-process footage from Insta360 hardware.

companies.name: REST API
companies.description: Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style for designing networked applications using standard HTTP methods and stateless communication between client and server. REST APIs define how client and server applications communicate over the web using GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and PATCH methods against resource-oriented URLs. REST is the dominant API paradigm, used by 89% of organisations as their primary API format. This index covers the REST API landscape including specifications, tools, frameworks, best practices, and educational resources.

companies.name: UL Solutions
companies.description: UL Solutions is a global leader in applied safety science, providing testing, inspection, certification, advisory, and software solutions to help customers innovate safely, demonstrate compliance, and bring trusted products to market. The company offers software products such as ULTRUS and ComplianceWire, customer portals (myUL, Product iQ), and the Marks and Labels Hub. UL Solutions does not currently expose a public developer-facing API portal with open documentation.

companies.name: Xamarin
companies.description: Xamarin was the San Francisco company behind the Mono-based cross-platform mobile development framework, letting developers build native iOS, Android, and Mac apps from a single C#/.NET codebase. Backed by investors including Insight Partners, it was acquired by Microsoft in 2016. Microsoft retired the Xamarin SDKs on May 1, 2024, with Xamarin.Forms succeeded by .NET MAUI. Xamarin shipped developer tooling and SDK packages rather than a public web API; its NuGet packages, docs, and GitHub organization remain its primary artifacts.

companies.name: XebiaLabs
companies.description: XebiaLabs was an enterprise DevOps software company behind XL Deploy (deployment automation), XL Release (release orchestration), and XL Impact (DevOps analytics), backed by Accel and Susquehanna Growth Equity. In February 2020 XebiaLabs merged with CollabNet VersionOne to form Digital.ai; xebialabs.com now redirects to digital.ai and the products continue as Digital.ai Deploy and Digital.ai Release. The XebiaLabs GitHub organizations, Maven/PyPI/Docker Hub packages, and the dist.xebialabs.com distribution site remain live, still shipping the xl CLI on the current Digital.ai version train. No public hosted API is served under the XebiaLabs brand — the product REST APIs are customer-hosted and documented at docs.digital.ai.

companies.name: CodeKarma
companies.description: CodeKarma is a production intelligence platform that maps 100% of production traffic directly to source code, giving engineering teams and AI agents code-level visibility into how software actually behaves in production. Its products include KarmaLens (an IDE plugin for JetBrains and VS Code surfacing dead code, method frequency, and performance hotspots), KarmaDomain (live API-level dependency graphs across microservices, databases, and async systems), KarmaPulse (an operations command center with API health, error drift, and AI root cause analysis), and KarmaIQ (an MCP server that feeds production context to AI coding agents such as Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Claude). Deployed as managed SaaS or bring-your-own-cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), CodeKarma is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and collects only behavioral telemetry — no PII, payloads, or request bodies. Founded by Anantharam Vanchi Prakash and Priyanka Nahata, based in Bengaluru, India, and backed by Prosus, Accel, Xeed Ventures, SenseAI Ventures, and Stargazer Ventures.

companies.name: Legion Security
companies.description: Legion Security is a browser-native AI SOC analyst that learns a security team's real workflows from inside the browser and then helps execute and automate them in phases: Learning Mode captures and maps how analysts actually work, Guided Mode runs those workflows with a human in the loop, and Autonomous Mode takes over the steps the team has signed off on. The platform targets alert triage, investigation, and evidence gathering in the security operations center, positioning agentic AI as a dependable teammate rather than a black box, with every captured insight visible and every action explainable. Legion Security operates a SafeBase trust center and publishes SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA, and CSA STAR Level 1 compliance documentation. The company is seed-stage and backed by Accel; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

companies.name: Community Labs
companies.description: Community Labs is an independent research organization founded in 2022 by Tate Berenbaum, oriented toward a single belief: access to the future of intelligence should not be gate kept by the hardware people can afford. The company raised a $30M seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, originally operating as a native software development company and venture studio accelerating developer tools and adoption of the Arweave permaweb, and has since refocused on local and consumer-hardware AI inference research. Its open source surface spans Hypura, a storage-tier-aware LLM inference scheduler for Apple Silicon that exposes an Ollama-compatible HTTP API, Autolab, an autonomous research orchestration framework, and the labscommunity GitHub organization of Arweave developer libraries including ArweaveKit, Arweave Wallet Kit, and the Arweave Storage SDK.

companies.name: Data Sciences International
companies.description: Data Sciences International (DSI) is a preclinical research instrumentation and services company for in vivo physiology and translational research, operating as part of Harvard Bioscience. DSI builds implantable and external telemetry systems, respiratory measurement (plethysmography, airway mechanics, pulmonary function), inhalation and smoke-exposure systems, iPRECIO infusion pumps, and behavioral monitoring (VivaMARS), paired with analysis software (Ponemah, FinePointe, NeuroScore) and surgical, data-analysis, GLP-validation and training services. It is a laboratory-instrument and life-sciences vendor rather than an API provider; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sparkles
companies.description: Sparkles (sparkles.dev) is a San Francisco developer-tools startup in Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch building AI coding agents for a whole team, not just engineers. A technical owner connects the company's GitHub repositories and configures environment variables, after which any teammate on a company email address can describe a change and have an agent implement it inside an isolated sandbox and open a GitHub pull request for developer review. Positioned as "Lovable for existing projects," it lets marketers, designers, and operations staff ship safe code changes without needing to know Git or the command line. As of this profile Sparkles exposes only a marketing and product website plus legal pages; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or OpenAPI, so this record captures verified company identity rather than an API surface.

companies.name: Crowdplat
companies.description: CrowdPlat, Inc. is a Pleasanton, California company (backed by 500 Global) that operates two platforms combining human expertise with AI. Its crowdsourcing marketplace connects enterprises with vetted specialists across 50+ countries for consulting, software development, R&D, and innovation challenges, delivered with US-based project management and milestone-driven scopes. Its AI Hire platform is recruitment technology that automates candidate evaluation through resume scoring, AI-generated screening questions, video interviews, and LinkedIn job promotion with auto-targeted outreach. Customers include federal agencies and enterprises such as Airbus, PayPal, and EPRI. No public developer/API program is published at this time.

companies.name: Ray Browser
companies.description: Ray Browser is an AI-powered web browser that learns a user's interests and browsing habits to personalize their internet experience. It ships a built-in agent that can run web searches and automate tasks, a curated daily Discover feed, and Ray Studio for building custom tools and dashboards without writing code. The product is currently in public beta with a free Starter plan that grants weekly credits for its AI features. Ray Browser is a consumer product; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

companies.name: BRICKS
companies.description: BRICKS is a no-code Platform-as-a-Service from BRICKS DAG, Inc. (Taipei, Taiwan) for building and managing interactive digital signage, kiosks, and multi-display stitched screens. A WYSIWYG editor lets designers and businesses create dynamic, data-driven displays — menu boards, wayfinding and crowd control, meeting-room panels, sports scoreboards, promotional posters, and NFT frames — deploy them to app-bound devices, control them remotely from mobile, and connect live data sources and APIs, all without writing code. BRICKS is a 500 Global Accelerator Taiwan (TTA 2022) company.

companies.name: Hyperpad
companies.description: Hyperpad (hyperPad) is a no-code, visual game development platform for iPad, often described as "HyperCard for iPad." Founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the London, Ontario company lets non-programmers build media-rich 2D games and interactive apps using a drag-and-drop, node-based behavior system with a built-in physics engine, particle effects, animation and audio tools, and a bundled asset library, then publish them to the Apple App Store as native apps while keeping 100% of royalties. Products include the paid hyperPad app, a free hyperPad Starter edition, and hyperPad Hub, a community arcade for playing games made with the platform. hyperPad is a consumer-facing creation tool and does not currently publish a public web API or developer platform.

companies.name: Muuktest
companies.description: MuukTest (MuukLabs) is an AI-powered test automation and managed QA services company founded in 2019 that helps software teams reach high end-to-end test coverage in weeks rather than months. It blends an AI-driven automation platform with expert QA engineers to deliver end-to-end, functional, regression, API, and performance testing across web, mobile, and API surfaces, using self-healing scripts (Playwright, Selenium, Appium), CI/CD integration, and detailed bug reporting with repro steps, logs, recordings, and Slack alerts. MuukTest is a managed testing service delivered through a Chrome recorder and a dedicated team rather than a self-service public developer API; it is backed by Techstars, the NSF SBIR program, MassChallenge, and Google for Startups.

companies.name: Newgen Software
companies.description: Newgen Software is a global provider of NewgenONE, a unified low-code digital transformation platform that orchestrates content services (enterprise content management), business process management (BPM/workflow), and customer communication management (CCM) for banks, insurers, government agencies, and healthcare organizations. Founded in 1992 and headquartered in New Delhi, India, the company is publicly listed (NSE/BSE) and serves enterprises worldwide with document management, intelligent document processing, case management, and process automation. Platform capabilities are exposed to customers and system integrators via REST APIs, but Newgen does not operate a public, self-service developer portal or publish OpenAPI/SDK artifacts on its marketing site.

companies.name: Rosebud AI
companies.description: Rosebud AI is an AI-powered game creation platform that lets anyone build and deploy playable 3D games and interactive worlds from natural-language prompts, a workflow the company calls "Vibe Coding" — you describe scenes, rules, and behaviors and an AI assistant named "Rosie" writes and applies the underlying JavaScript. The platform runs on a custom engine designed for AI-era game development, featuring deterministic WASM-based physics, native real-time multiplayer, instant link-based sharing, and a built-in "Juice API" for camera effects, particle systems, and spatial audio. Founded in 2019 in San Francisco by CEO Lisha Li (Ph.D. in machine learning, UC Berkeley), Rosebud AI is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company ships a hosted consumer product and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK packages, MCP server, or developer portal.

companies.name: Unitree Robotics
companies.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

companies.name: User Stories
companies.description: A curated collection of API user stories following agile methodology formats. User stories capture software requirements from the end-user perspective using the format "As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]". This repository indexes user story patterns for API consumers and producers across product management, developer experience, integration design, and platform engineering contexts. Teams use these to align stakeholders, prioritize API features, track progress, and adapt to evolving requirements throughout the API lifecycle.

companies.name: Cajal Technologies
companies.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.

companies.name: Phind
companies.description: Phind was an AI answer engine and coding assistant built for developers, offering conversational, multi-step technical search on the web and through a VS Code extension. Founded in 2022 by Michael Royzen and Justin Wei (Y Combinator S22), Phind trained its own code models and briefly held the top-ranked open-source coding model on Hugging Face. The phind.com product was a consumer/subscription service and never shipped an official public or partner developer API - the only genuinely public developer artifacts were its open-weight models on Hugging Face (Phind-CodeLlama-34B v1/v2, Python-v1, and later Phind-70B). Community "Phind API" projects on GitHub and RapidAPI are unofficial reverse-engineered wrappers, not an official interface. Phind shut down on January 16, 2026; Pro subscribers received prorated refunds and could export chat history through January 30, 2026 before servers were wiped. This entry is a historical record; API surfaces are modeled, not officially documented.

companies.name: 8base
companies.description: 8base is a comprehensive Backend-as-a-Service platform that transforms the entire software development lifecycle by providing AI-assisted design, auto-generated serverless GraphQL infrastructure powered by AWS, and low-code full-stack App Builder tools. The platform enables developers and digital agencies to build scalable, production-grade cloud applications with SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance options without managing DevOps complexity.

companies.name: Adalo
companies.description: Adalo is a visual no-code app builder that lets users design, build, and publish native iOS, Android, and web applications without writing code, combining a drag-and-drop canvas with AI-assisted generation and hosted Postgres-backed collections. The platform supports external data sources, pre-built feature templates, and 2,000+ integrations via Zapier and Make, hosting over a million apps. The Adalo API provides REST access to app collections and push notifications, secured with a per-app Bearer API key.

companies.name: Komodor
companies.description: Komodor is an autonomous AI SRE platform for Kubernetes observability, troubleshooting, and operations across multiple clusters. The platform surfaces cluster events, deployment timelines, dependency maps, and remediation runbooks to help platform and SRE teams diagnose incidents faster. Komodor exposes a REST API plus a Terraform provider for managing clusters, services, monitors, and policies, authenticated with API keys generated from the User Settings page.

companies.name: Runsybil
companies.description: RunSybil is an AI-native autonomous offensive security platform. Sybil — a system of AI agents — continuously penetration tests live applications and infrastructure, finding, exploiting, and validating real vulnerabilities without a human in the loop. It tests live applications black-box by default (no source code required), integrates with GitHub and GitLab to trigger targeted change testing on every code push, and validates every finding through a multi-agent pipeline before it surfaces, aiming to eliminate triage and false positives. RunSybil positions as a replacement for point-in-time penetration testing, legacy DAST/SAST scanners, and bug bounty programs, and also offers white-box testing for deeper codebase exploration. Founded in 2023 by Ari Herbert-Voss (OpenAI's first security hire) and Vlad Ionescu (Offensive Security Tech Lead at Meta), the company raised $40M led by Khosla Ventures and is trusted by security teams at Notion, Cursor, Turbopuffer, Baseten, and Thinking Machines Lab. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface is published at this time.

companies.name: Sourcehut GraphQL
companies.description: Sourcehut (sr.ht) is an open-source software forge offering version control, build automation, bug tracking, mailing lists, and more through a unified GraphQL API. Each service — git.sr.ht, builds.sr.ht, lists.sr.ht, todo.sr.ht, and others — exposes its own GraphQL endpoint at /query, enabling developers to query and manage their projects programmatically with a consistent interface.

companies.name: Visual Studio
companies.description: Microsoft Visual Studio is an integrated development environment (IDE) for building applications across .NET, C++, web, mobile, cloud, and game platforms on Windows and macOS. While the Visual Studio IDE itself is not exposed as a SaaS REST API, Microsoft provides developer-facing APIs for Live Share real-time collaboration (consumed via the vsls extension SDK) and the Visual Studio Marketplace REST API for discovering and distributing extensions, themes, and tools.

companies.name: WunderGraph Cloud
companies.description: WunderGraph Cloud is the managed cloud platform for WunderGraph Cosmo, the complete GraphQL Federation Stack that enables teams to build, manage, and scale supergraphs from any API across teams. It provides full lifecycle GraphQL API management including schema registry, composition checks, analytics, distributed tracing, and routing through a high-performance open-source federation runtime.

companies.name: Projectx
companies.description: ProjectX is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building Infinity (InfinityOS), a cloud operating system designed for AI agents. Infinity lets agents and humans orchestrate GPU workloads through a chat interface rather than traditional APIs, running multiple Windows and Linux applications — such as Blender, VS Code, DaVinci Resolve, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim — simultaneously, each on its own independent compute and GPU inside a single shared browser-based workspace with sub-minute cold starts. A public API, developer docs, status page, changelog, and blog are announced as coming soon; no programmatic API surface is published yet.

companies.name: caimitech
companies.description: caimitech.com is the domain of Wacai (挖财, Hangzhou Wacai Network Technology Co.), a Chinese personal-finance and wealth-management company founded in 2009 that offers accounting/bookkeeping apps, personal financial management (PFM) tools, wealth-management services, and credit solutions. Its developer surface is the Wacai Open Platform (挖财开放平台) — an HMAC-signed API gateway addressed by (api_name, api_version) pairs rather than REST paths, with first-party client SDKs in Java (published to Maven Central under com.wacai), Node.js, PHP, Go, and C#, plus a separate topic-based message gateway (pull/ack). Access uses an app_key/app_secret credential with MAC or RSA request signing and an optional token service. No OpenAPI document is published; this profile was enriched from the provider's public GitHub SDKs and package registries.

companies.name: Crosslayer Labs
companies.description: Crosslayer Labs is a network and web-infrastructure security company spun out of a Princeton University security research lab. Its founding team invented Multi-Perspective Issuance Corroboration (MPIC), an industry standard now required of every publicly-trusted Certificate Authority, which secures the issuance of every HTTPS certificate (~8 million per day). The company protects enterprises from website and API hijacks by discovering, analyzing, and continuously monitoring every layer of first- and third-party network infrastructure, correlating attack signals across the network stack for advanced threat detection and rapid mitigation.

companies.name: Luminal
companies.description: Luminal is an AI inference-optimization company that compiles machine-learning models ahead-of-time into optimized native code for GPUs and ASICs, aiming to deliver the fastest, highest-throughput inference available. Its core product is an open-source, high-performance general-purpose inference compiler written in Rust (the "luminal" crate), built around static computation graphs, a compile-time-checked GraphTensor API, composable neural-network modules, and pluggable graph compilers. Luminal ships two deployment paths: Luminal Cloud, a managed serverless inference service with automatic scaling, and licensed on-prem deployment with dedicated support and custom optimization. The company is backed by Felicis.

companies.name: MaxLinear
companies.description: MaxLinear, Inc. (NASDAQ: MXL) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Carlsbad, California that designs radio-frequency (RF), high-performance analog, and mixed-signal communications systems-on-chip (SoCs) for critical network infrastructure, the connected home, and industrial and multi-market applications. Its products integrate RF, analog, mixed-signal, digital signal processing, security engines, data compression, networking, and power management into single chips that power cable and fiber broadband modems, Wi-Fi 6/7 and wireline home routers, optical transceivers, 4G/5G base-station and backhaul infrastructure, and high-speed data-center interconnects. MaxLinear exposes developer surface primarily as hardware/firmware SDKs and C APIs (for example the Panther Storage Acceleration SDK and the MxL890x Raw Acceleration API) delivered with its silicon, along with design tools, simulation models, and a technical documentation library — it does not publish a public web/REST API. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

companies.name: Mobileum
companies.description: Mobileum is a telecom analytics and intelligence software vendor whose Active Intelligence Platform delivers AI-powered decisioning, risk management, and network insight for mobile network operators. Its product families span roaming management (traffic steering, GlobalRoamer, campaign management), risk management (revenue assurance and fraud detection via RAID), network security (cross-protocol signaling firewalls and SMS/voice protection), testing and service assurance (5G, eSIM, IoT, VoLTE testing, dsTest), customer experience, and data insights and monetization. Mobileum sells primarily to carriers as deployed/managed enterprise software and does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface.

companies.name: Robco
companies.description: RobCo is a Munich- and Austin-based industrial robotics company building software-defined, modular robotic automation delivered as Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) with zero upfront capital expenditure. Its modular robot arms (up to 8 axes, 40 kg payload, 2.5 m reach, 0.1 mm repeatability), the Alfie autonomous robot, the RobFlow no-code programming platform, RobCo Studio configuration and simulation tooling, and the RobVision AI vision system let manufacturers automate machine tending, palletizing, materials handling, and finishing tasks. RobCo serves manufacturing, food and beverage, logistics, automotive, wood, and defense customers, and is backed by Lightspeed, Sequoia Capital, Lingotto, Kindred Capital, and Promus Ventures.

companies.name: SiteAware
companies.description: SiteAware is the construction industry's first AI-powered Digital Construction Verification and Quality Management Platform for buildings. It verifies every installed element and flags real-time deviations across structure, envelope, and interior construction, giving field teams and business executives actionable data and analytics to catch issues before they lead to expensive rework. SiteAware is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

companies.name: Hesai Technology
companies.description: Hesai Technology is a global leader in 3D LiDAR perception, designing and manufacturing high-performance lidar sensors for autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, and industrial automation. Its sensors are deployed by major automotive OEMs and autonomous-vehicle companies across more than 40 countries. Hesai does not expose a public REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is source-distributed C++ SDKs, ROS and ROS2 drivers, and integration plugins (including an NVIDIA DriveWorks plugin) published on the HesaiTechnology GitHub organization, alongside a developer portal and downloadable firmware, manuals, and tools. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Hesai's public developer resources.

companies.name: ironSource
companies.description: ironSource is a Tel Aviv-based mobile game growth platform, acquired by Unity Technologies in a $4.4B all-stock deal that closed in November 2022 and is now operated as part of Unity's Grow Solutions group. The company builds an end-to-end suite for mobile game developers spanning ad monetization, user acquisition, and ad operations. Its flagship product LevelPlay is a unified in-app bidding and ad mediation platform that brokers Rewarded Video, Interstitial, and Banner ad demand across the ironSource Ads network, AdMob, AppLovin, Meta Audience Network, Pangle, Mintegral, Unity Ads, Vungle, and dozens of other ad sources. ironSource Ads is its self-serve ad network and user-acquisition platform offering CPI, CPE, ROAS-optimized, and SKAdNetwork-aware campaign management. Adjacent products include Aura (an on-device content marketplace for carriers and OEMs that originated from the 2021 Bigabid/Soomla portfolio and earlier hardware OEM deals), Tapjoy Offerwall (acquired 2022) for rewarded engagement, and Ad Quality for ad-content monitoring. Developer access is via a REST surface hosted at platform.ironsrc.com — including the Monetization Reporting API (v5/v4), ironSource Ads Reporting API, Application API (v6), Campaign API suite (Campaigns, Audiences, Country Groups, Bidding, Assets, Creatives), SKAN Reporting API, and Cost API — authenticated with Bearer tokens issued from the platform dashboard. Real client integration is delivered via native SDKs (iOS, Android, Unity, Flutter, React Native, Adobe AIR, Xamarin) plus the LevelPlay mediation adapter ecosystem published on github.com/ironsource-mobile. As of 2026 the developers.is.com knowledge center 301-redirects to docs.unity.com, consolidating ironSource documentation inside Unity Grow alongside Unity Ads. No public OpenAPI, Postman collection, or JSON Schema bundle is published by ironSource for the REST surface; documentation is human-readable HTML on docs.unity.com/en-us/grow.

companies.name: Truex Media
companies.description: TrueX (stylized true[X]) is an interactive, opt-in video advertising company now operating as part of Infillion. Its technology delivers "attention-based" ad experiences — Choice Cards and interactive engagement units that let viewers opt in to a single, longer branded interaction in exchange for an ad-free content break — across connected TV (CTV), over-the-top (OTT), mobile, and web. The company originated as SocialVibe (a Redpoint Ventures portfolio company), was acquired by 21st Century Fox, and is now a video advertising product within Infillion alongside MediaMath, InStadium, Gimbal, and Catalina. TrueX's integration surface is the TruexAdRenderer (TAR) client SDK — published first-party from the "socialvibe" GitHub organization for iOS, tvOS, Android, Roku, and CTV/HTML5 web via Swift Package Manager and CocoaPods — rather than a public REST API. Publishers embed the renderer, typically alongside Google IMA (client- or server-side ad insertion), to serve and measure interactive ads.

companies.name: Asserts.ai
companies.description: Asserts.ai is an observability intelligence platform for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry that automatically models the entities in your infrastructure and application metrics, applies golden-signal and SLO PromQL rules to surface anomalies, and correlates related failures into root-cause workbenches to cut mean-time-to-resolution. It also ships a Data Distiller for reducing metric cardinality and observability cost. Asserts was acquired by Grafana Labs in November 2023 and is now delivered as part of Grafana Cloud; its standalone website, docs, and GitHub organization are archived and no longer maintained.

companies.name: Buildah
companies.description: Buildah is an open-source, Linux-based command-line tool for building OCI-compliant container images without requiring a full container runtime or daemon. It allows building images from scratch or using Dockerfiles, with fine-grained control over image layers. Buildah supports rootless builds in unprivileged environments and integrates seamlessly with Podman and Skopeo as part of the containers organization. It is commonly used in Kubernetes-based CI/CD pipelines to avoid Docker-in-Docker complexity.

companies.name: Dokku
companies.description: Dokku is an open-source Docker-powered self-hosted Platform-as-a-Service that helps you build and manage the lifecycle of applications from initial push to scaling out. Often described as "the smallest PaaS implementation you've ever seen" and a self-hosted mini-Heroku, Dokku turns a single Linux host (or a multi-host scheduler such as K3s or Nomad) into a git-push deployment target that builds applications from Heroku-compatible buildpacks, Cloud Native Buildpacks, Nixpacks, Railpack, Dockerfiles, or pre-built Docker images. Dokku is MIT licensed, written primarily in Bash, and maintained by the Dokku organization on GitHub since 2013. It ships an extensive plugin ecosystem covering data stores (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, Redis, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, Meilisearch, Typesense), TLS via Let's Encrypt, HTTP basic auth, maintenance mode, redirects, schedulers for Docker, K3s and Nomad, multiple HTTP proxies (Nginx, HAProxy, Caddy, Traefik, OpenResty), CI integrations, and an official GitHub Action. Dokku's primary interface is the `dokku` CLI invoked over SSH; there is no first-party public HTTP REST API in core (the historical `dokku-api` Ruby wrapper is archived and unmaintained).

companies.name: Improbable
companies.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

companies.name: Scuba
companies.description: Scuba (Scuba Analytics, formerly Interana) is a real-time behavioral and customer analytics platform for self-service exploration of large-scale event data, backed by Battery Ventures and DCVC. The company is rebranding to Behavure AI and extending its behavioral query engine to detect drift, explain decisions, and govern AI agents across models, systems, and users. Scuba publishes product user guides, admin guides, a glossary, dated release notes, and a Tableau connector at docs.scuba.io (now docs.behavure.ai), but does not currently expose a public developer REST API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API specification.

companies.name: Conektto
companies.description: Conektto is an AI-assisted API design and lifecycle platform that helps teams design, simulate, generate, test, and deploy APIs. The platform bundles a Design Studio (NLP-driven contract design), an Autonomous Test Studio (mocking, test generation, test data, and performance testing), a Hybrid API Orchestrator, and an enterprise SDLC workspace. Conektto is delivered as a hosted SaaS workbench with a free Community Edition and a Pro Plan; it does not currently publish a public, self-service developer API for programmatic access to the Design Studio. Customer integrations are surfaced through the SaaS UI, GitHub workspace integrations, and custom enterprise engagements.

companies.name: Approxima
companies.description: Approxima is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building AI agents that test every pull request. Approxima plugs into your CI/CD pipeline and runs autonomous agents on each PR: the agents build your application in an isolated sandbox, exercise it in a real browser, and report exactly what is broken, with screenshots. The company positions itself as a trust layer for AI-assisted software development, letting engineering teams catch regressions and validate fixes end to end before code merges to production. As of this profile Approxima operates a marketing site and private login at approxima.ai and does not yet publish a public API, developer documentation, or an OpenAPI definition; this repo captures its identity and domain-security posture pending a public API surface.

companies.name: DZone
companies.description: DZone is one of the world's largest online communities and a leading publisher of knowledge resources for software engineering professionals. Founded in 1997 with roots in Javalobby, DZone reaches millions of developers each month with articles, tutorials, research guides, and Refcards covering topics including cloud architecture, Java, JavaScript, microservices, containers, data, DevOps, AI, and more.

companies.name: Playabl
companies.description: Playabl is a no-code, conversational game creation platform that lets anyone build games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Operated by Replkt, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator, Playabl turns natural-language prompts into playable games across genres including sports, idle, brainrot, dopamine, and think/puzzle categories, with no coding required. The product is a consumer-facing web application (playabl.ai); as of this profile Playabl does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public web presence.

companies.name: TAAI Labs, Inc
companies.description: TAAI Labs, Inc operates Sparkle (sparkle.security), an AI-first secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) platform, currently in beta, that aims to prevent vulnerabilities across the entire SDLC by embedding AI-powered security analysis into existing engineering workflows. Sparkle works across five phases — contextualize, design, build, validate, and govern — and deploys "Secure Agents" that surface risks, gather evidence, and track security decisions to give product security, AppSec, platform engineering, and engineering leadership teams audit-ready visibility across the secure SDLC. The company markets outcomes such as increased security-team productivity, reduced AI-generated risk, and full visibility, and is backed by 500 Global. The product is pre-general-availability and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation as of this profile.

companies.name: Wabi
companies.description: Wabi is a consumer AI mini-app platform — billed as "the first personal software platform" and a "YouTube of apps" — where anyone can create, discover, share, and remix AI-generated mini-apps from a single natural-language prompt while Wabi handles the underlying infrastructure, UI, hosting, and data. Founded by Eugenia Kuyda (founder of the AI companion app Replika) and backed by a roughly $20M pre-seed round (investors include Naval Ravikant, Garry Tan, Justin Kan, and Forerunner Ventures), Wabi is an invite/beta consumer product. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, or developer documentation — only the consumer web app and its Terms/Privacy pages.

companies.name: Avenue
companies.description: Avenue is an operations observability and workflow-automation platform that helps operations, RevOps, and support teams detect problems and act on them in real time. It connects to the tools and databases a business already runs on (Postgres, Google Sheets, Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Linear, Asana, Notion), watches for issues using custom rules and thresholds, and routes alerts into a shared task queue where teams triage and resolve them. A drag-and-drop playbook builder and an operational AI copilot automate routine responses, while metrics track resolution over time. Avenue is used by operations leaders at marketplaces, fintech, and healthcare companies. It was founded in 2021 and is backed by Y Combinator, Slack Fund, Accel, and Flexport.

companies.name: Prosimo
companies.description: Prosimo is a multi-cloud networking platform that gives enterprises a full-stack cloud transit, security, performance, observability, and cost-management layer across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud. Its Application eXperience Infrastructure (AXI) abstracts cloud-provider networking constructs and ties network transit, micro-segmentation, zero-trust policy, WAF, and observability into an autonomous, ML-driven control plane. Prosimo exposes that control plane programmatically through a first-party Terraform provider (prosimo-io/prosimo) for full lifecycle management of cloud gateways, network and application onboarding, policies, namespaces, and security profiles; a companion Pulumi bridge repository and reusable Terraform modules are published on GitHub. Prosimo was venture-backed by General Catalyst, WRVI Capital, and BlackRock; industry sources report it was subsequently acquired by Palo Alto Networks.

companies.name: Amplication
companies.description: Amplication is an open-source backend development platform that generates production-ready microservices — REST APIs, GraphQL endpoints, data models, DTOs, and supporting infrastructure code — from a domain model, embedding organizational best practices and standards so teams avoid repetitive backend coding. The project is TypeScript-based, distributed as @amplication npm packages and an `amp` CLI, and remains actively maintained on GitHub (16k+ stars, v3.15.0). Originally offered a hosted product at app.amplication.com; the hosted service and docs subdomain have since been retired and the amplication.com root now redirects to overcut.ai (the founders' agentic-SDLC venture), while the open-source project, npm packages, and Discord community continue.

companies.name: Skip
companies.description: Skip (originally Skip Protocol, skip.money) is the interchain infrastructure company that rebranded to Cosmos Labs and is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Interchain Foundation, leading engineering and growth for the Cosmos blockchain stack. Its skip.money and skip.build domains now redirect to cosmos.network. The team maintains the open-source Cosmos SDK, the Inter-Blockchain Communication protocol (IBC), the CometBFT consensus engine, and Cosmos EVM — the most widely adopted Layer 1 blockchain toolkit, deployed across 200+ chains. There is no independent Skip-branded hosted API; the public developer surface is the Cosmos SDK node REST + gRPC interfaces documented at docs.cosmos.network, with source on the cosmos GitHub organization.

companies.name: Standout
companies.description: Standout (standout.work) is an AI talent agent for tech professionals in the United States. Candidates run a CLI (`npx standout`) that assesses how they think, build, and debug to create a living, verified profile of capability rather than a resume. Standout matches candidates to hiring companies and brokers a direct introduction to the founder when a match looks right — no applications and no recruiter middle layer. It is free for candidates; companies pay only on a successful hire. Backed by Y Combinator.

companies.name: Sware (fka BTR)
companies.description: Sware (formerly BTR) is a life sciences software company providing AI-driven GxP validation for regulated life sciences and pharmaceutical organizations. Its Res_Q SaaS platform combines a decade of validation intelligence with a Data Cloud and AI agents that automate validation work, surface insights, and keep every decision explainable, traceable, and reversible. A companion product, GxPNext, delivers agentic validation built for software development so teams can embed GxP validation directly into their applications, ship faster, and simplify customer audits. Sware serves quality, regulatory, and engineering leaders across software validation, AI/ML validation, plant and equipment validation, and medical device / SaMD development, and publishes SOC 2 and ISO 9001 certifications. It is backed by Insight Partners. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI is available today (the Res_Q API page is password-gated), so this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain-security probe.

companies.name: Layer
companies.description: Layer is a living digital art platform that curates code-based generative artwork and ultra-high-resolution video art for everyday display. Its developer surface is an artist-facing, first-party TypeScript SDK (a browser global, $layer) that lets creators declare customizable parameters, register a canvas for screenshot capture, and supply generated video previews back to Layer Studio, alongside published guidelines for generative and Ultra Res artwork. Layer is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Emergence Capital, added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public developer documentation. Layer exposes a client-side SDK rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

companies.name: Extensity
companies.description: ExtensityAI is an AI research company building trustworthy, verifiable AI for enterprise environments through a neurosymbolic architecture that combines large language models with symbolic validation and knowledge-graph reasoning. Its flagship open-source framework, SymbolicAI, treats LLMs as programmable, differentiable primitives (Symbol objects) governed by Design-by-Contract validation, giving developers source-traceable, contract-enforced AI they can run on-premise with sovereign data control. The company also ships developer tooling including the ontoloom MCP server for building and exploring OWL 2 ontologies with AI agents. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

companies.name: OpenLLMetry
companies.description: OpenLLMetry is an open-source observability framework for LLM and generative AI applications, built on top of OpenTelemetry. Maintained by Traceloop under the Apache 2.0 license, it provides drop-in instrumentation for 30+ LLM providers, vector databases, and agent frameworks, and emits standardized GenAI traces over OTLP to any observability backend (Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, New Relic, Splunk, Langfuse, LangSmith, Braintrust, and the Traceloop platform). Its semantic conventions for LLMs have been upstreamed into the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.

companies.name: Stage
companies.description: Stage is a code review tool that reorganizes local git changes and pull requests into logical, ordered "chapters" so engineers can review and merge changes far faster — a workflow built for teams shipping large volumes of AI-generated code. Stage ships an open-source (MIT) command-line tool, "stagereview", that runs entirely on the developer's machine and works with any AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, opencode): it diffs the current branch or a GitHub PR, clusters the hunks into narrated chapters with a prologue, and opens them in a local browser SPA for review. The full hosted Stage experience lives at stagereview.app. Stage is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company founded by Charles Pan and Dean Stratakos.

companies.name: Apiphani
companies.description: Apiphani is a technology-enabled application managed-services company dedicated to helping businesses minimize the effort and risk of running their tier-1, mission-critical applications. It combines decades of enterprise operations experience with intelligent automation and machine learning to drive efficiency and reliability across SAP environments (S/4HANA, Business Suite, Cloud ERP) running on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Services span application technical management (ABAP, SAP Basis, application security), application hosting (ALM/APM), application infrastructure (auto-scaling, HA/DR), security management, and cloud migration and optimization. Apiphani's Luumen platform is an AI-native observability product with "Deep Automation" that detects and resolves issues before users notice, unifying application telemetry, security, and self-healing. The company is certified SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and CSA STAR, and is backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Drag Bot
companies.description: drag&bot is a web-based industrial robotics software platform for the intuitive setup, programming, and operation of industrial robots without prior robotics or coding skills. Founded in Stuttgart in 2016 and acquired by KEBA in 2021, it lets production workers assemble robot programs by dragging and dropping reusable Function Blocks. The platform is built on ROS (Robot Operating System), making it vendor-neutral across robot brands such as KUKA, ABB, Universal Robots, FANUC, Denso, Kinova, and Aubo, as well as a wide range of grippers and peripheral tools. Developers extend the platform with Python/JSON Function Blocks and ROS-based Components (hardware drivers), and integrate with factory equipment over Modbus TCP/IP and MQTT. drag&bot has been integrated into KEBA's Kemro X automation platform. Its programmatic surface is exposed as ROS services, topics, and messages rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

companies.name: GraphQL Code Generator
companies.description: Code generation tool from The Guild that generates TypeScript types, React hooks, resolvers, and SDKs from GraphQL schemas and operations, supporting 50+ plugins.

companies.name: Pienso
companies.description: Pienso is an interactive no-code AI and machine learning platform, founded in 2016 out of MIT by Karthik Dinakar and Birago Jones and headquartered in the Washington, DC / Arlington, VA area. It lets subject-matter experts explore, train, fingerprint, annotate, and deploy deep-learning and large language models over unstructured text — customer calls, emails, documents, and social content — through a point-and-click interface with no coding required. Product capabilities include Ingest, Train & Fingerprint, Annotate, Dataset Analysis, and PromptFactory, applied to use cases such as customer insight, content moderation, document intelligence, and risk detection. Pienso is deployed into the customer's own environment — AWS, Azure, GCP, Gcore, or on-premises — so data never leaves the customer's control, and the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; integration is sales-led and the platform runs as a self-contained system. Backed by Uncork Capital.

companies.name: VoidZero
companies.description: VoidZero is the JavaScript tooling company building a unified, high-performance open-source toolchain for web development: the build tool Vite, the test runner Vitest, the Rust-based bundler Rolldown, and the Oxc language toolchain (including the oxlint linter and oxc-parser), all brought together under the commercial unified entry point Vite+. Founded by Evan You, creator of Vite and Vue.js, and backed by Accel and Peak XV, VoidZero joined Cloudflare in 2026. The company ships its capabilities as open-source npm packages and command-line tools rather than as a hosted REST API.

companies.name: Azuqua
companies.description: Azuqua was a Seattle-based integration platform as a service (iPaaS) and no-code workflow-automation company, backed by Insight Partners and Techstars, that let business teams build integrations and automated workflows (FLOs) across SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Slack, Marketo and ServiceNow. Azuqua was acquired by Okta in 2019 and its workflow orchestration engine and connectors were folded into Okta Workflows (part of Okta Lifecycle Management). The standalone product is now end-of-life: azuqua.com serves an acquisition notice and the API is no longer available for purchase. This API Evangelist profile documents the surviving public developer surface (legacy ReadMe docs, changelog, llms.txt) and the product's lifecycle status.

companies.name: Optoscale
companies.description: Optoscale (OptoScale AS) is a Norwegian aquaculture technology company founded in 2015 in Trondheim that builds AI-powered, camera-based edge-computing monitoring for fish farming. Its Bioscope units capture real-time measurements of fish weight, biomass, sea-lice counts, welfare, behaviour and feeding, producing tens of thousands of validated measurements each day directly on the unit rather than on remote servers. Customers view trends, graphs and high-resolution imagery through the OptoScale web portal, export to Excel/CSV, and integrate the underlying data into their own analytics and farm-management systems via OptoScale's data API. OptoScale was acquired by Insight Partners in 2025.

companies.name: Use Cases
companies.description: A curated collection of practical API use cases across industries and technical domains. Use cases describe specific scenarios where APIs solve real-world problems, improve workflows, and enable integrations. This repository indexes use case patterns across industries including fintech, healthcare, retail, logistics, and enterprise software, helping API producers and consumers understand how APIs deliver value.

companies.name: EditorConfig
companies.description: EditorConfig helps maintain consistent coding styles for multiple developers working on the same project across various editors and IDEs. The EditorConfig project consists of a file format for defining coding styles and a collection of text editor plugins that enable editors to read the file format and adhere to defined styles. EditorConfig files are easily readable and work well with version control systems. The format uses an INI-style syntax compatible with the Python configparser library, with filepath glob patterns similar to gitignore.

companies.name: ReqBin
companies.description: ReqBin is an online HTTP/REST API client for testing API requests directly from the browser without plugins or software installation. It supports all HTTP methods, custom headers, request bodies, authentication schemes, and code generation for multiple languages. ReqBin is widely used by developers to test REST APIs, debug HTTP requests, and generate code snippets for API integration.

companies.name: Tenstorrent
companies.description: Tenstorrent is an AI hardware company designing Tensix and Tensix++ based AI accelerators on the open RISC-V architecture, including the Wormhole and Blackhole generations of cards, the TT-QuietBox workstation, and the Galaxy Blackhole 6U server housing 32 Blackhole chips. The company is unusual in the AI silicon space for shipping a fully open-source software stack including TT-Metal (the low-level kernel and operator library), TT-Forge (an MLIR-based compiler for PyTorch, JAX, and ONNX), TT-MLIR, TT-XLA, the TT-Inference-Server, and RISC-V cores and toolchains. Pricing is published from 999 dollars for an entry card up to 440,000 dollars for a base Galaxy supercluster. Tenstorrent does not currently offer a public hosted-inference API, so this profile catalogs hardware, SDKs, compilers, and open-source repositories rather than an HTTP API surface.

companies.name: Supermaven
companies.description: Supermaven was an AI code completion tool founded by Jacob Jackson (previously co-founder of Tabnine) and known for shipping the first code completion product with a 1,000,000-token context window — over thirty times the context of contemporary copilots — backed by the in-house Babble model and roughly 250 ms response latency. Supermaven delivered plugins for VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and Neovim, plus a chat surface that proxied GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and GPT-4 alongside inline completions, style adaptation, and codebase-aware suggestions. Anysphere — the company behind the Cursor AI code editor — acquired Supermaven on 12 November 2024 to power Cursor's next-generation Tab model, and on 21 November 2025 Supermaven was formally sunset: subscribers received prorated refunds, agent/chat features were retired, VS Code users were migrated to Cursor, and free autocomplete inference continues for existing JetBrains and Neovim users for the foreseeable future. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDK — Supermaven shipped as an IDE plugin product, and its long-context completion technology now lives inside Cursor.

companies.name: Bacca.ai
companies.description: Bacca.ai is an AI-driven Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) platform that deploys an autonomous agent functioning as a Tier-1 on-call engineer. It ingests operational context from Slack, Jira, documentation, logs, traces, and metrics to build a proprietary Knowledge Graph of an organization's systems, then contextualizes and deduplicates alerts, identifies root causes with high accuracy, automates incident war rooms and post-mortem generation, and surfaces reports on system failures and hotspots. Bacca reports cutting Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) by roughly 40-60%. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company deploys on Google Cloud (cloud or on-prem) with single-tenant data isolation and SOC 2 Type I & II attestation. Backed by Homebrew.

companies.name: MEQ Solutions
companies.description: MEQ Solutions is an Australian agrifood technology company delivering what it calls the world's only end-to-end measurement of red meat quality and yield. Its integrated hardware-and-software suite — MEQ Probe, MEQ Camera, MEQ Live, and MEQ Insights — gives producers, feedlots, processors, brands, retailers, and food-service operators objective, real-time carcass and eating-quality data. Deployed across Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and Brazil, MEQ has completed over 10 million scans across 60+ deployments and reports a demonstrated 10x ROI. The company is backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API surface is currently published; the meqinsights.com portal is a customer login.

companies.name: Squadio
companies.description: Squadio is a Tech Teams as a Service (TaaS) platform, backed by 500 Global, that lets companies spin up dedicated squads of vetted software engineers and tech talent to build, scale, and digitally transform their projects. The platform covers hiring tech talent, payroll management, MVP development, and talent buyout, and pairs clients with talent through an assisted onboarding flow that includes its Lama AI assistant. Squadio operates primarily across the MENA region and connects businesses with remote engineering teams rather than exposing a public developer API.

companies.name: Teserac
companies.description: Teserac is an AI-native infrastructure intelligence company building Neuron™, a unified platform for data center observability, intelligence, and workflow automation. Neuron ingests telemetry from every system in a facility and correlates it across existing DCIM, BMS, EPMS, and ITSM platforms into a single intelligence layer, surfacing anomalies before they become incidents to protect SLAs and shrink MTTR. Its proprietary Neuron Connect™ technology auto-discovers and configures devices and supports protocols including SNMP, OPC-UA, MQTT, Redfish, REST APIs, and Niagara/Tridium. Teserac is backed by Mayfield. As of this profile the company exposes a marketing site and an authenticated product demo (neuron.demo.teserac.ai) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Ai Fabrik
companies.description: AI Fabrik is an infrastructure company building an edge inference delivery network for high-performance AI tokens. Incubated within Gruve and led by founder Tarun Raisoni alongside Swati Deshpande and Tanuj Mohan, the company has deconstructed the traditional data center model and rebuilt every layer for real-time AI, delivering distributed inference close to users and cloud providers with sub-20ms latency, cost efficiency, and built-in compliance. AI Fabrik is deploying five initial production sites with 6,000+ B300 GPUs launching in 2026, backed by Mayfield, Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures, and Cisco Investments.

companies.name: Buglance
companies.description: Buglance is a crowdsourced software testing platform that connects companies with a global community of more than 50,000 professional bug hunters to find defects and quality issues in mobile apps, games, e-commerce sites, and web platforms before release. Testers can be targeted by country, age, gender, and device type across a fleet of 10,000+ real devices, and detailed, validated, severity-classified bug reports are typically delivered in under 24 hours through live analytics dashboards. Buglance is a 500 Global portfolio company and markets to mobile gaming, e-commerce and retail, and lifestyle and productivity teams. It is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Cega
companies.description: Cega is a decentralized exotic derivatives protocol building on-chain structured products for investors: exotic options such as Fixed Coupon Notes (pure options and bond + options) and Dual Currency Swaps that generate yield with built-in downside protection. Cega is live on Ethereum Mainnet and Arbitrum One (EVM) and on Solana, and exposes its protocol to developers through first-party TypeScript SDKs on npm (@cega-fi) plus a GraphQL subgraph rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from its VC portfolio.

companies.name: CodeMentor
companies.description: CodeMentor (codementor.io) is an on-demand marketplace that connects software developers with vetted expert mentors for live 1:1 coding help, code review, debugging, pair programming, and longer-term freelance engagements across dozens of programming languages and frameworks. Part of the Arc / CodeMentor group, it serves individual learners seeking real-time mentorship as well as companies hiring vetted remote developers. As of this profile CodeMentor exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this record was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with verified identity and domain-security signals.

companies.name: FiberSense
companies.description: FiberSense is a distributed fiber optic sensing (DFOS / distributed acoustic sensing) company that turns existing and purpose-built fiber optic cables into dense arrays of vibration and acoustic sensors for real-time detection, localization and classification of objects and events across critical infrastructure. Its AI/ML algorithms filter noise and false alarms in dense urban, marine and underground environments, delivered as a subscription-based sensing platform rather than a public developer API. Product lines include DigitalAsset (critical infrastructure asset protection), DigitalCity (urban infrastructure and utility monitoring), DigitalMarine (subsea and marine cable route monitoring) and DigitalLeak (pipeline leak detection). Backed by Prosus Ventures; customer support runs through an Atlassian service desk portal.

companies.name: Forterra
companies.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

companies.name: Fuchsia
companies.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Howdy
companies.description: Howdy is a nearshore talent platform that connects US companies with senior software engineers, data, DevOps, design, and product professionals across Latin America. Operating as an employer of record (EOR), Howdy handles recruiting, vetting, payroll, benefits, equipment, compliance, and team performance coaching through physical "Howdy Houses" in cities across the region. Founded in 2018 in Austin, Texas by Jacqueline Samira and Frank Licea, the company went through Y Combinator (W21) and acquired the Brazilian recruiting platform GeekHunter in 2023. It is a services/staffing business with no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, agent-facing, and legal surface.

companies.name: Mint State Labs
companies.description: Mint State Labs (mintstatelabs.com, operating as Wildnet Edge) is an AI-first custom software development and IT outsourcing company delivering custom AI, machine learning, mobile, web, and cloud engineering services to enterprises and Fortune 500 clients. Its offerings span custom AI model and agent development, generative AI, ChatGPT app development, mobile and web app development, DevOps, data engineering, business intelligence, and staff augmentation ("build a team" / white-label) across a broad set of frameworks and platforms. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; the public presence is a marketing and services site with no first-party API product, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Miuros
