companies.description: Miuros is a performance platform for customer service that provides AI-powered analytics, quality assurance (Review & Insights), and agent-assist automation (Assist) for international and scaling customer support teams. Founded as a standalone startup and backed by Techstars, Miuros was acquired by Dixa and is now offered as Miuros by Dixa. The Miuros product surface — Data sync, Review & Insights, Assist, and Miuros APIs — remains operational and is tracked on a dedicated Miuros status page, while platform developer documentation is served through the Dixa developer hub.

companies.name: Quago Technologies LTD
companies.description: Quago Technologies is a gaming analytics and fraud-detection company that uses machine learning and mobile device sensor data to protect and optimize mobile games. Its platform analyzes in-game behavioral and device-sensor patterns - without collecting personally identifiable information - to detect and manage cheating, identify user-acquisition (CPA) fraud, predict player churn, and optimize monetization and lifetime value. Quago is delivered to mobile game studios as an embedded SDK plus a backend analytics service rather than a public developer API; it was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Betdex
companies.description: Betdex Labs is the team behind BetDEX, a decentralized sports betting exchange, and the Monaco Protocol — an open-source, permissionless liquidity and betting-exchange protocol built on the Solana blockchain. Rather than a traditional REST API, Betdex exposes an on-chain integration surface: Solana programs plus first-party TypeScript client libraries (@monaco-protocol/client and @monaco-protocol/admin-client on npm) that let developers create markets, place and match orders, and settle outcomes directly against the protocol. Developer resources are published at betdex.com/developers with source under the MonacoProtocol GitHub organization.

companies.name: Blocto
companies.description: Blocto is a Web3 smart-contract wallet built by Portto that lets everyday users interact with decentralized applications without managing seed phrases, using a chain-agnostic account-abstraction architecture. For developers, Blocto ships a client-side integration surface — the JavaScript Blocto SDK, a Blocto-flavored Flow Client Library (FCL) fork, plus Go, Swift and Rust SDKs — to connect dApps to the Blocto wallet for authentication, transaction signing and account-proof verification across Flow, Ethereum, Solana, Aptos, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Optimism. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its public developer documentation and GitHub organization.

companies.name: CodeSecure
companies.description: CodeSecure is an application security testing company whose CodeSonar static application security testing (SAST) engine performs deep whole-program analysis of C, C++, Java, and other languages to find bugs, security vulnerabilities, and coding-standard violations, and whose CodeSentry binary software composition analysis (SCA) tool generates SBOMs and detects vulnerabilities in third-party and binary components. CodeSecure merged with AdaCore in 2025, combining SAST and SCA tooling with high-integrity software development for aerospace, automotive, defense, medical, and industrial customers. The tools support SARIF, CWE, MISRA, CERT, and OWASP as well as safety standards such as ISO 26262, IEC 61508, EN 50128, and DO-178C, and integrate with CI/CD, IDE, and issue-tracking pipelines rather than exposing a public developer REST API.

companies.name: Mate Security
companies.description: Mate Security operates an AI-powered Security Operations Center (SOC) platform built on a "Security Context Graph." It learns an organization's unique security environment, tools, and procedures within 24 hours of integration, then runs a continuous detection and response (CD/CR) framework: AI agents automatically investigate, triage, and respond to alerts using organizational context, generate new detections from closed investigations, and support human-in-the-loop threat hunting across disparate security tools and data sources. Mate Security is backed by Insight Partners. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity and security posture.

companies.name: Photoneo
companies.description: Photoneo is a Slovak (Bratislava, founded 2013) machine-vision company and a global pioneer of high-resolution structured-light 3D measurement. Its flagship products are the PhoXi 3D Scanner family and the MotionCam-3D, a parallel structured-light camera that captures moving scenes in real-time 3D, together with AI-enabled software such as Bin Picking Studio, Locator, and Palletizing for robotic automation. Rather than a hosted web/REST API, Photoneo exposes a developer surface through the PhoXi Control software and its official C++, C#, and Python device APIs, GenICam/GigE Vision standard connectivity, TCP/IP robot interfaces (UR, ABB, FANUC, Staubli, Mitsubishi, Kawasaki, Yaskawa), and a set of BSD-licensed example repositories on GitHub. Documentation lives in the Photoneo Knowledge Base (docs.photoneo.com) and the 3D scanning wiki. Photoneo (now part of the Brightpick Group) was acquired by Zebra Technologies.

companies.name: Rakuten Mobile
companies.description: Rakuten Mobile is the Japanese mobile network operator (MNO) of Rakuten Group, headquartered in Setagaya, Tokyo, and Japan's fourth nationwide carrier alongside NTT Docomo, KDDI, and SoftBank. Commercially launched in April 2020 and surpassing 10 million subscribers in December 2025, Rakuten Mobile built and operates the world's first fully cloud-native, end-to-end virtualized mobile network on Open RAN, with 4G population coverage of 99.9% and expanding 5G plus 700 MHz Platinum Band rollout. The same engineering effort spun out into Rakuten Symphony, a B2B business that productizes the Rakuten Mobile playbook as the Symworld platform — a cloud-native operating platform for telcos covering Open RAN (CU/DU/RIC, Symware distributed unit appliance), Symworld Cloud (Kubernetes-based hyperconverged telco cloud / CNP), OSS/BSS, site management, and a marketplace of pre-integrated cloud-native network functions from 50+ vendor partners. Symphony also offers Rakuten CPaaS (carrier-grade SMS, Confirm/OTP, and Short URL APIs running on the Rakuten Mobile network with JWT-authenticated REST endpoints at api.cpaas.symphony.rakuten.net) and Rakuten Communications Platform (RCP) for enterprise private 5G. Public, developer-accessible APIs are concentrated in the CPaaS suite; the Symworld platform APIs themselves are TM Forum-aligned but exposed under commercial engagement rather than a public developer signup.

companies.name: Saber
companies.description: Saber is a decentralized automated market maker (AMM) on the Solana blockchain, optimized for trading and providing liquidity between mean-reverting assets such as stablecoins and wrapped or pegged tokens. Its StableSwap program delivers low-slippage swaps and capital-efficient liquidity pools. Saber does not expose a REST/HTTP API; developers integrate through its on-chain StableSwap program using first-party TypeScript SDKs (the @saberhq/* packages on npm) and Rust crates (crates.io) that construct and submit Solana transactions. The project also maintains open-source Solana tooling, an asset/pool registry, and on-chain governance. Saber was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital.

companies.name: Sensors Data
companies.description: Sensors Data (神策数据) is a customer data analytics and CDP (Customer Data Platform) company. Its platform unifies customer data across channels into real-time customer profiles and provides product analytics, user profiling, marketing and ad attribution, A/B testing, and smart-operations tooling. Sensors Data processes 250+ billion data points daily, ships 50+ data-collection SDKs across web, mobile, mini-program and server-side languages, and serves 2,000+ enterprise customers with both cloud and on-premise deployment. An OpenAPI is exposed for ecosystem integration.

companies.name: Level AI
companies.description: Level AI (legally Ujwal Inc.) is a Mountain View, California contact center AI company founded in 2019 by Ashish Nagar, a former member of Amazon's Alexa conversational AI team. The company builds LLM-native customer experience intelligence and service automation for enterprise contact centers, with a platform spanning two product surfaces: a CX Delivery suite (AI Virtual Agent, Agent Assist, AgentGPT, Coaching, Manager Assist, Knowledge Bot, Auto Summary, Agent Screen Recording) and a CX Strategy suite (Auto-QA on 100% of interactions, Voice of the Customer theme detection, omnichannel Analytics, iCSAT, AI Workers). The proprietary full-stack AI platform includes Level AI's own ASR/Voice AI and semantic-intelligence layer trained on customer-service data, and is positioned for financial services, insurance, healthcare, retail, banking, and collections operations. Level AI exposes a public REST API for bidirectional data exchange with BI tools and existing contact center stacks, and ships native integrations across telephony, CRM, customer support, workforce management, CX management, communication, learning management, and SSO categories. The company has raised $73.1M to date (Series A 2021, Series B 2022 led by Battery Ventures, Series C $39.4M 2024 led by Adams Street Partners with Cross Creek, Brightloop, Battery Ventures and Eniac Ventures), holds a 4.7/5 rating on G2, and reports customer outcomes including 25% CSAT lift, 45% agent satisfaction improvement, and 90% time savings on manual QA. The Level AI GitHub organization (github.com/Level-AI) exists but is currently empty — there is no public OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source release; the API is documented and credentialed through the customer's tenant of the Level AI platform.

companies.name: Oriient
companies.description: Oriient provides software-only, hardware-free indoor positioning ("indoor GPS") and navigation delivered as a SaaS SDK. Its geomagnetic technology reaches roughly 1-meter (3-foot) accuracy indoors without Wi-Fi, beacons, or installed infrastructure, powering product finding, order picking, visitor navigation, asset tracking, and in-store analytics for retail, grocery, and smart-building customers across thousands of locations. Oriient New Media Ltd is based in Tel Aviv and is a Techstars portfolio company. Oriient ships first-party mobile SDKs (including a React-Native Product Location AI package on npm) rather than a public REST API; integration is gated behind a customer dashboard and sales.

companies.name: Relay.app
companies.description: Relay.app was a workflow automation platform (an AI-assisted alternative to Zapier and Make) that let teams build and run automated, multi-step workflows connecting external SaaS applications, with human-in-the-loop approval steps and AI actions embedded in the automation flow. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of 2026 the product has been discontinued: free users lost access on 2026-08-15 and paying customers on 2026-09-14, with the site now serving a shutdown notice and a data-export path only. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook reference are published for the platform.

companies.name: Aivar
companies.description: Aivar Innovations is an enterprise AI consulting and development firm that helps regulated and large organizations move agentic AI systems from pilot to scaled production. Alongside strategic AI consulting, custom AI development, managed AI/ML operations, data services, and cloud transformation, Aivar ships three accelerators: Convogent AI (autonomous voice and conversational agents in 16+ languages with sub-500ms latency), Velogent AI (governed agentic process automation for regulated industries), and Kubogent AI (enterprise AI infrastructure on Kubernetes). The company operates a professional-services model and does not currently publish a public, self-service API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Aptos Orbital
companies.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

companies.name: Customer Analytics
companies.description: Customer Analytics (CA) is a data, analytics and AI consultancy headquartered in Middleton, Wisconsin with a delivery centre in Guindy, Chennai, India. The firm delivers AI/ML and data analytics, data engineering, business intelligence and reporting, business solutions design and software development, platform implementation and software management (Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce), and quality assurance. Alongside these services it packages six productised offerings — DataWorks 360, BI Xpert 360, AI Assist 360, Retail AI Insights 360, PBILens 360 and Smart IoT Data Track 360 — and publishes case studies across healthcare, manufacturing, retail/B2B, education, agriculture, clinical research, warehouse operations, the art industry and government. Customer Analytics is a professional services company: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

companies.name: Jenkins Pipeline
companies.description: Jenkins Pipeline is a suite of plugins for the Jenkins automation server that supports implementing and integrating continuous delivery pipelines as code. It provides an extensible domain-specific language (DSL) with two syntax styles - Declarative and Scripted - and core building blocks (agents, stages, steps) for modeling simple-to-complex CI/CD workflows that are versioned with application source code via a Jenkinsfile.

companies.name: Silk Labs
companies.description: Silk Labs was an on-device artificial intelligence startup founded in 2015 by former Mozilla CTO Andreas Gal together with Chris Jones and Michael Vines, a team drawn from Mozilla's Firefox OS effort. The company's open-source Silk platform layered a Node.js runtime on Android so developers could build Internet of Things applications entirely in JavaScript, and it later shipped work on the "Sense" AI home camera focused on running real-time visual and audio recognition directly on the device. Silk Labs was backed by investors including 500 Global and was acquired by Apple in November 2018, after which it ceased independent operations; the silklabs.com domain is now parked on Apple nameservers. Its open-source Silk code, GitHub organization, and npm packages remain publicly available and are captured in this profile.

companies.name: Command Zero
companies.description: Command Zero, Inc. is an autonomous and AI-assisted security operations center (SOC) platform for enterprise security investigations. Founded in 2023, it applies "Governed AI" and a question-based investigation method to run complete investigations across identity, endpoint, email, cloud, and SaaS data sources — from initial alert through verdict — with every agent step logged, visible, auditable, and reproducible. Rather than a SOAR, SIEM, or XDR, it connects read-only to existing data sources via a federated data model (no ingestion, no data migration) and runs Tier-1 through Tier-3 triage, breach, phishing, malware, identity, insider-threat, incident-response, and threat-hunting workflows. The company reports 500K+ investigations completed, a 90% reduction in Tier-1 escalations, and 40%+ efficiency gains, and holds SOC 2 Type II. Command Zero is a portfolio company of a16z and Insight Partners; this profile was enriched from the provider's public website and llms.txt.

companies.name: Easypanel
companies.description: Easypanel is a modern, self-hosted server control panel powered by Docker and Docker Swarm that simplifies application deployment, database provisioning, and server management through an intuitive web interface. Operators can deploy applications from GitHub repositories using Heroku Buildpacks (Node.js, Ruby, Python, PHP, Go, Java), custom Dockerfiles, or Cloud Native Buildpacks; provision managed services for MySQL, MariaDB, Postgres, MongoDB, and Redis based on official Docker images; and launch 1-click templates from a community library of 100+ applications including WordPress, Ghost, Strapi, Directus, Appsmith, Appwrite, n8n, Activepieces, Anything-LLM, and AdGuard Home. The platform automates Let's Encrypt SSL certificate provisioning, supports zero-downtime deployments, exposes in-browser terminal, database CLI, and log inspection tools, and provides database backup automation. Easypanel is available as a one-click install on DigitalOcean, AWS, Vultr, Linode, Hostinger, and Kamatera marketplaces, or via manual Docker install on any Linux VPS. Commercial plans range from a generous Free tier through Hobby, Growth, and Business tiers with multi-user access control, white-labeling, and clustering. Easypanel exposes a web UI, a Hub for shared templates, and the Dockerizer tool, but does not currently publish a public REST API or first-party developer SDK for programmatic panel control.

companies.name: GraphQL Inspector
companies.description: Schema change detection and validation tooling that checks for breaking changes, deprecated fields, and coverage gaps between GraphQL schema versions, available as CLI, CI, and GitHub Action.

companies.name: Witness AI
companies.description: WitnessAI is an AI security and governance platform that lets enterprises safely deploy and manage AI across their workforce. Its platform spans three pillars: Observe (visibility into all AI activity, shadow-AI discovery, and cataloging of applications and agents), Control (governance policies, audit trails, and compliance across human and AI workforces), and Protect (runtime security that blocks prompt injection and jailbreaks and filters harmful outputs). It addresses data leakage, prompt-injection attacks, unauthorized agent activity, and compliance gaps. The company is backed by GV. As of this profile no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published; engagement is via sales/demo.

companies.name: Buildcheck
companies.description: Buildcheck is a Sweden-based cloud software platform that simplifies self-inspections and quality checklists for construction and infrastructure projects. The service uses AI to automatically generate project-specific inspection and control plans from uploaded building documents, then lets field teams document work on a mobile app with photo capture and digital signatures, share progress with clients through shareable links, and export organized PDF reports. It offers company-branded templates, role-based access, SSO and other enterprise features. Buildcheck was founded by Anders Jacobson (previously Next One Technology) and Johnny Wulcan (founder of Byggplanen). It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API or API documentation has been found on its site as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Scoutzie
companies.description: Scoutzie is a Y Combinator-founded company (2012) led by Kirill Zubovsky. It launched as a curated marketplace connecting startups with top mobile designers and developers, operating from 2012 to 2020, and has since transformed into an AI-powered MVP (minimum viable product) development agency that builds and ships startup products in roughly two weeks. Today Scoutzie sells product-development services, an MVP Agent, founder training, and SEO consulting rather than a public developer API. It was surfaced through the a16z portfolio graph and enriched here as an API Evangelist network company profile.

companies.name: Cotool
companies.description: Cotool is an AI platform for the defensive security "blue team" — AI agents that scale detection, response, and threat hunting across an organization's security stack. Its three products, Detect, Respond, and Hunt, let teams author detections from natural-language descriptions, automate alert response and playbook execution with human-in-the-loop controls, and monitor threat intelligence for relevance and coverage gaps. Cotool's stated mission is to "scale defensive security with tokens," giving defenders machine-speed operational advantages instead of being limited by headcount, improving coverage and cutting mean-time-to-respond (MTTR). Cotool is a San Francisco company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, WndrCo, and Homebrew. As of this profile it publishes a product and marketing site only — no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or MCP server was found.

companies.name: Suplari
companies.description: Suplari is an enterprise procurement intelligence platform that goes beyond spend analytics, using AI to clean, classify, and unify fragmented spend data across ERP, P2P, and spreadsheet sources. It delivers spend analytics, value orchestration, savings tracking, contract intelligence, and ESG intelligence, alongside procurement-specific AI agents (Suplari Worker, Assistant, and AI Studio) that integrate with SAP, Oracle, Workday, Coupa, Databricks, Snowflake, and Microsoft. Suplari was acquired by Microsoft in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: Blitzy
companies.description: Blitzy is an autonomous software development platform for enterprises with large legacy codebases. It reverse-engineers existing code into a knowledge graph, then orchestrates thousands of AI agents to modernize software and build new applications at the scale of 1 million to over 100 million lines of code, autonomously completing roughly 80% of a project before human engineers review and approve the result. Rather than training its own foundation models, Blitzy composes leading third-party models (Gemini, GPT, Claude). Founded by Brian Elliott (CEO) and Sid Pardeshi (CTO), the company is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts with an office in Pune, India, and is backed by Northzone.

companies.name: Raspire
companies.description: Raspire (RASPIRE) provides runtime security for mobile applications, positioning itself as the first line of defense for Android and iOS apps against AI-powered fraud attacks, API abuse, and runtime threats. Developers upload compiled apps (APK/IPA) and Raspire automatically hardens them with anti-fraud protection, app integrity verification, reverse-engineering prevention, and API protection, without requiring changes to application source code. The platform gives security teams real-time visibility into threats and blocks attacks in real time, and can integrate with existing SIEM systems and application monitoring platforms as part of a CI/CD pipeline. Raspire is a Y Combinator company. As surfaced to the API Evangelist network it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

companies.name: Mangata Finance
companies.description: Mangata Finance (Mangata X, since rebranded GASP) is a decentralized exchange built as a Substrate parachain in the Polkadot and Kusama ecosystem. It is designed for algorithmic traders and DeFi frontends, offering gas-free swaps, an omnichain ZK-rollup architecture, and a Proof-of-Liquidity consensus model where liquidity providers help secure the network. There is no REST or OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through a TypeScript SDK (@mangata-finance/sdk) that communicates with the Mangata Substrate node over Polkadot.js JSON-RPC/WebSocket, with published type-definition packages and open-source node, bridge, and dev-kit repositories under the gasp-xyz GitHub organization.

companies.name: Zebec Network
companies.description: Zebec Network is a blockchain infrastructure company (founded 2021, San Francisco; founder Sam Thapaliya) building real-time payroll, on-chain payments, multi-chain debit/crypto cards, and treasury management for web3 businesses and individuals. Its continuous-settlement streaming protocol began on Solana and now spans EVM chains, NEAR, and BNB via a Wormhole-based cross-chain bridge. Zebec exposes its capabilities to developers as a family of first-party TypeScript/JavaScript SDKs published on npm under the @zebec-network, @zebec-protocol, and @zebec-fintech scopes — covering payroll streaming, the vault, staking, the Silver/instant cards, the bridge, and the Solana DAO — documented at docs.zebec.io. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Kony
companies.description: Kony was a U.S. digital banking and low-code application platform company, best known for the Kony Quantum multiexperience development platform and the Kony DBX digital banking suite. Temenos acquired Kony and folded the digital banking business into Temenos Infinity and the Quantum platform into Temenos Quantum; non-banking Kony Quantum customers were transitioned to HCL Volt MX, managed by HCL Software. Kony no longer operates an independent developer program or public API. The kony.com apex and www hosts now redirect to the Temenos "Kony is now Temenos" announcement, docs.kony.com resolves to the Temenos Base Camp Quantum documentation, and only the authenticated Quantum Fabric Console at manage.kony.com is still served on the Kony domain. This profile is retained as an acquisition record pointing at its successors rather than as a live API provider.

companies.name: Rookout
companies.description: Rookout is a live application debugging platform founded in 2017 in Tel Aviv, Israel that lets developers set non-breaking breakpoints in running production, staging, and development applications to capture full-stack debug data — variables, stack traces, logs, and metrics — without redeploying, restarting, or stopping services. Rookout pioneered the "live debugger" category for cloud-native and Kubernetes-hosted applications and shipped language agents/SDKs for Python, Java/JVM, Node.js, .NET, Go, and Ruby that attach to running processes and stream snapshots back to the Rookout web IDE or developer's IDE. Dynatrace announced its acquisition of Rookout on July 31, 2023 and closed the deal in Q2 of Dynatrace's fiscal year ending September 30, 2023. The standalone Rookout product has since been folded into the Dynatrace platform as the Dynatrace Live Debugger (and Live Logger), and the rookout.com and docs.rookout.com domains now redirect to dynatrace.com. There is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, webhook catalog, or CLI for Rookout — the developer surface consists entirely of language agents, deployment integration examples, IDE extensions, and the Explorook desktop helper that exposes local source folders to the Rookout web debugger. The Rookout GitHub organization remains public and continues to maintain those agents, tutorials, and integration samples under Apache-2.0.

companies.name: Affirmed Networks
companies.description: Affirmed Networks is a mobile networking company founded in 2010 (Andover, Massachusetts) that pioneered fully virtualized, cloud-native mobile core software for service providers. Its portfolio spanned a Virtualized Evolved Packet Core (vEPC), the UnityCloud 5G Core, Private Network Service, Network Slicing, and service-automation/analytics tooling, deployed by 100+ mobile operators including AT&T, Orange, Vodafone, and Telus. The company was acquired by Microsoft in March 2020 and folded into the Azure for Operators initiative; the affirmednetworks.com site now operates as a Microsoft company marketing presence with no independent public developer portal or API. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners.

companies.name: Voya
companies.description: Voya GmbH is a software development and consulting company based in Hamburg, Germany, with nearshore TechHubs in Bucharest and Cluj, Romania. Founded in 2015 as an AI-powered chat-based business-travel booking platform backed by 500 Global, it became a wholly-owned Volkswagen Group subsidiary and has been an independent, founder-led company again since November 2024. Today Voya delivers end-to-end software development, applied AI solutions, and engineering team building for automotive, mobility, and travel clients including Volkswagen, Audi, CARIAD, Deutsche Bahn, and Lufthansa City Center. TISAX certified. Voya publishes no public API or developer portal.

companies.name: Alinia Ai
companies.description: Alinia is an AI compliance and control platform that helps enterprises deploy large language models and AI agents safely and in compliance with regulations, making AI systems "compliant by design" through regulation-informed control layers. The platform is built around three products: an Evaluation Engine that tests AI systems against company policies and regulatory standards (compliance red teaming), Guardrails that enforce compliance in real time — including a proprietary multilingual RAG Guard model that blocks hallucinations and irrelevance — and Monitoring that provides automated auditing, full traceability, and compliance reporting of AI activity. Alinia is model-agnostic and multilingual, targeting financial services, healthcare, and other heavily regulated industries, with named customers including Banco Santander and Origin Financial. The company was co-founded by Ariadna (CEO, previously Head of ML Platform at Twitter and Director of Development at IBM Watson) and Carlos (COO, previously AI Counsel at Hugging Face), operates offices in Barcelona, Valencia, New York, and Pittsburgh, and is backed by Speedinvest. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published.

companies.name: card.io
companies.description: card.io was a mobile SDK company that provided fast, easy credit-card scanning inside iOS and Android apps using the device camera, letting users capture card details by holding a card up to the lens instead of typing them. Founded around 2011 and backed by Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC), card.io was acquired by PayPal in 2012. Its scanning SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native were open-sourced in December 2014 under the card-io GitHub organization, and the product was ultimately discontinued. The company operated no public REST or web API; its product surface was a set of client-side mobile SDKs, all of which are now archived. This profile is maintained for network completeness and historical/portfolio context.

companies.name: houmo
companies.description: HOUMO.AI (后摩智能) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 that develops compute-in-memory (CIM / storage-and-computation integrated) edge AI chips for running large language models and other AI workloads on endpoint devices. Its products include the MOMAGIC (H30) series processors, LIQING M.2 modules, and Limou (LM 5050 / LM 5070 / LM 30) AI acceleration cards, paired with the Houmo Avenue software toolchain (PyTorch / TensorFlow / ONNX, CUDA-style front end) for model quantization, compilation, and deployment. The company targets edge inference, autonomous driving, embodied robotics, and intelligent mobile devices, and runs a developer community with documentation and downloads. This profile is a hardware / AI-chip vendor with a developer toolchain rather than a public web API provider; no REST/OpenAPI, OAuth, or hosted API surface was found.

companies.name: SST
companies.description: SST is an open source TypeScript framework for building full-stack applications on your own infrastructure. Originally known as Serverless Stack, it now ships as a single `sst.config.ts` file that uses Pulumi and Terraform providers under the hood to deploy components across AWS, Cloudflare, and 150+ other providers. SST covers Lambda functions, containers, queues, buckets, databases, cron jobs, and front-end frameworks like Next.js, Remix, Astro, and SvelteKit, with resource linking that wires components together without hardcoded ARNs. SST Console adds a hosted dashboard for logs, issues, deployments, and autodeploy from Git.

companies.name: Visual Studio Code
companies.description: Visual Studio Code is a free, open-source, cross-platform code editor developed by Microsoft for Windows, Linux, macOS, and the web, built on the MIT-licensed Code - OSS project and distinguished by features such as IntelliSense, debugging, integrated Git, and a marketplace with tens of thousands of extensions. VS Code is not a SaaS REST API; instead, developers extend the editor through the Extension API, a TypeScript / JavaScript programmatic interface that exposes nearly every aspect of the editor for customization. This index points to the Extension API documentation and surrounding developer resources.

companies.name: Bestow
companies.description: Bestow is a Dallas, Texas life insurance technology company building a unified SaaS platform for life insurance carriers, agents, and embedded partners. Founded in 2016, Bestow provides end-to-end and modular solutions across new business and policy administration, including a digital Application Suite for quote, illustration, and application journeys; an Underwriting engine and workbench with instant, fully automated decisioning powered by machine learning on actuarial data; an Agent Portal and sales management tooling; an Admin Portal and Customer Portal for self-service; TPA (Third-Party Administrator) services; a Performance IQ analytics surface; and a Data Optimization Suite for modeling, integrations, and activation. Bestow's Protect API and associated SDK power embedded life insurance — letting fintechs, banks, financial institutions, P&C carriers, mortgage platforms, and benefits providers offer instant term life, final expense, and IUL coverage inside their own apps and websites, with Bestow handling underwriting, payment, billing, policy delivery, and ongoing administration behind the scenes. Integrations span ACORD life and annuities data standards, Adyen for payments, Cloudflare for identity and security, and data vendors including Bevel, Clareto, EIS, ExamOne, and Human API ReFlex Select. There is no publicly accessible developer portal or API reference — partner documentation, sandbox access, and Protect API onboarding are gated behind a partner login at docs.bestow.com and arranged through Bestow's sales and partnerships team.

companies.name: Code Metal
companies.description: Code Metal is a Boston-based AI company building a verifiable code translation and optimization platform for mission-critical, edge, and regulated industries including defense, automotive, semiconductor, robotics, and aerospace. The platform ingests high-level research and prototype code (Python, MATLAB, Julia) and produces optimized, edge-ready low-level code across C/C++, Rust, VHDL, Verilog, CUDA, HIP, and ONNX, using a divide-and-conquer pipeline that instruments and tests, translates and verifies functional equivalence, then optimizes and benchmarks against target CPU/GPU/FPGA runtimes. Code Metal was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or specification surface; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

companies.name: domob
companies.description: Domob (多盟) is a Beijing-based mobile intelligent marketing and advertising technology company founded in September 2010, positioned as one of China's early smartphone advertising DSP and mobile ad-network platforms. It provides data-technology and content services spanning programmatic buying (DSP), the UGdesk user-growth platform, the BidMaster preferred buying platform, and the BlueNova traffic-monetization platform, alongside agency and short-video services partnered with ByteDance, Tencent, Kuaishou, Microsoft Advertising and Xiaohongshu. For developers and app publishers, Domob distributes first-party iOS and Android ad SDKs (banner, interstitial, splash, native and offerwall formats) plus Unity3D and Cocos2d-x game-engine plugins via its Domob-SDK GitHub organization; publishers obtain a Publisher ID and Placement ID from the Domob platform to monetize apps. In 2025 the Domob SDK passed CAICT dual-end (iOS/Android) security certification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched from public sources.

companies.name: PokéAPI GraphQL
companies.description: GraphQL beta endpoint for PokéAPI providing Hasura-powered queries over the complete Pokémon database including species, moves, abilities, items, evolutions, and game version data.

companies.name: Text'nPayMe
companies.description: Text'nPayMe is an award-winning B2B fintech company, established in Armenia and incorporated in the USA in 2022, that builds embedded payment solutions for banks, fintechs, telecoms, and online shops. Its two core products are a Payment Keyboard SDK, which embeds send-money transactions directly inside 150+ messaging, social, and gaming apps via a payment keyboard for iOS, Android, and a Chrome extension, and a Payment Gateway Hub for transaction routing, reconciliation, and reporting. The company markets an "Apex Security Layer" with proprietary encryption and risk management, supports cross-border payments, and joined the 500 Global accelerator after winning the Entrepreneurship World Cup 2022 National Finals. The SDK is delivered to enterprise customers through direct integration engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal, so no public API specification, developer documentation, or client packages are currently published.

companies.name: ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md
companies.description: ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md is a standardized file convention used in open source repositories to credit third-party software, libraries, inspirations, and other works that a project builds upon or is indebted to. It is a common practice for documenting attribution and provenance, complementing LICENSE, README, CONTRIBUTING, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT files as part of a healthy open source project structure. The file typically lists dependencies, their copyright holders, and the licenses under which they are distributed.

companies.name: Canary
companies.description: Canary is an AI QA engineer that reads your source code to understand developer intent. Push a pull request and Canary reads the diff, understands the intent, and runs feature and regression tests against your preview app across real browsers, catching broken auth flows, slow page loads, and failing checkouts before they reach production. Built by ex-Google, Windsurf, and Cognition engineers, Canary is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company positioned as the validation layer for AI-generated code.

companies.name: Prewitt Ridge
companies.description: Prewitt Ridge builds SysGit, "the collaboration layer for complex hardware" — an enterprise platform that applies software development practices to systems engineering. SysGit provides Git-based version control for requirements and system models, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) workflows, AI-assisted systems engineering automation, and SysMLv2 compliance for open-standards adherence. The platform targets defense and aerospace teams, with customers including the US Air Force, GTRI, Leidos, and Anduril. Prewitt Ridge is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or .well-known documents.

companies.name: Swytchcode
companies.description: Deterministic API-execution layer for AI agents and developers that sits between an agent and production APIs, handling auth, retries, idempotency, and policy control across 2,000+ APIs. Consumable via a public npm-installable CLI and a local MCP server, with a published llms.txt.

companies.name: Rally Network
companies.description: Rally Network (RLY Protocol, stewarded by the RLY Network Association) is a permissionless, open-source, multi-chain web3 mobile toolkit for developers. It provides natively embedded, self-custodial wallets and gasless (gas station / ERC-2771 relayer) transactions so mobile apps can let users create wallets, transfer tokens, claim NFTs, and deploy or call smart contracts without handling gas or seed phrases. The toolkit ships as first-party SDKs for React Native/Expo, Flutter, and Unity plus TypeScript libraries and a hosted dashboard for API keys and configuration. Rally Network is the successor to the original rally.io social-token platform (creator coins), which decentralized in 2021 and wound down its consumer sidechain in early 2023; the RLY Network Association now maintains the open protocol and developer tooling.

companies.name: Armory.io
companies.description: Armory.io was an enterprise continuous delivery and continuous deployment company built around the open-source Spinnaker project. Its products included Armory Continuous Deployment Self-Hosted and Managed (an enterprise Spinnaker distribution), Armory Continuous Deployment-as-a-Service (CDaaS) with a declarative GitOps deployment experience, and the Armory Scale Agent for Spinnaker and Kubernetes. Armory was backed by Insight Partners and was later acquired by Harness; the armory.io website now 301-redirects to harness.io and the CDaaS cloud service, developer portal, and status page are decommissioned, while the documentation site (docs.armory.io) and the Apache-2.0 GitHub organization (github.com/armory) remain live.

companies.name: Atmosplay
companies.description: Atmosplay was a mobile advertising technology company, founded in 2014 in Budapest, Hungary, that built interactive 3D "playable" ads and an ad-monetization platform for mobile game publishers. Its ATMIQ cloud gameplay engine let users try a game inside an ad without installing it, and its self-serve builder produced playable creatives for 3D and action games. Atmosplay shipped first-party mobile SDKs (Unity, iOS, Android) plus AdMob and MoPub mediation adapters for publishers to integrate interstitial, banner, and rewarded-video formats. Speedinvest led its Series A in 2016; the company was acquired by ZPLAY Information Technology on 2018-01-01. Its websites (atmosplay.com / atmosplay.net) are no longer operational; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization of SDK and adapter repositories. This profile is maintained for network completeness as an acquired/inactive portfolio lead.

companies.name: AVI Networks
companies.description: AVI Networks builds a software-defined application delivery platform - the Avi Vantage Platform / Avi Load Balancer - providing multi-cloud load balancing, web application firewall (WAF), GSLB, container ingress, and analytics driven by a central Avi Controller with a fully programmable REST API. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, AVI Networks was acquired by VMware in 2019 and the product is now offered by Broadcom as the VMware Avi Load Balancer. The controller exposes a comprehensive REST API with first-party Python, Go, and Java SDKs, a Terraform provider, and Ansible automation for intent-based, self-service application services across VMware, AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, and bare-metal environments.

companies.name: convergence
companies.description: Convergence AI was a London-based artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2024 by Marvin Purtorab (CEO) and Andy Toulis (CTO) building Proxy, a personal AI agent designed to complete open-ended administrative and web-browsing tasks across domains. Its approach centered on long-term memory and continual learning via a new class of models it called Large Meta Learning Models (LMLM). Convergence raised a $12M pre-seed led by Balderton Capital with participation from Salesforce Ventures and Shopify Ventures, and was acquired by Salesforce in May 2025 to strengthen Agentforce. Its lasting public surface is the convergence-ai GitHub organization, which open-sourced proxy-lite (a mini open-weights web-browsing agent), the proxy-lite-3b vision-language model on Hugging Face, the LM2 memory-model paper repo, and the WebGames agent benchmark.

companies.name: eBPF
companies.description: eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) is a technology that allows programs to run in a sandboxed virtual machine within the Linux kernel without changing kernel source code or loading kernel modules. It enables high-performance networking, security monitoring, observability, and tracing capabilities at the operating system level with minimal overhead. eBPF is governed as a standard by the eBPF Foundation under the Linux Foundation.

companies.name: Granulate
companies.description: Granulate is a real-time continuous optimization company acquired by Intel in 2022 and now offered as Intel Tiber App-Level Optimization. Its platform autonomously tunes OS-level and runtime behavior (scheduling, memory, networking) for compute, Kubernetes, and big-data workloads to cut CPU cost and latency without code changes. Granulate also maintains gProfiler, an open-source, low-overhead, system-wide continuous profiler that combines multiple sampling profilers (perf, py-spy, async-profiler, rbspy, PHP/.NET/Node.js) into a single flamegraph and optionally uploads results to the Granulate Performance Studio. gProfiler ships as an Apache-2.0 agent (github.com/intel/gprofiler), a self-hosted backend/UI (github.com/intel/gprofiler-performance-studio), a Docker image, and cloud-marketplace images. The former granulate.io developer surface now redirects to intel.com.

companies.name: Sound.xyz
companies.description: Sound.xyz was a web3 music platform and suite of on-chain tools that let artists release music as digital collectibles and host listening parties for new releases, building direct economic relationships with their communities. The consumer platform went offline on 2026-01-16 (with a successor project, Vault.fm), but Sound.xyz's first-party developer surface remains publicly published: the open-source Sound protocol (a permissionless Solidity smart-contract framework for music collectibles) and the official @soundxyz npm SDK ecosystem (@soundxyz/sdk, sdk-viem, legacy-sdk) for on-chain development, alongside GraphQL and caching infrastructure libraries. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; this profile now reflects the enrichment pipeline's findings.

companies.name: Weaveworks
companies.description: Weaveworks was the cloud-native company that coined the term "GitOps" and built the Weave family of open-source infrastructure tooling — Weave Net (multi-host container networking), Weave Scope (Docker/Kubernetes visualization and monitoring), Weave GitOps, and the widely used eksctl CLI for Amazon EKS. Backed by Accel and GV, the company ceased commercial operations in February 2024 after a planned acquisition fell through. It shipped no hosted REST API or client SDKs; its public surface was open-source Go tooling. Following the shutdown, Flux CD moved to the CNCF (graduated), eksctl transferred to the eksctl-io org jointly maintained with AWS, and the remaining Weave repositories became community-driven under the github.com/weaveworks organization. The former company website (weave.works) has lapsed and now redirects to a parked page.

companies.name: Salus
companies.description: Salus provides runtime validation and governance for AI agents. It sits between an agent and its tools as a policy-aware proxy that intercepts each action before it executes, then clarifies, rewrites, escalates for human review, or blocks it against organizational policies — managing commit-time risk on financial transfers, appointment changes, and data modifications before they alter customer data, finances, or records. Integration requires only an endpoint URL change (no agent rewrite), and Salus works across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, Retell, Vapi, and custom tools. Capabilities include evidence-based validation, PII detection, budget and loop protection, idempotency checks, human-in-the-loop escalation, self-repair of blocked actions, and integrated evals and observability. Salus is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco.

companies.name: AutoGen Studio
companies.description: AutoGen Studio is a low-code / no-code developer GUI from Microsoft Research for rapidly prototyping, composing, and debugging multi-agent AI workflows built on the AutoGen framework. Shipped as the `autogenstudio` Python package and launched with `autogenstudio ui`, it serves a FastAPI + React (Gatsby) web app on localhost that exposes four primary interfaces — Team Builder, Playground, Gallery, and Deployment — backed by a SQLModel persistence layer (SQLite by default; any SQLAlchemy-compatible backend such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL via `--database-uri`). The Team Builder offers drag-and-drop and JSON authoring of teams, agents, models, tools, and termination conditions fully aligned with AutoGen AgentChat's declarative component spec; the Playground streams live inter-agent messages and renders the control transition graph; the Gallery imports community components; and the Deployment view exports a team to Python, exposes it as an endpoint, and packages it for Docker. AutoGen Studio is built on AutoGen AgentChat / Core / Extensions and supports any OpenAI-compatible model endpoint (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, local vLLM/Ollama, etc.) via declarative `model_client` configuration, plus MCP tool integration. Authentication is experimental (GitHub OAuth + JWT only). Microsoft explicitly positions AutoGen Studio as a research prototype — not production-ready — and encourages teams that need authn/z, multi-tenancy, sandboxing rigor, or hardened deployment to build directly on the AutoGen framework instead. Companion to the broader AutoGen multi-agent framework, distributed under the Microsoft microsoft/autogen monorepo (CC-BY-4.0 docs, MIT code).

companies.name: Captain's Eye
companies.description: Captain's Eye is a Haifa, Israel-based maritime AI company (founded 2020 by Uri Ben Dor and Doron Oizerovich, backed by Techstars) that delivers real-time video analytics software for maritime and industrial safety. Its SaaS platform connects to existing CCTV cameras, radar, and thermal sensors aboard merchant vessels, yachts, cruise ships, ports, and on-land petrochemical and energy sites, applying custom neural networks and commercial AI models to detect fires, smoke, leaks, sea pollution, missing protective gear, unauthorized access, and equipment failures. It provides real-time alerts, remote monitoring, incident documentation, and operational data collection, monitoring 5,000+ cameras and having detected 100,000+ events. Access is delivered through a private web application and mobile apps rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: Chemix
companies.description: Chemix is an artificial-intelligence company building an end-to-end, AI-enabled power system for batteries, organized around the themes of power safety, observability, and predictability. Based in Sunnyvale, California, the company applies generative and machine-learning techniques to make battery behavior more transparent and predictable across the battery lifecycle. Chemix is a Mayfield-backed portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this profile the company is pre-launch ("more product details coming soon") and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; this record captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture only.

companies.name: Chronicle Labs
companies.description: Chronicle Labs is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) company building infrastructure for teams running AI agents in production. The platform turns production data into staging environments: it reconstructs real end-to-end workflows from production data streams, generates test scenarios from those workflows, runs agents against replicated production environments (its Backtest Arena), and monitors live agents with autonomous fix and rollback. The pitch is to help engineering teams prove their AI agents work before they ship, replacing hand-built evals and "vibe-deploying" with backtesting against a team's actual operational reality. Typical customers run AI agents in customer service, payments, refunds, and other high-stakes workflows, and Chronicle Labs reports integrating with 100+ production tools. Founded in San Francisco by Ayman Saleh (CEO) and Rowan Zyadeh. At profiling time the product is accessed via a hosted web application behind sign-up; there is no public API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK, and the company publishes an llms.txt at its primary host.

companies.name: Osly
companies.description: Osly is an AI workflow automation platform (a product of Alore AI) that lets startups and prosumers build N8N-based AI workflows from natural language, with no coding required. Users describe automations in plain English to generate email sequences, lead categorization and personalized outreach, spin up internal dashboard UIs, and connect 50+ apps including HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Drive, Notion, LinkedIn and Shopify. Osly was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a marketing site and a hosted application, but no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Auradine (Velaura AI)
companies.description: Auradine, Inc. is a Silicon Valley semiconductor and infrastructure company founded in 2022, in 2026 rebranded as Velaura AI, Inc. The company designs ultra-low-power compute solutions for data center, edge, and physical AI applications, anchored by its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform that reduces the power required for AI compute while maintaining performance. Its Teraflux product line delivers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware (3nm ASICs, air- and hydro-cooled miners, containers, and fleet management software) deployed by leading Bitcoin data center operators. Auradine raised over $300 million across its funding rounds, including a $153M Series C, and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Auradine/Velaura AI publishes no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Biren Technology
companies.description: Biren Technology (Shanghai Biren Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company that designs general-purpose GPUs (GPGPUs) for AI training, inference, and high-performance computing. Its flagship BR100-series accelerators are programmed through BIRENSUPA, a CUDA-like software platform that bundles the BRCC compiler, a hardware abstraction layer, deep-learning and general-compute acceleration libraries, and a developer toolchain with support for PyTorch, TensorFlow, and PaddlePaddle. Biren distributes its drivers, SDK, and documentation through its developer.birentech.com developer community rather than a public web/REST API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

companies.name: Cron Systems
companies.description: Cron Systems (now operating as Cron AI) builds deep-learning perception software for 3D sensor and LiDAR data. Its flagship platform, senseEDGE, performs real-time 3D object detection, classification, and tracking from point-cloud data at the edge, with multi-sensor fusion and adverse-weather resilience. The technology serves intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, autonomous mobility, smart cities, and security and surveillance — powering use cases such as traffic management, autonomous tolling, crowd and queue management, smart parking, vehicle counting, and airport and aircraft-movement monitoring. Object output is emitted as JSON and Flatbuffers binary over WebSocket, with a web-based configuration and visualizer utility, VPN and PTP time-synchronization support, and a privacy-preserving, GDPR-compliant design. Cron AI was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

companies.name: DayOne
companies.description: DayOne is a hyperscale data center company delivering next-generation digital infrastructure for cloud, AI, and edge computing workloads. Spun out of the GDS International business and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, DayOne develops and operates strategically located, interconnected data center campuses across Asia-Pacific — Singapore, Johor (Malaysia), Batam (Indonesia), Hong Kong, Tokyo, and Bangkok — and is expanding into Europe with a launch market in Finland. The company positions itself as a build-to-suit and hyperscale partner focused on power availability, connectivity, and sustainable operations rather than as a public API or developer-platform provider; there is no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface at this time.

companies.name: Dorado Software Inc
companies.description: Dorado Software, Inc. is a Roseville, California infrastructure management software company whose Cruz and Redcell product families deliver resource management, orchestration, monitoring, and automation for data centers, AI infrastructure, enterprise campuses, and service-provider networks. The Cruz suite spans DCIM, network performance management, fabric and compute orchestration, compliance, and agentic-AI operations, discovering and controlling multi-vendor devices over SNMP, CLI, NETCONF, and REST/HTTPS. Dorado Software is backed by Insight Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, portal, or SDK surface was found.

companies.name: Gherkin
companies.description: Gherkin is a business-readable, domain-specific language created to support Behavior-Driven Development (BDD). It lets teams describe software behavior in plain text using a structured Given-When-Then syntax that is human-readable and machine-parsable. Gherkin is the language used by Cucumber and many other BDD tools to define executable specifications and acceptance tests.

companies.name: morewis
companies.description: Morewis (摩尔元数) is a Chinese industrial software company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian, that develops cloud-based Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for the manufacturing sector. Its Morewis Cloud industrial internet platform, MoreDEV low-code development platform (including the WisIDE cloud IDE), and MoreAgent / N³ industrial AI large model let manufacturers build and run smart-factory applications with reduced hand coding. Reference clients include Haier, Hisense, Aisino, Inspur, and 3Trees Group. The company raised a ~100M yuan Series B led by Qiming Venture Partners. No public English-language REST API, OpenAPI, SDK, or GitHub organization was found; the developer surface is a China-hosted low-code industrial application platform.

companies.name: SilverStream
companies.description: Silverstream AI builds infrastructure for autonomous AI agents, focused on making web-browsing and enterprise-workflow agents reliable enough for real-world, production use. Its work includes Silverstream Bench (a platform for storing, reviewing, and sharing Claude Code sessions), the open Pasta-1T dataset of web trajectories for training browser agents, and benchmark results such as 94% accuracy (2-sigma reliability) on ServiceNow tasks. The company emerged from stealth in March 2025 with a $1.2M pre-seed round. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and product pages but no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface, so most API-facing enrichment is not applicable.

companies.name: Binaris
companies.description: Binaris was a fast, low-latency Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platform for running production Node.js workloads in the cloud. Founded in 2017 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, its developer surface centered on the `bn` command-line tool and Node.js SDK (published to npm as `binaris` and to Docker Hub as `binaris/bn`), which let developers scaffold, deploy, invoke, and inspect serverless functions in seconds. Authentication was via a Binaris API key (`BINARIS_API_KEY`). The company later explored a "Shift" programming model (`@binaris/shift-fetch-runtime`). The hosted platform at binaris.io / binaris.com is no longer in service, but the first-party client packages and a 42-repository GitHub organization remain publicly available and are captured here.

companies.name: Concord Systems
companies.description: Concord Systems was a Brooklyn, New York stream-processing company founded in December 2014 by Alexander Gallego and Emilio Del Tesoro, and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It built a high-performance distributed stream processing framework written in C++ on top of Apache Mesos, aimed at letting application developers and data scientists write real-time streaming computations ("operators") in the language of their choice — Python, Ruby, Go, Java/Scala, Node.js or Haskell — with Kafka and Amazon Kinesis connectors and a CLI for deploying topologies. Akamai Technologies acquired the company in an all-cash transaction in September 2016 and folded the technology into its IoT edge data platform for real-time messaging and log processing. The company is discontinued: concord.io is parked and the documentation site is gone. Its interface was a Thrift-based operator driver API rather than an HTTP/REST API, so there is no OpenAPI or event surface to catalog; the surviving first-party developer artifacts are the github.com/concord organization and the client libraries still published on PyPI, RubyGems and pkg.go.dev.

companies.name: Continual
companies.description: Continual was an operational-AI / MLOps platform for the modern data stack, founded by Tristan Zajonc (previously Sense, acquired by Cloudera) and Tyler Kohn (co-founder of RichRelevance). It let data and analytics teams declaratively build, deploy, and continuously maintain production predictive models directly inside cloud data warehouses — Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery — using SQL and dbt as the primary interface rather than bespoke ML pipelines. The company raised a seed round led by Amplify Partners and a $14.5M Series A in 2022. The product is now dormant: continual.ai is a parked single-page shell, the documentation host redirects to the homepage, and the last release of the first-party Python CLI + SDK on PyPI was in March 2023. This profile captures the verifiable public artifacts that remain — the PyPI package, the GitHub organization, and a live domain-security posture.

companies.name: Ionic Security
companies.description: Ionic Security was an Atlanta, Georgia data-protection and dynamic-authorization company whose Machina platform let developers add data access, control, and protection to any application with a small amount of code. Machina provided an API-driven service layer for just-in-time enforcement of data-access policies — evaluating user, device, service, environment, and data attributes to allow or deny each request — backed by client SDKs for Java, C, C++, C#, Objective-C, Python, and JavaScript, a Machina CLI, and cloud-storage integrations for AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Storage. Ionic was venture-backed (GV, Kleiner Perkins, Ten Eleven Ventures) and was acquired by Twilio in April 2021 for roughly $30.2 million to accelerate Twilio's data-security capabilities. The company's developer domains (ionic.com, dev.ionic.com, api.ionic.com) are no longer live, but the first-party SDKs and CLI remain published on Maven Central, PyPI, and the IonicDev GitHub organization.

companies.name: Kinvey
companies.description: Kinvey was a mobile Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS / mBaaS) platform providing app developers with hosted data storage, user management and authentication, file storage, push notifications, caching/offline sync, and serverless business logic through its Flex (FlexData / FlexFunctions) services. It shipped first-party client SDKs for web, Node.js, iOS/macOS (Swift), Android/Java, Xamarin/.NET, NativeScript, Angular/Ionic, and Cordova/PhoneGap, plus a command-line utility for managing apps, environments, and Flex microservices. Kinvey was acquired by Progress Software; the standalone developer surface has since been retired (kinvey.com redirects into Progress and the GitHub organization was archived in February 2025), though the published SDKs and CLI remain available on their package registries.

companies.name: Open Souls
companies.description: Open Souls is an open-source framework and philosophy for building "AI souls" — agentic, embodied digital beings with personality, drive, and ego, built on top of large language models. The Soul Engine framework (distributed as the soul-engine npm package and CLI) models agency, memory, emotion, and goal-setting through WorkingMemory, cognitiveSteps, and MentalProcesses abstractions, describing itself as "NextJS + Vercel for the minds of digital beings." The project is now legacy: the opensouls.org site is parked and the hosted Soul Engine cloud service is no longer operating, but the open-source framework and npm packages remain published under the opensouls GitHub organization. Open Souls was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Quantive (fka Gtmhub)
companies.description: Quantive (formerly Gtmhub) is a strategy-execution and OKR (Objectives and Key Results) SaaS platform, historically backed by Insight Partners. The company and its "Quantive Results" product have since been acquired and folded into WorkBoard — quantive.com now redirects to workboard.com and the developer portal (developer.quantive.com) has been decommissioned. The public REST API and OpenAPI reference are no longer reachable, but first-party developer tooling remains published on public registries: the @gtmhub/sdk extensibility SDK on npm (for building marketplace plugins and insights) and the gtmhub-cli command-line client (distributed via Homebrew, Chocolatey, and GitHub releases). This profile captures the surviving developer surface.

companies.name: Rubric Labs
companies.description: Rubric Labs is an applied AI lab based in Canada that helps companies build and ship intelligent, agent-powered applications. Rather than selling a public API product, Rubric Labs operates as an engineering partner and maintains open-source tooling for AI-first development, including create-rubric-app (a full-stack AI project scaffold inspired by create-next-app), maige (open-source infrastructure for running natural-language workflows on your codebase), and tokenmaxx (a local proxy that aggregates LLM token usage across Codex and Claude Code accounts). The team partners with companies such as Cal.com and Trigger.dev, works with Neon, Vercel, and LangChain, and publishes engineering writing on its blog. As of this profile there is no self-service developer API, hosted API reference, SDK, or pricing surface to score — this is a services and open-source lab, not an API provider.

companies.name: Stamplay
companies.description: Stamplay was a backend-as-a-service and API-integration platform — billed as "Lego for developers" — founded in 2012 (Turin, Italy; later San Francisco) and backed by 500 Global. It let developers assemble application backends by visually wiring together third-party APIs, authentication providers, hosted data objects, webhooks, and static site hosting on stamplayapp.com, driven by a JavaScript SDK, a Node.js SDK, and the `stamplay` CLI. The product has been discontinued: the company was acquired (widely reported as Apple, 2019), the stamplay.com domain is now held via MarkMonitor and returns no HTTP response, every source repository in the GitHub organization is archived, and the npm SDK/CLI packages were last published in 2016. This API Evangelist profile preserves the historical developer footprint (SDKs and CLI) rather than a live API surface.

companies.name: Suborbital
companies.description: Suborbital was a developer-tools company building a WebAssembly-based extensibility platform: the Suborbital Extension Engine (SE2, formerly Suborbital Compute), a hosted service for running sandboxed third-party plugins; E2 Core / Reactr, a function scheduler for Go and WebAssembly; Sat, a tiny fast Wasm edge-compute server; Grav, an embedded decentralized message bus; and the subo CLI for building Wasm plugins and scaffolding projects. Suborbital was acquired by F5 in 2023 and the hosted product was subsequently wound down; the suborbital.dev domain has since been repurposed as an unrelated content blog. The first-party open-source client libraries (npm @suborbital/*, the se2-go Go client, and the subo CLI) and the 32-repo GitHub organization remain publicly available.

companies.name: Volterra
companies.description: Volterra was a Santa Clara-based distributed cloud company founded in 2017 by Ankur Singla, Harshad Nakil, and Ashish Ranjan, offering the VoltMesh (multi-cloud networking and security) and VoltStack (edge application deployment) SaaS platforms on a global application delivery network. Backed by roughly $50M from Khosla Ventures, Mayfield, M12, Samsung NEXT, and Itochu Technology Ventures, Volterra was acquired by F5 in January 2021 for approximately $500M and became the foundation of F5 Distributed Cloud Services. Its API surface (ves.io.schema, console.ves.volterra.io) is catalogued in the F5 Distributed Cloud Services profile, while the Volterra-branded Terraform provider and vesctl CLI remain published and maintained by F5.

companies.name: GitOps
companies.description: A operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development such as version control, collaboration, compliance, and CI/CD, and applies them to infrastructure automation. GitOps uses Git as a single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications.

companies.name: Result
companies.description: Result is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) all-in-one business operating system that lets internet entrepreneurs start and run companies end-to-end. The platform unifies app development with built-in payments, AI-powered marketing and content creation, automated customer support, financial analytics, branding and design tools, market research, SEO optimization, legal incorporation, and investor fundraising into a single surface, tied together by a "Company Brain" that retains business context from day one. Founded by Aaryan Kushwah (CEO) and Savio Martin (CTO), the product is in private beta with a public waitlist and does not yet publish a developer/API surface.

companies.name: SheetRocks
companies.description: SheetRocks is a spreadsheet engine embedded directly into the business platforms teams already use. Branded "The Spreadsheet for Everywhere," it brings keyboard-driven data entry, formula-based analytics, and spreadsheet-in-the-loop workflows inside host applications such as Salesforce (live), WooCommerce and Gravity Forms (beta), and Shopify, HubSpot, and ServiceNow (announced). The product targets operators, analysts, and builders who want a familiar grid plus instant workflow invocation without leaving their platform of record. SheetRocks is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public REST/GraphQL API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface; it does publish product documentation, a free sandbox, and a responsible security-disclosure policy.

companies.name: AdColony
companies.description: AdColony was a mobile advertising and app-monetization company known for its high-definition video and interactive (Aurora HD) mobile ad SDKs and its Publisher and Advertiser reporting APIs. AdColony was acquired by Digital Turbine in 2021; adcolony.com and its developer support/docs hosts now 308-redirect to digitalturbine.com, so the historical reporting-API and helpdesk documentation is no longer served. The first-party AdColony mobile ads SDKs for iOS (CocoaPods) and Android (Maven Central) remain published, and the iOS SDK source remains archived on GitHub.

companies.name: Nebu
companies.description: NEBU (legal entity NEBU LAH SDN. BHD., Malaysia) is an early-stage, AI-powered DevOps-as-a-Service platform positioned as "the missing brain for your cloud" — offering intelligent understanding of cloud infrastructure rather than scripted automation alone. Founded in 2024, the company markets AIOps/MLOps-style cloud management, cost optimization, and intelligent automation for enterprise cloud estates, and self-states a security posture of SOC 2 Type II readiness, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance. As of this profile the product is pre-launch ("we're building what comes next") with a single-page marketing site and no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs yet. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead; the only machine-readable surface found is a valid RFC 9116 /.well-known/security.txt.

companies.name: Rollup AI
companies.description: Rollup is a browser-based, real-time collaboration platform for engineering teams building complex hardware. It supports the full hardware development lifecycle across modular tools for systems engineering, systems modeling, requirements management, technical documentation, CAD viewing, and design reviews, with modules that interlink so changes propagate across a project. Rollup markets first-class APIs and developer-friendly features so teams can integrate it into new and existing systems; the platform exposes a REST API (authenticated with API keys or OAuth tokens) with pagination and websockets. Rollup serves early-stage hardware companies from small satellite builders to robotics firms, and offers Self-hosted and GovCloud options for ITAR/EAR export-controlled data. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Thiel Capital ($5.6M seed) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company.

companies.name: SUSE
companies.description: SUSE is a global provider of open source enterprise solutions including SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES), SUSE Rancher Prime for Kubernetes management, SUSE Manager (SUMA) for Linux systems management, and SUSE Edge and Security solutions. SUSE products expose REST and "A-REST" APIs for automation, configuration, and integration. The SUSE Manager API and Rancher API provide programmatic control over systems, clusters, and policies.

companies.name: xiaoyi
companies.description: Xiaoyi Technology (小蚁科技), operated by Shanghai Yunyi Zhilian Technology (上海云蚁智联) and best known for its YI-brand cameras, is a Shanghai-based smart-imaging company that emerged from the Xiaomi ecosystem. It builds action cameras, the M1 mirrorless camera, smart home/security cameras, dash cams and in-car rearview systems, VR cameras, and handheld gimbals, and now positions itself around computer vision, edge intelligence, and edge computing solutions for smart mobility, smart home, smart retail, smart parks, and smart communities, selling through JD and Tmall storefronts. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment - the developer subdomain (dev.xiaoyi.com) returns 502, api.xiaoyi.com serves only a placeholder page, and no API documentation, OpenAPI specs, official GitHub organization, or first-party registry packages were located.

companies.name: Integrated Development Environment
companies.description: Integrated Development Environment (IDE) is a software application that consolidates the core developer workflow into a single interface, typically combining a source code editor, build automation tools, debugger, version control integration, intelligent code completion, refactoring, and language server protocol (LSP) support. Modern IDEs increasingly integrate AI coding assistants, agentic tooling, remote development containers, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to extend the surface area beyond local file editing.

companies.name: Integration Patterns
companies.description: Integration Patterns are design patterns and best practices for integrating different software systems and applications, including messaging, data transformation, and service orchestration approaches. Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP), as cataloged by Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf, provide a technology-independent vocabulary and visual notation harvested from proven solutions to recurring integration problems, organized into Messaging Channels, Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Endpoints, and System Management.

companies.name: Ratify
companies.description: Ratify is a CNCF Sandbox open-source verification framework for container images and other supply chain artifacts in Kubernetes environments. It enables policy-driven artifact ratification by coordinating any number of pluggable verifiers (signatures, SBOMs, scan results, attestations) against a given policy, integrating with Kubernetes admission webhooks via the Gatekeeper policy engine. Ratify is developed by the ratify-project GitHub organization (originally a Microsoft open-source project), written in Go, and distributed as a CLI tool, Go library, and Kubernetes admission webhook server. It supports OCI-compliant artifact stores including Azure Container Registry, Amazon ECR, and Docker Hub. Ratify exposes an internal HTTP verification API (v2alpha1) consumed by its webhook server but does not publish a public-facing REST API or OpenAPI specification.

companies.name: Theta EdgeCloud
companies.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients.
