Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

companies.name: Conifer
companies.description: Conifer (YC S26) builds Sage, a local-first AI runtime and workspace that runs models entirely on your own machine. Its inference engine is written from scratch in Rust, reaching up to 60% faster decode than llama.cpp on Apple Silicon, and pairs an editor, integrated terminal, file viewers, and an agent runtime inside a kernel-level sandbox so tool calls only touch what you allow. Conifer routes each request to the cheapest capable model, starting with free on-device inference and falling back to cloud only when needed, cutting AI spend by up to 80%. The desktop app ships as Juniper for macOS, Windows, and Linux with no accounts, no telemetry, and no cloud dependency. Conifer is proprietary and distributed as compiled binaries; it currently exposes no public web API.

companies.name: Deep Interactions
companies.description: Deep Interactions is a collaborative, humans-in-the-loop AI builder for product teams, launched out of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch. The platform helps teams move from business goals through design and development to a deployed AI product, turning messy ideas, data, and tools into working software in a single afternoon while maintaining code organization and product coherence. It positions itself as the context layer that lets a whole team build in sync — integrating with existing tools such as Slack, Figma, GitHub, Vercel, and Supabase — rather than producing disconnected solo prototypes. The company is currently at a waitlist-only stage and does not yet publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Diamond
companies.description: Diamond (diamond.io) is an early-stage, managed serverless data backend for teams, positioned as "your project, but with AI." The product promises a world-class serverless database where teams bring their own data sources, AI-assisted setup so no schema configuration is required, team collaboration with role management, and single sign-on via Google, Microsoft, and LDAP. As of this profile the public surface is a pre-launch landing page with a "create your workspace" signup form and a sign-in page; no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, pricing, changelog, or status page are published yet. Diamond Inc. is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and enriched from the provider's public web surface.

companies.name: Fifth Door
companies.description: Fifth Door is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) AI-native gaming startup founded by Amir Ghazvinian and Daniel Kan that lets anyone create, share, and play games simply by describing what they imagine, with no coding required. Its generative-AI platform turns natural-language prompts into playable, customizable games, aiming to collapse the time, cost, and technical complexity of traditional game development for players, creators, and studios. Backed by Felicis, the company runs a consumer web app and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

companies.name: Hex Security
companies.description: Hex Security is a Y Combinator (W26) security startup building autonomous AI agents that perform continuous penetration testing against web applications, APIs, and infrastructure. Instead of point-in-time annual pentests, Hex's agents probe systems around the clock — chaining exploits together, validating each finding with a working proof-of-concept, and delivering triaged, reproducible results with no false positives. The product surfaces high-severity issues such as SQL injection, broken access control / IDOR, authentication bypass, and unauthenticated remote code execution. Founded by Ahmad Khan, Huzaifa Ahmad, and Prama Yudhistira. As of this profile Hex Security is pre-public-API: it operates a marketing site (hex.co) and a product application (app.hex.co) but does not yet publish a developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or public API surface.

companies.name: Nazar
companies.description: Nazar (nazar.ai) is an AI-powered database performance and cost optimization platform that helps engineering and DBA teams monitor, analyze, and tune their databases. It supports Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, MariaDB, Amazon Aurora, Oracle, and SAP HANA across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments. Capabilities include SQL.AI, an LLM-based tuning assistant, offensive SQL monitoring for slow-query detection, real-time lock visibility, and anomaly detection. Founded in Recife, Brazil and backed by 500 Global, Nazar counts financial-services and travel companies among its customers.

companies.name: Nuvelar
companies.description: Nuvelar is an Argentine technology solutions firm founded in 2014 that designs and builds digital experiences across consulting, hardware, software, and design. Its flagship product, Nuvelar Display, is a cloud platform for creating, distributing, and managing digital-signage content networks with content scheduling, player monitoring, dynamic templates, multi-format support, and social/weather/RSS integrations. Beyond the platform, Nuvelar builds custom interactive installations — videowalls, interactive tables, and branded experiential systems for clients such as Adidas. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the latest enrichment pass Nuvelar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

companies.name: SevOne (Turbonomic)
companies.description: SevOne and Turbonomic are enterprise IT operations products now part of IBM's AIOps portfolio. IBM SevOne Network Performance Management (NPM) delivers real-time, multi-vendor network monitoring, flow analytics, and capacity planning across hybrid and enterprise networks. IBM Turbonomic is an application resource management (ARM) platform that continuously analyzes application demand and automates resourcing, scaling, and placement decisions across on-premises, cloud, and Kubernetes environments to assure performance while reducing cost. Both products expose REST APIs, but those APIs are hosted on the customer's own appliance / deployment rather than on a public developer portal, so there is no public base URL or published OpenAPI to catalog: the Turbonomic REST API is served from the appliance (for example the /vmturbo/rest path with its bundled Swagger UI), and SevOne exposes the SevOne NMS API and SevOne Data Insight API from the deployed instance. Product and API reference documentation is published by IBM.

companies.name: Skyfri
companies.description: Skyfri is a cleantech software and hardware company headquartered in Oslo, Norway that builds an operating platform for owners and operators of solar and battery energy assets. Founded in 2021, Skyfri combines an edge-native monitoring and control device (the SSI hardware, which speaks Modbus and SCADA over isolated RS-485 ports to inverters, meters, and sensors) with a cloud platform that automates operations, maintenance, and asset performance management. The software delivers real-time data processing, operational management, weather forecasting, dynamic benchmarking, plant insights, and fault detection to monitor generation and address underperformance and equipment failure across a global portfolio of solar and battery assets. The company has offices in Denver, London, Oslo, Singapore, and Bangalore and is backed by Speedinvest. Skyfri exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; its platform is delivered as a customer application at app.skyfri.com.

companies.name: Syntropy
companies.description: Syntropy is an autonomous, agentic coding application built for complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks. A developer describes a feature in natural language and Syntropy plans, writes, and tests the implementation, returning a production-ready pull request without the developer having to manage a terminal or an IDE agent session by hand. The product emphasizes large-context handling for heavy, real-world codebases ("no context ceiling, no truncation"), supports custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations so it can pull in a team's own tools, and joins Slack to post updates as tasks complete. Syntropy is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco, founded by Saahil Sundaresan and Andrew Kuik. As of this profile it ships as a hosted end-user coding product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

companies.name: Vitesse
companies.description: Vitesse is a universal physical-AI platform for industrial machines, founded by the team behind Tesla's "Model 3 automation hell" fix alongside leaders from SpaceX, Siemens, and Safran. It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Lattice Health
companies.description: Lattice Health is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) healthcare company building AI governance as a managed service for hospitals. The platform sits beside an existing clinical stack and taps the HL7 and DICOM signals that deployed imaging and clinical AI models already emit, with no rip-and-replace integration, then continuously measures population drift (PSI), subgroup fairness disparity under HHS Section 1557, latency against target, and silent vendor model-update detection across every vendor model running in production. Rather than another dashboard, Lattice delivers a per-role signed PDF report each morning to IT directors, CMIO/CIO, and compliance officers, cryptographically signed with the institution's own signing key so any recipient, including outside counsel or a regulator, can verify the artifact offline with standard open-source tooling and no Lattice account or infrastructure. Radiologist thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback on AI results is aggregated at model level and folded into the next morning's findings. The company positions itself around standards alignment (IHE UPS-RS work-list status, AI-Results and ERA classification, ONC HTI-1, FDA Predetermined Change Control Plan envelopes with automatic breach detection) and HIPAA-safe egress with a strict-mode PHI redactor, deployed on-premise or in the customer's private cloud so PHI stays behind the hospital firewall. As of this profile Lattice Health publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification, SDKs, or pricing; it is a pre-public-API company tracked here as an AI governance and clinical AI oversight lead.

companies.name: Cumulus Networks
companies.description: Cumulus Networks was a computer networking company founded in 2010 that developed Cumulus Linux, an open Linux-based network operating system for bare-metal and white-box data-center switches, along with NetQ, a network operations and telemetry platform. It was a pioneer of open, disaggregated networking, letting operators run a standard Linux distribution on commodity switching hardware. NVIDIA acquired Cumulus Networks in May 2020, and the products are now part of NVIDIA's Ethernet switching and networking software line. The former cumulusnetworks.com and docs.cumulusnetworks.com domains now redirect to NVIDIA's networking documentation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, Battery Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital.

companies.name: Defer
companies.description: Defer was a Paris-based, Y Combinator-backed (W23) zero-infrastructure background jobs platform for Node.js and TypeScript developers, founded in 2022 by Bryan Frimin and Charly Poly. The product converted regular JavaScript/TypeScript async functions into managed background jobs with configurable retries, throttling, concurrency controls, scheduled crons, multi-environment support, alerting, and a hosted dashboard — removing the need for developers to operate their own queues, workers, and Redis-style infrastructure. Defer shipped client SDKs and framework integrations (Next.js, RedwoodJS) and a CLI/build pipeline that uploaded function bundles to the Defer cloud for execution. The company appears to have wound down its hosted service in 2024 — the defer.run domain now 301-redirects to digger.tools, no end-of-service post-mortem is publicly linked from the homepage, and the GitHub organization (github.com/defer-run) last saw meaningful activity in July 2024 with the final defer.client release v2.3.0 cut on 2024-03-06. The open source client libraries remain available but are effectively unmaintained and the hosted backend they depended on is no longer operational. This catalog entry preserves the historical footprint of Defer as part of the 2022-2024 wave of "zero-infrastructure" background-job and durable- execution startups (Inngest, Trigger.dev, Hatchet, Temporal Cloud, Restate) so the design pattern and the players who pursued it remain discoverable in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Fourier Intelligence
companies.description: Fourier (Fourier Intelligence, founded 2015 and headquartered in Shanghai, China) is a full-stack robotics company that develops core robot technology and finished robot products. It began in rehabilitation robotics — exoskeletons and upper/lower-limb rehab devices such as the ArmMotus and ExoMotus lines and the RehabHub intelligent rehabilitation ecosystem — and has expanded into general-purpose humanoid robots (the GRx series, including GR-1 and GR-2), smart actuators (FSA), and dexterous hands. Fourier publishes first-party developer SDKs for robot control through its FFTAI GitHub organization: the RoCS (Robot Control System / General Robotics OS) client libraries for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and the fourier-grx control stack for the GRx humanoid series. Fourier is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. These are device/robot-control developer libraries rather than a hosted web API; the company publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Habana Labs
companies.description: Habana Labs is an artificial-intelligence processor company, now part of Intel, that designs deep-learning accelerators for AI training and inference. Its Gaudi (training) and Goya (inference) processors — sold today as the Intel Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 AI accelerators — are programmed through the SynapseAI software suite, which integrates with PyTorch and DeepSpeed and ships reference models, containers, and installation tooling. Habana was founded in 2016 in Israel and acquired by Intel in 2019. Its public developer surface is not a hosted web API but an open-source SDK and toolchain: the HabanaAI GitHub organization (reference models, PyTorch bridge, setup/install, plus vLLM and Megatron forks) and the Intel Gaudi documentation at docs.habana.ai. This profile catalogs that developer footprint for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Interlink
companies.description: interLink is an abstraction layer that extends the Kubernetes Virtual Kubelet interface, enabling pods to execute on remote resources such as HPC batch systems (SLURM, HTCondor), virtual machines, remote Kubernetes clusters, and serverless platforms. It comprises a Virtual Kubelet that converts pod execution requests into remote API calls and a modular interLink API Server with provider-specific sidecar plugins, with built-in OpenTelemetry observability, TLS/mTLS, and OAuth2 authentication.

companies.name: KDDI
companies.description: KDDI Corporation is a Japanese multinational telecommunications operator headquartered in Tokyo, providing mobile, fixed-line, broadband, and enterprise ICT services. KDDI markets its consumer mobile services under the au brand, alongside UQ mobile and povo, and serves enterprise customers globally through KDDI Global and KDDI America. The company operates the KDDI Open API for Developers portal exposing inquiry-gated product APIs including the au PAY Mini App platform, an XR/MEC low-latency application API, a PPM consent management API, and an au mobile Identification Support Service for KYC/identity verification. KDDI also runs the au OPEN DEVICE DEVELOPER SITE for cellular module device certification, and a KDDI Cloud Platform Service knowledge site with developer API references for cloud infrastructure. In 2025 KDDI became an equity partner in Aduna, the GSMA/Ericsson-backed network API venture aggregating CAMARA-aligned carrier APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location) across global operators. Public OpenAPI specifications are not openly published; API access is provided through contact/inquiry workflows after partner onboarding.

companies.name: Spiral
companies.description: Spiral (SpiralDB) is a multimodal data platform built for the "machine consumer" — frontier AI systems and agents. It unifies video, images, audio, embeddings, point clouds, sensor streams, tables, and text under one query language and coordinate-frame system, serving everything from raw bytes to model-ready tensors at machine-scale throughput for pretraining pipelines and agentic access. Spiral is the creator of Vortex, a high-performance extensible columnar data format (100x faster random access and 10-20x faster scans vs. Apache Parquet) now incubating under the Linux Foundation, along with the FastLanes, FSST, and ALP compression libraries. The hosted Spiral warehouse is currently invite-only (Request Access); the public developer surface today is the open-source Vortex ecosystem (Python and Rust bindings). Backed by Amplify Partners and General Catalyst.

companies.name: A Capital
companies.description: A.Capital Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded by Ronny Conway, a former partner at Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and one of the first employees at Google Ventures. The firm provides funding, talent, and strategic counsel to founders building at the frontier of technology, with a portfolio spanning AI and machine learning (OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Character.ai), developer tools (Notion, Replit, Databricks), and crypto and consumer platforms (Coinbase, Uniswap, Reddit, Airbnb). A.Capital differs from standard venture models by customizing investment amounts rather than enforcing ownership thresholds, advising without mandatory board seats, and staffing full-time Talent Partners to help early-stage teams hire and build their organizational foundation. This profile was surfaced via the a16z network (through founder Ronny Conway's a16z tenure) and enriched from the firm's public website. A.Capital is a venture capital firm and does not publish a developer-facing API surface, developer portal, or API artifacts.

companies.name: Keploy
companies.description: Open-source, AI-native testing platform that captures real production API traffic with eBPF and replays it in CI as deterministic tests, auto-generated mocks, and production-like sandboxes with zero code changes. Offers a Cloud REST API, a hosted MCP server, llms.txt, and generated agent skills.

companies.name: Physical Property Testing
companies.description: Physical Properties Testers (PPT) Group is a Halifax, UK based multinational manufacturer of physical property test and measurement instrumentation, built through acquisition around four brands: James Heal (textile testing including bursting strength, abrasion and tear), Mecmesin (universal testing machines, torque testers and digital force gauges), Alluris (handheld force gauges and force/torque instrumentation) and Lansmont (shock, vibration and drop testing systems). The group designs, produces and services testing equipment that verifies the physical integrity and quality of raw materials, components and finished products across textiles, packaging, manufacturing and consumer goods. It is a hardware and laboratory-instrumentation business with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Registered in England and Wales (company no. 09210539); a portfolio company of SK Capital Partners since March 2025 (previously backed by Battery Ventures). This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched with company identity from public sources.

companies.name: Carevision Inc.
companies.description: Carevision Inc. is an AI-powered digital health company whose platform turns any camera into a 60-second contactless cardiometabolic wellness scanner. Using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) and deep learning models trained on 12M+ patient records, it extracts 30+ physiological parameters — including heart rate, blood pressure indicators, stress index, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation — and produces a comprehensive digital health persona covering 15+ cardiometabolic conditions. Carevision operates under the FDA General Wellness Policy (it is not a medical device or diagnostic tool) and is delivered as a kiosk, an embedded/white-label SDK for iOS and Android, or a web integration to hospitals and clinics, health insurers, pharmacy chains, diagnostic laboratories, wellness apps, and teleconsultation platforms, integrating with EMR/HIS systems.

companies.name: CYBAVO
companies.description: CYBAVO was a digital asset security company (founded 2018, Taipei/Singapore) providing institutional-grade cryptocurrency custody and wallet infrastructure. Its flagship CYBAVO Vault delivered MPC-based (Multi-Party Computation) custody with a policy/workflow engine, REST API, and client SDKs, alongside the CYBAVO Wallet App SDK for embedding secure private-key storage into mobile apps. Circle Internet Financial acquired CYBAVO in June 2022; the team and technology became the foundation of Circle Web3 Services and Circle Programmable Wallets. The cybavo.com developer surface has since been wound down (redirects to circle.com), but the first-party @cybavo Wallet/Auth SDKs remain published on npm and are maintained under Circle's circlefin GitHub organization.

companies.name: ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md
companies.description: ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md is a template file that pre-populates new issue forms with structured sections, guiding contributors to provide necessary information when reporting bugs or requesting features in GitHub repositories.

companies.name: Protectt AI
companies.description: Protectt.ai (Protectt.ai Labs Pvt Ltd) is an AI-native, full-stack mobile application security and fraud-control platform for Android and iOS. Its products — AppProtectt (RASP with 100+ runtime protections against hooking, spoofing, reverse engineering, tampering, MITM and SMS exploitation), SDKProtectt (SDK hardening/obfuscation), and ApiProtectt (API security) — embed as a lightweight SDK with zero performance overhead and no disruption to release cycles. The company targets banking, financial services and regulated enterprises (RBL Bank, Yes Bank, BSE, Bajaj Finserv, LIC), is ISO 27001 / ISO 42001 / ISO 22301 and PCI DSS certified, and aligns to RBI, SEBI and NPCI security mandates. It is headquartered in Mumbai with offices in Dover (Delaware, US) and Dubai (UAE). Protectt.ai ships enterprise SDKs to customers rather than a public developer portal or open API — no OpenAPI, SDK registry package, or public API reference is published.

companies.name: Anki
companies.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

companies.name: Cloudcoreo
companies.description: CloudCoreo was a Seattle-based cloud security startup (founded 2016, seed round led by Madrona Venture Group) that built a cloud configuration and vulnerability-assessment platform to identify and remediate misconfigurations across public multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP). VMware acquired CloudCoreo in February 2018 and folded the team and product into VMware Cloud Services, where it became the basis of CloudHealth Secure State. The standalone CloudCoreo service and developer surface have since been retired: cloudcoreo.com is now a parked/for-sale domain and there is no live public API. The CloudCoreo GitHub organization remains, hosting the now-deprecated first-party CLI. This profile is a historical/lineage record, not an active API provider.

companies.name: Epsagon
companies.description: Epsagon was an observability and application performance monitoring (APM) company, founded in 2017, that provided automated distributed tracing for serverless and containerized applications — AWS Lambda, Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Ruby, and Java — correlating traces, metrics, and logs to help teams identify and fix problems fast without manual instrumentation. Epsagon was acquired by Cisco in 2021 and folded into Cisco's observability portfolio, after which the product was sunset. The epsagon.com developer surface (docs, dashboard, and API subdomains) no longer resolves. Its surviving public footprint is the github.com/epsagon organization and the first-party instrumentation SDKs still hosted on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Go modules, NuGet, and Maven Central. This profile captures that remaining, verifiable footprint.

companies.name: Floobits
companies.description: Floobits was a real-time collaborative code editing service — "remote collaboration tools for dev teams, work together, apart." It shipped editor plugins for Sublime Text, Vim, Neovim, Emacs, Atom, and the IntelliJ family of IDEs, plus flootty, a shared-terminal tool for pair terminal sessions. Plugins connected editors to shared Floobits workspaces where multiple developers edited the same files and terminals in real time over a synchronizing backend (built on a diff-match-patch model). Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of 2026-07-19 the hosted service at floobits.com no longer resolves in DNS and the GitHub org has had no activity since December 2022; the open-source editor plugins and the flootty PyPI package remain the durable public surface.

companies.name: Heyzap
companies.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

companies.name: Immunio
companies.description: IMMUNIO was a Montreal-based application security company (founded 2013) that built a real-time RASP (Runtime Application Self-Protection) platform to detect and block attacks against web applications and APIs without requiring code changes. Its product shipped as language-native agents for Ruby on Rails, Python (Django/Pyramid/Flask), Node.js/Express, Java, PHP, Scala and .NET, covering the OWASP Top 10 including Cross-Site Scripting and SQL Injection. The company raised roughly $8M from Bloomberg Beta, WhiteStar Capital, Real Ventures, Hoxton Ventures and BDC, and was acquired by Trend Micro in November 2017, where the technology was folded into Trend Micro's hybrid cloud and container security for the DevOps lifecycle. The immun.io and docs.immun.io properties have since been retired; the durable public surface today is the first-party agent libraries on RubyGems, PyPI and npm and the IMMUNIO GitHub organization.

companies.name: Kano Computing
companies.description: Kano Computing is a London-based technology company founded in 2013 by Alex Klein, Saul Klein and Yonatan Raz-Fridman that began by shipping build-it-yourself computer and coding kits designed to teach STEM and creative computing to children on top of Raspberry Pi hardware. Its catalog spanned the Kano Computer Kit, motion-sensor and Harry Potter / Star Wars coding wands, the Windows-based Kano PC built with Microsoft, and the Stem Player and Stem Video Projector consumer devices. Kano paired the hardware with Kano Code, a block-to-text creative-coding platform, and Kano World, an online making and sharing community. The company entered administration in 2023 and its assets now trade under the Stem brand; its developer footprint survives as open-source tooling in the KanoComputing GitHub organization and the npm @kano scope rather than a hosted API.

companies.name: Kik (Kin)
companies.description: Kik (Kin) refers to the Kin cryptocurrency created by Kik Interactive, the messaging company, as a blockchain-based digital currency for use inside consumer applications. Kin originally launched on a fork of the Stellar network and later migrated to Solana, shipping first-party developer SDKs (JavaScript/Node and Python) under the kinecosystem GitHub organization and a developer program at developer.kin.org. The Kin project is now defunct: the developer surface no longer resolves, every kinecosystem repository is archived, the published SDKs are deprecated, and Kik itself was acquired by MediaLab AI Inc. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and is retained as a historical record of a wound-down crypto developer surface.

companies.name: LaunchKit
companies.description: LaunchKit was a set of web-based tools for mobile app developers, built by Cluster Labs, Inc. in San Francisco and backed by GV. Its products included Screenshot Builder for App Store screenshots, Review Monitor for App Store review alerts, a Sales Reporter, hosted App Websites, and Super Users and Cloud Config delivered through the LaunchKit iOS SDK. LaunchKit joined Google in 2016 and the codebase was released as open source under Apache 2.0. There is no live hosted LaunchKit API, developer portal, or documentation today; the surviving surface is a self-hostable Django/JavaScript codebase on GitHub plus an unmaintained Objective-C SDK on CocoaPods. The original launchkit.io domain is no longer company-controlled and now serves an unrelated content site.

companies.name: Microverse
companies.description: Microverse is an online education platform that trains people worldwide to become remote software developers, founded by Ariel Camus with the stated mission of connecting one million people to remote jobs by 2030. Its model pairs students across time zones for peer collaboration that mirrors distributed engineering teams, and it historically charged tuition only after graduates secured a job. Microverse also runs Leap, an English-practice platform for developers. It is a private, distributed company backed by investors including Y Combinator, Hack.VC, and General Catalyst. Microverse does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web presence and security posture.

companies.name: Opsani
companies.description: Opsani was an enterprise software company based in Redwood City, California that delivered an ML-driven cloud platform for Continuous Optimization as a Service (COaaS), automatically and continuously tuning cloud-native (Kubernetes) application configurations for the best balance of performance, availability, and cost. Opsani was acquired by Cisco in January 2022 and folded into the Cisco AppDynamics full-stack observability portfolio (subsequently part of Splunk). The company no longer operates an independent API surface — opsani.com now redirects to Splunk and docs.opsani.com no longer resolves. The one surviving public first-party artifact is the open-source Servo (servox) optimization agent, still published on PyPI and hosted at github.com/opsani.

companies.name: Placenote
companies.description: Placenote (Vertical AI Inc.) was a San Francisco company that built a cloud-hosted persistent augmented-reality toolkit — a "Persistent AR" SDK that let developers save, reload, and share ARKit/Unity spatial maps so digital content stays anchored to a physical location across sessions and devices. It shipped native client SDKs for iOS (Swift, via the PlacenoteSDK CocoaPod) and Unity, plus multiplayer AR samples such as PlaceInvaders and web mesh-viewing examples. The product was consumed as mobile SDKs backed by a cloud mapping/localization service rather than a public REST API, so no OpenAPI or web API surface was published. The company is now defunct: placenote.com no longer resolves to a live product (the domain is parked) and the docs/cloud service are offline. The Placenote GitHub organization and the published SDKs remain the only live, first-party developer surface, which is what this profile captures.

companies.name: Source.dev
companies.description: Source.dev builds AI-native software tooling that helps device manufacturers develop, build, and update the operating systems that run intelligent devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles. Its platform virtualizes source access (SourceFS) to cut Android checkout-and-build times from hours to minutes, replays build steps across languages and systems for faster CI, and uses LLM-driven merging (Harmony AI / Continuous Merges) to automatically resolve conflicts when applying security patches and OS upgrades to large, long-lived codebases like AOSP. The company is a sales/demo-led platform for device makers and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface.

companies.name: Streamroot
companies.description: Streamroot was a Paris-founded video-delivery company (backed by Partech and Techstars) that built a peer-to-peer / multi-CDN "Mesh Delivery" and DNA SDK to offload live and on-demand video traffic onto a hybrid CDN+WebRTC peer mesh, reducing bandwidth cost and improving scale for broadcasters and OTT platforms. The developer surface was a client-side (browser and native player) delivery SDK distributed as video-player plugins (video.js, Clappr, hls.js, AVPlayer) rather than a server-side REST API. Streamroot was acquired by CenturyLink — now Lumen Technologies — in 2019 and folded into Lumen's CDN / Mesh Delivery product line. The standalone streamroot.io website and developer docs are offline; the surviving public assets are the (now Lumen-operated) GitHub organization and a set of official but deprecated npm player-plugin packages.

companies.name: Tracelytics
companies.description: Tracelytics was a Boston/Providence application-tracing (APM) startup, backed by investors including Google Ventures, that built full-stack distributed tracing for web applications. AppNeta acquired Tracelytics in 2012 and the product became AppNeta TraceView; SolarWinds acquired TraceView in 2016, and AppNeta itself was acquired by Broadcom in 2021. The company no longer operates independently — the tracelytics.com domain no longer resolves and its TraceView Data API (api.tracelytics.com) is defunct — but its verified GitHub organization and first-party TraceView instrumentation packages remain published on RubyGems and npm.

companies.name: Uninstall
companies.description: Uninstall.io was a mobile "uninstall intelligence" platform built by Songline Analytics (Bengaluru/Singapore, founded 2015) whose iOS and Android SDKs tracked app uninstalls, surfaced uninstall reasons, and drove re-install campaigns for customers like Snapdeal, Axis Bank, Zalora, and BankBazaar. Backed by 500 Startups India, Rajan Anandan, and Hive Data, it was acquired by Singapore healthtech company Mobile Health in July 2018. The uninstall.io domain is now parked for sale and no public API surface remains; the GitHub organization and first-party mobile SDKs survive as the public footprint.

companies.name: Zenaton
companies.description: Zenaton was a workflow-as-code SaaS that let developers orchestrate background jobs, asynchronous tasks, and long-running business processes directly in application code (Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go) rather than wiring queues and cron by hand. Founded in France and backed by Accel and Point Nine, it processed 10M+ workflow executions monthly across 100+ companies. The product is now DISCONTINUED: the API and app hosts (api.zenaton.com / app.zenaton.com) no longer resolve, the client SDK repositories are archived (last active ~2020), and the zenaton.com domain redirects to co-founder Gilles Barbier's personal site. This profile is retained as verified history — the archived first-party SDKs remain published on npm, PyPI, Packagist, RubyGems, and pkg.go.dev.

companies.name: Aerohive
companies.description: Aerohive Networks was a cloud-managed networking company founded in 2006 by Changming Liu and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It pioneered controller-less, cloud-managed Wi-Fi and edge networking, managed through its HiveManager NG (later ExtremeCloud IQ) platform and access points. Aerohive went public on the NYSE under the ticker HIVE and was acquired by Extreme Networks in a deal that closed on 2019-08-09 for approximately $272 million. The company operated an Aerohive Developer Program with a public developer portal (developer.aerohive.com) and REST APIs for the HiveManager NG / ACS platform, plus a GitHub organization of reference applications. Following the acquisition the products were folded into ExtremeCloud IQ, and the legacy Aerohive API and its developer portal were retired (shutdown dated 2026-07-12), with integrators directed to migrate to the Extreme Platform ONE Developer Portal. This profile enriches the historical Aerohive API surface; it is a retired/acquired provider.

companies.name: Bash Shell
companies.description: GNU Bash (Bourne Again SHell) is the default Unix shell and command-line interpreter on most Linux distributions and macOS. Developed by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, Bash provides a rich scripting language with variables, control structures, functions, I/O redirection, job control, and process management. Bash scripts are the foundational automation tool for system administration, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps tooling, and software build systems.

companies.name: Downjoy (当乐网)
companies.description: Downjoy (当乐网, d.cn) is a Chinese mobile game distribution and community platform operated by Beijing Downjoy Information Technology Co., Ltd (北京当乐信息技术有限公司). The site offers mobile game downloads, gaming news and original editorial content, game-related video, community features, and game rankings and recommendations. Downjoy also runs an open platform at open.d.cn where game publishers and developers register, create and submit games, integrate the Downjoy SDK, and manage launch and updates. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enriched with verified public identity and infrastructure probes.

companies.name: Ermetic
companies.description: Ermetic is a cloud security company founded in 2019 that pioneered cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM) as part of a unified, identity-first cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) spanning AWS, Azure, and GCP. The platform provides full visibility into permissions and entitlements across multi-cloud environments, least-privilege and just-in-time access controls, anomaly detection against behavioral baselines, and compliance and cloud security posture management (CSPM). Ermetic raised roughly $100M from investors including Accel, Norwest Venture Partners, Glilot Capital Partners, and Target Global, and was acquired by Tenable in October 2023 for approximately $265M. The product now ships as Tenable Cloud Security; the ermetic.com domain redirects to Tenable, and the former Ermetic customer application (us.app.ermetic.com) exposes a login-gated REST API.

companies.name: Excelero Storage
companies.description: Excelero was a software-defined storage company whose flagship product, NVMesh, delivered distributed, low-latency shared NVMe block storage across a server cluster with a Kubernetes CSI driver and a management CLI. Excelero was acquired by NVIDIA in 2022 and no longer operates as an independent company; its NVMesh product and documentation are now part of NVIDIA. The former excelero.com domain 301-redirects to nvidia.com/en-us/excelero/. This profile was surfaced as a battery-ventures portfolio company; the enrichment pipeline found no independent Excelero API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal to harvest.

companies.name: FUNDING.yml
companies.description: GitHub configuration file specifying funding platforms and links for project sponsorship, displayed as a Sponsor button on the repository page. Supports platforms including GitHub Sponsors, Patreon, Open Collective, Ko-fi, Liberapay, Tidelift, Buy Me a Coffee, IssueHunt, Polar, thanks.dev, LFX Mentorship, and custom URLs.

companies.name: Indoo Rs
companies.description: indoo.rs (indoo.rs GmbH) was a Vienna, Austria based Indoor Positioning System (IPS) startup founded in 2010 that built indoor mapping, localization, and routing technology plus a mobile SDK for developers and device manufacturers. Its solution combined Wi-Fi, BLE/iBeacon, sensor fusion, and dead-reckoning (SLAM-style) navigation to deliver real-time indoor positioning with accuracy down to roughly two meters. Backed early by Speedinvest, indoo.rs was acquired by Esri on February 28, 2019; its software became part of Esri's ArcGIS Indoors and its Vienna headquarters became the Esri R&D Center Vienna focused on IPS. The indoo.rs domain now redirects to the ArcGIS Indoors product, and the company no longer operates an independent public API or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Speedinvest portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

companies.name: Raft
companies.description: Raft is a consensus algorithm for distributed systems designed to be understandable and provide the same guarantees as Paxos, used for distributed log replication and leader election in fault-tolerant systems.

companies.name: SlideRule
companies.description: SlideRule is a no-code risk decisioning platform that lets risk and operations teams build, test, and deploy automated decision logic for fraud, credit, compliance, and trust-and-safety use cases without writing code. Its rules engine combines SQL and API data connectors, real-time analytics, A/B testing, backtesting, shadow mode, and case-management automation, and exposes a single API to trigger decision workflows. SlideRule has announced it is joining Block, Inc.; its standalone developer documentation surface (docs.sliderule.io) is no longer publicly reachable, so no live API specification could be harvested during enrichment.

companies.name: SpringSource
companies.description: SpringSource was the software company behind the open-source Spring Framework for Java. Founded in 2004 as Interface21 by Rod Johnson and colleagues, it was venture-backed (Accel, Benchmark) and acquired by VMware in 2009. The Spring portfolio subsequently moved through Pivotal and VMware Tanzu and is maintained today by Broadcom. The springsource.com domain now 301-redirects to spring.io, the current home of the Spring ecosystem. SpringSource exposed no standalone public API of its own; this profile documents the historical company and its lineage into today's Spring projects.

companies.name: WeaveAPI - OpenAI-compatible AI API Gateway
companies.description: WeaveAPI is an OpenAI-compatible /v1 gateway for calling supported model families (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax) through a clean OpenAI-compatible API. Keep your SDK, change the base URL, and manage keys, balance, usage, and top-ups in a hosted console. Prepaid pay-as-you-go pricing with a $1 signup credit.

companies.name: HAMI
companies.description: HAMI (Heterogeneous AI Computing Virtualization Middleware) is an open-source project that enables GPU virtualization and sharing for Kubernetes workloads, allowing multiple AI containers to share GPU resources efficiently.

companies.name: Moven
companies.description: Moven (Movencorp Newco Inc.) is a New York City fintech founded in 2011 by Brett King and Alex Sion. Originally a direct-to-consumer mobile banking and financial-wellness app, the company pivoted in 2020 to a business-to-business model, licensing its spending-analytics and financial-wellness technology to banks, credit unions, and other fintechs through open APIs and SDKs. Its data-driven engagement modules power companion and challenger-bank experiences such as TD Bank's MySpend and Westpac's CashNav. Moven's API and SDK surface is partner-gated behind a demo/sandbox request rather than a self-serve public developer portal, so no public OpenAPI, reference documentation, or GitHub organization is available for catalog harvesting.

companies.name: AltexSoft
companies.description: AltexSoft is a technology and solution consulting company that provides software development and IT consulting services to businesses across various industries. Specializing in travel and hospitality, healthcare, and finance sectors, AltexSoft helps companies design, build, and implement innovative technology solutions to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experience, and drive business growth.

companies.name: Axera Tech
companies.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.name: Bsquare
companies.description: Bsquare is an IoT and edge-software company known for Windows IoT device licensing, OS consulting (Windows, Linux, Android), device management, and its DataV IoT analytics and SquareOne data platform. Bsquare was acquired by Kontron; the bsquare.com domain now 301-redirects to www.kontron-americas.com, and the Bsquare brand operates as part of Kontron's connected-device software portfolio serving healthcare, avionics, energy, manufacturing, logistics, transportation, and hospitality. No independent public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile carries the honest enrichment of the domain's live security and DNS posture.

companies.name: CIX Technology
companies.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

companies.name: Daqstra
companies.description: Daqstra is an AI-native operating platform for complex test infrastructure, giving aerospace, energy, and robotics teams observability and orchestration for the physical world. The platform connects data-acquisition hardware (National Instruments, PLCs, and custom equipment) at the edge, centralizes and versions test data in the cloud, and orchestrates hardware sequences and test logic as code through Python and REST APIs. Daqstra Edge streams live signals from physical hardware, Daqstra Hub (Strata Hub) organizes test-campaign data with AI-powered insight, and the Daqstra API lets engineers drive test runs programmatically instead of through manual CSV workflows. The company was founded by aerospace-propulsion and avionics engineers and is backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch).

companies.name: Digitalk
companies.description: Digitalk, Inc. was an American object-oriented software tools vendor and a Trinity Ventures portfolio company, best known for Smalltalk/V — a commercial Smalltalk development environment first released in 1986 for MS-DOS, preceded by "Digitalk Methods" in 1983. It was founded by George Bosworth, Jim Anderson, Mike Teng and Barbara Noparstak, and its product line grew into Visual Smalltalk Enterprise. In July 1995 Digitalk merged with its principal competitor ParcPlace Systems; the combined company was later renamed ObjectShare, announced a shift away from Smalltalk toward Java in 1997, and active development of the Digitalk line ended shortly after. The final release, Visual Smalltalk Enterprise 2000, shipped in September 2000. Cincom retains the right to sell and support VSE 2000 for existing licensees and Seagull Software owns the virtual machine. Digitalk predates the public web API era and operates no developer platform, public API, or live web presence today; this profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Event-Driven Architecture
companies.description: Event-driven architecture (EDA) is a software architecture pattern promoting the production, detection, consumption of, and reaction to events. In this pattern, systems are designed to respond to state changes asynchronously through event messages. EDA enables loose coupling between services and is widely used in microservices, real-time data processing, and distributed systems. Foundational specifications include AsyncAPI for describing event-driven APIs and CNCF CloudEvents for a common event format.

companies.name: Fleksy
companies.description: Fleksy (Thingthing Ltd) was a keyboard technology company that built a mobile Keyboard SDK — a white-label, privacy-focused typing engine that iOS and Android developers could embed in their own apps. The SDK provided autocorrect, next-word prediction, swipe/gesture typing, customizable themes, and a plugin system, and the Fleksy keyboard once held Guinness World Records for the fastest typing. Fleksy distributed a native mobile SDK rather than a public web/REST API, so it exposes no OpenAPI, GraphQL, or hosted developer portal. Backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest, the company's public web presence (fleksy.com, docs.fleksy.com, fleksy.dev) no longer resolves and the business appears defunct; this profile captures the surviving public artifact — the first-party FleksySDK CocoaPods pod for iOS.

companies.name: Fritz.ai
companies.description: Fritz.ai was a Boston-based mobile, on-device machine learning platform, backed by Uncork Capital, that gave iOS and Android developers SDKs plus a hosted service for training, deploying, and managing ML models directly on devices. That original developer platform has since wound down, and the fritz.ai domain now hosts an unrelated AI-tools review and ranking content site (guides, glossary, interviews, and tool comparisons) with no public API, SDK, or developer program. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Uncork Capital portfolio graph and is retained as a historical company record; no live API surface was found during enrichment.

companies.name: Macromedia
companies.description: Macromedia was a developer-tools and interactive-media software company (Flash, Dreamweaver, ColdFusion, Shockwave, Director, Fireworks) surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and kleiner-perkins. Adobe acquired Macromedia in 2005; www.macromedia.com now 301-redirects to www.adobe.com and the domain serves Adobe's canonical security.txt / PSIRT disclosure surface. This profile is a legacy company lead in the API Evangelist network with no independent live API surface of its own.

companies.name: Micro-Service Architecture Patterns
companies.description: Design patterns and best practices for building distributed systems using microservices architecture, including service decomposition, communication patterns, data management, and deployment strategies.

companies.name: Nubity
companies.description: Nubity is an AWS Premier Tier cloud consulting and managed services provider serving enterprises across Latin America, with operations in Mexico and Argentina. It helps organizations modernize legacy systems, migrate to and build cloud-native applications on AWS, deploy cloud contact centers and GenAI and business-intelligence solutions, run managed services and DevOps practices, apply Well-Architected cost optimization, and strengthen cloud security and business continuity. Nubity is a professional-services firm and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: eBPF Foundation
companies.description: The eBPF Foundation is a Linux Foundation project that advances eBPF technology by guiding upstream development, promoting its benefits, and enhancing its security and reliability. eBPF enables programmable kernel functionality for networking, observability, tracing, and security without changing kernel source code. The Foundation itself does not operate a public API; it stewards the technology and community.

companies.name: .Gitignore
companies.description: Git configuration file specifying intentionally untracked files and directories that Git should ignore, preventing build artifacts, dependencies, and secrets from being committed.

companies.name: Cerrion
companies.description: Cerrion builds enterprise-grade video AI agents for manufacturing. Its platform connects to existing or provided factory cameras to monitor production lines in real time, using pre-trained visual triggers to automatically detect and respond to quality defects, safety hazards, process deviations, and equipment issues. The closed-loop system can slow or stop machines, raise alarms, and escalate alerts while giving operators root-cause insight, helping manufacturers resolve problems up to 50% faster and cut downtime and scrap. Cerrion is deployed in live production across glass, food & beverage, tableware, sawmilling/timber, and CPG environments (customers include Unilever, Riedel, Schott Zwiesel, Stölzle Lausitz, Sisecam, and Verallia). Zurich-based and backed by Creandum, Y Combinator, Goat Capital, 10x Founders, and Session VC. No public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Empirix
companies.description: Empirix was a communications and contact-center test, assurance, and monitoring company backed by Matrix Partners. Its products spanned network and application performance testing, VoIP and IVR quality assurance, contact-center monitoring, and end-to-end customer-experience assurance for carriers and enterprises. Empirix was acquired by Infovista in 2020; its testing and monitoring portfolio now operates under the Hammer Technologies brand, which is evolving into VistaCX (Voice Explorer, CallMaster, VoiceWatch, HammerRTC, VistaOne). The company exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal; empirix.com now redirects to hammer.com. This profile is a network stub enriched from public web surfaces only.

companies.name: Airbrite
companies.description: Airbrite was an early commerce-infrastructure startup (a16z portfolio) that offered a hosted order-management and payments/commerce backend API for merchants and developers, with JavaScript and Python client SDKs and an embeddable checkout. The product was later rebranded and pivoted to "Celery" (pre-order / crowdfunding commerce). Airbrite is now defunct: its primary developer domains (airbrite.io, getairbrite.com) no longer resolve and airbrite.com is a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, API reference, or hosted API to enrich. What remains verifiable is the public github.com/airbrite organization and the client libraries still published on npm and PyPI. This profile records that residual, evidence-backed surface; most enrichment artifact types are legitimately empty because the provider no longer operates.

companies.name: Aptera
companies.description: Aptera (Aptera Software, Inc.) was a custom software development consultancy based in Fort Wayne, Indiana, founded in 2003 and specializing in the Microsoft stack — .NET, SharePoint, Azure, business intelligence, and web and mobile application development, plus legacy application modernization, DevOps, UI/UX design, quality assurance, and security and compliance services for enterprise clients. It employed more than 100 people and was the largest web development firm in northeast Indiana before being acquired by IT services provider Core BTS on June 30, 2021, after which it ceased to operate as an independent brand. Battery Ventures lists "Aptera, Inc." on its all-companies page as an exited investment, which is how this record entered the API Evangelist network. Aptera was a services firm rather than an API producer: enrichment found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDK, webhook surface, or MCP server. Its only surviving public technical footprint is a GitHub organization of engineering-practice repositories (coding katas and workshop material).

companies.name: Augtera Networks
companies.description: Augtera Networks is an AI-native networking (Network AIOps) company founded in 2016 and based in Palo Alto, California. Its Network AI platform ingests telemetry from network devices, applies machine-learning anomaly detection (including gray failures), eliminates noise, performs incident root-cause identification, noiseless ticket creation, and auto-mitigation/remediation for data-center and enterprise networks. The platform exposed a Topology REST API for device discovery/lifecycle and DevOps/ITSM integration. Augtera was acquired by NVIDIA in December 2024 and folded into the NVIDIA Spectrum-X networking portfolio; its standalone augtera.com site now 301-redirects to nvidia.com, so no independent public developer/API surface remains. Added to the API Evangelist network as a bain-capital-ventures portfolio lead.

companies.name: Binpress
companies.description: Binpress was a marketplace for commercial source code and open-source software components, founded in 2011 in Israel by Adam Benayoun (CEO) and Eran Galperin (CTO) and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global). The platform let developers publish, discover, buy, and sell SDKs, libraries, and code components on a 70/30 revenue split, growing to roughly 1,000 listings with GitHub integration and later adding hosted storefronts for digital goods. The company was acquired by CodersClan in 2016 and no longer operates as an active developer platform; the binpress.com domain has since been repurposed as an unrelated digital-business content site with no public API. This profile originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead surfaced into the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Bouffalo Lab
companies.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

companies.name: Bump
companies.description: Bump Technologies was a Mountain View, California mobile software company (2008-2014) behind Bump, an iOS and Android app that let two people exchange contacts, photos and files by physically bumping their phones together. Bump servers correlated accelerometer, location and network signals from two handsets to match the pair, then brokered the transfer. The company published a first-party Bump API and iOS/Android SDKs so third-party apps could embed the same proximity-matching handshake. Backed by Y Combinator, Sequoia Capital and a $16M Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz in January 2011, Bump was acquired by Google in September 2013 and both the app and its developer API were discontinued on January 31, 2014. The company's bu.mp domain still serves its shutdown notice and the archived SDK repositories remain public under the bumptech GitHub organization; there is no live API surface.

companies.name: CoreOS
companies.description: CoreOS was a San Francisco-based container infrastructure company founded in 2013 that built a lightweight, automatically-updating Linux distribution (Container Linux, originally CoreOS Linux) and a family of now-foundational cloud-native open source projects: etcd (the distributed key-value store at the heart of Kubernetes), the Quay container registry, the Tectonic enterprise Kubernetes platform, the rkt container engine, flannel networking, Clair image-vulnerability scanning, and Ignition provisioning. Red Hat acquired CoreOS in January 2018 for approximately $250 million. Its technologies were folded into Red Hat's portfolio — Container Linux became Red Hat CoreOS and the community Fedora CoreOS, Tectonic merged into OpenShift, Quay continues as Red Hat Quay, and etcd and rkt were donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The company no longer operates independently; coreos.com redirects to Red Hat OpenShift. The github.com/coreos organization remains active as the upstream home for Fedora CoreOS components such as Ignition, Butane, and fleetlock.

companies.name: Dashbase
companies.description: Dashbase, Inc. was a San Jose, California based developer of a next-generation log analytics and search platform, positioned as a lighter, real-time alternative to heavier log-management and observability stacks for DevOps and engineering teams. The company was a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (dashbase.io) no longer resolves / times out and its GitHub organization retains only a single archived fork, so the company appears to be defunct or to have been acquired and wound down; no live developer surface, API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation could be located. This profile is retained as a network record with only verifiable facts.

companies.name: Distelli
companies.description: Distelli was a Seattle-based DevOps and application-deployment company founded in 2013 by Rahul Singh and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It offered a SaaS platform and command-line tooling for building, deploying, and managing applications across servers and cloud infrastructure, later adding a Docker container pipeline and a Kubernetes (K8s) dashboard for managing container clusters. Puppet acquired Distelli in September 2017 and rebranded its products — the VM/CI-CD dashboard became Puppet Pipelines for Applications and the Kubernetes dashboard became Puppet Pipelines for Containers. The standalone Distelli company, product, and API no longer operate: the distelli.com domain is parked and the Distelli GitHub organization is archived and explicitly "no longer supported nor actively maintained." This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record (a16z) in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: ElasticBox
companies.description: ElasticBox was a multi-cloud application management and deployment platform founded in 2011 by former Microsoft engineers Alberto Arias Maestro, Amadeo Casas, and Ravi Srivatsav (AngelPad-backed, offices in San Francisco and Madrid). Its "boxes" model let enterprise IT define, version, and orchestrate application deployments across more than a dozen clouds — AWS, Microsoft Azure, IBM SoftLayer, VMware, vCloud Air and others — with a self-service catalog, a REST API (token-authenticated, JSON), and a Jenkins CI plug-in. The company raised roughly $12.4M across three rounds, including a $9M Series A in 2014 with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Nexus Venture Partners, Intel Capital and Sierra Ventures. CenturyLink acquired ElasticBox in June 2016 and rebuilt the technology as CenturyLink Cloud Application Manager (now part of Lumen). The standalone ElasticBox product, its developer portal, and its public API documentation have been retired; the elasticbox.com domain no longer serves the platform. This profile is preserved as a historical portfolio-lead record — no live, first-party API surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: Engine ML
companies.description: Engine ML was a machine-learning infrastructure startup (founded 2018, backed by Kleiner Perkins) that offered a hosted platform for distributed model training and experiment tracking. Its product surface centered on the `engine` command-line tool and the `eml` Python library, which let data scientists launch experiments, track code, system utilization, logs, and output files, and run image classifiers (PyTorch/TensorFlow/Keras) against datasets such as MNIST. The company appears to be defunct: engineml.com serves an empty page behind an expired TLS certificate (expired March 2023), the documentation site docs.engineml.com returns an empty S3 bucket, and the public GitHub organization (EngineML) has not been updated since 2020-2021. No live API, OpenAPI description, package-registry release, or reachable developer docs could be found. This profile preserves the historical identity and the still- live GitHub organization as the only verifiable surviving surface.

companies.name: Fimio
companies.description: Fimio was a developer-tooling startup founded in 2022 in Oakland, California by Omoju Miller (formerly of Google and GitHub). Its first product was an ML-trained fraud-detection / malicious-smart-contract reputation API for Web3 builders (Ethereum), with data supported by Spice AI, released as an alpha. The company later repositioned around "collaborative tooling for serverful applications" and "reproducible builds made easy." Fimio appears to be defunct: as of the enrichment probe both fimio.xyz and www.fimio.xyz 302-redirect to google.com, the docs/api subdomains do not resolve, the blog returns 404, and the GitHub organization (fimio-xyz) was archived on 2026-01-27 with only Careers and feedback repositories and no published API artifacts. It was backed by a ~$2.19M seed led by Neo with Redpoint Ventures, Protocol Labs, The House Fund and angel investors.

companies.name: General Galactic Corporation
companies.description: General Galactic Corporation was an early-stage web3 studio founded by Rob Mee (founder of Pivotal Labs) and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It built open-source Ethereum developer tooling published under the generalgalactic GitHub organization, including eip4361-tools for Sign-In With Ethereum (EIP-4361), the ERC721Sequential (ERC721S) gas-optimized NFT contract, an ENS registry (skyteller-ens-registry), and related SIWE authentication utilities. The company wound down its products and experiments in 2023; its site now runs as an ENS/IPFS page announcing the closure. This profile catalogs the remaining public open-source and package footprint. No hosted or public API is currently operated by the company.

companies.name: Gestoos
companies.description: Gestoos was a computer-vision company that built a real-time gesture-recognition and touchless-interaction SDK, letting developers add camera-based hand-gesture and motion control to interactive installations, digital signage, kiosks, and embedded devices. Its public developer surface centered on an interactive SDK with sample integrations (including bindings for the Cinder C++ creative-coding framework). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment its primary web presence at gestoos.com is offline — the domain no longer resolves to the company and now redirects to an unrelated parked site — and the only surviving public developer asset is the gestoos GitHub organization, whose most recent activity dates to 2020. This profile is retained as a historical network record; the API/SDK product appears discontinued.

companies.name: Gigacatalyst
companies.description: Gigacatalyst is a Y Combinator-backed enterprise AI platform that turns customer requirements into configured software demos, POCs, UAT environments, and implementation workspaces by writing real configurations through a customer's existing product APIs. It embeds an AI customization layer directly into SaaS applications so that sales, solutions-engineering, and customer-success teams can build the missing features and workflows they need using natural language, while inheriting the host product's authentication and role-based access controls, sandboxed execution, and AI model restrictions. Gigacatalyst is an API consumer: it operates on top of other providers' APIs rather than publishing its own public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Heptio
companies.description: Heptio was a Seattle-based cloud-native software company founded in 2016 by Craig McLuckie and Joe Beda, two of the original co-creators of Kubernetes, to help enterprises adopt and operate Kubernetes. It built a suite of widely used open-source Kubernetes tools including Ark (later renamed Velero) for backup and restore, Sonobuoy for conformance testing, Contour as an Envoy-based ingress controller, ksonnet, and Gimbal. Heptio was acquired by VMware in November 2018 and folded into the VMware Tanzu portfolio; the company brand was retired and most of its open-source projects were migrated from the github.com/heptio organization to github.com/vmware-tanzu. This profile is preserved as a historical/defunct-company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Micro
companies.description: Micro is an open source project building a Go framework and runtime for cloud-native services and AI agents. Its flagship library, go-micro (go-micro.dev/v6), provides pluggable abstractions for service discovery, RPC transport, message brokering, and configuration, and is described by the project as a Go agent harness and service framework. Micro is developed in the open on GitHub under the micro organization. The micro.dev site is a minimal landing page rather than a hosted developer portal, and the project ships no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, developer console, or SaaS control plane at this time.

companies.name: MoPub
companies.description: MoPub was a mobile advertising and app-monetization platform providing ad-network mediation, advanced bidding, and a real-time marketplace/exchange plus open-source iOS and Android SDKs for mobile publishers. Founded in 2010, it was acquired by Twitter in 2013, then sold to AppLovin for $1.05B in a deal that closed January 2022. AppLovin migrated publishers to its MAX platform and shut down MoPub's mediation, advanced bidding, and marketplace on 2022-03-31, with dashboard/reporting retired by 2022-04-30. MoPub is now defunct: www.mopub.com redirects to applovin.com and the developer/API surface (developers.mopub.com) is offline. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct record; there is no live MoPub API to enrich.

companies.name: NODA AI
companies.description: NODA AI is a defense-technology company building autonomous force orchestration for the frontlines. Founded in 2024 in Austin, Texas by Global War on Terrorism veterans, it develops URZA, an AI-native strategic orchestration platform that acts as a tactics repository and reasoning engine for real-time task brokering across vendor-agnostic, mixed-fleet autonomous assets, integrated with 30+ OEM vehicles and control systems from subsurface to space; and LARIA, a synthetic weapons-and-tactics training environment that uses digital-twin modeling to develop and test autonomous plays. In February 2026 the company raised a $25M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners to serve the U.S. Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the UK Ministry of Defense. NODA AI is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Bloomberg Beta. It publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; its GitHub organization holds no public repositories.

companies.name: Nodejitsu
companies.description: Nodejitsu Inc. was a cloud Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) for hosting and deploying Node.js applications, founded in New York in April 2010 by Charlie Robbins, Marak Squires, and Paolo Fragomeni. It offered a `jitsu` command-line deployment tool and an application hosting platform, and stewarded popular open-source Node.js projects (forever, jitsu, flatiron, haibu, node-http-proxy). GoDaddy acquired Nodejitsu in February 2015 and wound down the PaaS the same year, directing customers to migrate elsewhere. The company is defunct - the nodejitsu.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live API surface; only the archived GitHub organization survives.

companies.name: Optimyze
companies.description: Optimyze (Optimyze.cloud Inc.) was a Zurich, Switzerland based continuous-profiling startup, seeded by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) in 2020, and the maker of Prodfiler — a whole-system, eBPF-based continuous profiler that observed CPU and memory usage down to the individual line of code across C/C++, Rust, Go, PHP, Python, Java, Scala, Ruby and Perl, with roughly 1% CPU overhead and no source-code changes or on-host debug symbols. Optimyze was acquired by Elastic N.V. in October 2021 and its Prodfiler technology was folded into Elastic Observability as Elastic Universal Profiling. The independent company no longer operates: the optimyze.cloud domain no longer resolves, the GitHub organization was archived in 2024, and the Prodfiler developer sub-sites (documentation, app, community) are offline. No independent public Optimyze API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal exists to enrich; this profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

companies.name: Rome Tools
companies.description: Rome Tools, Inc. was the company behind Rome, a unified, Rust-based developer toolchain for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, HTML, Markdown, and CSS, intended to consolidate the roles of a formatter, linter, compiler, and bundler (replacing tools like Babel, ESLint, webpack, and Prettier) into a single fast tool. Rome shipped as a command-line tool and VS Code extension rather than as a hosted web service, so it has no REST/HTTP API, OpenAPI, webhook, or event surface. The project's GitHub repository (github.com/rome/tools) was archived on 2026-07-21 as read-only, the rome.tools domain no longer resolves, and the effort has been succeeded by the community-maintained Biome project (biomejs.dev). Rome Tools was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms it is a defunct open-source CLI toolchain with no API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Snaproute
companies.description: SnapRoute was a cloud-native networking startup, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Norwest Venture Partners, that built a containerized, microservices-based network operating system (its FlexSwitch / Cloud-Native Network OS) aimed at running switch software with the same DevOps tooling used for application infrastructure. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/snaproute) reflects that focus — OpenConfig and YANG tooling (pyang/pyangbind), OpenNetworkLinux, netlink, sFlow, and a Docker-based training lab — but it has been dormant since 2020 and ships no published REST/OpenAPI interface, SDKs, or developer portal. The company no longer operates independently: the snaproute.com domain now 301-redirects to infoblox.com, so there is no live API surface to enrich. This profile records the verifiable remnants (GitHub organization, domain posture) rather than a working developer program.

companies.name: Thundra
companies.description: Thundra was an application observability and security platform for serverless, container, and VM workloads, best known for AWS Lambda monitoring and debugging. Its products included Thundra APM (distributed tracing), Sidekick (remote debugging), and Foresight (CI pipeline test observability). Founded in 2018 out of OpsGenie and backed by Battery Ventures, its assets were acquired by Catchpoint in April 2023 and the service has been discontinued — thundra.io now redirects to Catchpoint's acquisition announcement and the GitHub organization states "Thundra is no longer in service." Its open-source agents and plugins remain published on npm, PyPI, Maven Central, NuGet, and pkg.go.dev.

companies.name: Twirl
