companies.description: Twirl is a data platform and orchestrator that lets teams build data products faster by combining BigQuery, dbt, Python, and Google Cloud services (GCS, Dataflow) in a single git-backed project. Backed by Creandum. As of July 2026 the twirldata.com website and docs.twirldata.com both return 404 (GitHub Pages) and no public API surface is available; the remaining public artifacts are the twirldata GitHub org (twirl-examples) and a placeholder PyPI package (twirldata 0.0.0, "Client SDK for the Twirl data platform").

companies.name: uberVU
companies.description: uberVU was a social media analytics and monitoring company, backed by Seedcamp, that offered brand-insight dashboards and a metrics API before being acquired by Hootsuite in 2014. The company no longer operates independently - ubervu.com now 301-redirects to blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-analytics/, its former metrics API is retired, and its GitHub organization is dormant. This profile is kept as a historical record of a VC-portfolio company with no current public API surface.

companies.name: Utopia
companies.description: Utopia was an online platform for designing, coding, and shipping React applications, pairing a visual design tool with a code editor over one source of truth. A 2020 Seedcamp portfolio company, it was built in the open as the MIT-licensed concrete-utopia/utopia monorepo (3.8k stars) with a first-party utopia-api npm library. The project has been dormant since mid-2025, utopia.app now serves a parked placeholder page, and no network API was ever published.

companies.name: Wupima
companies.description: Wupima, Inc. was a Virginia-based mobile social intelligence company that did business as Hook Mobile, backed by 500 Global (500 Startups). Its App Growth Engine (AGE) product offered iOS and Android SDKs and an API that let mobile app and game developers grow their user base through word-of-mouth SMS/MMS social invitations, device targeting, and conversion analytics. The company, founded by Terry Hsiao, was active roughly 2010-2016 and is now defunct - wupima.com is a dead S3 bucket (403 AllAccessDisabled) and hookmobile.com has been taken over by an unrelated domain squatter serving spam, so no live website, developer portal, or API surface remains. Profile retained as a historical 500 Global portfolio record.

companies.name: Aethero
companies.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: AI-Prime (Paidao Intelligence)
companies.description: AI-Prime (Paidao Intelligence / 湃道智能) is a Shanghai-based industrial-safety AI company founded in 2017 that builds computer-vision, deep-learning, and knowledge-graph platforms for high-hazard industries. Its full-stack products span an AI industrial-safety monitoring cloud platform, 40+ safety-scenario models (PPE detection, unsafe behavior, equipment leaks, fire/smoke, work-process compliance), a self-learning AI model-development platform, and Prime-Edge smart hardware (edge-computing boxes, inspection robots, AR work mirrors, and edge cameras) serving the chemical, steel, coal, oil & gas, energy, and mining sectors. AI-Prime is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It is an enterprise B2B provider with no public developer API program; this profile captures its identity and web presence.

companies.name: BlackSky
companies.description: BlackSky Technology (NYSE: BKSY) is a Herndon, Virginia headquartered real-time space-based intelligence company that operates a high-revisit Earth observation constellation and delivers AI-enhanced tactical ISR (intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance) imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and global security customers. BlackSky's flagship product is the Spectra platform — a cloud-based intelligence hub that provides on-demand satellite tasking, sub-90-minute imagery delivery, automated AI-driven object detection and change monitoring, archived imagery access, and a secure tasking and delivery API. The company operates Gen-2 satellites at 83 cm resolution and a newer Gen-3 constellation delivering 35 cm class very-high-resolution imagery with infrared sensors, inter-satellite links, and on-board AI processing, manufactured at BlackSky's facility in Tukwila, Washington. Commercial offerings include BlackSky ON-DEMAND (flexible global tasking) and BlackSky ASSURED (dedicated, contracted persistent monitoring capacity). BlackSky's Spectra tasking and imagery API is integrated into partner platforms including Esri ArcGIS, UP42, and the STAT (Satellite Tasking API) community spec, however the API is access-controlled for vetted defense, intelligence, and enterprise customers and is not exposed as a public self-service developer portal — there is no public Spectra developer documentation site, OpenAPI specification, or open SDKs at the time of this entry. The customer revenue model is subscription-based Spectra ON-DEMAND and ASSURED contracts, Mission Solutions custom engagements, and through marketplace partners.

companies.name: Cerenovus
companies.description: Cerenovus (cerenovus.ai) is a San Francisco AI software company backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch), founded in 2026 by a team out of Harvard and NYU Stern. It builds "the AI company brain" — software that reads everything a company produces (email, chat, documents, CRM, ERP, tickets, meeting notes) and returns findings with citations back to the source. Its products are Noesis (the enterprise flagship company brain built for CEOs, CFOs, and private-equity operating partners), Midas (an AI sales platform that runs inside a company's existing CRM and is paid out of the revenue it produces), and Compendium (shared real-time context and durable memory for engineering and customer-facing teams and their AI agents, including shared Claude Code sessions). Cerenovus is not affiliated with the similarly named Johnson & Johnson MedTech neurovascular device business.

companies.name: Colony Capital (DigitalBridge Group)
companies.description: Colony Capital was a diversified real estate and hospitality investment firm founded by Tom Barrack in 1991. In June 2021 the company rebranded as DigitalBridge Group, Inc. (NYSE: DBRG) — completing a multi-year pivot from traditional real estate to pure-play digital infrastructure investing. The Boca Raton, FL-based alternative asset manager now operates exclusively across five digital infrastructure categories: data centers, macro cell towers, fiber networks, small cells, and edge infrastructure. DigitalBridge manages approximately $119B in assets across 45+ portfolio companies including Vantage Data Centers, DataBank, Switch, Vertical Bridge, Zayo Group, GD Towers, Boingo Wireless, AtlasEdge, Scala Data Centers, Yondr Group, and ExteNet Systems. In December 2025 SoftBank Group announced a definitive agreement to acquire DigitalBridge for approximately $4 billion, with the deal expected to close in the second half of 2026. DigitalBridge itself publishes no developer API, SDK, or public OpenAPI surface — it is a holding company whose programmable surface lives inside its individual portfolio companies (e.g., Zayo, DataBank, Switch), each of which is profiled separately in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Constelli
companies.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Docker Swarm
companies.description: Native clustering and orchestration solution for Docker containers that turns a pool of Docker hosts into a single virtual host. Docker Swarm enables deploying applications across multiple machines and provides high availability and load balancing for containerized workloads.

companies.name: Dockerfile
companies.description: A text file that contains instructions for building Docker container images, defining the application environment, dependencies, and configuration in a reproducible way. Dockerfiles accelerate software delivery cycles and improve collaboration between development and operations teams.

companies.name: effx
companies.description: effx was a San Francisco developer-tools startup, founded in 2018 by Joey Parsons, that built a modern microservice catalog to help engineering teams navigate and operate microservices architectures — tracking service ownership, cataloging services, enforcing service standards, tracking migrations, and supporting incident response. The company raised a $3.9M seed round led by Kleiner Perkins alongside Cowboy Ventures. effx was acquired by Figma in 2021; the product was shut down and the team joined Figma's engineering organization. effx.com is now an acquisition/farewell notice and there is no live API, developer documentation, SDK, or public source surface to enrich.

companies.name: Fox-Tech
companies.description: FOX-TECH CO. is a New Taipei City, Taiwan IoT company (founded 2016, backed by 500 Global and SparkLabs Taipei) that digitally transforms farming, logistics, cold-chain, and manufacturing operations. Its TempHawk platform pairs wireless temperature, humidity, CO2, light-intensity and soil-EC sensors over Sigfox LPWAN with web and mobile apps and cloud data analytics, helping the perishable-goods value chain monitor conditions, manage risk, and meet policy compliance. Recognized on the Forward Fooding FoodTech 500. No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published.

companies.name: Instaplay
companies.description: Instaplay is an AI-native social gaming platform that turns plain-text prompts into playable multiplayer games with no coding required. Users describe a game idea in natural language ("a two-player pong game where paddles shrink after every point") and the platform generates a playable prototype that can be tested, remixed, and shared via link within seconds. It supports party, co-op, competitive, local, online, and solo formats. Founded in San Francisco and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch, Instaplay frames games as a training ground for world models and embodied agents on the path to AGI.

companies.name: Monolith AI
companies.description: Monolith AI develops artificial-intelligence software for engineering product development, helping R&D and test-lab teams validate physical products faster. Its cloud SaaS platform pairs a notebook-style workspace with proprietary self-learning models built for engineers: a Test Data Validation module whose anomaly detector flags errors across hundreds of data channels, a Test Plan Optimisation module whose next-test recommender can cut test plans by up to 70%, and a System Calibration module that tunes performance across operating conditions. It serves battery, automotive, aerospace and defense, and industrial and medical engineering teams. Monolith AI is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. No public developer API, portal, or SDKs are published at this time.

companies.name: Owens-Illinois (O-I Glass)
companies.description: Owens-Illinois (now O-I Glass) is one of the world's leading manufacturers of glass containers, supplying glass packaging to the food, beverage, beer, wine, spirits, and pharmaceutical industries. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

companies.name: PhishMe
companies.description: PhishMe is a phishing defense and security awareness company founded in 2011 by Rohyt Belani and Aaron Higbee, and rebranded as Cofense in 2018 following its acquisition by a private-equity consortium. The company pioneered simulated-phishing training and crowd-sourced phishing detection, and today operates the Cofense phishing-defense platform spanning Phishing Detection and Response (PDR), security awareness training, managed phishing defense, and threat intelligence. Originally backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead. The company markets a connected, AI-assisted platform for post-perimeter phishing remediation rather than a public developer API; product, integration, and threat-intelligence capabilities are surfaced through customer and partner channels.

companies.name: /dev/agents
companies.description: /dev/agents (homepage sdsa.ai) is building a next-generation operating system for AI agents - a cloud platform, developer tools, and new UI primitives meant to let autonomous agents coordinate work across a user's apps and devices instead of people navigating individual applications. It was founded in 2024 by David Singleton (former Stripe CTO and Google Android VP of Engineering), Hugo Barra, Ficus Kirkpatrick, and Nicholas Jitkoff, and raised a $56M seed round at a $500M valuation led by Index Ventures with CapitalG and Conviction. As of this profile the company is pre-launch: it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation yet, so this API Evangelist entry captures verified company identity and domain posture only.

companies.name: /dev/fast
companies.description: /dev/fast is an AI-native code forge — code review, deployment infrastructure, and hosting rebuilt for the AI era. The product reframes code hosting, review, and CI/CD around software written and shipped by agents: an RFC-style review surface optimized for human taste and judgement, a multi-agent software factory that dispatches, supervises, and merges work from many cloud agents, agent-native CI/CD where the agent writes declarative pipeline code testable locally, and a fine-grained permission system, with every agent run captured and replayable. Founded in 2025, /dev/fast is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company based in San Francisco, currently invite-only. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from its public surface; no public API, developer documentation, or machine-readable specification is published yet.

companies.name: Aemon
companies.description: Aemon is an autonomous AI research-and-development engineer founded in 2025 by Ray Xu and Richard Zhou and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Given an engineering problem and a measurable objective, Aemon reads state-of-the-art research, then generates, tests, and evolves thousands of candidate approaches at machine speed to discover optimal solutions that can exceed what human experts find. The team demonstrated the approach by setting a new world record on the NP-hard circle-packing optimization problem for under $10 of compute, beating a prior Google DeepMind result. Aemon is an early-stage, demo-first enterprise product headquartered in San Francisco; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

companies.name: AirKit
companies.description: AirKit (Airkit.ai) was a low-code platform for building customer-facing digital experiences and, later, AI-powered customer service agents, backed by Accel and Emergence Capital. The company was acquired by Salesforce (announced 2023) and its technology now underpins Salesforce Agentforce. As of this enrichment pass, www.airkit.com 301-redirects to salesforce.com/agentforce and the domain's CAA records point to salesforce.com, so AirKit no longer operates an independent developer surface, API, documentation, or portal of its own — all first-party discovery URLs resolve into Salesforce properties. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; enrichment beyond domain-level DNS/TLS evidence is not applicable.

companies.name: Airplane
companies.description: Airplane was a Benchmark-backed developer platform for building internal tools, dashboards, and operational workflows by turning scripts into shareable tasks and UIs. It was acquired by Airtable in 2023 and the product was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct: the website www.airplane.dev no longer connects, the airplane.dev apex resolves to a domain-parking IP, and the airplanedev GitHub organization was archived on 2026-02-03 with no public repositories. No live API, developer portal, documentation host, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: Amberpoint
companies.description: AmberPoint was an enterprise software company founded in 2001 that provided runtime management, monitoring, and governance solutions for Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) and distributed web-services applications. Its products let organizations discover, secure, monitor, and enforce policy across complex multi-application business processes and message flows, and competed in the SOA management space alongside vendors integrated into enterprise middleware stacks. AmberPoint was acquired by Oracle on February 8, 2010, with its technology folded into Oracle Fusion Middleware and Oracle Enterprise Manager. The company no longer operates independently; the amberpoint.com domain is held by Oracle and no longer serves a public developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record surfaced from a venture-capital portfolio.

companies.name: Amixr.io
companies.description: Amixr was an incident-response and on-call management startup that provided alerting, escalation, and on-call scheduling for engineering and DevOps teams, integrating with monitoring stacks such as Grafana and Prometheus. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Grafana Labs in December 2021 and its product was folded into Grafana OnCall (now part of Grafana IRM). The standalone amixr.io product and developer surface have been retired; the domain no longer serves an active website, developer portal, or API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record following enrichment.

companies.name: Anon
companies.description: Anon is an enterprise AI agent platform that builds production-ready AI agents for companies. Its offerings include computer-use agents that automate long-running browser workflows, hosted web agents that perform tasks across multiple systems, and an agent authentication toolkit that gives developers tools to authenticate agents across third-party services. Originally positioned as an automated authentication layer for the gen-AI age, Anon has raised $14M from Forerunner Ventures, Union Square Ventures, and Abstract Ventures. As of this profile the company does not publish a public self-serve API, SDK, developer portal, or MCP server; engagements are handled directly (hello@anon.com).

companies.name: API Fortress
companies.description: API Fortress was an API testing and monitoring platform that let engineering teams author, run, and continuously monitor functional and integration tests against REST and SOAP APIs, in the cloud or via an on-premise Docker-based agent. It was acquired by Sauce Labs in January 2020 and its capabilities were folded into the Sauce Labs API Testing product. The standalone apifortress.com developer surface has since been retired; as of this enrichment pass the domain no longer resolves (parked Route53 nameservers, no A records), the apifortress GitHub organization returns 404, and there is no live first-party API, docs, SDK, or well-known surface remaining to enrich.

companies.name: Aporeto
companies.description: Aporeto was a zero trust cloud security company providing machine identity-based microsegmentation, a distributed firewall, and Kubernetes network security for hybrid and multi-cloud application workloads. Backed by DCVC and Wing Venture Capital, Aporeto was acquired by Palo Alto Networks in December 2019 (~$150M) and its identity-based microsegmentation platform was folded into Prisma Cloud. The company no longer operates an independent product, brand, or developer surface; aporeto.com now redirects to Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Cloud. This profile is retained as a network record of the acquired company; no standalone API, developer portal, or specification surface exists to enrich.

companies.name: AppBistro
companies.description: AppBistro, operated by MMTG Labs, was an application marketplace for the Facebook Pages platform that let brands and page administrators discover, install, and manage third-party apps to boost engagement and reach on their fan pages. It also built AppGalleries, a white-label app-store platform. A TechCrunch Disrupt 2010 finalist, the San Francisco startup raised a $550K convertible note (Sand Hill Angels, 500 Startups, i/o Ventures, Zelkova Ventures, Seraph Group, and angels including Alfred Lin) and was acquired by mobile ad network InMobi on 2012-07-13, after which the product and its five-person team (co-founders Ryan Merket and Nalin Mittal) wound down. The company is defunct and appbistro.com no longer resolves; no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists to enrich.

companies.name: Appurify
companies.description: Appurify was a mobile app and website testing platform that let developers automate testing and optimization of native and web apps on real iOS and Android devices across OS versions and simulated network conditions. Founded and backed by DCVC and GV, Appurify was acquired by Google in June 2014 and its technology was folded into Firebase Test Lab (formerly Google Cloud Test Lab). The company no longer operates independently; the appurify.com domain now redirects to the Firebase Test Lab documentation and Appurify's standalone developer API and product have been discontinued.

companies.name: Arilinc
companies.description: Aril Inc. (Arilinc) is a fabless semiconductor company in Los Gatos, California designing efficient AI processors and memory technology for edge inference. Its two core products are the Aril Standard Cell Memory, a patented on-chip memory offering roughly 40% lower active power and 3.6x smaller area, and a scalable RISC-V-based AI Processor Engine delivering hundreds of TOPS of inference per block with integrated vector and matrix engines. The company targets robotics, industrial automation, drones, defense and aerospace, autonomous vehicles, and edge vision systems where power efficiency is critical. Founded by a team of engineers who have collectively shipped 20M+ processors and worked on silicon for Cisco, Intel, AMD, and Google. Arilinc sells custom silicon and IP to hardware makers rather than a public developer API; it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

companies.name: Audos
companies.description: Audos is a New York-based AI-native startup studio and "publishing house for everyday entrepreneurs," founded in 2024 by Henrik Werdelin and Nicholas Thorne (the team behind Prehype, BarkBox, Ro, and Managed by Q). It helps non-technical solo founders turn expertise into million-dollar AI businesses, giving them AI-powered business-building tools, up to $25,000 in funding, and paid-social distribution in exchange for a ~15% revenue share, aiming to launch startups at massive scale. Audos raised an $11.5M seed round led by True Ventures (with backing from Niklas Zennstrom) and acquired No Cap. Its product surface is a consumer/entrepreneur web platform; the api.audos.com backend is private and auth-gated, with no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Axon
companies.description: Axon is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building real-time predictive intelligence on a brain-inspired architecture. Its approach centers on small, efficient "world models" that learn continuously on-device rather than depending on large models or the cloud, giving an edge-first design lower latency and lower cost. The initial focus is high-frequency trading and capital markets, where real-time prediction is decisive, with future applications targeted at wearables, edge devices, and robotics. Axon is backed by Northzone, Concept Ventures, a16z Speedrun, and EWOR. As of this profile the company is pre-product with no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal; this repository tracks it in the API Evangelist network for enrichment as its developer surface emerges.

companies.name: Bionic Stork
companies.description: Bionic Stork Ltd. (operating as Bionic, bionic.ai) was an Application Security Posture Management (ASPM) company founded in Tel Aviv, Israel. Its agentless platform mapped application architectures in production — services, APIs, dependencies, data flows and SBOMs — to surface and prioritize security, data-privacy and operational risk for cloud-native applications. Backed by Insight Partners, Cyberstarts and Battery Ventures (including a $65M Series B), Bionic was acquired by CrowdStrike in 2023 for a reported ~$350M and folded into CrowdStrike Falcon ASPM. bionic.ai now 301-redirects to CrowdStrike and the company has no independent public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Bit.io
companies.description: Bit.io was a serverless, shareable PostgreSQL database platform that let developers spin up cloud Postgres databases in seconds, load and query data, and share them via a link, with programmatic access over the standard Postgres wire protocol. Founded by Adam Fletcher and Jonathan Mortensen and backed by Battery Ventures, bit.io was acquired by Databricks in May 2023; the standalone product was sunset on June 29, 2023 (database exports available through July 29, 2023) and the team moved to Databricks. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired network record — there is no live API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface to enrich.

companies.name: Bluedata Software Inc
companies.description: BlueData Software Inc was a big-data infrastructure company whose EPIC platform ran Hadoop, Spark, and other analytics workloads in Docker containers on-premises and in the cloud. It was a dcvc (Data Collective) portfolio company and was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2018; its technology now lives on as the HPE Ezmeral Container Platform. The original www.bluedata.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's container-platform page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

companies.name: BlueStripe Software
companies.description: BlueStripe Software was an application performance management (APM) vendor headquartered in the Research Triangle Park area of North Carolina. Its flagship product, FactFinder, provided application-aware infrastructure performance monitoring and end-to-end transaction tracing across distributed servers, letting operations teams map and troubleshoot how applications behaved across physical, virtual, and cloud infrastructure. The company was backed by Trinity Ventures and other venture investors before being acquired by Microsoft in April 2015, after which its technology was folded into Microsoft System Center and the Operations Management Suite (OMS) and the standalone BlueStripe product and developer surface were discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; the company no longer operates an independent website, developer portal, or API.

companies.name: Brooktrout Technology
companies.description: Brooktrout Technology, Inc. was a Needham, Massachusetts telecommunications company founded in 1984 that designed fax and voice-processing hardware and software for computer telephony integration (CTI), including the TR114 and TR1034 fax boards and the SR140 host-based (software) fax product. Its developer kit, the Brooktrout SDK, provided C/C++ APIs for building fax, voice, and unified-messaging applications. Brooktrout was acquired by Excel Switching in 2000 (forming Brooktrout Technology / Excel), and the Brooktrout product line later became part of Dialogic, which continues to ship and document the Dialogic Brooktrout SDK. The brooktrout.com domain now redirects to Dialogic; Brooktrout survives as a legacy product brand rather than an independent company, and it has no standalone modern web-API developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead.

companies.name: buddybuild
companies.description: buddybuild was a mobile continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform for iOS and Android apps, offering automated builds, testing, user feedback, and over-the-air deployment to testers. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired by Apple in January 2018; the standalone service was wound down through 2018-2019 and its capabilities were folded into Apple's Xcode Cloud. The buddybuild.com domain now redirects to developer.apple.com/xcode-cloud/, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface remains. Retained as a network record of an acquired/defunct provider rather than an active enrichment target.

companies.name: Builder.ai
companies.description: Builder.ai was a London-based AI-assisted software development platform, originally founded in 2016 as Engineer.ai by Sachin Dev Duggal, that let customers assemble custom web and mobile applications from reusable building blocks orchestrated by an AI assistant branded "Natasha." Positioned as a no-code/low-code "human-assisted AI" app factory, it raised large rounds from investors including Insight Partners, Microsoft, the Qatar Investment Authority and SoftBank's DeepCore. The company collapsed into insolvency and entered administration in 2025 amid a revenue-restatement controversy, and its public web and developer surfaces are no longer operational. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record; no live API, developer portal, or documentation could be verified during enrichment.

companies.name: Cascade
companies.description: Cascade (www.cascade.io) was a no-code data analysis platform founded in 2019 by Jake Fuentes and Jon Brelig that let non-technical business teams import large datasets, transform and combine them with no-code tools, then visualize and present findings as interactive data apps (positioned as a cloud-native, collaborative alternative to Alteryx). The company wound down in 2023 after failing to reach breakout growth; www.cascade.io now serves a retrospective "What Cascade Did" page. As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment probe there is no public API, developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation surface to enrich, so this profile carries identity only.

companies.name: CliQr Technologies *
companies.description: CliQr Technologies was a San Jose, California cloud management software company, backed by GV (Google Ventures) and Google Capital, that built the CloudCenter platform for application-defined hybrid cloud orchestration. Its single application profile let enterprises model, deploy, and manage workloads across bare-metal, virtualized, and container environments and across public clouds (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, IBM SoftLayer, Rackspace) and private clouds (OpenStack, CloudStack, VMware vCloud). Cisco announced its intent to acquire CliQr for $260 million in March 2016 and folded the product into Cisco CloudCenter as part of its hybrid cloud strategy; CliQr no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no active developer surface, API, or documentation.

companies.name: Cmd *
companies.description: Cmd was a Vancouver, Canada-based cybersecurity startup founded in 2016 that built runtime security and observability purpose-built for Linux infrastructure, giving security and DevOps teams real-time visibility and policy-based control over user activity across cloud workloads. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), which led its $15M Series B in 2019, Cmd raised roughly $21.6M total before being acquired by Elastic in August 2021, where its technology was folded into the Elastic Security cloud workload protection and Limitless XDR offering. Co-founders Jake King (CSO) and Santosh Krishan joined Elastic through the acquisition. Cmd no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live API, developer portal, or public API surface; this profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Curtiss-Wright
companies.description: Curtiss-Wright is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions, and services mainly to the aerospace, defense, commercial power, process, and general industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans rugged embedded computing, mission-critical avionics, electronic packaging, naval propulsion, reactor coolant pumps for nuclear power, surface treatment services, industrial valves, sensors, data acquisition systems, telemetry ground stations, emergency arresting systems for military aircraft, and electronic systems for naval shipbuilding programs. The company traces its lineage to the aviation pioneers Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers and today operates across the Defense Electronics, Naval & Power, and Aerospace & Industrial segments.

companies.name: D2iQ
companies.description: D2iQ (formerly Mesosphere, maker of DC/OS) was an enterprise Kubernetes company whose flagship product, the D2iQ Kubernetes Platform (DKP), delivered production-grade Kubernetes cluster provisioning, day-2 operations, and application management across cloud, on-premises, edge, and air-gapped environments. D2iQ was acquired by Nutanix in early 2024; DKP was folded into and rebranded as the Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP), which launched in May 2024. The independent D2iQ web and developer surfaces are now retired: d2iq.com redirects to nutanix.com/d2iq and docs.d2iq.com redirects to the Nutanix support portal, so D2iQ no longer operates a first-party public API, developer portal, or artifact surface of its own. This profile is retained as a historical / acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Dazz
companies.description: Dazz is a cloud security company specializing in Application Security Posture Management (ASPM) and code-to-cloud risk remediation. Its platform correlates findings across code, cloud, and on-prem infrastructure into a single unified view, maps vulnerabilities back to their root cause in source code, and gives security and engineering teams a remediation engine to prioritize and fix issues across the application lifecycle. Co-founded and led by CEO Merav Bahat, Dazz was backed by Insight Partners, Greylock, Cyberstarts, and others. Wiz announced its acquisition of Dazz on November 21, 2024 to extend its Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) with Dazz's remediation capabilities; the dazz.io domain now redirects into Wiz. This profile has no independent public developer/API surface.

companies.name: DCHQ
companies.description: DCHQ (Data Center HQ) was a cloud automation and Docker container management platform out of San Francisco, offering both a hosted PaaS (DCHQ.io) and self-hosted on-premise editions for modeling, deploying, and managing container-based applications across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Rackspace, and OpenStack. The platform covered application modeling (Docker Compose / JSON), infrastructure automation, multi-tenant governance and access controls, and lifecycle management including monitoring, backup, and auto-scaling, with integrations for Docker, GitHub, and Jenkins. The company is now defunct — its primary domain (dchq.co) no longer resolves and dchq.io serves a frozen 2020 marketing snapshot with no live developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record; no live API artifacts were available to enrich.

companies.name: deepfactor
companies.description: Deepfactor was an application security (AppSec / ASPM) platform for cloud-native and containerized applications. Its integrated approach combined software composition analysis (SCA), software bill of materials (SBOM) generation, container image scanning, and container runtime security into a single developer-security platform. Its differentiating capability was runtime software composition analysis / runtime reachability, correlating static scans with observed runtime application behavior so teams could prioritize vulnerability remediation based on true usage. Use cases spanned Shift-Left & DevSecOps, supply chain security, SBOM, container runtime security & compliance (SOC 2), and cloud-native application security. Backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the public website is offline — the apex domain (deepfactor.io) returns a Cisco 503 error page and the WP Engine-hosted www/docs hosts return "Site is not available", and DNS for the apex resolves to Cisco infrastructure; there is no live developer portal, API, SDK, CLI, GitHub organization, or published package to harvest.

companies.name: DevOps
companies.description: DevOps is a cultural and technical movement that combines software development and IT operations to shorten the development lifecycle and deliver high-quality software continuously. It emphasizes automation, collaboration, monitoring, and infrastructure as code to bridge the gap between building software and running it in production. DevOps spans tooling categories including version control, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, observability, and security integration.

companies.name: DevSecOps
companies.description: Development, Security, and Operations methodology that integrates security practices within the DevOps process, emphasizing security automation and collaboration throughout the software development lifecycle. DevSecOps treats security as code, favors continuous monitoring and proactive testing, and delivers compliance and security capabilities as services consumable by development teams. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

companies.name: Diamanti
companies.description: Diamanti was a San Jose, California infrastructure company (founded 2014) that built hyperconverged, bare-metal infrastructure purpose-built for containers and Kubernetes. Its flagship Ultima platform paired plug-and-play appliances with hardware-accelerated networking and storage I/O cards, and its Spektra software added multi-cluster, hybrid-cloud Kubernetes management across on-premises and public-cloud environments. As of this enrichment pass the company appears to be defunct / to have ceased operations: www.diamanti.com resolves but returns a captcha-walled placeholder (HTTP 202, noindex) with no reachable developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface.

companies.name: Dirig Software
companies.description: Dirig Software, Inc. was a Nashua, New Hampshire software company that built application and system management software for eBusiness — agent-based performance monitoring and automated problem correction for J2EE application servers (WebLogic, WebSphere), web infrastructure, and hosted service-provider environments, sold both direct to enterprises and through OEM and service-provider channels. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures. Its web presence at dirig.com carried full product, partner, and support content through roughly 2003, degraded to a broken holding page under the name "Dirig Corporation" from early 2004, and by late 2006 the domain was a parked Sedo for-sale page. As of this enrichment pass the company has no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind; dirig.com now resolves to an unrelated third-party endpoint returning a bare "OK" health response. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network — there is nothing to enrich and nothing to score.

companies.name: Envariant
companies.description: Envariant is building the control layer for foundation models — an AI interpretability SDK that lets teams inspect, steer, and control model behavior. The SDK exposes a compact set of primitives: detect and causally trace behaviors like hallucinations or invariant violations, reason inductively and steer outputs programmatically, extract human-readable domain principles, and synthesize targeted edge cases — moving verification upstream, directly into the model's latent space, with no bespoke engineering required. Envariant is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco. The SDK is in pre-release beta, so no public API, OpenAPI, or developer documentation is available yet; this profile captures the company identity ahead of a public developer surface.

companies.name: EraDrive
companies.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Escher Reality
companies.description: Escher Reality was an augmented reality and computer vision startup founded in 2016 by Ross Finman (CEO) and Diana Hu (CTO), with roots in the MIT Sandbox program. It built cloud backend services for cross-platform, persistent, multi-user mobile AR — shared experiences that neither Apple ARKit nor Google ARCore offered at the time — letting multiple users interact with the same virtual objects anchored to the real world. The company raised roughly $3 million and was based in Sunnyvale, California. In February 2018 Escher Reality was acquired by Niantic (creator of Pokemon GO); its team and technology were folded into the Niantic Real World Platform (now Lightship), and the standalone company and its developer/SDK offering were discontinued. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record; there is no independent, active API or developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: Everest
companies.description: Everest is an early-stage Y Combinator (Fall 2025 / F25) startup based in San Francisco building agent-ready technical support for developer tools. Its premise is that a growing share of a devtool's users will be coding agents rather than humans, and Everest helps devtool companies sell to and support those coding agents with instant technical support. The company was founded in 2026 by co-founders Yolanda Cao and Spencer McKee. As of this profile Everest operates a single marketing landing page (everestagi.com) with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface yet published; this record is maintained as a lead for the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Evident.io
companies.description: Evident.io was a cloud security posture management company, founded in 2013, best known for the Evident Security Platform (ESP) — an agentless SaaS service that continuously monitored Amazon Web Services (and later Microsoft Azure) accounts for security misconfigurations, compliance drift, and risk across services like IAM, S3, EC2, and CloudTrail. ESP scored findings against frameworks such as CIS Benchmarks, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2, and exposed its analysis programmatically through a REST API so teams could automate remediation and wire results into their DevSecOps pipelines. Palo Alto Networks acquired Evident.io in March 2018 for roughly $300M and folded the technology into what became Prisma Cloud. The standalone evident.io product, developer portal, and API have been retired; the domain is now defensively held with no live website or API surface. This record is retained for historical/network-graph completeness — there is no live API to enrich.

companies.name: FiftyThree
companies.description: FiftyThree, Inc. was a New York City-based technology company that built tools for mobile creativity, best known for Paper (Apple's 2012 iPad App of the Year), the Pencil Bluetooth stylus, and Paste, a collaborative presentation tool. The company raised a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) in 2013 and, in July 2014, shipped the FiftyThree SDK so third-party iOS apps such as Procreate and Noteshelf could integrate the Pencil stylus (pairing, palm rejection, surface pressure). FiftyThree's assets and patents were acquired by WeTransfer on August 21, 2018, and the standalone products and developer surface were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no live public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI to enrich.

companies.name: FogHorn Systems (Johnson Controls)
companies.description: FogHorn Systems was a Sunnyvale, California developer of edge AI and machine learning software for the industrial and commercial Internet of Things (IIoT). Its Lightning Edge AI platform and Lightning EdgeML brought real-time streaming analytics and ML inference to constrained on-premises edge hardware for predictive maintenance, machine optimization, and operational intelligence use cases. Johnson Controls acquired FogHorn in January 2022 and folded its team and technology into the OpenBlue suite of smart, autonomous building solutions, with the former Sunnyvale headquarters operating as a Johnson Controls "AI Hub." FogHorn no longer operates as a standalone brand and publishes no independent public developer surface — no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization resolve as of this enrichment pass; the former foghorn.io/foghorn.ai domains are parked. This profile is retained as a network company record with no public API artifacts to harvest.

companies.name: General Instinct
companies.description: General Instinct is a San Francisco company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building the deployment layer for physical AI. Founded in 2026 by Bill Jiao and Guanming Wang, it distills, quantizes, and deploys large frontier AI models onto constrained edge hardware so robotics, drone, and physical-AI teams can run low-latency models fully offline on devices like NVIDIA Jetson, mobile NPUs, ARM CPUs, the Apple Neural Engine, and Snapdragon. Its first product, Instinct Edge, takes a model, a target device, and a latency budget and returns an offline runtime that hits the budget on-device with no cloud calls, handling model compression, custom kernel optimization (CUDA, Metal, ARM NEON), and the data-to-serving pipeline. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment searched the public web and found a marketing landing page but no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested. This profile captures the company identity plus the security posture of its public web surface, and remains an identity-only lead pending a discoverable API.

companies.name: Gitprime
companies.description: GitPrime was a software engineering analytics and developer-productivity company founded in 2015 in Durango, Colorado, backed by Y Combinator and DCVC. Its product mined data from Git repositories, code review, and ticketing systems to give engineering leaders visibility into team throughput, code churn, and delivery health. Pluralsight acquired GitPrime in 2019 (~$170M) and rebranded it as Pluralsight Flow; in February 2025 Appfire acquired Flow from Pluralsight, and Appfire has announced that Flow will be discontinued on December 31, 2027. The independent gitprime.com domain no longer resolves and www.gitprime.com redirects to appfire.com/flow/info, so there is no standalone GitPrime developer portal, public API, or specification to enrich; any surviving API functionality now lives under the Appfire Flow product. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct company record.

companies.name: Gnip
companies.description: Gnip was a social media data aggregation company founded in 2008 in Boulder, Colorado by Eric Marcoullier and Jud Valeski. It became the first authorized reseller of the Twitter "firehose" and delivered enterprise-grade access to real-time and historical social data from Twitter, Tumblr, WordPress, Disqus, StockTwits and many other sources through products such as PowerTrack, Historical PowerTrack, the Search API, the Audience API and the Engagement API. Twitter acquired Gnip in April 2014 and folded its technology into Twitter's enterprise data platform; the Gnip brand and standalone APIs were retired and gnip.com now 301-redirects to the Twitter/X enterprise developer documentation. This profile is preserved for historical/network completeness — Gnip is no longer an independent provider.

companies.name: Good Manufacturing Practices
companies.description: A system of processes, procedures, and documentation that ensures products are consistently produced and controlled according to quality standards, commonly used in pharmaceutical, food, and medical device manufacturing. Proper implementation reduces legal and operational risk while supporting audit readiness.

companies.name: Hardware Intelligence
companies.description: Hardware Intelligence is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup based in San Francisco building an end-to-end, agent-native toolchain for chip design. Founded in 2026 by Athreya Anand, the company applies agentic AI and ultrafast feedback loops to the semiconductor design and verification workflow. Its first product, Wave, is a terminal-native waveform debugger with a verification agent built in, aimed at accelerating hardware debugging and design iteration. At the time of profiling the company is pre-launch with early-access pilots and a waitlist; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity only and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: Hyper 4
companies.description: Hyper (heyhyper.ai) is a Y Combinator-backed startup building "the self-driving company brain" — a knowledge-management platform that assembles a centralized, self-maintaining knowledge graph from a team's emails, Slack, GitHub, calendars, and other work sources, then feeds that context back into AI agents and tools so they act with accurate company memory and require fewer repeated corrections. Founded in 2026 by Shalin Shah and Kanyes Thaker and based in San Francisco, the company was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this profile Hyper is very early-stage, publishing only a marketing landing page at heyhyper.ai with no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface yet available; this record captures verified company identity and will be re-enriched as a developer platform is published.

companies.name: idsmanager
companies.description: IDSManager (Jiuzhou Yunteng, 九州云腾) is a Chinese enterprise cybersecurity vendor providing unified identity management and zero-trust security. Its IDaaS platform centralizes account lifecycle, authentication, and authorization around a 5A framework (application center, unique accounts, single sign-on, centralized authorization, transparent auditing). The product line spans the IPG identity authentication series, MFA combining biometrics and digital certificates, the SPG secure application authentication series with Web and API gateways, and an SDP identity-defined perimeter for zero-trust access. It targets cloud migration, mobile-office security, and regulatory compliance across internet, finance, government, manufacturing, and education sectors. No public developer portal, API, or SDK is currently published.

companies.name: Incognito Technologies
companies.description: Incognito Technologies Private Limited is a Jaipur, India-based information technology services and software consultancy (incorporated December 2011, CIN U72200RJ2011PTC036364, offices in Bani Park, Jaipur). The firm offers custom software development, web and mobile application development, cloud and data services, IT infrastructure management, digital transformation, and enterprise ERP consulting. It is a professional-services provider rather than a public API producer; as of this enrichment pass no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI) has been located, and the corporate website (inctech.in) was unreachable when probed.

companies.name: Infiot
companies.description: Infiot was a secure access service edge (SASE) and intelligent edge networking startup that combined SD-WAN, zero trust network access (ZTNA), security service edge, and cloud-delivered edge intelligence into a single-vendor, AI-driven service for connecting branch, remote, and IoT sites. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Netskope in August 2022 and its technology was folded into Netskope's Borderless SD-WAN and Converged Access product line. Infiot no longer operates an independent brand, developer portal, API reference, or public API host; the former infiot.com domain now 301-redirects to Netskope's Converged Access product page, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio lead with its acquisition status recorded.

companies.name: Information Technology Infrastructure
companies.description: Information Technology Infrastructure encompasses the hardware, software, networks, and facilities used to support the delivery, management, and operation of IT services. This includes servers, storage, networking, data centers, and cloud infrastructure components.

companies.name: Instart Logic
companies.description: Instart Logic was a web application performance and security company founded in 2010 (originally as Zettata) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. It pioneered an endpoint-integrated cloud delivery architecture that paired a cloud service with a client-side JavaScript engine (the Nanovisor) running in the browser to accelerate web and mobile web applications, optimize and stream images (SmartVision), and defend applications with bot management and a web application firewall. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, Tenaya Capital, Greylock, Sutter Hill Ventures and others across roughly $140M+ in venture funding, the company's technology assets were acquired by Akamai Technologies in early 2020, after which the business wound down. No live developer or API surface remains: the instartlogic.com domain resolves to no website host and is served by Akamai nameservers.

companies.name: Institut für Produktqualität
companies.description: Institut für Produktqualität (ifp) is an independent analytical testing laboratory based in Berlin, Germany, providing laboratory analysis, testing, and consulting services for food, feed, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the provider publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or machine-readable discovery surface; its public website is served behind bot-protection (HTTP 401) and exposes no /.well-known documents. This profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only.

companies.name: InVisionApp
companies.description: InVision (InVisionApp, Inc.) was a digital product design collaboration platform founded in 2011 by Clark Valberg and Ben Nadel. It built a suite of tools for prototyping, design handoff, and real-time collaboration — including interactive prototypes, Inspect/Specs for developer handoff, DSM (Design System Manager), Boards, and the Freehand online whiteboard. At its peak InVision was valued near two billion dollars and backed by Battery Ventures, Accel, Tiger Global, and others, serving product design teams as a challenger to Adobe. As Figma surged, InVision's business declined: it sold the Freehand whiteboard product to Miro in 2023, and wound down all remaining services on December 31, 2024, after which customer content was permanently deleted. The invisionapp.com domain now redirects to Miro. InVision historically exposed a public REST API with OAuth and webhooks for its design platform, but that developer surface has been retired along with the product.

companies.name: Iomob
companies.description: Iomob (The Internet of Mobility) was a Barcelona-based Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) technology company founded in 2017. Its platform let cities, transport operators, and corporations orchestrate multimodal, door-to-door journeys — combining public transit, ride-hailing, taxis, micromobility, parking, and demand-responsive transport — through unified journey-planning APIs, native iOS/Android SDKs, and customizable white-label apps. Iomob's MaaS platform and SDK were acquired by Busup in January 2025 to build a corporate mobility platform; the Iomob UK entity was dissolved in September 2025 and the public website (iomob.net) is currently offline (Cloudflare 526 origin error). No public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK packages, or GitHub organization could be verified during enrichment — Iomob's APIs and SDKs were delivered under B2B/partner agreements.

companies.name: Kamcord
companies.description: Kamcord was a San Francisco-based mobile technology company (Y Combinator, Summer 2012) founded by Aditya Rathnam, Kevin Wang, and Matt Zitzmann. It offered an iOS and Android SDK that let game developers embed in-app gameplay recording, live streaming ("appcasting"), and social sharing to YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook, and grew to roughly 200 million device installs. The company later pivoted to a short-form mobile screen-content social network ("shots"). In November 2017 Lyft acquihired most of the ~15-person team, including co-founders Rathnam and Wang, and Kamcord wound down its consumer app, live streaming, and developer SDK by the end of 2017. The company is DEFUNCT and no longer operates any developer program or API. The kamcord.com domain has since been repurposed by an unrelated lifestyle/blog publisher and is NOT associated with the original Kamcord.

companies.name: Kimono Labs
companies.description: Kimono Labs was a developer-tools startup that let users turn any website into a structured API without writing code, using a visual point-and-click tool to define data selectors that Kimono would crawl on a schedule and expose as JSON/CSV endpoints and RSS feeds. Founded in 2014 by Pratap Ranade and Ryan Rowe and backed by Cowboy Ventures, the company was acquired by Palantir Technologies in February 2016, after which the hosted cloud service at kimonolabs.com was shut down on 29 February 2016; a downloadable Kimono Desktop application was released as a farewell so existing scrapers could continue running locally. The company is defunct and operates no live API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

companies.name: Kiva Software
companies.description: Kiva Software Corporation was a pioneer of the internet application server, founded in May 1994 by chairman and CEO Keng Lim and headquartered in Mountain View, California. In January 1996 Kiva shipped what is widely credited as the industry's first web application server, giving companies a platform for developing and deploying transaction-oriented business applications on the web — and the first Java application server to market, with C++ application development supported alongside it. The product line comprised the Kiva Enterprise Server (deployment and management runtime), the Kiva Application Builder (graphical development tool), and the Kiva SDK with Java and C++ foundation classes; the company also ran the Kiva Enterprise Alliance Program (KEAP) for end-to-end partner solutions. Customers included Bank of America, E-Trade, Travelocity, Internet Shopping Network, Hong Kong Telecom, and Pacific Bell Internet. Kiva raised roughly $13.9 million across two rounds from Weiss Peck & Greer, Greylock, Discovery Ventures, Sippl MacDonald Ventures, Norwest Venture Capital, and Trinity Ventures, and is listed in the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio as a 1996 early-stage investment. In December 1997 Netscape Communications acquired Kiva for approximately $180 million in stock (6.3 million Netscape shares), and the Kiva Enterprise Server became the Netscape Application Server — which went on to become the iPlanet Application Server under the AOL/Netscape–Sun Microsystems alliance, then Sun ONE Application Server and Sun Java System Application Server. Kiva has not operated independently since 1997, published no public developer API in the modern sense, and has no live web presence today (the historical www.kivasoft.com domain is now parked and listed for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Lightspeed and Trinity Ventures portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: LogicLoop
companies.description: LogicLoop was a low-code / no-code operations-automation platform that let non-engineering teams write SQL-based business rules on top of their company data to trigger alerts, reviews, and automated actions for use cases like fraud and risk monitoring, logistics, and customer onboarding. Founded in 2021 by Jesika Haria and Jackie Xu, it raised roughly $4.5M from Accel and First Round Capital, offered an AI SQL Copilot (plain-English-to-SQL) and a REST API for managing rules, schedules, notifications, and embedded dashboards. LogicLoop was acquired by Hummingbird (risk and compliance) on 2024-09-18; its website (www.logicloop.com), docs (docs.logicloop.com), and API hosts no longer resolve, so no live API surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: Lytmus
companies.description: Lytmus was a technical-interview and coding-assessment platform for hiring engineers. Candidates worked live in a browser-based, fully functional Ubuntu virtual machine (Terminal, editors, Chrome) so recruiters could run pair-programming phone screens and evaluate real coding skills across languages and full-stack scenarios, priced in per-session plans. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment probing (2026-07-20) found no developer portal, API, documentation, or ./.well-known surface; the company was acquired by GitHub in 2019 and its product has since been shut down, so lytmus.io now serves stale content and lytmus.com is a parked, for-sale domain. No API artifacts exist to enrich.

companies.name: Mainframe
companies.description: Mainframe (Mainframe Group, Inc.) is a software development and marketing services company building products for the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem. It offers three service areas — Risk Management (protocol parameter optimization and stability), Development (DeFi and blockchain financial solutions), and Marketing (brand reach and audience engagement) — and has produced projects including Hifi, Pooled NFT, Sheet Heads, and Crown Ribbon. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Mainframe publishes a Webflow marketing site only, with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Microservice Architecture
companies.description: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services organized around business capabilities. Widely used by developers to build, maintain, and scale software applications efficiently.

companies.name: Microservice Design
companies.description: Architectural approach for building applications as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services that are organized around business capabilities. Covers principles, patterns, and best practices for designing effective microservice-based systems.

companies.name: Muir Test Systems
companies.description: Muir Test Systems is a company in the Battery Ventures portfolio, operating in the test-and-measurement space. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 searched the web, npm/PyPI/Maven/other package registries, and probed for a developer/API surface and found no publicly discoverable developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted MCP server. No production website domain for the company resolved during probing, so domain, well-known, and security probes could not be run. This profile remains a company-only lead with no API artifacts.

companies.name: Neversitup
companies.description: Neversitup is a Bangkok, Thailand based software development and IT outsourcing company delivering end-to-end digital software along with web, mobile, and backend engineering and dedicated developer placement for clients. It also builds and operates its own consumer fintech products, including the Piggipo and Piggipo Go credit-card management apps and the Fast Loan lending platform, on a stack spanning Python, Node.js, React, Kotlin, and Swift running on AWS and Firebase. As of this enrichment pass Neversitup publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs; it operates as a services and product company rather than an API provider.

companies.name: Nimsoft
companies.description: Nimsoft was a SaaS-based IT infrastructure and application monitoring and service-desk company, founded in 1998 as Nimbus Software in Oslo, Norway and later headquartered in Redwood City, California. Backed by Northzone and JMI Equity, it was acquired by CA Technologies in March 2010 for roughly $350 million, after which its products were folded into CA Unified Infrastructure Management (UIM). CA was in turn acquired by Broadcom in 2018, and the former Nimsoft monitoring capability now lives on as Broadcom DX Unified Infrastructure Management. The www.nimsoft.com domain today resolves to Broadcom infrastructure, and Nimsoft has no independent developer portal, public API, or OpenAPI surface of its own.

companies.name: Noondual-canvas for design and code
companies.description: Noondual-canvas for design and code is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of homebrew and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: developer-tools. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Nova Metrix
companies.description: Nova Metrix is a geotechnical, environmental, and materials-testing instrumentation company headquartered in Wakefield, Massachusetts and founded in 2009. It designs and manufactures sensors, instruments, monitoring software, and consumables for structural-health monitoring, construction, civil engineering, energy, and medical markets, operating in more than 90 countries. Nova Metrix is the parent of a family of specialist geotechnical and fiber-optic brands including Roctest, Sensornet, Sherborne Sensors, Soil Instruments, Westbay Instruments, DGSI, Waterloo Hydrogeologic, and Van Essen Instruments. It is backed by Battery Ventures, Commonwealth Capital, and Ascent Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Nova Metrix publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile carries verified company identity rather than an API surface.

companies.name: Numerify
companies.description: Numerify was an IT business analytics company that provided a cloud-based System of Intelligence for IT operations, applying AI and machine learning to data from ITSM, DevOps, and application-performance tools to predict change risk, reduce incidents, and improve software delivery. Numerify was acquired by Digital.ai in 2020, and its capabilities now live inside Digital.ai's Change Risk Prediction / Intelligence product line. The standalone numerify.com domain 301-redirects to digital.ai, and the company publishes no independent public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Observo
companies.description: Observo AI built an AI-native data pipeline (telemetry pipeline) platform that optimizes security and observability data in flight, filtering, enriching, and normalizing logs, metrics, and traces into standard schemas like OCSF to cut SIEM and observability data volume and cost before ingestion into the SOC. Founded in 2022 and backed by Felicis, Observo AI was acquired by SentinelOne; the observo.ai domain now 301-redirects to SentinelOne's Singularity AI Data Pipelines product, its documentation host (docs.observo.ai) is authentication-gated, and there is no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or programmatic surface to enrich.

companies.name: Observo Ai
companies.description: Observo AI was an AI-powered data pipeline platform for observability and security telemetry. Its product reduced log and event volume (filtering low-value data by up to ~80%), normalized diverse telemetry formats into standardized schemas such as OCSF, and enriched data at ingest before it reached a SIEM or observability backend. Founded to tame the roughly 35% annual growth of security and observability data, the company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was subsequently acquired by SentinelOne, where the technology now ships as Singularity AI Data Pipelines. The former observo.ai domain now 301-redirects to SentinelOne and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface.

companies.name: Octarine
companies.description: Octarine was a cloud-native application security startup that built a security platform for Kubernetes and service-mesh environments, providing runtime visibility, policy enforcement, and threat detection for containerized workloads and microservices. Backed by Accel and Samsung NEXT, Octarine was acquired by VMware in May 2020 and its technology was folded into VMware Carbon Black Cloud and the Tanzu portfolio to deliver Kubernetes and container security. As an independent company Octarine no longer operates a public developer or API surface; its former domain octarinesec.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company / acquisition record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: OneASP
companies.description: OneASP (Application Security Protection) is the runtime application security product line of OneAPM (Beijing Blue Ocean Xuntong Technology / 蓝海讯通), a Qiming-backed Chinese IT operations management (ITOM) and application performance monitoring vendor founded in 2008. OneASP delivered runtime application self-protection (RASP) for web applications, and was also marketed internationally under the OneRASP brand. As of enrichment (2026-07), no standalone OneASP developer portal, public API, or SDK surface resolves - the oneasp.com brand domain no longer resolves and OneASP appears to be a legacy/absorbed product line of the parent OneAPM platform.

companies.name: opsmatic
companies.description: Opsmatic was a San Francisco-based infrastructure monitoring startup founded in 2013 that delivered a cloud service for real-time visibility into configuration changes and configuration "drift" across dynamic cloud infrastructure, alerting DevOps and operations teams so they could troubleshoot and reduce downtime. New Relic acquired Opsmatic in November 2015 to enter the infrastructure monitoring market, and the company no longer operates as an independent entity. The opsmatic.com domain now redirects to newrelic.com and there is no live independent developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. This record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio profile.

companies.name: Parstream
companies.description: ParStream was a big-data analytics database company founded in 2011 in Cologne, Germany by Michael Hummel, Joerg Bienert and Norbert Heuber. Its columnar, GPU-accelerated OLAP database was built for Internet-of-Things environments, filtering and analyzing billions of records in sub-second time at the edge of the network, with query access via SQL and a JSON query format plus a C++ API for user-defined query nodes. Cisco acquired ParStream on October 26, 2015 and folded the team into its Data and Analytics Group; the standalone product was declared obsolete and retired in 2018. The former parstream.com domain now redirects to a Cisco end-of-life product page, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or discovery surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: PiCloud
companies.description: PiCloud was a cloud-computing startup founded in 2009 that offered a pay-as-you-go, serverless platform for running Python workloads across public (AWS) and private clouds without provisioning, configuring, or managing virtual servers — popular for batch processing, high-performance computing, and scientific computing. It raised a seed round from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, Plug and Play, and Greylock. The team was acquired by Dropbox in November 2013 and the PiCloud service was shut down on February 25, 2014 (its platform lived on briefly as the open-source Multyvac project). The picloud.com domain is now parked, and there is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

companies.name: Process Sensing Technologies
companies.description: Process Sensing Technologies (PST) is a measurement instrumentation group that designs and manufactures precision sensors and analyzers for moisture, humidity, dew point, oxygen, and trace gas measurement across industrial, pharmaceutical, food, and life-science applications. Its brand portfolio includes Michell Instruments, Rotronic, Analytical Industries, Ntron, SensoScientific, and Isensix, spanning process gas analysis and real-time environmental monitoring. The company now operates under the DwyerOmega brand following its combination with Dwyer Instruments. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; probing of its public web surface found hardware, software downloads, calibration tooling, and monitoring platforms but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal.

companies.name: Pub/Sub
companies.description: A messaging pattern where publishers send messages to topics without knowledge of subscribers, and subscribers receive messages from topics they're interested in, enabling asynchronous and decoupled communication between services. Modern distributed architectures rely on it to coordinate workloads across multiple nodes and regions.

companies.name: README.md
companies.description: Standard repository documentation file providing project overview, setup instructions, and usage examples. Automatically displayed on repository landing pages by GitHub, GitLab, and other hosting platforms.

companies.name: Rivet Design
companies.description: Rivet is a design agent that works alongside your coding agent: given a prompt or an existing application, it explores dozens of distinct visual and UI design directions in parallel so you can compare them side by side and pick the one that fits, instead of iterating on a single design by hand. As of this profile it is an early-stage product presented through a marketing landing page at tryrivet.design; no public API, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, or developer documentation are published yet, so the API Evangelist network tracks it as an identity-only company profile.

companies.name: Rocana
companies.description: Rocana (formerly ScalingData) was an IT operations analytics company founded in 2014 in San Francisco and backed by GV. Its product captured and analyzed all machine data from all sources across data-center infrastructure, keeping it online and queryable for years so operations teams could perform root-cause analysis and surface emerging IT problems before they caused outages. The company raised roughly $19.4M before being acquired by Splunk in 2017, after which the independent Rocana product and brand were wound down. It was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment on 2026-07-21 confirmed there is no live public website (rocana.com no longer resolves), no developer portal, no API, and no client packages — the company no longer operates independently.

companies.name: Rogue Wave Software
companies.description: Rogue Wave Software was a developer-tools and high-performance-computing software company known for products such as TotalView, Klocwork, IMSL numerical libraries, PV-WAVE, and its Zend PHP and open-source support lines. It was acquired by Perforce Software in 2019 and the brand has since been fully absorbed into Perforce; the historical roguewave.com domain now 301-redirects wholesale to perforce.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. This enrichment pass found no independent Rogue Wave API surface, developer portal, documentation, or well-known endpoints — everything resolves to Perforce.

companies.name: Scoreloop
companies.description: Scoreloop was a Munich, Germany based mobile social gaming company that provided a cross-platform SDK adding social features to mobile games - online leaderboards, achievements, player challenges, friend invites, and in-game virtual currency and monetization. The Scoreloop SDK supported Android, iOS, Windows Phone, Samsung Bada, Marmalade/AirPlay, and Unity 3D, and at its peak was used by more than 3,000 game developers. The company was backed by earlybird and was acquired by Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 2011; the standalone Scoreloop platform and its developer service were subsequently wound down.
