This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead - there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remaining (the scoreloop.com domain now serves a suspended page and no developer host resolves), so no API artifacts are available to harvest.

companies.name: SDSA
companies.description: SDSA (stylized as /dev/agents) is a stealth-stage startup building what it describes as a next-generation operating system for AI agents, aiming to make agentic applications a robust part of everyday consumer software through new UI patterns, a reimagined privacy model, and a developer platform for shipping more capable apps. The company was founded by David Singleton (former Stripe CTO), Ficus Kirkpatrick, Hugo Barra, and Nicholas Jitkoff, and is backed by SV Angel. As of this profile the company is pre-product: sdsa.ai is a single marketing/recruiting page with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or developer portal yet available. This entry was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with what is publicly verifiable.

companies.name: Semmle
companies.description: Semmle was a semantic code-analysis company whose engine let developers write queries (in its QL query language) to find security vulnerabilities and their variants across large codebases, and which powered the free open-source code review platform LGTM.com. Its technology was adopted by Uber, NASA, Microsoft, and Google. GitHub acquired Semmle in September 2019 and folded the QL engine into what is now CodeQL and GitHub code scanning; the standalone Semmle and LGTM.com products were retired and www.semmle.com now redirects to the GitHub acquisition announcement. This profile is retained as a historical (acquired) company lead in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Simpo
companies.description: Simpo is a no-code digital adoption platform (DAP) that lets enterprise product and customer-success teams build in-app onboarding flows, guided walkthroughs, announcements, surveys, and contextual help without writing code. End users are guided at the point of need inside the software they already use, driving feature adoption, engagement, and retention. Founded in 2016 by Yohanan Hruschev and Yuval Karmi and headquartered in San Francisco, Simpo raised a $4.5M seed round led by Redpoint Ventures in 2019 and was acquired by WalkMe in October 2021. The product is a snippet/embed-installed browser layer rather than a public developer REST API; it exposes no OpenAPI, SDK, or public developer documentation surface, and the primary web host is no longer reachable following the acquisition.

companies.name: Skipjaq
companies.description: Skipjaq, Inc. was a machine-learning performance-optimisation startup that marketed itself as "Performance Optimisation as a Service" and was backed by Accel. Its proprietary automated workload-optimisation software ran repeated optimization tests against a customer's application (hosted in the cloud on AWS EC2 instances behind Elastic Load Balancers) and used machine learning to tune configuration for better application performance, throughput, and latency without manual, expert tuning. The product was delivered as a cloud SaaS and was offered under a beta test agreement. The company is now defunct: the skipjaq.com domain no longer resolves on any common TLD (.com/.io/.ai/.co.uk all return no A/NS records as of 2026-07-21), the last archived snapshot of the site dates to May 2025, and there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, first-party SDK, or live API surface. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio lead.

companies.name: SkyGiraffe
companies.description: SkyGiraffe was an enterprise-grade mobility platform that let companies build customized, job-specific mobile apps with no coding, connecting mobile workforces to corporate systems of record such as SAP, Oracle, Salesforce and ServiceNow. In 2016 the company added developer access, exposing a single secure endpoint for third-party apps to read from and write to those backend enterprise systems through the SkyGiraffe platform. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global), Microsoft Ventures, and Trilogy Equity Partners across ~$10.5M in funding, SkyGiraffe was acquired by ServiceNow on October 25, 2017 and its technology and team were absorbed into ServiceNow's Now Platform mobile capabilities. The independent skygiraffe.com domain no longer hosts a product, developer portal, or API — it 301-redirects to ServiceNow's acquisition announcement — so there is no live, independent API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Smarterer
companies.description: Smarterer was a Boston-based skills-assessment company that used crowdsourced, adaptive tests to rapidly quantify people's proficiency across 400+ technical, social, and business skills. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), it opened a REST API in March 2015 that let partners embed tests, pull score data, and build leaderboards and profiles on top of its assessment engine. Pluralsight acquired Smarterer for roughly $75M in November 2014, absorbed its test engine into the Pluralsight learning platform, and wound down the standalone product. The smarterer.com domain no longer serves a site (defensively held via MarkMonitor, no DNS A record) and there is no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Sqreen
companies.description: Sqreen was a Paris- and San Francisco-based application security company offering Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), an in-app Web Application Firewall, and account-takeover and attack protection delivered through language agents for Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP, Java and Go. Backed by Y Combinator, Greylock and Point Nine, Sqreen was acquired by Datadog in 2021 and its technology was folded into Datadog Application Security Management. The standalone sqreen.com product, dashboard and developer APIs have since been decommissioned; the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical company lead and has no live, independent API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Stateless
companies.description: Stateless was a Boulder, Colorado network-infrastructure startup (founded 2016) that built a software platform for network automation in the hybrid multi-cloud era, delivering network functions such as firewalls and load balancers through an "as a service" consumption model with an emphasis on simplicity, scalability, and evolvability. Backed by Speedinvest, the National Science Foundation, Drive Capital, and Matchstick Ventures, with its last funding announced in December 2022. The company now appears defunct — its former domains (stateless.net, getstateless.com) redirect to domain-parking "for sale" pages and no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains.

companies.name: Talaria Technologies
companies.description: Talaria Technologies, Inc. was a developer-tools startup based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2011, that built a dynamic web application server and runtime infrastructure for web developers — notably a just-in-time (JIT) compiler and runtime for PHP intended to help developers build and run websites more efficiently. It was surfaced as an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) portfolio/investment-list company. Per public company-intelligence sources (indexed.vc, PrivCo, Bloomberg, CB Insights), Talaria was acquired by Google in 2013 and ceased operating as an independent company; it maintains no active website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

companies.name: Tara Ai
companies.description: Tara AI (Y Combinator W15, originally Gradberry) was a San Jose-based engineering efficiency platform that used fine-tuned LLMs over source control and project data to measure cycle times, benchmarks, and delivery velocity, integrating with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, and Slack. Backed by Aspect Ventures, Y Combinator, and Slack Fund (~$13M raised). As of July 2026 the company is listed as permanently closed on Crunchbase and tara.ai is a parked domain; no public API, developer docs, or SDKs were ever published, and the TARAAI GitHub org has no public repositories.

companies.name: Tcell Io
companies.description: Tcell Io (tCell.io) was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no active web presence - its former domain tcell.io now resolves to a third-party domain-parking page (parklogic.com) and returns no company site, developer portal, documentation, or API surface. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, well-known discovery documents, SDKs, or other machine-readable API artifacts could be found. This profile is retained as a network record; there is nothing enrichable until the company publishes an active developer surface.

companies.name: Unamo
companies.description: Unamo was a Warsaw, Poland based SaaS suite offering SEO monitoring, social media monitoring, and conversion rate optimization, formerly known as Positionly, and backed by Point Nine Capital. The company appears defunct as of July 2026, with unamo.com no longer resolving in DNS and the pre-rebrand positionly.com site serving stale 2017-era content whose API, signup, terms, and privacy pages return 404. No public API surface, client packages, or developer documentation remain online.

companies.name: Velocity
companies.description: Velocity was an Israeli DevOps / site-reliability-engineering startup that helped engineering teams move faster — originally by letting developers spin up on-demand, fully isolated, production-like development environments, and later by applying AI to automate SRE and major-incident-response workflows so engineers could focus on solving problems instead of chasing alerts. On November 10, 2025 Velocity was acquired by BigPanda (the Insight Partners-backed agentic AIOps / IT operations company) to accelerate its AI Detection and Response product; founder and CEO Tal Kain joined BigPanda as VP of AI Detection and Response. The velocity.tech domain now redirects to bigpanda.io and Velocity no longer operates an independent public developer surface, API, or documentation portal.

companies.name: Vlocity
companies.description: Vlocity was an industry-cloud software company founded in 2014 (by David Schmaier and team) that built vertical CRM applications on the Salesforce Platform for communications, media, energy, insurance, health, and the public sector, along with the OmniStudio low-code toolset (OmniScript, FlexCards, DataRaptor, Integration Procedures). Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Accel, Sutter Hill Ventures, and Salesforce Ventures, Vlocity was acquired by Salesforce in 2020 and folded into Salesforce Industries; the platform now ships as Salesforce OmniStudio. Vlocity no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no independent developer portal or public API — its domain (vlocity.com) is defunct (HTTP 503) and is now operated by Salesforce (confirmed via SPF/DMARC delegation to salesforce.com and a Salesforce, Inc. TLS certificate). Any API surface lives under Salesforce OmniStudio.

companies.name: Waffl
companies.description: Waffl is an early-stage website builder — a drag-and-drop platform for creating a website and growing a small business from customizable templates. As of this profile the product is pre-launch ("Coming Soon" at waffl.io) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it carries no API surface to enrich yet.

companies.name: WebMynd
companies.description: WebMynd, later known as Trigger.io, was a 500 Global backed startup that built Forge, a toolkit for building cross-platform mobile applications from HTML, JavaScript, and CSS with native device access. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company now appears inactive, its trigger.io domain no longer serves a live website (only email MX/SPF records remain) and no API, developer documentation, or SDK surface could be located during enrichment.

companies.name: Ximian
companies.description: Ximian was a Boston-based open source software company founded on October 19, 1999 by Miguel de Icaza and Nat Friedman -- originally incorporated as International GNOME Support, then Helix Code, and renamed Ximian in January 2001. It advanced the GNOME desktop, built the Evolution email and collaboration client and Ximian Connector, ran the Red Carpet software-update service, and launched the Mono open source .NET implementation. Surfaced via the Battery Ventures portfolio, Ximian was acquired by Novell on August 4, 2003 to strengthen Novell's enterprise Linux business; after Attachmate acquired Novell in 2011 the founders went on to create Xamarin (acquired by Microsoft in 2016). Ximian no longer operates: www.ximian.com still resolves on Novell infrastructure but permanently redirects every path to novell.com/linux/ximian.html, which forwards to suse.com -- there is no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical identity record.

companies.name: Zebrium
companies.description: Zebrium was an AIOps startup that used unsupervised machine learning to automatically detect anomalies and surface root cause from log data, correlating logs and metrics into plain-language incident summaries without manual rules or training. Backed by Accel, the company was acquired by ScienceLogic in 2022 and its technology folded into the ScienceLogic AIOps / SL1 platform (now surfaced as Skylar). The independent zebrium.com developer/API surface has been retired: the domain 301-redirects to sciencelogic.com and no standalone Zebrium API, documentation, or specification remains publicly discoverable. This profile is retained as a network lead recording the acquisition and the residual domain footprint.

companies.name: AT&T
companies.description: AT&T Inc. is a multinational telecommunications holding company providing wireless and wireline communications, broadband, and business networking to consumers and enterprises. Its developer surface spans four programs: the legacy AT&T Developer Program (SMS, MMS, in-app messaging, speech and OAuth), the MVNX APIs for mobile virtual network operators, the Alliance enterprise wireline APIs for service qualification and ordering, and the invite-only Network API Accelerator Program exposing GSMA CAMARA network APIs — SIM swap, device status, number verification, quality on demand, network insights and mobility threat detection.

companies.name: Lima
companies.description: Lima launches Linux virtual machines on macOS with automatic file sharing, port forwarding, and containerd integration for running containers.

companies.name: Secure-By-Design
companies.description: A software development approach that prioritizes security from the initial design phase through implementation, ensuring security considerations are built into the foundation of systems rather than added as an afterthought. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

companies.name: OCI
companies.description: OCI (Open Container Initiative) is an open governance structure for creating open industry standards around container formats and runtimes. OCI defines standards for container images, distribution, and runtime specifications used by Docker, Kubernetes, and other container technologies.

companies.name: Scrum
companies.description: Scrum is an agile project management framework that organizes work into fixed-length iterations called sprints, typically lasting two to four weeks. It defines clear roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers) and ceremonies (sprint planning, daily standups, retrospectives) to enable teams to deliver value incrementally and continuously improve.

companies.name: SecOps
companies.description: Security Operations - the practice of integrating security practices into IT operations to identify, manage, and respond to security threats and vulnerabilities in real-time while maintaining system performance and availability. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

companies.name: Secure Software Development Life Cycle
companies.description: A framework that integrates security practices and considerations into every phase of the software development process, from initial design through deployment and maintenance, to minimize vulnerabilities and ensure secure applications. It is used across a range of industries and technical contexts to improve efficiency and outcomes.

companies.name: Secure Software Development Lifecycle
companies.description: A framework that integrates security practices into every phase of the software development process, from design and development through testing and deployment, to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities early. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

companies.name: Semantic Kernel
companies.description: An open-source SDK that lets you easily build agents that can call your existing code, enabling AI orchestration with LLMs like GPT-4, plugins, and memory capabilities. It forms a core part of modern AI/ML pipelines and intelligent automation systems.

companies.name: Service Oriented Architecture
companies.description: An architectural pattern where software components provide services to other components through a communication protocol over a network. Services are loosely coupled, reusable, and can be independently deployed and maintained.

companies.name: Tinfoil Security
companies.description: Tinfoil Security was a web application and API security scanning company that provided automated dynamic (DAST) vulnerability testing for web apps and REST APIs. It was acquired by Synopsys in 2016 and folded into the Synopsys Software Integrity Group, which later became Black Duck. As of this enrichment pass its domain tinfoilsecurity.com no longer serves an independent site — every path returns an HTTP 302 redirect to blackduck.com — and there is no standalone Tinfoil Security developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, package registry presence, or /.well-known discovery surface remaining. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and is retained as an acquired/defunct lead with no live API surface to harvest.

companies.name: Apcera
companies.description: Apcera was an enterprise container and policy management platform founded in 2012 by Derek Collison, offering a "trusted cloud" runtime that layered fine-grained, policy-driven governance over workloads, containers, and services across hybrid infrastructure. Backed by a16z and DCVC, the company took a majority investment from Ericsson in 2015, was fully acquired by Ericsson in 2016, and the platform was subsequently wound down around 2017. The company is defunct - its primary domain (apcera.com) no longer resolves to a company site (it 301-redirects to an unrelated third party), and there is no live developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or reachable API host to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record only.

companies.name: Event Sourcing
companies.description: Event sourcing is an architectural pattern where state changes are stored as a sequence of immutable events rather than just the current state. Instead of storing only the current state of data, event sourcing stores all changes as a log of events, enabling complete audit trails, temporal queries, and event-driven projections.

companies.name: Extreme Programming
companies.description: Extreme Programming (XP) is an agile software development methodology that aims to produce higher quality software and improve quality of life for the development team. XP emphasizes customer satisfaction through frequent releases, continuous integration, test-driven development, pair programming, and collective code ownership.

companies.name: Micro-Service Architecture
companies.description: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services, each running in its own process and communicating through lightweight mechanisms like HTTP APIs. Modern development teams rely on it to improve code quality and delivery speed.

companies.name: Microservices Architecture
companies.description: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services, each running in its own process and communicating through lightweight mechanisms like HTTP/REST APIs. Widely used for building scalable, cloud-native applications.

companies.name: Microservices Design Patterns
companies.description: Architectural patterns and best practices for designing, building, and maintaining microservices-based applications, including patterns for communication, data management, deployment, and resilience.

companies.name: Object-Oriented Programming
companies.description: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a software development paradigm that organizes software design around data, or objects, rather than functions and logic. OOP uses concepts like classes, inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism to enable modular, reusable code design.

companies.name: Power Tools
companies.description: Power Tools is an index of API capabilities, developer tooling, and utilities curated by API Evangelist. This collection aggregates developer-facing APIs and SDKs that support automation, productivity, and integration use cases.

companies.name: Programming Paradigm
companies.description: Programming paradigms are fundamental styles of computer programming that provide a framework for thinking about and structuring code, including object-oriented, functional, imperative, declarative, and other approaches.

companies.name: Prototypes
companies.description: Early models or preliminary versions of products built to test concepts, validate designs, and gather feedback before full-scale production or development. Effective use of this practice reduces bugs in production and supports a culture of quality-driven development.

companies.name: Quality Standards
companies.description: Frameworks and benchmarks that define acceptable levels of quality for products, services, or processes to ensure consistency and meet customer expectations. Proper implementation reduces legal and operational risk while supporting audit readiness.

companies.name: Stackmob
companies.description: Stackmob is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: developer-tools. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Services Patterns
companies.description: Design patterns and architectural approaches for building microservices and service-oriented applications. Modern distributed architectures rely on it to coordinate workloads across multiple nodes and regions.

companies.name: .Gitattributes
companies.description: Git configuration file defining path-specific settings for line endings, diff handling, merge strategies, and binary file detection.

companies.name: SDLC
companies.description: Software Development Life Cycle - A systematic process for planning, creating, testing, and deploying software systems. Effective use of this practice reduces bugs in production and supports a culture of quality-driven development.

companies.name: Security by Design
companies.description: A software development approach that integrates security considerations and practices from the initial design phase through the entire development lifecycle, rather than adding security as an afterthought. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

companies.name: Serverless Patterns
companies.description: A collection of serverless architectures and patterns for building applications on AWS, featuring ready-to-use templates and best practices for Lambda, API Gateway, EventBridge, and other serverless services. Cloud adoption of this technology supports flexibility, cost optimization, and rapid deployment.

companies.name: Methodology
companies.description: Methodology is a concept entry covering systematic approaches and processes used in technology, software development, and computing to address specific technical challenges and improve outcomes.

companies.name: PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
companies.description: Template file that pre-populates pull request descriptions with structured sections like change summary, testing steps, and checklist items.

companies.name: SECURITY.md
companies.description: Security policy document describing supported versions, vulnerability reporting procedures, and responsible disclosure guidelines for a project.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

companies.name: 500 Global
companies.description: 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) is a global venture capital firm and startup accelerator founded in 2010 by Dave McClure and Christine Tsai and headquartered in Palo Alto / Silicon Valley, California. The firm invests from pre-seed to pre-IPO in globally ambitious technology founders, built on the belief that "talent lives everywhere, but capital and opportunity does not." 500 Global pioneered a "lots of little bets" seed strategy, backing hundreds of companies per fund with smaller initial checks, and has grown one of the industry's largest truly global seed portfolios: 3,000+ companies across 80+ countries with $300B+ in cumulative portfolio valuation, including 35+ companies valued at $1B+ and 160+ valued at more than $100M. It runs regional and thematic practices spanning Southeast Asia, Latin America, MENA, Africa, Japan, Korea, Thailand, and Eurasia, plus a Sustainable Growth strategy (health, climate, agriculture, gender, education), flagship accelerator programs, and the VC Unlocked investor-education program that has trained 1,400+ investors. As of April 30, 2025 the firm reported approximately $2.3B in assets under management. Notable investments include Canva, Grab, Talkdesk, Credit Karma, Twilio, and Bukalapak.

companies.name: Accel
companies.description: Accel is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded in 1983 by Arthur Patterson and Jim Swartz and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with additional offices in San Francisco, London, and Bangalore, India. Accel describes itself as "the first partner to exceptional teams everywhere," backing founders from seed and early stage through growth worldwide. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, consumer, artificial intelligence, fintech, cybersecurity, infrastructure and developer tools, security, media, and healthcare, and operates dedicated funds for the US, Europe/Israel, and India/Southeast Asia. Accel is known for its "prepared mind" investment philosophy and for backing category-defining companies including Facebook, Slack, Dropbox, Atlassian, CrowdStrike, UiPath, Qualtrics, Spotify, Flipkart, Swiggy, Freshworks, 1Password, Vercel, Scale AI, Anthropic, and Perplexity. Its portfolio spans more than 100 unicorns, dozens of IPOs, and hundreds of acquisitions. In 2024 Accel raised a $650M fund for European and Israeli startups, and in 2025 raised a fund for India and Southeast Asia. This profile tracks Accel's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Acceptance Criteria
companies.description: Acceptance criteria are predefined conditions that a product, feature, or user story must meet to be considered complete and acceptable by stakeholders. These criteria establish clear, testable requirements that guide development, validate when work is done, and serve as the foundation for automated testing through frameworks like Cucumber, SpecFlow, and Behave. APIs in this space support requirements management, behavior-driven development (BDD), test execution tracking, and agile project management workflows.

companies.name: ACID
companies.description: ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) is a set of properties that guarantee database transactions are processed reliably even in the face of errors, power failures, or system crashes. These four properties ensure that data remains accurate and consistent, making ACID compliance a fundamental requirement for relational databases, distributed systems, and financial APIs.

companies.name: Actor Model
companies.description: The Actor Model is a mathematical model of concurrent computation where the fundamental unit of computation is an actor, an entity that processes messages asynchronously and maintains its own private state. It provides a powerful abstraction for building highly concurrent and distributed systems, used in frameworks like Akka and languages like Erlang.

companies.name: Addition
companies.description: Addition is a New York City-based venture capital firm founded in 2020 by Lee Fixel, the former head of Tiger Global Management's private equity business. The firm invests in founder-led, technology-enabled companies across multiple stages, allocating roughly one-third of its capital to early-stage investments and the remainder to growth-stage opportunities. Sectors of focus include software and SaaS, fintech and payments, artificial intelligence and machine learning, developer tools and infrastructure, cybersecurity, consumer, logistics, and clean energy. Typical checks range from about $10M to $200M, with a reported sweet spot near $30M-$50M. Addition operates a streamlined solo-GP model with Fixel as sole managing partner making final investment decisions, enabling fast conviction. Across Addition One through Addition Five (2020-2023) the firm raised roughly $7B-$7.3B in committed capital. Notable investments include Stripe, Snyk, Hugging Face, Chainalysis, Navan, dLocal, Delhivery, Airwallex, Freshworks, Warby Parker, and Lyra Health.

companies.name: Allianz Technology Standards
companies.description: A collection of technology standards and guidelines maintained by Allianz for software development, API design, architecture, and engineering practices. Allianz follows API-first development using OpenAPI specifications, Backend for Frontends (BFF) architecture, and standardized patterns for pagination, sorting, webhooks, and asynchronous processing.

companies.name: Altimeter Capital
companies.description: Altimeter Capital is a technology-focused investment firm founded in 2008 by Brad Gerstner in Boston, Massachusetts, launched during the financial crisis with less than $3 million from friends and family. Headquartered in both Boston, MA and Menlo Park, CA (on Sand Hill Road), Altimeter runs a life-cycle crossover platform that backs technology companies from early stage through IPO and beyond: it manages a long/short public equity fund investing in technology companies alongside private growth equity funds targeting both early- and later-stage tech ventures. Brad Gerstner, founder, chairman and CEO, looks for platforms rather than products - businesses with network effects, expanding margins, and leaders who can adapt and scale - and has been a vocal proponent of an AI "supercycle" driven by accelerated computing and data-center demand. Altimeter also sponsored two SPACs (Altimeter Growth Corp, which merged with Grab, and Altimeter Growth Corp 2). Notable private and pre-IPO investments include Snowflake, Confluent, Okta, UiPath, GitLab, Unity, Roblox, SoFi, Plaid, ByteDance, Epic Games, dbt Labs, Baseten, and Anthropic. Reported assets under management have ranged from roughly $6.75B (Sep 2024) to higher figures across sources; Altimeter self-describes as "a technology-focused investment firm built by a founder for founders."

companies.name: Amplify Partners
companies.description: Amplify Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with a second office in San Francisco. Amplify positions itself as "the first investor for technical founders" — engineers, researchers, and scientists who have felt a problem viscerally and are compelled to spend a decade solving it. The firm invests primarily at the seed and Series A stages, with check sizes generally ranging from roughly $1M to $10M (often around $3M at seed), and continues to back companies through growth and IPO. Its thesis concentrates on deep technical categories: developer tools and computing infrastructure, machine learning and artificial intelligence, data and analytics, cybersecurity, and digital biology. In June 2025 Amplify announced roughly $900M in new capital across three vehicles — Fund 6, Fund 6 Select, and Amplify Bio. Notable portfolio companies include Datadog, Fastly, dbt Labs, Temporal, Chainguard, LangChain, Runway, and Recursion.

companies.name: Andreessen Horowitz
companies.description: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is a Silicon Valley venture capital firm founded in July 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. The firm invests across the full lifecycle from seed to venture to growth-stage technology companies, deploying stage-based checks that range from roughly $1M-$5M into early application bets up to hundreds of millions of dollars into its largest AI positions. a16z organizes around dedicated practice areas: AI, American Dynamism, Bio + Healthcare, Consumer, Crypto, Enterprise, Fintech, Games, Infrastructure, plus specialty vehicles including the Cultural Leadership Fund, Perennial, and the Speedrun accelerator. With over $90B-$100B+ in assets under management as of early 2026 and a public portfolio of more than 1,000 companies, a16z is one of the largest and most influential venture firms in the world, known for its operator-led platform model and notable investments including Airbnb, Coinbase, GitHub, Figma, Stripe, Databricks, Anduril, and OpenAI.

companies.name: API-First
companies.description: API-First is a software development methodology where APIs are treated as first-class citizens and designed before implementation begins. In an API-first approach, teams establish API contracts as the foundation of architecture, enabling parallel development, reusable services, consistent interfaces, and faster time-to-market. Organizations adopting API-first report 30-40% faster product releases (Gartner 2025) and significantly improved developer experience. The approach is foundational for microservices, headless architectures, and AI agent integrations.

companies.name: Architectural Design Patterns
companies.description: Architectural Design Patterns are reusable solutions to commonly occurring problems in software architecture. They provide templates for designing system structure, component interactions, and overall organization of applications across a range of industries and technical contexts.

companies.name: Arthur Ventures
companies.description: Arthur Ventures is a Minneapolis, Minnesota venture capital firm that invests in early-stage B2B software companies with a global reach. The firm backs capital-efficient, founder-led software businesses across the United States and internationally, partnering with teams building enterprise and vertical SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools, and data infrastructure. Arthur Ventures manages approximately $2B in assets under management, including roughly $800M in current active funds, and supports a portfolio of 60+ active companies. Notable portfolio investments include ThreatLocker, DNSFilter, Nucleus Security, DataCamp, Total Expert, Recast Software, CertifID, Hudu, Stream, and Macabacus. The firm is led by general partners Patrick Meenan, Ryan Kruizenga, and Andrew Heim, with offices at 250 Nicollet Mall in downtown Minneapolis.

companies.name: Atomico
companies.description: Atomico is a London-headquartered European venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Niklas Zennstrom, co-founder of Skype and Kazaa. Atomico partners with Europe's most ambitious technology founders from the earliest stages to pre-IPO across two dedicated teams: a Venture team that invests predominantly at Series A alongside occasional Seed opportunities, and a Growth team that invests from Series B to pre-IPO. In September 2024 the firm closed its largest ever fundraise, $1.24 billion across two funds - a $754M Atomico Growth VI vehicle and a $485M Atomico Venture VI vehicle - bringing total capital raised across seven funds to more than $5 billion. Growth-stage checks typically range from roughly $10M to $50M+. Atomico invests broadly across enterprise software, fintech, consumer, health, AI, developer tools, infrastructure, industrial and climate technology, with an explicit thesis that European technology has come of age. The firm operates offices in London, Paris, Berlin and Stockholm and is known for backing category-defining companies including Klarna, Stripe, Supercell, Graphcore, DeepL, Pipedrive, Truecaller, Wellhub, Lilium, Compass, Hinge Health and Sorare. Atomico also publishes the annual State of European Tech report, the definitive data-driven analysis of the European technology ecosystem.

companies.name: AUTHORS.md
companies.description: AUTHORS.md is a file format standard used in open-source and collaborative software projects to list the original creators, primary authors, and significant contributors of a project. Often required by open-source licenses such as GPL and Apache 2.0 to provide proper attribution, the AUTHORS.md file documents who wrote what portions of a codebase, their email addresses, and the scope of their contributions. Related standards include CONTRIBUTORS.md, All Contributors specification, and REUSE/SPDX contributor attribution frameworks.

companies.name: Balderton Capital
companies.description: Balderton Capital is a London-headquartered venture capital firm focused exclusively on backing European-founded technology companies. Founded in 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe and fully independent since 2007, Balderton is one of Europe's largest and most established venture firms, with over $7 billion in assets under management across dedicated early-stage and growth funds. The firm invests from Seed through Series B and follows on into growth stages, writing checks across sectors including fintech, artificial intelligence, B2B SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, digital health, gaming, marketplaces and climate. Balderton is known for a founder-centric model, running a dedicated founder wellbeing and performance platform and an executive/talent network to support portfolio companies. Notable investments over the firm's history include Revolut, GoCardless, Depop, Darktrace, Contentful, Dream Games, Wayve, Aircall, Citymapper, Talend, MySQL, Recorded Future, Sophia Genetics and The Hut Group (THG).

companies.name: Benchmark
companies.description: Benchmark is an American early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey, and Val Vaden, and headquartered at 140 New Montgomery Street in San Francisco, California (with a second office in Woodside). Benchmark is known for its distinctive equal partnership structure, where a small number of general partners share ownership and carry equally with no junior/senior hierarchy and no managing partner. The firm concentrates on leading first institutional rounds — typically Series A — and historically kept fund sizes small (around $425M) with a focus on consumer, marketplaces, social, open source, developer tools, infrastructure, enterprise software, fintech, crypto, and artificial intelligence. Benchmark has backed transformational companies including eBay, Uber, Twitter, Instagram, Snap, Dropbox, Discord, Docker, Zendesk, Confluent, Elastic, New Relic, Asana, Amplitude, Nextdoor, Stitch Fix, Yelp, OpenTable, Zillow, Red Hat, Airtable, Benchling, Cockroach Labs, Chainalysis, HackerOne, Contentful, Modern Treasury, Stytch, and, more recently, AI-native companies such as LangChain, Cerebras, MindsDB, Lovable, Legora, Gumloop, and Starcloud. In 2026 Benchmark broke with tradition to raise roughly $2B across two new vehicles, including its first-ever dedicated later-stage growth fund. This profile tracks Benchmark's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Bessemer Venture Partners
companies.description: Bessemer Venture Partners (BVP) is one of the oldest and largest venture capital firms in the world, founded in 1911 out of the fortune of steel magnate Henry Phipps and headquartered in San Francisco, California. With more than $20 billion in assets under management and investment teams in San Francisco, Silicon Valley, New York, Boston, London, Bangalore, and Tel Aviv, Bessemer invests globally across seed, early, and growth stages, and runs a dedicated private equity buyout arm, BVP Forge. The firm invests across artificial intelligence and machine learning, cloud and infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, healthcare and biotech, consumer, marketplaces, vertical software, data, deep tech and defense, and crypto/web3. Bessemer has backed transformative companies including Shopify, Twilio, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Yelp, DocuSign, Wix, Fiverr, Toast, ServiceTitan, PagerDuty, Auth0, Box, and Canva, and is known for publishing its "Anti- Portfolio" of missed opportunities, its Atlas research roadmaps, and its cloud/state-of-the-industry benchmark reports. Investing out of its 12th early-stage fund (a $3.85B vehicle), Bessemer was ranked among the largest venture firms by five-year fundraising. This profile tracks Bessemer's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Bloomberg Beta
companies.description: Bloomberg Beta is an early-stage venture capital firm that invests in companies making business work better, with a particular focus on the future of work, machine intelligence, and technologies reshaping how companies operate. Founded in 2013 and capitalized entirely by Bloomberg L.P. (though it invests independently), the firm runs approximately $450M across five $75M funds - its 2013, 2016, 2019, and 2022 vintages plus a first opportunity fund for follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies. Bloomberg Beta writes seed and early-stage checks (roughly $1M-$7M), leads or co-leads rounds, and is known for operating in public: its entire "operating manual," investment criteria, and full publicly announced portfolio live openly on GitHub, and it open-sources its Series Seed, SAFE, and note investment documents. The firm operates from San Francisco (140 New Montgomery St.) and New York (731 Lexington Ave.), backs founders across developer tools, infrastructure, security, AI, and enterprise software, and measures itself primarily on founder NPS.

companies.name: BOND
companies.description: BOND is a San Francisco-based growth-stage venture capital firm founded in 2018 by Mary Meeker, Mood Rowghani, Noah Knauf, and Juliet de Baubigny as a spinout of the Kleiner Perkins Digital Growth Fund. BOND backs proven, high-growth internet and software companies that have already established product-market fit, helping them scale globally toward IPO readiness. The firm invests primarily at the late/growth stage (roughly Series C and beyond) and is known for Mary Meeker's influential multi-hundred-page Internet Trends and AI Trends reports. Sectors span artificial intelligence, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, health and biotech, consumer and marketplaces, and frontier hardware. BOND has raised three funds - $1.25B (2019), $2B (2021), and $2.5B (2022) - and its portfolio and track record include Canva, OpenAI, Stripe, Postman, Netlify, Revolut, Ironclad, Applied Intuition, DoorDash, Duolingo, and Uber.

companies.name: Canaan Partners
companies.description: Canaan Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1987 as a management buyout spin-out from General Electric's venture unit. The firm invests in "visionaries with transformative ideas," backing companies from seed through Series A across a roughly 60/40 split between technology and healthcare. On the technology side Canaan funds developer tools, security, infrastructure, fintech, consumer, AI, and frontier/deep-tech companies; on the healthcare side it specializes in de novo biotech creation, therapeutics, and medical devices. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut with offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, and New York City, Canaan has raised roughly $7 billion across 13 funds and is actively deploying Fund XIII. Over its 37-year history the firm reports a track record of 73 IPOs and 152 M&A exits, with notable investments including Instacart, LendingClub, The RealReal, DexCom, Match.com, Snyk, Turo, Cardlytics, and Day One Biopharmaceuticals.

companies.name: Circuit Breaker
companies.description: The Circuit Breaker is a stability pattern for distributed systems and API architectures that prevents cascading failure when a downstream service degrades. A breaker wraps a remote call and tracks failures against a threshold; when the threshold is exceeded the breaker "opens" and short-circuits subsequent calls (typically returning an error or fallback) without contacting the downstream service. After a cooldown the breaker enters a "half-open" probe state and either resets to "closed" on success or re-opens on failure. The pattern was popularized by Michael Nygard in *Release It!* and is now standard in resilient microservice and API gateway design.

companies.name: Coatue Management
companies.description: Coatue Management is a global technology-focused investment manager founded in 1999 by Philippe Laffont, headquartered in New York City with offices in Menlo Park, San Francisco, London, and Hong Kong. Originally launched as a technology hedge fund, Coatue now invests across public and private markets through venture, growth, tactical (structured debt and equity), and public equities strategies, emphasizing data-driven research and responsible risk management. The firm backs disruptive, high-growth technology companies with a strong current thesis around artificial intelligence, software, cloud and data infrastructure, fintech, and frontier/space, writing checks that range from early-stage venture ($500K–$10M) through large growth and public-market allocations. Coatue managed roughly $54–55B in assets as of end of 2024 and counts Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, SpaceX, Figma, and Cursor among its private portfolio companies.

companies.name: Code First
companies.description: Code-first is an API design and software development approach where the application's source code is the primary source of truth and the API contract (OpenAPI document, GraphQL schema, gRPC proto, type definitions) is generated from that code via decorators, annotations, type inference, or runtime introspection. It contrasts with the design-first (or contract-first) approach in which a hand-authored OpenAPI/GraphQL/Proto contract is written first and code is scaffolded from it. Code-first approaches are widely used in TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, and C# ecosystems where strong type systems make schema generation reliable.

companies.name: Command Line Interface
companies.description: Command Line Interface (CLI) is a text-based way of interacting with software by typing commands at a prompt. Modern CLI design draws on decades of UNIX conventions while incorporating contemporary practices around discoverability, human-friendly output, machine-readable formats, configuration, subcommands, and progressive disclosure of complexity. CLIs remain a central surface for developer tools, infrastructure automation, package managers, build systems, and anything that benefits from scripting and composition.

companies.name: Configuration Language
companies.description: Configuration languages are formats and DSLs used to express the desired state of software systems, infrastructure, applications, and APIs. Configuration languages span a spectrum from simple text-based formats (INI, JSON, YAML, TOML) to typed and templated formats (HCL, Cue, Dhall, Pkl, Jsonnet, KDL) that support imports, schemas, and validation. The choice of configuration language shapes how teams describe Kubernetes manifests, Terraform infrastructure, OpenAPI specs, CI pipelines, and developer environments.

companies.name: Consensus
companies.description: Consensus is the distributed systems problem of getting a set of unreliable processes to agree on a value or sequence of values. Consensus algorithms power state-machine replication for databases, key-value stores, configuration systems, and blockchains. The consensus topic spans classical crash-fault tolerant algorithms (Paxos, Raft, Multi-Paxos, Zab, Viewstamped Replication) and Byzantine fault tolerant algorithms (PBFT, Tendermint, HotStuff, Casper FFG/CBC), and the impossibility result FLP that bounds what is possible in fully asynchronous models.

companies.name: copilot-instructions.md
companies.description: copilot-instructions.md is a GitHub Copilot custom instructions file placed at .github/copilot-instructions.md in a repository. It provides repository-specific guidance and preferences that GitHub Copilot Chat, Copilot in the IDE, and the Copilot coding agent automatically inject into prompts when working in the repository. The file is plain Markdown in natural language, helping the AI understand build, test, validation, framework, and style conventions so it can produce code that is consistent with the project's expectations and reduce pull request rejections caused by avoidable lint, CI, or convention failures.

companies.name: Craft Ventures
companies.description: Craft Ventures is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in late 2017 by repeat entrepreneurs David Sacks and Bill Lee, built "by founders for founders" and rooted in the operator playbook of the PayPal Mafia. The firm invests across early and growth stages, writing checks that range from micro-seed positions through double-digit millions, and specializes in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, and enterprise software prized for high-growth, high-margin, recurring-revenue economics. Craft is known for its rigorous, metrics-driven SaaS operating framework and hands-on support spanning talent, go-to-market, community, and finance. Beyond core SaaS, the portfolio spans artificial intelligence, developer tools, fintech and crypto, cybersecurity, digital health, defense, and frontier technology. The firm manages roughly $3.3 billion in assets across four early-stage funds and two growth funds, including Craft Ventures IV ($712M) and Craft Ventures Growth II ($608M). Notable investments include Airbnb, Affirm, Reddit, Uber, Lyft, Palantir, Slack, ElevenLabs, Supabase, Anduril, and Neuralink. Headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in New York City and Austin, Texas, and a primarily United States geographic focus.

companies.name: Creandum
companies.description: Creandum is a leading European early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 by Staffan Helgesson and headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, with additional offices in Berlin, London, and San Francisco. The firm backs founders building global, category-defining technology companies from seed to IPO and beyond, with its tagline "we back the companies of tomorrow before it's obvious." Creandum invests across software and SaaS, artificial intelligence, fintech, consumer, marketplaces, developer tools, and infrastructure, primarily across Europe with a growing US presence. Typical investment checks range from roughly $200K to $10M, and the firm manages around $2B in assets, having closed a €500M fund to back European early-stage startups. Its portfolio of 150+ companies includes some of Europe's most successful tech businesses such as Spotify, Klarna, Depop, Trade Republic, Pleo, Neo4j, iZettle, Bolt, Kry/Livi, Lovable, and Navan. This profile tracks Creandum's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: crob.at
companies.description: Free, no-login web tool for sharing Pokémon Showdown teams as visual pages, with a public REST API for creating/retrieving teams, generating random teams, and fetching sample teams.

companies.name: CRV
companies.description: CRV (formerly Charles River Ventures) is one of the oldest venture capital firms in the United States, founded in 1970 to commercialize research coming out of MIT. The firm invests early — primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, with occasional Series B — leading rounds in enterprise, consumer, developer tools, security, data infrastructure, AI, and bioengineering companies. CRV has backed more than 750 companies since inception across 18 funds, raising over $4.3 billion (including a recent $600M early-stage fund), and has seen 80-plus of its portfolio companies reach public-company status. Notable investments include DoorDash, Airtable, HubSpot, Datadog, Zendesk, Patreon, Mercury, Vercel, Cursor, Postman, Kong, Tailscale, Ring, and PillPack. The firm is headquartered in San Francisco (52 Zoe Street) with a long-standing Bay Area presence and offices in Menlo Park, CA and Cambridge, MA.

companies.name: Data Quality Standards
companies.description: Data Quality Standards is the landscape of frameworks, standards, and tools used to define and measure the accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness of data. It spans ISO/IEC 25012 and ISO 8000, the DAMA-DMBOK data quality dimensions, EDM Council DCAM, and open source and commercial tooling like Great Expectations, Soda, dbt tests, Monte Carlo, and Anomalo.

companies.name: Electric Capital
companies.description: Electric Capital is an engineering-led venture capital firm founded in 2018 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, investing in founders building frontier technologies across crypto, cryptography, distributed systems, and AI. The firm backs user-owned technology and cryptographic infrastructure that reduces reliance on intermediaries and gives users control, privacy, and access. Electric Capital invests from pre-seed through growth, with typical checks ranging from roughly $1M to $15M+, and has deployed more than $3B since inception across multiple funds (including a $1B raise announced in 2022). Its portfolio spans DeFi, layer-1 and layer-2 infrastructure, exchanges, developer tools, security, identity, and select AI, fintech, healthcare, and deep-tech companies, with notable investments including Solana, Kraken, EigenLayer/EigenCloud, dYdX, Magic Eden, Sui/Mysten Labs, NEAR, Consensys, and Aave. The firm is also known for authoring the widely cited annual Electric Capital Developer Report.

companies.name: Emergence Capital
companies.description: Emergence Capital is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, focused exclusively on early-stage B2B / enterprise software. Its founding thesis — that business software would move to the cloud — produced some of the defining SaaS bets of the era, including a contrarian 2003 investment in Salesforce and being the sole venture backer of Veeva's 2008 Series A. The firm runs a deliberately high-conviction, low-volume model in which each partner makes roughly one investment per year, enabling deep engagement with every founder. Its current thesis centers on "AI-native services" — companies that sell outcomes rather than software subscriptions, whose service margins improve as AI models improve — alongside AI infrastructure, physical-world AI, and horizontal and vertical SaaS. Emergence closed Fund VII at $1B in March 2025 (its largest fund, following Fund VI at $575M in 2021), has deployed less than $2.5B to generate $9B+ in realized returns, and its portfolio companies are collectively worth over $450B. Notable investments include Salesforce, Zoom, Veeva, Box, Bill.com, Gusto, Doximity, and Ironclad. Reported outcomes: 90%+ of early-stage investments raised successful follow-ons, 20%+ surpassed a $1B valuation, and 10%+ went public.

companies.name: EQT Ventures
companies.description: EQT Ventures is the early-stage venture capital business within EQT Group, launched in 2016 and operating out of Stockholm with investment-advisory offices in London, Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam, and the United States (San Francisco / New York); the funds themselves are domiciled in Luxembourg. The firm is a sector-agnostic, conviction-led lead investor that backs what it calls "Generation-Defining Companies" from pre-seed and seed through Series A and B, writing checks that reported ranges place between roughly EUR 1M and EUR 75M (most commonly EUR 2M-50M) and following on as companies scale. EQT Ventures has raised approximately EUR 2.3B across three funds (EQT Ventures I, II, and III) and is staffed largely by ex-founders and operators who provide hands-on support in addition to capital. Its focus spans AI, SaaS and developer tools, fintech, healthtech, climate and deeptech, robotics and aerospace, gaming, and consumer/marketplaces. Notable investments include Wolt, Depop, Typeform, AnyDesk, Netlify, Fly.io, Einride, Small Giant Games, Kry, and Beamery.

companies.name: First Round Capital
companies.description: First Round Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Josh Kopelman and Howard Morgan, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York and Philadelphia. First Round invests almost exclusively at the earliest stages of company creation, typically writing lead checks in the $750K to $4M range, and partners (many of them former founders) work side-by-side with companies through their first few years. The firm is a generalist that seeks contrarian insight into how markets work, with concentration in enterprise software, AI, fintech, healthcare, hardware, and consumer. Since founding it has backed 500+ startups and was the first institutional investor in Uber; its portfolio includes Notion, Roblox, Square, Looker, Upstart, Verkada, Warby Parker, Flatiron Health, and Clay. First Round also runs The Review, a widely read operator-focused editorial publication, and self-reports roughly $2.5B in assets under management.

companies.name: Foundry Group
companies.description: Foundry Group is a Boulder, Colorado venture capital firm founded in 2007 by Brad Feld, Seth Levine, Ryan McIntyre, and Jason Mendelson. The firm invests in early-stage technology startups across the United States, organizing its work around long-lived, horizontal investment themes (such as "glue", "protocol", "distribution", and "human computer interaction") rather than narrow verticals, with a particular affinity for hardware, robotics, consumer internet, developer tools, and B2B SaaS. Foundry pioneered a "network-driven" model that operates both as a direct investor in startups and as a limited partner in a curated network of more than 40 partner venture funds. The firm manages more than $3.0B for its limited partners, has made 320+ investments and 70+ exits, and is known for radical transparency through the books, blogs, and podcasts of its partners. Notable investments include Fitbit, Zynga, SendGrid, MakerBot, Gnip, Mapbox, SeatGeek, and WHOOP. In 2022 the partners announced Foundry would not raise another fund, continuing to steward its existing funds and portfolio through their life.

companies.name: GGV Capital
companies.description: GGV Capital (Granite Global Ventures) was a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco, Shanghai, Beijing, and Singapore. GGV invested from seed through growth stage across Social/Internet and consumer, Enterprise Tech and SaaS, and Smart Tech (fintech, infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, AI, and cross-border commerce), with a distinctive US–Asia bridge thesis. At its peak the firm managed roughly $9.2B in assets under management and backed more than 400 companies, including 44 unicorns and dozens of IPOs — among them Airbnb, Slack, Square, Affirm, HashiCorp, Coinbase, Peloton, Opendoor, Poshmark, StockX, BigCommerce, Grab, Alibaba, ByteDance, Zendesk, and Xpeng. On March 29, 2024 GGV Capital ceased using the GGV brand and split into two independent successor firms amid US–China tensions: Notable Capital (US/international, led by Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon, ~$4.2B AUM) and Granite Asia (Asia, led by Jenny Lee and Jixun Foo, ~$5B AUM). The former ggvc.com companies surface now redirects to Notable Capital, which carries the US/international portfolio graph. This profile tracks GGV Capital's identity and portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: GV
companies.description: GV (formerly Google Ventures) is the venture capital arm of Alphabet, founded in 2009 by Bill Maris and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area with additional offices in New York, Cambridge, and London. With Alphabet as its sole limited partner, GV operates with the reliability of a single LP, the autonomy of a traditional venture firm, and deep technical expertise, investing from seed through growth stage across technology and life sciences. Its focus areas span AI, enterprise, consumer, frontier tech, and life sciences, with a heavy recent emphasis on the AI frontier, from applications and developer tools to infrastructure and healthcare. GV manages over $13 billion in assets and supports roughly 400 active portfolio companies across North America, Europe, and Israel. The firm has backed notable companies including Uber, Slack, GitLab, Nest, Flatiron Health, Lemonade, Vercel, Isomorphic Labs, and insitro, with a track record of more than 80 IPOs and 230+ M&A exits.

companies.name: Homebrew
companies.description: Homebrew is a San Francisco-based seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2013 by Hunter Walk (a former product leader at Google and YouTube) and Satya Patel (a former VP of Product at Twitter, partner at Battery Ventures, and product leader at Google). Named after the Homebrew Computer Club, the firm practices high-conviction, concentrated seed investing, taking board-level positions and acting as an extension of the founder's team. Roughly 90% of its investments are pre-seed and seed, with initial checks in the $100K-$500K range and the ability to follow on up to $25M+ in later rounds. Homebrew backs mission-driven founders working on large, urgent, and valuable problems across fintech, AI/ML, healthcare, climate, defense, logistics, real estate, and consumer, focused on companies operating in the Americas. After a decade of institutional funds that backed companies such as Chime, Plaid, Gusto, and Mercury, Homebrew announced in 2021 that it would stop raising outside LP capital and invest only its own money going forward under the banner "Homebrew Forever."

companies.name: Index Ventures
companies.description: Index Ventures is a global venture capital firm founded in Geneva in 1996 by Neil Rimer, David Rimer and Giuseppe Zocco, and headquartered in London with offices in San Francisco, New York, Geneva and Jersey. The firm invests across the full startup lifecycle through dedicated vehicles: Origin (seed), Venture (early-stage) and Growth funds, backing companies from seed to IPO. It focuses on artificial intelligence and machine learning, business applications, data, fintech, security, healthcare, entertainment, media, mobility, retail, open source and the future of work. Index has raised roughly $15B in total capital, including $2.3B announced in 2024 ($800M early-stage, $1.5B later-stage). Notable investments include Adyen, Figma, Datadog, Discord, Revolut, Wise, Robinhood, Roblox, Confluent, Anthropic, Scale AI and Wiz. Its philosophy emphasizes backing founders on character and vision — 'we invest in who you are, not just what you do.'

companies.name: Insight Partners
companies.description: Insight Partners is a global software-focused venture capital and private equity firm founded in 1995 by Jeff Horing and Jerry Murdock and headquartered in New York City, with additional offices in London, Tel Aviv, and Palo Alto. The firm invests in high-growth technology and software ScaleUp companies at every stage from early (Series A) through growth and late-stage pre-IPO, deploying checks that range from roughly $5M up to $500M+ and pairing capital with a dedicated in-house operations team (Insight Onsite) that provides talent, sales, marketing, and product expertise to accelerate scaling. Sector emphasis spans enterprise software broadly, including cybersecurity, fintech, AI/ML, DevOps, data infrastructure, and healthtech. With approximately $90B in regulatory assets under management as of 2025 and more than 875 companies backed worldwide, Insight is one of the largest technology investors in the world, with a portfolio and exit history that includes Twitter, Shopify, DocuSign, Wix, SentinelOne, HelloFresh, N26, Alteryx, and AppDynamics.

companies.name: Institutional Venture Partners
companies.description: Institutional Venture Partners (IVP) is a later-stage venture capital and growth equity firm founded in 1980 by Reid Dennis and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco and London. One of the oldest venture firms in Silicon Valley, IVP concentrates on the fastest-growing, most prominent late-stage and growth-stage technology companies each year, typically writing checks in the $10M to $100M range and taking a long-term view toward value creation. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, fintech, cybersecurity, developer tools and cloud infrastructure, data and AI, consumer internet, media, gaming, and healthcare. Across roughly 45 years and 18 funds (Fund XVIII closed at $1.6B in 2024) IVP has backed more than 400 companies and seen 135+ IPOs, with roughly $7B–$8B in assets under management. Notable investments and exits include Netflix, Twitter, Snap, Coinbase, Dropbox, GitHub, Slack, Datadog, CrowdStrike, HashiCorp, UiPath, Robinhood, Klarna, Wise, Figma, Grammarly, Rubrik, Discord, Anthropic, Perplexity, and DeepL.

companies.name: JSON Schema
companies.description: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for annotating and validating JSON documents, widely used for defining API request and response shapes across REST APIs. The current stable specification is Draft 2020-12. JSON Schema differentiates between the instance being validated and the schema document containing the validation rules, and supports URI-based references for recursive and cross-document definitions.

companies.name: Kindred Ventures
companies.description: Kindred Ventures is a San Francisco-based, earliest-stage venture capital firm founded in 2014 by Steve Jang and led today as a partnership with Managing Partners Steve Jang and Kanyi Maqubela. The firm backs visionary and relentless founders building the future with technology and science, investing primarily at the pre-seed and seed stage and often partnering with entrepreneurs before a company is even formed. Kindred runs a deliberately concentrated, high-touch model of roughly 25 companies per fund, and has backed 100+ startups whose aggregate market capitalization now exceeds $200B. It invests across AI and new computing, crypto/web3, fintech, consumer, health and wellness, climate tech, mobility and logistics, and developer tools and infrastructure. With around $600M in assets under management, notable investments and exits include Uber, Coinbase, Poshmark, Reddit, Postmates, Blue Bottle Coffee, Perplexity, Tala, Magic Eden, dYdX, and PlayAI (acquired by Meta in 2025).

companies.name: Kleiner Perkins
companies.description: Kleiner Perkins is one of Silicon Valley's oldest and most storied venture capital firms, founded in 1972 by Eugene Kleiner and Tom Perkins and headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Shanghai. Across more than five decades and 21 venture funds plus 6 growth funds, the firm has invested over $10 billion and backed more than 900 ventures, including foundational companies such as Amazon, Google, Genentech, Electronic Arts, Juniper Networks, Intuit, Spotify, Figma, Robinhood, DoorDash, Duolingo and Databricks. Kleiner Perkins partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond across early and growth stages, with seed rounds averaging roughly $4-5M and Series A rounds around $17-18M. In 2026 the firm announced its twenty-second venture fund, KP22, a $1B early-stage fund, alongside $2.5B in new growth funds. Current investment focus centers on artificial intelligence and AI safety, enterprise software, developer tools and infrastructure, healthcare and biotech, fintech, hardtech and autonomous systems, and cybersecurity, with a thesis that the right idea, team and partners can create an entirely new industry.

companies.name: Kubernetes Operators
companies.description: Kubernetes Operators are a method of packaging, deploying, and managing Kubernetes applications that extend the Kubernetes API to create, configure, and manage instances of complex applications on behalf of a Kubernetes user.

companies.name: Leadout Capital
companies.description: Leadout Capital is an early-stage venture capital fund headquartered in Portola Valley, California, founded in 2018 by Ali Rosenthal — an early Facebook business hire who drove growth of Facebook Mobile, later VP of Partnerships at Wealthfront, and previously of Goldman Sachs M&A and General Atlantic. The firm leads, co-leads, or takes a significant position in pre-seed and seed rounds, organizing its thesis around "founder-market fit": founders with a unique insight about a market, often born of the founding team's lived experience and their ability to build empathy with the customers they are innovating for. Leadout looks for products with strong network effects, unique data sets, organic and viral growth characteristics, great unit economics, and long-term defensibility. Its 46-company portfolio spans SaaS, vertical SaaS, marketplaces, healthcare, consumer and commerce, and infrastructure/developer tools, and includes Expo, Cloudsmith, Creatify AI, AtoB, R-Zero, Near Space Labs, Pavilion, Momentum, Axiom Cloud, and theCut. Leadout is a partner fund within Foundry Group's network-driven limited-partner model.

companies.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
companies.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners is a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Barry Eggers, Christopher Schaepe, Ravi Mhatre, and Peter Nieh, and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Lightspeed invests from seed through Series F and beyond, backing bold builders across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud and enterprise infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, consumer, gaming, and healthcare/biotech. The firm operates as a single global team across roughly a dozen offices in the United States, Europe, Israel, India, and Southeast Asia, with U.S./Europe/Israel run by Lightspeed Management Company (LSVP) and India/Southeast Asia by Lightspeed India Partners (LSIP). Lightspeed reports managing on the order of $25B+ (up to $40B+ by some self-reported figures) across the Lightspeed platform. Notable investments and exits include Anthropic, Mistral AI, ElevenLabs, Wiz, Rubrik, Cato Networks, Stripe, Affirm, Snap, Nutanix, MuleSoft, AppDynamics, Nest, Grafana, ngrok, Faire, and Navan.

companies.name: Linux Server
companies.description: Linux Server is a topic catalog covering management, administration, and monitoring interfaces used to operate Linux servers in production. It organizes references to systemd, cockpit, the Linux audit framework, package managers (apt, dnf, rpm), configuration management and provisioning tooling, and remote administration protocols commonly used on Linux servers.

companies.name: Matrix Partners
companies.description: Matrix Partners (now branded simply "Matrix") is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1977 by Paul Ferri, investing from idea through Series A. Headquartered in San Francisco at 535 Mission Street with a long-standing East Coast office in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the firm is run by former founders and company builders who describe themselves as "contrarians who invest with conviction," backing founders with deep technical expertise and a specific vision of the future. Matrix is a generalist early-stage investor across AI / frontier tech, B2B and enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthtech, infrastructure, and semiconductors, typically writing seed and Series A checks and leading rounds. Over nearly five decades the firm has backed foundational technology and consumer companies including Apple, HubSpot, Zendesk, Canva, Afterpay, Oculus, Fivetran, Flock Safety, Quora, Postmates, GOAT, and Suno, with a track record spanning semiconductors and networking through today's AI-native startups.

companies.name: Modal
companies.description: Modal is a serverless cloud platform for AI and data workloads. Modal lets developers write ordinary Python and run it on remote GPUs and CPUs with sub-second cold starts, instant autoscaling, and declarative container images. The platform's primitives — Functions, Sandboxes, Volumes, Images, Secrets, Dicts, Queues, Schedules, and Web Endpoints — cover inference, fine-tuning, multi-node training, batch processing, agent code execution, and HTTP/web APIs. Modal sells per-second metered compute across the full NVIDIA GPU lineup (T4 → B200) under Starter, Team, and Enterprise plans. Modal Labs raised a $355M Series C in 2026 and is used in production by Decagon, Runway, Physical Intelligence, Suno, Chai Discovery, Lovable, Quora, Reducto, and many others.

companies.name: Northzone
companies.description: Northzone is a multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 1996 in Oslo and now headquartered in London, with additional offices in New York, Stockholm, Berlin and Amsterdam. The firm partners with founders across the United States and Europe from Seed through Growth, positioning itself as a single long-term partner from the first check all the way to IPO, with check sizes ranging from roughly $1M to $50M. Over nearly three decades Northzone has raised 13 funds, backed more than 250 companies, produced 18 unicorns and 14 IPOs, and reports $3.1bn+ in assets under management; its most recent flagship vehicle raised approximately €1bn. Northzone invests broadly across AI, enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthcare, climate and energy, and infrastructure and developer tools, and is known for early backing of category creators including Spotify, Klarna, Trustpilot, Kahoot!, Personio, TrueLayer, Avito and iZettle. The firm supports portfolio companies through a Platform team and a network of 500+ operators drawn from companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Stripe.

companies.name: Point Nine Capital
companies.description: Point Nine Capital is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Berlin, Germany. It is one of Europe's best-known seed investors, specializing in B2B SaaS, B2B marketplaces, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health, and increasingly AI across digital, physical, and biological domains. Point Nine typically writes initial checks of roughly $1M-$10M (EUR 0.5M-5M) and aims to be the first institutional investor for "v0.9" founders graduating from friends-and-family capital. The firm runs a deliberately small, equal partnership in which each partner works closely with only 6-8 companies at a time to provide deep operational support. Since inception it has backed more than 160 startups across 30+ countries, including early bets on Algolia, Chainalysis, Clio, Contentful, Delivery Hero, Docplanner, Factorial, Front, Loom, Mambu, NexHealth, Revolut, Typeform, Zendesk, and Westwing, with 11+ companies reaching unicorn status.

companies.name: QR Code Crafter
companies.description: Public QR code generation API by Brand Aspect Ltd supporting 27+ payload types (URL, WiFi, vCard, payments) with six export formats, bulk generation, and capability-managed dynamic redirect QR codes. Offers machine-readable OpenAPI, WebMCP browser-agent surface, llms.txt, and ai.txt agent guidance.

companies.name: QR Code Crafter APIs
companies.description: Public REST API and agent-native QR code generation platform by Brand Aspect Ltd, offering static QR generation across 27 payload types, six export formats, bounded bulk generation, and managed dynamic URL redirects with capability-token management.

companies.name: Redpoint Ventures
companies.description: Redpoint Ventures is a Silicon Valley venture capital firm founded in 1999 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Los Angeles and a history of China-focused funds in Beijing and Shanghai. Redpoint is a multi-stage investor that backs founders from seed and early stage through growth, running dedicated early-stage and growth teams. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, AI and AI infrastructure, cloud and data infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, consumer internet, healthcare, crypto/web3, and marketplaces. Typical checks range from roughly $0.5M-$2M at seed and $2M-$8M at Series A up to $10M+ at growth stage. As of 2025 Redpoint managed about $4.5 billion in assets, and its partners have participated in 130+ IPOs and acquisitions including Netflix, Snowflake, Twilio, Pure Storage, Zendesk, Stripe, HashiCorp, and HomeAway. The firm launched its tenth flagship fund, a $650M vehicle, in 2025, and publishes the annual InfraRed report on the leading private cloud and infrastructure companies. This profile tracks Redpoint's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: SAFe Agile
companies.description: The Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) is an enterprise-scale agile framework developed by Scaled Agile, Inc. that provides guidance for implementing agile practices across large organizations with multiple teams. SAFe organizes around five core disciplines: Lean Portfolio Management, Team and Technical Agility, Product Development Flow, Large Solution Integration and Delivery, and Leadership and Culture. Organizations use SAFe to align stakeholders, coordinate Agile Release Trains (ARTs), track PI objectives, and accelerate delivery of value. SAFe tools integrate with CI/CD pipelines, ERP systems, and planning platforms to support enterprise agile transformation.

companies.name: Sapphire Ventures
companies.description: Sapphire Ventures is a global software venture capital firm that partners with expansion-stage enterprise technology companies it believes can become category leaders. Originally founded in 1996 as the venture arm of SAP, the firm spun out as an independent company in 2011 and rebranded to Sapphire Ventures in 2014. Sapphire manages over $10 billion in assets under management and typically invests Series B through IPO, with check sizes commonly ranging from roughly $2M to $30M, while its Sapphire Sport and Sapphire Partners arms address early-stage sports/media and fund investing respectively. The firm concentrates on Enterprise AI and B2B software, including data and analytics, cybersecurity, DevOps and developer tools, fintech, health tech, and vertical SaaS. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, New York, and London, Sapphire backs companies of consequence and supports them with a large platform team that drives executive talent and customer introductions.
