The portfolio spans 30+ IPOs and 80+ exits including DocuSign, Square, Wise, monday.com, JFrog, Auth0, MuleSoft, and LinkedIn.

companies.name: Scale Venture Partners
companies.description: Scale Venture Partners (ScaleVP) is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Foster City, California, that invests primarily at Series A and Series B in founders applying AI to how businesses actually work. The firm traces its origins to 2000 as BA Venture Partners, the venture arm of Bank of America, and became an independent partnership in 2007. Scale focuses on AI and B2B software spanning applications, developer tools and infrastructure, and security, and leads roughly 80% of the rounds it joins. Initial checks typically range from $5M to $50M, sized to the round, and the firm looks for signed customers and repeatable demand (commonly $500K–$5M ARR) rather than a fixed revenue bar. Scale reports about $2.8B in assets under management and is currently deploying its $900M Fund VIII, raised in 2022. It invests across North America, Europe, and Israel, and pairs capital with a Go-To-Market advisory bench of CROs, CMOs, and CFOs. Scale has produced 11 IPOs — among the highest rates for early-stage firms — with notable investments including DocuSign, Box, HubSpot, BILL, and JFrog.

companies.name: Schema Design
companies.description: Schema Design is the practice of defining the structure, constraints, and semantics of data models used in APIs, databases, and data exchange formats. It encompasses schema-first API design approaches, data modeling methodologies, type systems, and tooling for creating, validating, and evolving data schemas. Key formats include JSON Schema, OpenAPI components/schemas, GraphQL types, Protocol Buffers, Apache Avro, and database DDL. Good schema design improves API consistency, enables automated validation, supports code generation, and facilitates interoperability between systems.

companies.name: Schema Stitching
companies.description: Schema Stitching is a GraphQL technique for combining multiple GraphQL schemas into a single unified API gateway. It enables developers to compose distributed GraphQL services, integrate third-party APIs, and build federated data layers by merging types, queries, and mutations from multiple subgraphs into one executable schema. The primary implementation is provided by The Guild's graphql-tools library, with support for type merging, stitching directives, schema delegation, and automated query planning.

companies.name: Seedcamp
companies.description: Seedcamp is Europe's original first-cheque seed fund, founded in May 2007 and headquartered in London, United Kingdom. It backs founders from day one, writing first cheques primarily at the pre-seed and seed stages (typically between roughly $350,000 and $1 million) and following winners into later rounds through its Select fund toward Series B and beyond. Seedcamp is broadly sector-agnostic across software and technology, with concentrations in artificial intelligence, fintech, healthtech, cybersecurity, open-source, enterprise software, and developer tools. In June 2026 the firm announced it had raised $320 million — $220 million for Seedcamp VII (its flagship first cheque fund) and $100 million for the Select fund — pushing assets under management past $1 billion. The "Seedcamp Nation" now spans 500-plus companies, including publicly listed UiPath and Wise and unicorns such as Revolut, Synthesia, Sorare, Pleo, wefox, and viz.ai. Seedcamp Investment Management LLP is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority.

companies.name: Sequoia Capital
companies.description: Sequoia Capital is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded by Don Valentine in 1972 and headquartered at 2800 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California. Sequoia partners with founders from idea to IPO and beyond, investing across seed, early, and growth stages, and has backed transformative companies including Apple, Google, Oracle, Cisco, NVIDIA, PayPal, YouTube, Airbnb, Stripe, WhatsApp, Instagram, DoorDash, Snowflake, and Reddit. Its stated mission is to "help the daring build legendary companies," with a current focus on artificial intelligence and AI agents, autonomous systems, fintech, developer tools and infrastructure, healthcare, and consumer technology. Following its 2024 restructuring, Sequoia operates primarily across the US and Europe, while its former India/SEA and China arms became the independent firms Peak XV Partners and HongShan. This profile tracks Sequoia's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Shasta Ventures
companies.description: Shasta Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 and based in Silicon Valley (Portola Valley / Menlo Park, on and around Sand Hill Road, California). Founded by Rob Coneybeer and Ravi Mohan (with Tod Francis and Jason Pressman among its long-tenured Managing Directors), the firm invests primarily at the Series A stage in United States technology startups, typically leading rounds and taking board seats. Shasta has roughly $1.3B under management across multiple funds (Fund II $250M, Fund III $265M, Fund IV $300M) and a 20-year track record. Its thesis centers on enterprise software / SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, data intelligence, camera / computer vision, and consumer subscription products, pairing capital with operational support (Shasta Elevate) for technical founders. Notable investments include Anaplan, Zuora, Nest, Nextdoor, Apptio, Eero, Sendbird, Tonal, Lattice, Highspot, SentinelOne and Turo, with 12 unicorns, multiple IPOs and dozens of acquisitions across its history.

companies.name: Slow Ventures
companies.description: Slow Ventures is a generalist early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, with additional offices in Boston and New York. The firm leads pre-seed and seed rounds, writing typical checks of roughly $500K to $3M (averaging around $1.75M), and explicitly rejects thematic investing in favor of backing experienced founders with deep, hard-won domain expertise and genuine conviction. Slow's thesis funds rapid, high-stakes experimentation: capital that tests a novel risk or hypothesis whose validation dramatically increases a company's value and that cannot easily be funded another way. As a generalist, Slow invests across consumer and social, fintech, SaaS and enterprise/developer tools, healthcare, crypto/web3, the creator economy, and real-world operations (SMB acceleration, buyouts/rollups, franchising). The firm runs a dedicated Creator Fund backing creator-led businesses, and has deployed roughly $800M+ across multiple fund vintages since inception. Notable investments include Pinterest, Slack, Robinhood, Nextdoor, Postmates, Opendoor, Wealthfront, Casper, PillPack, Airtable, Gusto, and Solana.

companies.name: Software Design Architectural Patterns
companies.description: Software architectural patterns are reusable solutions and best practices for organizing software system architecture. Key patterns include MVC (Model-View-Controller), Microservices, Layered Architecture, Event-Driven Architecture, CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation), Hexagonal Architecture, and Service-Oriented Architecture. These patterns are documented by Microsoft Azure Architecture Center, AWS Well-Architected Framework, and the broader software engineering community.

companies.name: Specification
companies.description: A subject-matter collection covering API specifications, specification formats, specification-driven development, and the broader specification landscape. This includes OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, GraphQL SDL, Arazzo, gRPC Protocol Buffers, RAML, API Blueprint, and other machine-readable API description formats. Specification-first development treats the API contract as the source of truth for code generation, documentation, testing, and governance.

companies.name: SpectrumOutage API
companies.description: Community-powered REST API for live Spectrum internet, TV, and phone outage data across the US. Independent tracker, not affiliated with Charter Communications or Spectrum. Provides aggregate stats, outage reports, city/state/ZIP status, and map pin data.

companies.name: Spot
companies.description: Spot by Flexera provides cloud infrastructure automation and optimization solutions. The platform includes Elastigroup for compute workload management across spot, reserved, and on-demand instances, Ocean for Kubernetes and container infrastructure automation, and Eco for cloud commitment management. The Spot API enables programmatic control over all platform capabilities including administration, compute groups, Kubernetes clusters, and cost optimization.

companies.name: SUPPORT.md
companies.description: SUPPORT.md is a GitHub community health file that describes how users can get help with an open source project. When present in a repository root or .github/ directory, GitHub automatically links to it from issue creation flows, directing users to appropriate support channels before filing bugs.

companies.name: Susa Ventures
companies.description: Susa Ventures is a San Francisco-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2013 by Chad Byers, Leo Polovets, and Seth Berman on the belief that founders are the lifeblood of progress. Susa is a high-conviction, low-volume seed investor that concentrates on data-centric companies with durable competitive moats such as proprietary data, economies of scale, and network effects, and it deliberately caps each partner at a small handful of active companies so it can operate alongside founders in a late-stage, hands-on manner at the earliest stages. The firm invests primarily at pre-seed and seed (occasionally Series A), writing initial checks that typically range from roughly $1M to $5M across artificial intelligence, fintech, healthcare, logistics and supply chain, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, and consumer. Susa is known for a founder-first posture (it avoids forcing founders out) and for an unusually high seed-stage unicorn hit rate, with notable investments including Robinhood, Flexport, Andela, Newfront, Stord, Human Interest, Mux, Stedi, Viz.ai, and Casetext. The firm closed Fund V at $175M in 2025 and also runs the experimental Humba Ventures vehicle for frontier bets. This profile tracks Susa's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: SV Angel
companies.description: SV Angel is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Ron Conway, one of Silicon Valley's most prolific angel investors. The firm runs two vehicles: an early-stage Seed Fund that writes roughly $200k checks into pre-seed and seed rounds, and a later-stage Growth Fund that invests at Series B and beyond. SV Angel is a founder-first, high-conviction investor that deliberately does not lead rounds, takes no board seats, and writes smaller checks as part of a larger syndicate so it can act as a neutral "routing layer" and advocate for founders. It is famous for its "Inflection Point Approach" — showing up at critical moments around fundraising, M&A, and business development. The firm invests almost entirely in US-based, software-driven companies across consumer and enterprise, and its portfolio has produced dozens of unicorns and landmark outcomes including Google, Airbnb, Coinbase, Stripe, Slack, Instacart, DoorDash, Reddit, Pinterest, GitHub, Databricks, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

companies.name: Techstars
companies.description: Techstars is a global pre-seed startup accelerator and investor founded in 2006 by David Cohen, Brad Feld, David Brown, and Jared Polis in Boulder, Colorado, and headquartered in New York City. Operating a worldwide network of mentorship-driven accelerator programs across cities including Boulder, Boston, Chicago, New York, London, and Tokyo, Techstars runs an intensive three-month program that provides each accepted company roughly $220,000 in capital — a $20,000 convertible equity agreement for a minimum 5% of common stock plus an optional $200,000 uncapped MFN post-money SAFE (Asia-Pacific programs at ~$100,000). The firm is largely sector-agnostic but is especially active in AI/ML, fintech, SaaS, developer tools, healthcare, climate, space and defense, and critical infrastructure, and operates on its signature "Give First" philosophy. Techstars has backed more than 10,000 founders, producing dozens of unicorns and notable companies including Twilio, SendGrid, DigitalOcean, Uber, Remitly, Chainalysis, ClassPass, DataRobot, and PillPack, with portfolio companies collectively raising tens of billions in follow-on capital.

companies.name: Threshold Ventures
companies.description: Threshold Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California that backs founder-led technology companies at the threshold of breakout growth. Threshold is the 2019 rebrand of Draper Fisher Jurvetson (DFJ), the storied Sand Hill Road firm founded in 1985; managing partners Emily Melton and Josh Stein spun the venture practice into an independent, focused fund. Threshold pursues a high-conviction strategy, concentrating on a small number of Series A and Series B investments and partnering hands-on with founders for the long term, frequently holding board seats through IPO and beyond. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health and healthcare, and AI. Its portfolio has produced 10 unicorns, 3 IPOs, and 17 acquisitions, and includes Box, Twilio, Redfin, Remitly, Doximity, Rippling, LaunchDarkly, Livongo, and Talkdesk. Threshold has invested in roughly 87 companies and raised a ~$250M fund following the rebrand.

companies.name: Thrive Capital
companies.description: Thrive Capital is a venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Joshua Kushner and headquartered in the Puck Building in New York City. The firm builds and invests in internet, software, and technology-enabled companies across the full lifecycle, from early-stage seed bets through growth and late-stage positions, and also incubates new companies through its Thrive Incubations program. Thrive concentrates its capital in a relatively small number of high-conviction positions across artificial intelligence, fintech, enterprise software, consumer internet, media and entertainment, healthcare, defense technology, and developer tools. The firm has scaled its funds steadily from a $5M first fund in 2009 to Thrive X, its tenth fund, which closed in early 2026 at over $10 billion (roughly $1B for early-stage and $9B for growth), bringing the firm to approximately $50 billion in assets under management. Nitin Nohria, the former dean of Harvard Business School, serves as executive chairman. Thrive is widely known as one of the earliest and most significant backers of OpenAI, Stripe, and SpaceX, and its portfolio includes Instagram, GitHub, Databricks, Ramp, Scale AI, Anduril, Robinhood, and Plaid.

companies.name: Trinity Ventures
companies.description: Trinity Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1986 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with more than three decades of history backing mission-driven entrepreneurs across technology and consumer markets. The firm takes a deliberately personal, low-capital-to-partner approach to early-stage investing, positioning itself as "the call you want to make, not the call you have to make" and emphasizing intellectual candor and lasting founder relationships. Trinity invests primarily at seed, Series A and Series B, with checks generally ranging from roughly $1 million to $15 million and averaging around $5 million. Its focus spans enterprise software and cloud infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, digital media and marketing technology, consumer products and services, healthcare, and artificial intelligence. Over nine funds the firm has managed on the order of $1.3 billion in assets and produced a track record that includes multiple unicorns, IPOs and roughly 130 acquisitions. Notable investments include Starbucks, New Relic, Auth0, Turo, Care.com, Zulily, Blue Nile, Aruba Networks, Infoblox, Cohesity, Outreach, InfluxData, Contentful and Docker. Trinity invests primarily in the United States.

companies.name: True Ventures
companies.description: True Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Jon Callaghan and Phil Black and headquartered in Palo Alto / San Francisco, California. Operating under a "first to believe" thesis, True writes the initial institutional check and stays invested through every subsequent stage of a company's journey, concentrating on pre-seed, seed, and Series A rounds with check sizes reported in the roughly $500K-$15M range. The firm invests broadly across technology and founder-led categories including software and developer infrastructure, consumer products and internet, healthcare and life sciences, hardware and robotics, climate and energy, security, and AI. With more than $3.8B in committed capital, True has backed 1,050+ founders across 500+ companies since inception, with notable early checks into Fitbit, Peloton, Ring, Automattic/WordPress, HashiCorp, Duo Security, Sweetgreen, Bluesky, and Splice. True is known for its founder-first platform, the True University founder camps, and long-term conviction-led early ownership.

companies.name: Uncork Capital
companies.description: Uncork Capital is a San Francisco-based seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Jeff Clavier, who formalized his angel portfolio into one of Silicon Valley's earliest dedicated seed funds; it operated as SoftTech VC until rebranding to Uncork Capital in 2017. Led by managing partners Jeff Clavier and Andy McLoughlin, the firm invests at the seed stage with a "first to believe" conviction style, typically targeting 10-15% ownership and writing seed checks broadly in the $1.5M-$4M range across B2B applications and SaaS, developer tooling, infrastructure and security, consumer and marketplaces, frontier tech/hardware, and AI/ML. In May 2025 the firm closed $300M in fresh capital across Uncork VIII (a $225M seed fund) and Uncork Plus IV (a $75M growth fund), bringing it to roughly $1.2B in assets under management. Across 275+ investments and 100+ outcomes, its portfolio and exits include SendGrid, Fitbit, Poshmark, Postmates, Eventbrite, LaunchDarkly, Tailscale, Front, Shippo, ClassDojo, Groq, Human Interest, Carrot Fertility, and GPTZero.

companies.name: Union Square Ventures
companies.description: Union Square Ventures (USV) is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 by Fred Wilson and Brad Burnham and headquartered at 817 Broadway in New York City. USV invests at the edge of large markets being transformed by technological and societal pressures, historically backing large networks of engaged users that are differentiated through user experience and defensible through network effects, and more recently companies that broaden access to knowledge, capital, and well-being. The firm invests primarily at Seed and Series A across three strategies — a Core fund, a Climate fund, and an Opportunity (later-stage) fund — with check sizes typically ranging from roughly $1M at seed to the low-to-mid single-digit millions at Series A. USV runs a small, collegial partnership and focuses on social media, marketplaces, developer tools, learning/education, health, fintech, web3/decentralized protocols, energy, and climate. It reports roughly $1.9B in assets under management across 14 funds. Notable investments include Twitter, Etsy, Coinbase, Stripe, Cloudflare, MongoDB, Twilio, Duolingo, Kickstarter, Stack Overflow, SoundCloud, and Carta.

companies.name: Y Combinator
companies.description: Y Combinator is the most influential startup accelerator in the world, founded in 2005 by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Tappan Morris, and Trevor Blackwell. Originally split between Cambridge, Massachusetts and Mountain View, California, YC consolidated in Silicon Valley and is now headquartered in San Francisco. YC runs a three-month program four times a year (winter, spring, summer, fall), each batch typically funding 250-300 early-stage startups. Its standard deal invests $500,000 in every company: $125,000 for 7% of the company on a post-money SAFE, plus $375,000 on an uncapped SAFE with a Most Favored Nation (MFN) provision. YC has funded more than 5,000 companies with a combined valuation exceeding $600 billion, including Airbnb, Stripe, Coinbase, DoorDash, Instacart, Dropbox, Reddit, Twitch, GitLab, and Ginkgo Bioworks. The firm is led by president and CEO Garry Tan, a General Partner and himself a YC alum. YC is sector-agnostic but heavily developer-tools, AI, fintech, B2B/SaaS, infrastructure, healthcare, and hard-tech oriented, and its alumni network of 6,000+ founders, plus Demo Day, Startup School, Work at a Startup, and Hacker News, form the connective tissue of the modern startup ecosystem.
